summary_text: A grumpy child is asked if they want a banana. They stay grumpy. Then they are offered a banana and a ball, but they are still grumpy. It is not bad.

video_title: 👦🏿 Jabari Jumps
summary_text: Jabari went to the diving board with his dad. He had finished swimming lessons and passed his swim test, so he said he was ready to jump. He watched the other kids climb the tall ladder and jump into the water. Jabari climbed up too, but the ladder felt very tall. He came back down and said he was tired. Then he remembered he had not done his stretches and said tomorrow might be a better day. His dad told him it was okay to feel a little scared and to take a deep breath. Jabari took a deep breath, climbed up again, and walked to the end of the board. He looked out, felt ready, and jumped into the water. He splashed down and came back up. His dad said, “Jabari, you did it,” and Jabari said he was a great jumper and that a surprise double backflip was next.

video_title: 👧🏻 My Body Belongs to Me From My Head to My Toes
summary_text: Clara says her body belongs only to her, and it is very special. When she was a baby, her body looked different, but now she is growing and changing. Sometimes Clara likes to be close to people. She likes hugs from Papa, sitting on Granny’s lap, holding a little baby’s hands, and tickling a friend. These touches feel nice and cozy when both people want them. But Clara also says that sometimes she does not want to be touched. She does not like too much tickling, big sloppy kisses, a dog licking her, or being held too tight. When she does not like touch, she says, “Stop it! Don’t touch me. I don’t want you to.” She also says no when she does not want to touch someone else. If someone does not stop after she says no, Clara should tell a trusted person. Clara decides who may touch her and when.

video_title: 🐱 Pete the Cat's Family Road Trip
summary_text: Pete, Bob, Mom, and Dad go on a road trip across the United States. Dad puts the bags on the roof, and Mom picks the music. Their first stop is Niagara Falls, where they ride a boat and see the big waterfall up close. Then they visit Boston and walk the Freedom Trail. They take a photo by Paul Revere’s house. Next, they go to New York City and ride an elevator to the top of One World Trade Center. They see the Statue of Liberty. In Savannah, they ride a riverboat, and Pete orders a slice of peach pie. In Key West, Pete meets a six-toed cat and talks to it. In New Orleans, the family hears jazz music and dances in the street. Soon, the car gets a flat tire on Route 66, but Mom and Dad change it, and the trip continues.

video_title: 🐰 The Story of the Easter Bunny
summary_text: On a snow-cold day, a round old couple worked in their snug little house to get ready for Easter. The round old man blew the insides out of eggs, and the round old woman painted them with pretty colors. The little rabbit watched. Later, they made straw baskets together and then chocolate eggs on a spring day when the snow was melting. When Easter came, they gave every child in the village a straw basket full of eggs. One year, the round old couple were asleep when there was still work to do. The little rabbit hopped onto the table, put the eggs into the baskets, and carried them down the lane. He left one basket for every child. The next year, he colored the eggs, cooked the chocolate, wove the baskets, and delivered them too. The children learned that the Easter bunny came. After many years, the old couple could not help anymore, so the little rabbit found a new hidden place to make the Easter baskets. Now he and his friends work there every year, and on Easter morning he still delivers the baskets.

video_title: 🦊 My Lucky Day
summary_text: One day, a hungry fox was getting ready to hunt when he heard a knock at his door. A piglet was outside. The fox opened the door, grabbed the piglet, and said it was his lucky day. He wanted to make a pig roast for dinner. The piglet asked to be washed first because he was dirty. The fox agreed and gave him a bath. Then the piglet said he was too small and should be fed first so he would make more meat. The fox agreed again and cooked him a nice dinner. After that, the piglet said his meat was tough and needed a massage to become tender. The fox worked very hard, pushing and squeezing the piglet. The piglet kept asking for more, and the fox grew tired and passed out. The piglet then picked up the rest of the cookies and went home. He relaxed by a warm fire and looked in his address book to see who to visit next.

summary_text: In the bakery, Arnie says hello to all the other donuts, like plane, Lonjon, donut holes, chimichu, powdered, and jelly. Then he notices one very big new shape outside. The others say it is much bigger than all of them and must be a special donut made from a whole batch of dough. Arnie tries to help figure out what kind of donut it is. He guesses it might be a long john, but long johns have filling coming out of the top. Then he says it might be a donut with no hole, but it has no frosting or sprinkles either. Arnie keeps checking and says it is almost like not a donut at all. Finally, he realizes it is a giant cookie made by Mr. Baker Man with a giant cookie cutter. Arnie still says it would look good with a frosting sprinkle mustache.

video_title: 🐸 Froggy's First Kiss
summary_text: The week before Valentine’s Day, Froggy thought about candy and love at school. In class, Miss Witherspoon told him to pay attention, but Froggy kept looking at the new girl, Frogalina. At recess, he saw her smile and fell on his head. At lunch, Frogalina sat beside him and gave him a juicy apple. The next day, she gave him a heart-shaped cookie. Later, the class made paper valentines, and Froggy wrote “I love you” on one card and hid under his desk so no one would see it. When he stood up, he bonked his head, and everyone laughed. The next day, Frogalina gave him a kiss on the cheek. Froggy felt strange and flopped away. On the bus, everyone teased him. At home, his mother asked about school and valentines. On Valentine’s Day morning, Froggy gave his mother breakfast in bed and gave her the heart that said “I love you.” His mother gave him many candy kisses.

summary_text: Ivan was a silverback gorilla who lived at the big top mall. He was happy because the mall was his home and his friends were there too. His friends included Soma, Murphy, Henrikh, Frankie, Bob, and Ruby. Ruby was the newest one, and Ivan showed her many things, like sneakers, a turtleneck, and crayons. He told her he used crayons to make drawings of beetles, bananas, places, and old friends. Ruby wanted to draw too, so Ivan gave her a crayon. She drew Ivan’s eye and then her own, and she said their eyes were the same. Ruby wanted to draw herself, but there was no crayon for her skin. Ivan gave her a silver crayon that Julia had saved for him. Ruby used it and saw that silver was the right color for how Ivan made her feel.

video_title: 🐦 Grumpy Bird
summary_text: Bird woke up feeling grumpy. He was too grumpy to eat, play, or fly, so he said, “Looks like I’m walking today.” Bird walked past sheep, rabbit, raccoon, beaver, and fox. Each one asked what he was doing, and Bird said he was walking. The other animals liked this and decided to walk with him. Bird kept walking, and the other animals walked too. Then Bird stopped, and the other animals stopped. Bird stood on one leg, and the other animals stood on one leg too. Bird jumped, and the other animals jumped too. Bird saw that this was fun. He forgot about being grumpy and asked everyone to fly back to his nest for a snack.

Next, the child wishes for deer horns, a wheel spout, a long long tail, and a long long nose. Each wish seems good at first, but then the child thinks about the trouble it would cause. A long nose might make Dad make the child do work all day. After thinking about all these things, the child decides that these wishes are not so good after all. In the end, the child says it is best to be just like me.

At the end, the child counted all the wacky things and got rid of the shoe on the wall.

When the colony hears it, Wilbur runs home, gets into his favorite outfit, and comes back fast. That day, some mole rats were naked and some wore clothes. After that, all the mole rats had a great time, no exceptions.

Finally, the cat called in more help from his hat, and many little cats came to clean the snow. At last, the house and yard were clean again.

video_title: 💤 Dr. Seuss's Sleep Book

It also tells about sleep talkers and sleepwalkers, and about a group that sleeps and walks while looking for soup. A fish is safe at night because all the fish are too sleepy to bite. At the end, the story says the number of sleeping creatures is enormous, and it ends with a quiet good night.

video_title: 🐭Chester’s Way by Kevin Henkes Read Aloud for Kids | Best Kids Story About Friendship & Change ✨ SWY
summary_text: Chester liked doing things the same way every day. He cut his sandwiches diagonally, got out of bed on the same side, and always double knotted his shoes. He ate toast with jam and peanut butter for breakfast and carried a tiny first aid kit. His best friend Wilson was just like him, so they did many things together. They played only if the other played, used hand signals, and shared the same ideas about food and games. One day Lily moved into the neighborhood. Lily did things her own way, wore band-aids, used disguises, and carried a squirt gun. At first Chester and Wilson hid from her. Then older boys bothered Chester and Wilson, and Lily scared them away while dressed as a fierce cat. After that, the three became friends. They ate lunch together, had a sleepover, shared breakfast, and taught each other new tricks. Now Chester, Wilson, and Lily do many things together.

The story then follows three Halloween tricksters: a sister dressed as a witch, a brother wearing bones, and a child dressed as a ghost in an old pillowcase.
They roam the streets, play tricks, and get treats, and they even scare one another and their mother.
The children buy a big orange pumpkin, scoop it out, carve a face into it, and place a candle inside to make a jack-o'-lantern.
Later, they count ghosts in different places around the house, from the pantry to behind the storyteller.
A green goblin waits outside, but is told to go away.
The story ends with trick-or-treating, bobbing for apples, avoiding a haunted house, running from a black cat, and then coming home full of candy and cake to dream about Halloween.

video_title: 🦴 Bony Legs | Engaging Read Aloud for Kids | Stories With Yaya 📚
summary_text: Bony Legs was a mean witch who lived deep in the woods in a hut on chicken feet. She had iron teeth and waited for children. Sasha lived nearby with her aunt. One morning, Sasha went to borrow a needle and thread. She carried bread and butter and some meat for lunch. On the way, she found the hut and went inside. At the gate, she used the butter to make the hinges quiet. She gave her bread to a hungry dog and her meat to a sad cat. Then Bony Legs told Sasha to get into the tub so she could cook her for supper and locked the door. Sasha was scared, but the cat helped her. The cat gave her a silver mirror, and the dog gave her a wooden comb. Sasha ran away. Bony Legs chased her, but Sasha threw the mirror and it became a lake. Then she threw the comb and it grew into tall trees. Bony Legs could not get past them, so Sasha went home safely.

video_title: VEGETABLE SOUP - Read Aloud - Sesame Street
summary_text: Cookie Monster was very hungry and waited for his groceries to come. When the doorbell rang, a delivery girl brought a box. Cookie Monster looked inside and did not see cookies. He found carrots, celery, broccoli, a beet, a squash, an onion, and potatoes. He used the carrots like a pencil and a hat, the celery like a back scratcher, the broccoli like a feather duster, the beet like a top, the squash like a telephone, the onion like a ball, and the potatoes like things to juggle. Then Ernie and Bert came in with the wrong groceries. They said the supermarket had mixed up the orders. They showed Cookie Monster that the vegetables were for soup. Bert and Ernie washed and cut the vegetables, cooked them, and waited until the soup was ready. Cookie Monster cooled the soup, then ate it all. After that, he ate the cookies too.

video_title: The Littlest Christmas Elf - Read Aloud - Bedtime Story
summary_text: Alistister the Elf left Elfen Corners for the North Pole. The village said goodbye, and the mayor said Santa had asked for their merriest elf. At the North Pole, Alistister was the littlest elf, and head elf Macafferty could not find him a job. He could not hammer a wagon, paint a dollhouse roof, stuff bears, or sweep with the big broom. The other elves laughed and said he was useless. Alistister felt sad and ran away. He hid by the wood pile near the reindeer pen and met an old elf named Nicholas. Nicholas asked his name and invited him to help with the reindeer. Alistister fed the reindeer, watered them, and sang songs with Nicholas. Later, Nicholas was gone, and Alistister worried and went to Santa’s house. There he found Nicholas, who was really Santa Claus, and learned he had a special job: to ride in the sleigh and help with Christmas Eve deliveries.

Bert’s fairy boat carries people in cars back and forth all day. Rodeo Rosy bounces over the sandy range in her jeep, Ernie’s tugboat pushes the big ocean liner into port, and Tot’s blimp glides over the city while everyone waves. Harry Monster drives the Sesame Street bus all around town and takes people where they want to go. At the last stop, everybody gets off.

Red crossed the finish line first. The bears cheered, and Little Red won the road race.

video_title: THE KITTEN WHO THOUGHT HE WAS A MOUSE | Storytime | Read Aloud
summary_text: Five mice lived in two nests, one outside for summer and one inside for winter. One day they found a tiny lost kitten in their nest. He was gray and black, with his eyes still closed. The mice felt sorry for him and let him stay. Father mice said they could bring him up to be a good mouse, and Lester named him Mickey. Mickey grew up eating seeds and bugs and sleeping with the mouse family. He learned about cats, dogs, people, and mouse traps. In the house, Mickey helped the mice by making the cat Hazel look for him while Lester and the sisters went to the pantry. Then Peggy and Paul saw Mickey and knew he was a kitten. They left milk for him, and he drank it every night. Soon Mickey learned to trust them. Peggy held him, and he made his first purr. At last Mickey learned he was a cat. He stayed with Peggy and Paul, visited the mice, and still helped keep Hazel away from the pantry.

After Mouse is clean and fed, he leaves the mess and goes back to bed.

video_title: MISS SPIDER’S TEA PARTY | KID’S READ ALOUD | STORYTIME
summary_text: Miss Spider sat alone and drank tea while she looked at the sky and the leaves. She wished for friends to stay with her so she could give them cakes and tea. First, two beetles, Ike and May, came out of the woodwork, but they were scared and ran away. Then three fireflies came inside at night and flew away when they saw her web. Four bumblebees would not stop for tea. Five bugs peered from the shadows, but Miss Spider found they belonged to a broom. Six ants came in with two rubber bugs, but they would not drink her tea. Seven butterflies were there too, but Miss Spider did not see them. Eight places were set at the tea table, but no guests stayed. Nine moths saw a thunderstorm, and they flew away when Miss Spider came down with a tray. Miss Spider cried because she was still all alone. Then a wet moth could not fly, so she gave him a cloth, tea, and pie. When his wings were dry, she helped him fly away. He told Ike, and Ike told May, and soon many insects came to tea. Miss Spider was no longer alone.

video_title: THE ICKY STICKY FROG | Storytime Read Aloud
summary_text: On a pretty blue lake, a very quiet little green frog sat on a big brown log. A fly flew by. Frog did not make a sound. He looked at the fly, then out came his sticky, long tongue, and the fly was gone. Next, a green grasshopper hopped by. Frog stayed quiet again and watched it. Then his sticky tongue came out, and the grasshopper was gone too. After that, a pretty butterfly flew by. Frog looked at the butterfly. Out came his sticky, long tongue one more time, and gulp, the frog was gone. This story shows what happens in nature when one animal eats another.

First they built a house of bricks, then a house of concrete, then a very strong house with metal and locks. Each time, the pig came, asked to be let in, and said he would huff and puff and blow the house down. The pig could not blow the houses down, so he used bigger tools and destroyed them. video_title: Owl At Home | Tear Water Tea | Read-Along | 1975 Scholastic Record | Read By Arnold Lobel
summary_text: Owl took a kettle from the cupboard and said he would make tear water tea. He put the kettle on his lap and sat very still. Then Owl thought of sad things, like chairs with broken legs, songs with forgotten words, spoons lost behind the stove, books with torn pages, stopped clocks, mornings nobody saw, mashed potatoes left on a plate, and pencils that were too short to use. As he thought about these things, he began to cry. His tears dropped into the kettle. He cried and cried until the kettle was full. Then Owl said, “That does it.” He stopped crying and put the kettle on the stove to boil. At last he filled his cup and drank the tea. He said it tasted a little salty, but tear water tea was always very good.

He felt happy and was not sad anymore.

video_title: Amelia Bedelia | Kids Books Read Aloud
summary_text: On her first day at work, Amelia Bedelia comes to the Rogers house with a list from Mrs. Rogers. Mr. and Mrs. Rogers leave in their car, and Amelia Bedelia decides to make them a surprise lemon meringue pie before she starts. Then she reads the list and does each job in a very exact way. She changes the towels in the green bathroom by cutting them with scissors, because she thinks “change” means make them different. She dusts the furniture with dust powder, draws the drapes by making a picture, and puts the lights out by unscrewing the bulbs. She measures two cups of rice by filling two cups with rice. When meat is delivered, she trims the steak with lace and ribbon and dresses the chicken in clothes. When Mr. and Mrs. Rogers come home, they are surprised by her work. At first they are upset, but then they taste the pie and decide Amelia Bedelia can stay.

She sat in the middle of the room, then answered the class roll in a funny way until Miss Edwards told her to say her name. The class made clay animals, listened to music, visited the library, and ran in gym. At lunch, Amelia Bedelia ate sloppy joe and then jumped rope her own way. For free time, she made daisies for her mother, but Miss Edwards told her to sit down and glue herself to her seat. Amelia Bedelia did, and she got stuck. Miss Edwards later said she was a new teacher too, and Amelia Bedelia said they both deserved gold stars. Miss Edwards tapped her head and said, “Tag, you are it until tomorrow,” and Amelia Bedelia was happy to come back to school.

video_title: Nate the Great (Nate the Great)
summary_text: Nate the Great, a detective, got a call from Annie after breakfast. Annie said she had lost a picture of her dog, Fang. Nate came right over, put on his detective suit, and left a note for his mother. At Annie’s house, he looked in her yellow room and searched the desk, bed, and wastebasket, but he did not find the picture. Annie told him that Rosamond and her brother Harry had seen it, so Nate went to ask them questions. Rosamond had many cats, and while Nate was there, he found her lost cat, Super Hex, by tripping over his tail. Then Nate met Harry, who was covered in red paint. Nate saw that Harry had painted a clown, a house, a tree, and a monster with three heads. Nate noticed the monster was orange because Harry had painted red over the yellow picture of Fang. Annie was upset, but the case was solved.

video_title: Good Driving, Amelia Bedelia
summary_text: On her birthday, Amelia Bedelia is told by Mr. and Mrs. Rogers to take the day off. She decides to visit her cousin Alkaloo, and Mr. Rogers lets her use the car. Amelia Bedelia has not driven in years, but she shows her license and goes for a drive with Mr. Rogers beside her. On the road, they see cows in the field and then cows on the road, so Mr. Rogers tells her to stop. He also asks her to steer straight and later to push on the horn, which helps scare the cows away. Then they get lost while Mr. Rogers looks at a map and Amelia Bedelia asks people for directions, but comes back with directions instead of a crossroad. After more confusion about a fork in the road and a bear left, Amelia Bedelia turns the wrong way and they get a flat tire. Mr. Rogers cannot fix it because the jack and spare tire are missing, so a tow truck driver named Jack helps pull the car back to town. At home, Cousin Alkaloo arrives, and everyone celebrates Amelia Bedelia’s birthday with cake.

video_title: Teach Us, Amelia Bedelia
summary_text: The telephone rang, and Amelia Bedelia answered it. Mrs. Rogers told her that the new teacher’s plane was late and asked her to go to Mr. Carter’s office at school. Amelia Bedelia hurried to school and told Mr. Carter that the telephone was broken. Mr. Carter said the children were wild and gave her Miss Lane’s list. He brought her to the classroom and said, “This is your new teacher,” then left. Amelia Bedelia was surprised, but she decided to do everything on the list. She called the roll by looking for a real roll, sang a song, and then read aloud from a book. When the list said “run run run,” she ran around the room and the children ran after her. Later, she helped with planting bulbs, free time, quiet time, art, and practice play. At the end, she took the children to her house, made toffee apples, and sent them home when school was over. Then the real new teacher, Miss Reid, arrived with Mrs. Rogers.

video_title: Nate the Great Goes Undercover (Nate the Great)
summary_text: Nate the Great is a detective. One morning, he and his new dog, Sludge, are walking when Oliver, Nate’s neighbor, says someone is tipping over his garbage can every night. Nate says he will help. He asks Rosamond and Esmeralda questions, but neither of them takes the garbage. Nate checks books at the library and learns that some night animals go out after dark. That night, he hides in Oliver’s garbage can, but nothing happens. Then he follows a new clue and walks to a field. There he finds a skunk near some garbage. Nate writes to Oliver and says the skunk was the garbage snatcher. Later, Oliver says the garbage can is tipped again. Nate thinks harder, hides near the can again, and waits. This time Sludge comes to the can, and Nate sees that Sludge is the one taking the garbage. Nate gives Sludge a bone and dog food, and the case is over.

video_title: Danny and the Dinosaur
summary_text: Danny went to the museum and saw many things, including bears, guns, swords, and dinosaurs. He loved dinosaurs and wished he had one. Then a dinosaur spoke to him and said it could take him for a ride. Danny climbed on, and they went into town. A policeman stared, and a dog chased them because it thought the dinosaur was a car. Danny and the dinosaur went to buildings, the ball game, and the zoo. The dinosaur helped people cross the street and carry bundles. At the zoo, everyone came to see the dinosaur instead of the other animals, so the zoo man asked it to go away. Then Danny found his friends, and the children asked for rides. They played games, learned tricks, and played hide and seek. When it got late, the children went home. Danny said goodbye, and the dinosaur went back to the museum. Danny went home alone, but he knew they had a wonderful day.

video_title: The Lost List (Nate the Great)
summary_text: Nate the Great was on vacation with his dog Sludge when his friend Claude came to the yard. Claude had lost his grocery list and needed it before lunch. He remembered some things on the list, like salt, milk, butter, flour, sugar, tuna fish, eggs, and baking powder. Nate drew a map between Claude’s house and the grocery store and searched the road with Sludge. The map blew toward Rosamond’s house, so Nate went there. Rosamond was covered in flour and making fishy cat pancakes for her white cats. Nate saw Annie outside with Fang, and Fang had a paper in his mouth. The wind blew the paper away, but Nate caught it. He first thought it was the list, but it was only his map. Later, Nate returned to Rosamond’s house and saw her recipe. He realized the recipe was Claude’s grocery list. He gave the list back just before Claude arrived.

video_title: Flat Stanley and the Bees
summary_text: Stanley Liam Chop lived with his mother, his father, and his little brother Arthur. Stanley was flat because a bulletin board fell on him, but he still liked to eat. One hot summer day, he asked if the honey buns were done. Mrs. Lamb Chop said no and said it was too hot to bake. Mr. Lamb Chop helped cool everyone off by doing “the fan.” Arthur folded Stanley like an accordion, and Mr. Lamb Chop flapped him back and forth. Then Mrs. Lamb Chop told the boys to go outside and play. Stanley and Arthur used their new slippy slide and met Tom and Sam. They played slide, tag, and hide and seek. Later, they heard a cry and followed the sound up a hill. Tom was standing still because bees were around him after he bumped a beehive. Stanley and Arthur tried “the fan” again, but the bees only moved a little. The boys ran down the hill, then Stanley used the slippy slide to help them go fast home. The bees came inside too, but they stopped at the honey buns. Mrs. Lamb Chop laughed and said it was too hot for warm buns anyway. She said they needed ice cream.

summary_text: Since the day he hatched, Owl wanted to be a knight. He dreamed of being brave, clever, and having many friends. Then one day, nights began disappearing from the castle, so Owl applied to night school. To everyone’s surprise, he was accepted. Owl studied hard and graduated with honor, even though he had trouble with a sword, a shield, and staying awake in the day. He was sent to the night watch at the castle wall. One very dark and quiet night, Owl heard a whoosh and called out. A Dragon answered and said he was hungry. Owl was afraid, but he said he was a knight. The Dragon said Owl looked like a snack. Owl then said he was too small and suggested pizza instead. The Dragon loved pizza. They talked and found they had many things in common. After that, no more nights disappeared, and Owl kept watch every night.

summary_text: One winter morning, a new girl named Maya came to class with the principal. Maya wore old clothes and shoes that were not good for snow. Miss Albert put Maya in the empty seat next to Chloe. Maya smiled at Chloe, but Chloe did not smile back. At lunch and in the schoolyard, Maya tried to play with Chloe, Kendra, and Sophie, but they said no. Maya showed them jacks, cards, pickup sticks, a doll, and a jump rope, but the girls still would not play. The weather got warmer, and one day Maya came wearing a pretty dress and fancy shoes. The next day her seat was empty. Miss Albert taught the class about kindness by dropping a stone into water and showing how the ripples spread. Soon she said Maya would not return because her family moved away. Chloe went home feeling sad and thought about all the kind things she did not do. At the pond, she dropped stones into the water and watched the ripples spread.

video_title: Do You Want To Be My Friend | A Gentle Wordless Story Read Aloud for Kids
summary_text: A little mouse looks for a friend. He sees a long green tail and asks, “Do you want to be my friend?” The tail belongs to a horse, but the horse is busy eating and does not answer. The mouse keeps going and asks an alligator, a lion, a hippopotamus, a baby seal, a chimpanzee, a peacock, a red fox, a kangaroo, and a giraffe to be his friend. Each time, the animal is not the friend he wants. Then the mouse sees a tiny tail like his own. It is another little mouse, and he asks again, “Do you want to be my friend?” This time, the answer is yes. The two mice are happy to be friends. Then they see a long green tail winding around the house. It is a snake. The mice run to the tree, then go down into the ground where they are safe and cozy.

A tiger sits in a cold cage with black flames and black rays. At the end, a duck is named. It quacks, likes puddles and ponds, and bottoms up when it eats.

video_title: The Giant Jumperee |  Feelings and Friendship Story
summary_text: Rabbit was hopping home when he heard a loud voice inside his burrow. He called for help. Cat came first. Rabbit said there was a giant jumper in his burrow. Cat said she would slink inside and pounce on him. But then Cat heard the loud voice, and she got scared too. She asked Bear for help. Bear said he would put his big furry paw inside and knock the giant down. But Bear heard the voice and got scared. Bear asked Elephant for help. Elephant said he would wrap his trunk around the giant and toss him away. But Elephant heard the voice and got scared too. Then Elephant asked Mama Frog for help. The other animals said the giant was too scary. Mama Frog still went to the burrow and told the giant to come out. She counted one, two, three, and out jumped baby frog. He said, “Hello, mama. I’m the giant jumperie.” Mama Frog said he was coming home for tea.

video_title: The Tale of Benjamin Bunny | Classic Kids Read Aloud | Beatrix Potter
summary_text: One morning, little Benjamin Bunny sat on a bank and heard a pony coming. A gig came along the road with Mr. McGregor and Mrs. McGregor inside. In the wood nearby lived old Mrs. Rabbit and her children, Flopsy, Mopsy, Cottontail, and Peter. Benjamin found Peter sitting alone by the fur tree. Peter had no coat or shoes because he had lost them in Mr. McGregor’s garden. Benjamin told Peter that Mr. McGregor and Mrs. McGregor were out for the day. The two rabbits went to the wall and looked into the garden. Peter’s clothes were on the scarecrow. Benjamin helped Peter get them back. They then filled Peter’s pocket handkerchief with onions and ate lettuce in the garden. Soon they were frightened by a cat, so they hid under a basket. Peter and Benjamin stayed there until old Mr. Bunny came, chased the cat away, and took the rabbits home. Peter’s mother was glad he had found his clothes, and the onions were hung in the kitchen.

summary_text: One morning, Benjamin Bunny sat on a bank and heard a pony coming. A gig drove by with Mr. McGregor and Mrs. McGregor in her best bonnet, so Benjamin knew they were away for the day. In the wood, he found his cousin Peter Rabbit sitting sadly in a red cotton handkerchief. Peter told Benjamin that Mr. McGregor had chased him in the garden and taken his clothes. Benjamin and Peter climbed down into the garden by a pear tree and found Peter’s coat and shoes on the scarecrow. They took them back and then filled the handkerchief with onions. Peter wanted to go home, but they could not climb back with the vegetables. They went another way and hid under a basket when a cat came. The cat sat on the basket for five hours. At last old Mr. Bunny came, chased the cat into the greenhouse, and took Benjamin, Peter, and the onions home. Mr. McGregor later found the cat locked in the greenhouse. Peter got home safely, and his mother forgave him because he had his coat and shoes back.

video_title: Welcome Little One
summary_text: On the day the child was born, the family felt love at first sight. They welcomed the little one and held the baby tightly. They would teach the child to see life in different ways and help make dreams come true. The world felt more wonderful when they saw the child’s beautiful face.

In the end, the berry world fills up with moonberry, starberry, cloudberry, boomberry, and zoomberry, and everything is buried in berries. It ends with a big berry jam called a jambori.

She tells about dropping her lunch tray at school and about trying to help Andrew cut his hair, which still caused trouble. Karen lives part of the time at Mommy’s house with Mommy, Seth, and Rocky, and this weekend she is at Daddy’s house, where many people live. She says she has lots of twos, like two pairs of shoes and two birthdays. At Mommy’s house, Gucci was lost for two days, Mala is getting worse, and Karen cannot fall asleep. At Daddy’s house, she tells Daddy she has been awake for hours, but he says Chrissy put her to bed only 20 minutes ago. Karen keeps thinking about Mrs. Porter, whom she believes is a witch. Daddy tells her to stop spying on Mrs. Porter and think pleasant thoughts. Karen thinks of ice cream, cartoons, pets, birthdays, and roller skating, and then she dreams about skating on a steep hill and meeting a bunny.

video_title: Baby-Sitters Little Sister  by Katy Farina " Karen`s Roller Skates"
summary_text: Karen Brewer is almost seven and loves roller skating. She can go fast, turn, stop, and try tricks. Her parents are divorced, so Karen and her brother Andrew spend weekends at Daddy’s house. One Saturday, Karen wants to skate while Andrew rides his trike with Shannon, the dog. Karen forgets her wrist guards and tries to jump over coffee cans. She falls, and her wrist breaks. Daddy takes her to the emergency room. At the hospital, nurses take x-rays, and Dr. Humphrey puts Karen’s wrist in a cast. Karen feels upset because she cannot skate for a long time. At home, she starts collecting autographs on her cast. Ricky, another child with a cast, has many signatures too. Karen asks friends, neighbors, and even Mrs. Porter, who is called a witch, to sign her cast. In the end, Karen gets many names and feels proud of her cast, even though she must wait for her wrist to heal.

video_title: Baby sisters Little Sisters 1 by Katy Farina
summary_text: Karen Brewer is six years old and lives with two families because her mom and dad divorced and married other people. She and her brother Andrew spend every other weekend at Daddy’s house, where it is noisy and busy. Karen also thinks Mrs. Porter, who lives next door, is a witch and calls her Morbida Destiny. One night, Karen sees Midnight, Mrs. Porter’s cat, and gets very scared. Later, Karen thinks she sees Mrs. Porter and Midnight fly away on a broomstick. Karen and her friend Hani watch the house, spy on the garden, and hear words like “midnight” and “important meeting.” Karen believes a witch meeting will happen next door. She and Hani make up a spell and go to Mrs. Porter’s house to warn the “witches.” But Grandma comes to the meeting and says it is really the Sunnybrook Gardeners Club. Karen must apologize, and Daddy makes her write a sorry note. Karen still thinks Mrs. Porter is a witch, even after the mistake.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth: Beekle
summary_text: Beagle was an imaginary friend who lived on an island far away where imaginary friends were made. Every night, he stood under the stars and waited to be chosen by a real child and given a special name. Night after night, his turn did not come. Beagle grew tired of waiting, so he did something unexpected. He set sail in a very small boat and crossed unknown waters to reach the real world. The real world felt strange at first. No one listened to music, and everyone seemed to need naptime. Then Beagle saw a place that felt familiar. He looked for a friend, but no one came. He climbed to the top of a tree and waited sadly. Soon he heard a noise below. A girl named Alice appeared, and she drew a picture of him. At first, they did not know what to do, but soon they became friends. Beagle and Alice shared snacks, told funny jokes, and went on many new adventures together.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth: Episode 6, Hoot Owl
summary_text: Hooda the owl is hungry at night. He says owls are wise and that he is a master of disguise. First, he makes himself look like a carrot so he can catch a rabbit, but it does not work. Then he dresses up like a baby lamb and a fluffy sheep, hoping to catch a lamb, but that does not work either. After that, he changes into a pigeon costume, but the pigeon is still not caught. Hooda keeps going because he is still hungry. Next, he hides as a school girl, then as a waiter, and he looks for pizza. This time the disguise works, and Hooda gets the pizza. After eating the last bite, he feels tired but satisfied. Then he changes back into his plain self and disappears into the dark night.

video_title: Bedtime Stories:  Paperbag Princess
summary_text: Elizabeth was a princess who lived in a castle and was going to marry Prince Ronald. Then a dragon smashed the castle, burned her clothes, and carried Ronald away. Elizabeth could not find any clothes left, so she put on a paper bag and followed the dragon. She found his cave and knocked on the big door. The dragon said he was busy and told her to come back tomorrow. Elizabeth kept talking to him and asked if he was the smartest and fiercest dragon. The dragon breathed fire again and again, then flew around the world for her. He got so tired that he fell asleep. Elizabeth quietly walked past him, opened the cave door, and found Ronald. Ronald said she looked messy and was wearing a dirty paper bag. Elizabeth said Ronald looked like a bum. They did not get married.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth:  Rot: The Cutest in the WORLD!
summary_text: Rot Rot is a mutant potato, and he thinks he is the cutest thing in the world. He sees a sign for a “cutest in the world” contest and quickly enters. Rot sings a happy song about being the cutest and lines up with the other contestants. He sees many others, including a baby with floppy ears, a cuddly kitten, puppies, and jellyfish. The other contestants do not think Rot will win. Rot thinks about eating everyone, but he does not do it. He tries to make himself cuter by adding big ears, whiskers, and other things, but nothing helps. Then Rot decides to be himself. He goes on stage, smiles, and shows his best side. The judges like him very much and give him a big trophy. Rot sees his reflection in the shiny trophy and says he is the cutest in the world.

When he sees a sign for the “cutest in the world” contest, he enters at once and sings that he is the cutest in the world. At the contest, he sees other contestants, including a baby with floppy ears, a kitten, puppies, and jellyfish. He thinks about changing himself by adding big ears, whiskers, or pink colors, but none of it makes him feel cuter. In the end, Rot decides to be himself. He goes onstage, smiles, and shows his best side. The judges are impressed and give him a big trophy. Rot sees his reflection in the shiny trophy and says again that he is the cutest in the world.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: How to Catch a Star
summary_text: There was a boy who loved stars very much. Every night, he looked at the stars from his window and wished for one of his very own. He dreamed that the star would be his friend and that they would play hide-and-go-seek and take walks together. One day, the boy decided to catch a star. He got up early at sunrise, but he could not see any stars, so he waited and waited. He waited through lunch and dinner. At last, just before the sun went away, he saw a star. He tried to jump for it, then climbed the tallest tree, but it was still too far. He tried many ways to reach it, but none worked. Then he saw something in the water. It was a baby star. He could not hold it in his hands. Later, he found a starfish on the sand and brought it home as his new friend.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: The Man Who Didn't Wash His Dishes
summary_text: A man lived alone in a little house on the edge of town. He cooked his own supper, cleaned his own house, and made his own bed. One night he came home very hungry and made a big supper. It was so much food that he got tired and left the dishes in the sink. The next night he was even hungrier, so he made an even bigger supper and left those dishes too. Day by day, the dirty dishes grew. They filled the sink, then the table, then the bookshelves, then the floor, and even blocked the door. Soon he had no clean dishes left. He ate from a soap dish, then an ashtray, then flower pots, candy dishes, vases, and even the pots he cooked in. His house became full of dirty things, and he could not find his bed or his sink. Then it rained. He loaded everything into his truck and let the rain wash it clean. After that, he put everything away and washed his dishes right after supper every night.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth: Episode 8, Snow Suit Story!
summary_text: Thomas’s mother bought him a new brown snow suit. Thomas did not like it and said it was ugly and that he would not wear it. The next day, his mother told him to put on his suit for school, but Thomas said no. She tried to get him into the snow suit, and they had a big fight. At school, the teacher asked Thomas to put on his suit, but Thomas said no again. The teacher tried to make him wear it, and they fought too. After that, the teacher ended up wearing Thomas’s snow suit. Then the principal came in and told Thomas to put on his snow suit. Thomas still said no. The principal tried to help, but he ended up wearing the teacher’s dress, and the teacher wore the principal’s suit. Thomas later came back, fixed the clothes mix-up, and finally wore the snow suit. The next day, the principal quit and moved to Arizona.

video_title: Bedtime Stories - Speak Up, Molly Lou Melon
summary_text: Molly Lou Melon was a tiny girl with a big heart. Her mom told her to be true to herself, take responsibility, accept others, and use her strong voice to help people. Molly Lou tried to do these things. At school, she sat with Ronald Durkin and Gertie. Tina Bonkel snickered at them, but Molly Lou stood up and said they were friends. In winter, Molly Lou and Bettina Bonklehead painted on their desks by mistake. Molly Lou said, “me,” and cleaned the desks during recess. In spring, a new boy, Garvin Grape, came to school and talked about gravity. Bettina made fun of him, but Molly Lou said gravity was a big deal and gave Garvin a note inviting him to recess. On the first day of summer, Bettina tripped Garvin, and his glasses flew away. Molly Lou caught the glasses and told Bettina to never do that again. Ronald and Gertie helped Garvin up, and the friends shouted together.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: Welcome Back Sun
summary_text: In a small village in Norway, the sun has been gone for many months. The child goes to school in the dark and comes home in the dark. The child calls this long dark time the mercatidin. Mama feels tired and fretful, and Papa works all day inside and does not see the sun. Mama tells a story about a little girl who once climbed Mount Gausta when the sun was lost. The girl walked through snow and cold wind, found the sun behind a black cliff, and led it back to the village. People still make that climb to see the sun. The child asks Papa if they can climb the mountain too, but Papa says to wait. As the days pass, Mama and the child gather branches and put them in water by the window. Then Papa, Mama, and the child pack food and climb up the mountain with other people. At the pass, the sun appears, everyone cheers, and they eat together. Later, the child wakes at home and sees the sun on the snow and the first buds opening. Spring has come.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth:  Piranhas Don't Eat Bananas
summary_text: Brian offers food to some piranhas. He asks if they want a banana, silver beet, peas, and juicy plums. The piranhas keep saying no and tell Brian that piranhas do not eat apples, beans, veggies, greens, melons, or bananas. They say they eat feet, knees, and bums, and they also say Monroe eats feet, not knees, so he must be a piranha. Brian says fruit is best, but the piranhas tell him to stop talking. Brian says he will stop only if they try his fruit platter. They take it, and Brian watches them gobble up banana, pineapple, and apple. Brian asks if it is yucky or yum. The piranhas say it is very nice, but they still prefer bum.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth and her cousin, Ollie!
summary_text: Ronan was a mighty barbarian leader who invaded, raided, and traded for gold, jewelry, weapons, and tools. One raid went wrong when he found a book and first thought it was useless. He tried to get rid of it, but after seeing a picture, he began reading. He read the first sentence, then more and more until late at night. The next day, his friends Krom, Gunner, and Helgi found him reading instead of raiding. Ronan went raiding with them, but he could not stop thinking about the book. After the raid, he hurried home and read to the end. Soon he wanted more books, so he raided and read again and again until books piled up on his boat. To solve the problem, he built a library and opened it with a celebration. At first his friends mocked books, but Ronan read aloud to them, gave out library cards, recommended books, and started a book club. In the end, the barbarians read books too.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth:  Bark, George!
summary_text: George's mother says, “Bark, George.” But George does not bark. She tries again and says that cats go meow and dogs go woof. George still does not make the right sound. She says ducks go quack quack and dogs go woof, but George makes a strange sound instead. Then she says pigs go oink and dogs go ARF, but George still cannot bark. George's mother takes him to the vet. The vet reaches deep inside George and pulls out a cat. Then he reaches inside again and pulls out a pig. After that, he reaches deep inside one more time and pulls out a cow. George finally barks. George's mother is happy, and she takes George home and shows him off to everyone she meets.

video_title: Bedtime Stories:  Purple, Green & Yellow
summary_text: Bridgette wanted coloring markers like her friends had, but her mother said no because markers can make a mess. Bridgette said she wanted washable markers that come off with water, so her mother bought 500 washable coloring markers. Bridgette drew pretty pictures of lemons, roses, and oranges, and her mother said she was an artist. After a week, Bridgette wanted new markers again, so her mother bought 500 markers that smelled like flowers, fruit, and even cow plops. Bridgette drew more pictures, then got bored again. She asked for super indelible markers that never come off, and her mother bought 500 permanent markers. Bridgette used them for a while, then colored her fingernails, fingers, hands, face, and belly button many colors. She tried to wash them off, but they stayed on. video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth:  Mustache Baby written by Bridget Heos
summary_text: When Baby Billy was born, his family saw that he had a mustache. His mother asked what it meant, and the nurse said they would have to wait and see if it was a good guy mustache or a bad guy mustache. At first, Billy’s mustache was good. He became a cowboy, tamed a bronco, protected cattle, cared for hurt animals, fixed fences, and later became a painter, a ringleader, a sword fighter, and a police officer. People liked Officer Billy. But as Billy grew, his mustache grew and curled up at the ends. Then it became a bad guy mustache. Billy turned to crime and became a cat burglar, a criminal, and a train robber. He even stole the tracks. When he planned to rob a bank, his getaway car was too slow, and his mother caught him. Billy was sent to jail. After a long time, he felt sorry for his thievery and wished his bad mustache would go away. Then his mother got him out of jail, and his father said the new neighbors had a baby coming to play.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth:  Hooray for Hat!
summary_text: Elephant woke up grumpy. When the doorbell rang, he stomped downstairs and said, “Go away! I’m grumpy.” On the doorstep was a present. Elephant opened the box and found hats. He liked the hats and felt a little happier. Zebra was not happy at first and said, “Go away! I’m grumpy.” Elephant gave zebra a smooth hat, and zebra smiled. They cheered, “Hooray for a hat!” Then they went to turtle, who stayed in his shell, and gave turtle a hat too. Turtle cheered. Next they showed owl. Owl did not want to look, but elephant gave owl a hat, and owl smiled. Elephant, zebra, turtle, and owl marched to lion. Lion did not want visitors, but elephant gave lion his last hat. Lion was still sad because a friend was not feeling well. So elephant, zebra, turtle, owl, and lion made a surprise for giraffe and gave giraffe all the hats. Giraffe felt better, and everyone cheered and said to be a good friend.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth:  The Word Collector by Peter H. Reynolds
summary_text: Jerome collected words. While other people collected stamps, rocks, coins, art, bugs, baseball cards, or comic books, Jerome listened for special words everywhere he went. He wrote down words like Peru, Willow, Emerald, Cage, Drift, Bloom, Geometry, Kaleidoscope, Symphony, Aromatic, Vociferous, Effervescent, Molasses, Bellow, and Rex. He kept his favorite words in scrapbooks and sorted them into groups like dreaming, science, sad, action, and poetic. One day, while carrying his words, Jerome slipped and the words flew everywhere. As he picked them up, he saw new and surprising word pairs, and he began making poems and songs from them. He used simple words too, like “I understand,” “I’m sorry,” “Thank you,” and “You matter.” The more words he collected, the better he could share his thoughts and feelings. At the end, Jerome poured his words into the wind from a hill, and children below began to catch words too.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: Ruby Finds a Worry
summary_text: Ruby loved swinging high and exploring faraway places in the garden. One day she found a small worry, and it kept growing bigger and bigger. The worry was with her at breakfast, at school, and at night, and it stopped her from doing the things she loved. Ruby tried to ignore it, but she kept worrying about the worry, and that made it huge. Then Ruby saw a boy sitting alone in the park who looked sad, and she noticed he had a worry too. Ruby asked him what was wrong, and as he talked, his worry got smaller. Ruby then talked about her own worry, and her worry shrank too. Soon both worries were gone, and Ruby felt like herself again. Ruby learned that worries do not have to stay forever, and talking to someone can make them shrink.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: The Little Red Caboose
summary_text: The Little Red Caboose always came last on the train. First came the big black engine, then the boxcars, oil cars, coal cars, and flat cars. Boys and girls waved at the engine and listened to the other cars go click, but they often turned away before the Little Red Caboose arrived. The little red caboose felt sad and wished he were a box car, a coal car, an oil car, a flat car, or even the big black engine. One day the train went up a long, tall mountain. The train got slower and slower, and it looked like it might slide back. The Little Red Caboose saw this and slammed on his brakes. He held tight to the tracks and stopped the train from slipping down. Then two big black engines pushed from behind and helped the train reach the top. Everyone cheered, and the other cars said the children saved their biggest waves for the Little Red Caboose because he saved the train.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: The Saggy Baggy Elephant
summary_text: A happy little elephant danced through the jungle, saying one, two, three, kick. But his big feet shook the ground, and his kicks knocked over trees and bushes. One day he met a parrot, who asked why he was shaking the jungle and what kind of animal he was. The elephant said he lived alone and called himself Suki. The parrot said his ears, nose, and skin were too big and saggy, and called him saggy baggy. Suki tried to smooth his skin, but it did not help. Then a tiger came by and said exercise might help, so Suki ran, rolled, and walked in different ways. After that, the parrot told him to soak in the river like a crocodile. Suki went into the water, but a crocodile came and scared him away. Suki hid in a dark cave, where a hungry lion came near. Then a herd of big gray elephants rushed in and chased the lion away. They told Suki he was a perfectly dandy little elephant, and Suki danced happily with them while the parrot watched.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: The Little Red Hen
summary_text: The Little Red Hen lived in a barnyard with her three chicks, a duck, a pig, and a cat. She found some grains of wheat and asked who would help her plant them. The duck said, “Not I.” The pig said, “Not I.” The cat said, “Not I.” So the Little Red Hen planted the wheat herself. When the wheat grew tall and golden, she asked who would help cut it. Again, the duck, pig, and cat would not help, so she cut it herself. Then she took the wheat to the Miller, and the Miller ground it into flour. The Little Red Hen made the flour into dough and baked the bread herself. When the bread was ready, the duck, pig, and cat wanted to eat it. But the Little Red Hen said no, because they had not helped. She and her three chicks ate the warm bread.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: The New Potty
summary_text: The boy says he is a big boy and wears underpants with skateboards. His little sister is a baby and wears diapers. One day, Mom says it is time for the little sister to use a potty. The family goes to the store and buys a pink potty chair. At home, the little sister wants to carry it inside, but she does not want to sit on it and cries because she is scared. The boy sits on the potty first, and then she is not scared anymore. He gets her a book, and she stays on the potty. Mom moves the potty downstairs so the little sister can sit on it while she watches TV. She sits on it at dinner, puts her doll on it, and tries to put the boy’s monkey on it too. That night, she sleeps with the potty by her bed. In the morning, she uses the potty, gets new underpants, and later has some accidents, but then she uses the potty the right way.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: Tawny Scrawny Lion
summary_text: There was a tawny, scrawny lion who was always hungry. He chased monkeys, kangaroos, zebras, bears, camels, and elephants, but he never got fat. The other animals were afraid of him and talked to him from far away. Then a fat little rabbit came by, and the big animals asked him to talk to the lion. The rabbit went close and counted the lion’s ribs. He said the lion looked too scrawny, so he should come to the rabbit’s house for supper. The rabbit said there would be carrot stew with his five sisters and four brothers. The lion went with him. On the way, the rabbit stopped to pick berries, mushrooms, and herbs, and then he caught fish. At the house, nine rabbits were cooking stew. They gave the lion stew and berries until he was full and fat. After that, he did not want to hunt anymore. He kept visiting the rabbits for supper instead.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: Tawny Scrawny Lion
summary_text: Once there was a tawny, scrawny lion who was always hungry. Every day he chased different animals: monkeys on Monday, kangaroos on Tuesday, zebras on Wednesday, bears on Thursday, camels on Friday, and elephants on Saturday. Even though he caught them, he only grew thinner and hungrier. The other animals were afraid, so they sent a fat little rabbit to talk to him. The rabbit counted the lion’s ribs and invited him to supper. He said his five fat sisters and four fat brothers were making carrot stew. The lion followed him, but the rabbit kept stopping to pick berries, mushrooms, herbs, and fish. At the rabbit’s house, nine rabbits shared stew and berries with the lion until he was full and could not move. After that, the lion was no longer hungry for the other animals. He returned every day for carrot stew instead of hunting, and the animals were glad. When they asked the rabbit what he had said, he answered that they had forgotten to talk because they had such a good time.

summary_text: Long ago, King Stefan and Queen wished for a child. A baby girl was born, and they named her Aurora. At a big feast, three good fairies came to bless the baby. Flora gave beauty, and Fauna gave song. But Maleficent came too. She was angry because she was not invited. She gave a bad curse: before Aurora’s 16th birthday, she would prick her finger on a spinning wheel and die. Meriwether changed the curse so Aurora would fall into a deep sleep instead. The king had all spinning wheels burned, and the fairies took Aurora to live in the woods. They called her Briar Rose. When Briar Rose turned 16, she met a handsome young man and fell in love. The fairies told her she was Princess Aurora and took her home. Maleficent made Aurora touch a spindle, and she fell asleep. Prince Philip fought Maleficent, killed the dragon, and kissed Aurora. She woke up, and everyone was happy.

video_title: Disney's "The Little Mermaid" | Classic Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: Ariel is a little mermaid and the youngest daughter of King Triton. She lives under the sea, but she loves human things more than the ocean world. One day, Ariel and her friend Flounder search inside old sunken ships. Ariel finds a chest with treasures and puts a fork and a pipe in her pouch. Then Flounder sees a shark. Ariel and Flounder swim fast through the ship, but the shark follows them. They escape when the shark gets stuck in an anchor. After that, Ariel and Flounder visit Scuttle the seagull. Scuttle says the fork is a dingle hopper and the pipe is a snurf blast, but he is wrong. Later, Ariel sees Prince Eric on a big ship. She thinks he is handsome. A storm comes, the ship breaks, and Eric falls into the sea. Ariel saves him and carries him to shore. She sings to him, then leaves before the crew sees her. Ariel goes back to her cave and thinks about seeing Eric again.

video_title: MICKEY MOUSE Heads for the Sky | Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: One day Mickey Mouse saw a plane fly fast over his car. Mickey wanted to fly too, so he decided to take flight lessons. He went shopping and bought a pilot’s jacket, a cap, and a scarf. The next day he met his teacher, Ducky Lindy, at the airport. Mickey learned that flying is not as easy as it looks. He practiced many lessons, learned about buttons in the cockpit, and learned how to stop a spiral and fly upside down. While Mickey was busy, Minnie, Goofy, Donald, and Daisy asked him to play, but he was always learning to fly. Soon Ducky said Mickey was ready for his first solo flight. Mickey flew well and passed the test. Then he looked for his friends and found them having a picnic with a banner that said, “We miss Mickey.” Mickey landed, joined them, and ate lunch. After that, he said he would take them for plane rides, and Minnie became his first passenger.

summary_text: Rapunzel lived in a tall tower with her very long hair. Every day, Mother Gothel said, “Rapunzel, let down your hair,” and Rapunzel pulled her up. Mother Gothel used Rapunzel’s magic hair to stay young and beautiful. Rapunzel did not know that Mother Gothel had stolen her from the king and the Queen. Rapunzel had a friend named Pascal. On her birthday, she saw shining lights in the sky and wished to go see them. Then Flynn, a thief, came to her tower. Rapunzel thought he wanted her hair, but he did not. Flynn took Rapunzel to see the lights. They met friendly people, escaped from Maximus and the Royal Guards, and found their way out of a cave with Rapunzel’s glowing hair. Rapunzel saw the kingdom celebrate the Lost Princess. She learned the truth, and Flynn came back to save her. Mother Gothel hurt Flynn, but Rapunzel’s tear brought him back. Rapunzel went home to the king and the Queen.

video_title: Long Goes to School - Read Aloud Kids Book - A Bedtime Story with Dessi! - Story time
summary_text: On the first day of Dragon School, Long goes with his new classmates, Camila, Willie, and Mia. Professor McKay welcomes them and says they will learn their special talents. First, the class tries to cook with fire breath. Professor McKay shows them how to roast a potato with a bright burst of fire. Then the young dragons try, but each one makes a mess. Camila makes lava, Willie makes fire, Mia makes ash, and Long only sprays water because dragons from his home breathe water, not fire. Long worries and tries many ways to make fire, but nothing works. He practices and practices, yet he still cannot do it. At the end of the week, the class gets ready for a picnic. The others cook their food, and Long is asked to roast the pumpkin. He feels sad and thinks he will let everyone down. Professor McKay tells him to try his best. Long remembers to relax and focus, and this time his water turns into hot steam. The pumpkin is steamed, and the class enjoys the picnic together.

video_title: Otto The Otter, A Big Surprise - Read Aloud Kids Book - A Bedtime Story with Dessi!
summary_text:
Otto the otter has visited the small pond near the grey house for a long time. The people there named him Otto and like to watch him swim, play, and eat. He comes often, but not every day, and after a few hours he leaves through a creek to another pond. At night he goes away, and the people do not know where he sleeps. One winter he stayed away for a long time, and when he came back in spring, he arrived with two babies. Then the people saw that Otto was really a girl, and they changed her name to Opal.

Opal’s babies are called pups. She kept them safe in a den when they were tiny. Later she brought them to the pond, taught them to swim, and showed them how to find food under the water. video_title: Creepy Pair of Underwear! - Read Aloud Kids Book - Bedtime Stories with Dessi!
summary_text: Jasper Rabbit needed new underwear, so Mom took him to the store. He saw a pair of creepy underwear that looked cool and comfy, and he asked Mom to buy them. That night, Jasper wore them to bed, but they glowed a ghoulish greenish glow. He got scared, changed into plain white underwear, and hid the creepy pair in the laundry hamper. The next morning, the creepy underwear were on him again, so he threw them in the garbage. But they came back in his dresser drawer. Jasper mailed them to China, but they returned with chopsticks. Then he used Mom’s sewing scissors to cut them up. After that, he checked his drawer and found plain white underwear. He thought the creepy underwear were gone, but they still came back. Jasper finally took a shovel, dug a deep hole at Creek Hanger Hill, and buried them. When he got home, he found only plain white underwear in his drawer. Later, he bought more creepy underwear with his allowance and hung them up like string lights. That night, he was not scared and slept happily.

video_title: Have you filled a bucket today? READ ALOUD 📚
summary_text: Everyone in the whole wide world carries an invisible bucket. The bucket holds good thoughts and good feelings. When a bucket is full, a person feels happy. When it is empty, a person feels sad and lonely. Other people can fill a bucket, and we can fill our own buckets too. A bucket is filled when someone shows love, says something kind, gives a smile, or does something nice. This is called bucket filling. A bucket is dipped into when someone is mean, makes fun of others, ignores them, or bullies them. That is bucket dipping. Dipping does not help anyone feel better. Filling someone else’s bucket also fills your own bucket. The story gives examples like saying I love you to Mom and Dad, smiling at the bus driver, inviting the new kid to play, writing a thank you note to the teacher, and talking kindly to Grandpa. Bucket filling is easy, and it makes home, school, and the neighborhood better places.

At last, they reached Montgomery with tears of joy. Dr. King says people should answer hate with love, violence with kindness, and keep marching together for freedom.

Later, they tried to stay in a hotel, but the desk man turned them away. They drove all night and kept singing. Many places would not let them eat, so they ate picnics by the road. In Tennessee, they stayed with Daddy’s friend Eddy and his wife, Alice. Eddy told them about Jim Crow and said they should look for Esso stations. At one Esso station, they learned about The Negro Motorist Green Book. Daddy bought one, and Ruth kept it. It helped them find places to stay, even when the car broke down. In the end, they reached Grandma’s house soon after, and Ruth gave Brown Bear to a scared little boy at the inn.

video_title: Follow the Drinking Gourd by Jeanette Winter read aloud
summary_text: Long ago, before the Civil War, an old sailor named Peg Leg Joe worked on a cotton plantation and helped enslaved people escape. At night, after work, he taught them a song called “Follow the Drinking Gourd,” which was really a secret map to freedom. One day, Molly saw that her husband James had been sold to another master. That night, Molly, James, their son Isaiah, old Hattie, and Hattie’s grandson George sang Joe’s song and followed the stars. They ran through fields, crossed a stream, and hid from the master’s hounds. For many nights and days, they traveled by the signs in the song, sometimes hungry and sometimes in danger. A farm boy once brought them food, and later they reached the Ohio River, where Peg Leg Joe was waiting. He carried them across and sent them to safe houses on the Underground Railroad. In the end, they reached Lake Erie, boarded a steamship, crossed to Canada, and were safe at last.

video_title: Follow the Drinking Gourd by Jeanette Winter read aloud
summary_text: Long ago, before the Civil War, an old sailor named Peg Leg Joe worked on a cotton plantation and secretly helped enslaved people escape. He taught them a song that gave directions to freedom: “follow the drinking gourd.” When Molly saw her husband James sold to another master, she, James, their son Isaiah, old Hattie, and Hattie’s grandson George used Joe’s song and began running at night. They followed the stars, crossed a stream, and hid from the master’s hounds in the woods. For weeks they traveled by night and hid by day, sometimes finding berries, corn, or fish, and sometimes receiving help from kind people. A farm boy shared food with them, and later Peg Leg Joe met them at the Ohio River and carried them across. After that, they moved from safe house to safe house on the Underground Railroad, hiding in barns and secret rooms, until they reached Lake Erie and crossed into Canada, where they were finally safe.

summary_text: My name is Zuri. My hair kinks, coils, and curls in its own way. Daddy says it is beautiful, and Zuri feels proud. She likes that her hair helps her be herself. The next day, Zuri woke up very early all by herself because she was too excited to sleep. It was a big day. Daddy was still sleeping, and Zuri tiptoed past him with Rocky.

video_title: The Three Ninja Pigs Read Aloud with Comprehension Questions | Homeschool Curriculum & Activities
summary_text: A wolf loved to huff and puff and blow houses down. The three little pigs were tired of him, so they went to a new ninja school. Pig one learned some beginner moves but quit after less than two weeks. Pig two learned jiu-jitsu and could block and punch, but he also stopped studying. Pig three worked hard at karate every day. She learned many moves, broke boards, and earned her last belt. Then the wolf went to Pig One’s straw house and tried to make him run. Pig one swung and missed, so the wolf chased him to Pig two. Pig two tried to kick the wolf, but the wolf blew the door down. The pigs ran to Pig three. Pig three bowed, fought the wolf with flips and kicks, and broke a stack of bricks. The wolf got scared and ran away. The pigs were happy, and they kept training at school.

video_title: The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind | POC Kids Book Read Aloud, Comprehension Questions & Service Project
summary_text: William lived in a small village in Malawi where there were no lights and very little money. At night he dreamed about machines, trucks, and radios, and he listened to his grandpa’s stories. But when the rains stopped, the sun dried the fields and the maize turned to dust. William’s father told the children to eat only one meal a day, and then William had to leave school. He felt sad and sat under a mango tree for many weeks. Later, he found a library with science books and learned how engines and radios worked. One picture showed a windmill that could make electricity and pump water. William decided to build his own “electric wind.” He collected parts from a junkyard and built a machine with help from his cousin Jeffrey and his friend Gilbert. When the wind blew, the blades turned and a bulb lit up. Later, he used his windmill to power lights and pump water for his family.

video_title: Pelé (Little People Big Dreams) Children’s Book Read Aloud Video, Reading Questions and Activities
summary_text: Little Edson Arantes do Nascimento grew up playing soccer on the streets of Bauru, Brazil. His friend P gave him the nickname Pelé. Edson did not have a real ball, so he made one from a sock, newspapers, and string. One day he found his father crying because Brazil had lost the World Cup final. Edson promised that one day he would win that championship for him. He played in amateur leagues and amazed people with his ball control and tricks. A coach helped him leave his shoe factory job and move to Santos. When the club saw the 15-year-old boy play, they were impressed. Pelé kept practicing, scored his first official goal, and soon became the season’s top scorer. With his first paycheck, he bought his parents a new house. At 16, he joined Brazil’s national team for the World Cup in Sweden, and Brazil won its first World Cup. Pelé later won two more World Cups, became a world legend, and helped bring people together through soccer.

video_title: Rosa Parks Children's Book Little People Big Dreams Read Aloud Video, Reading Questions & Activities
summary_text: Rosa grew up near Montgomery, Alabama, with her mother, brother, and grandparents. Her grandparents told her about slavery and how black people were treated unfairly even after slavery ended. Rosa saw white children ride the school bus to a big school, while she had to walk to a one-room school for black children. When she grew up, she still had to follow unfair rules in stores, on buses, and in public places. Rosa married Raymond, who worked for fairness, and she began helping fight for more rights for black people. One day, a bus driver told her to give up her seat for a white person, but Rosa said no. She was taken to jail, and when she came home, she kept fighting. Many black people stopped riding the buses, and they walked instead. After a year, the Supreme Court said bus segregation was wrong. Rosa later moved to Detroit and kept working for fair schools, jobs, houses, voting rights, women’s rights, and the rights of people in prison.

Lola asks her cousin Leticia, Mrs. Bernard, Jonathan, other neighbors, and Mr. Mir about the island. They tell her about big bats, lots of music, dancing, coconut water, sweet mangoes, bright colors, and hot weather. Lola’s mother also tells her about the hurricane that blew houses away when Lola was born. Then Mr. Mir tells Lola about a terrible monster that scared the island for many years until heroes fought it and banished it. Lola stays up drawing page after page until her island book is finished. The next day she brings it to class, and when Miss Obie asks to see it, Lola opens the book and the island seems to burst out.

video_title: Stand Tall Molly Lou Melon Read Aloud
summary_text: Molly Lou Melon was the shortest girl in first grade, and she had buck teeth, a funny voice, and clumsy hands. She did not mind because her grandma taught her to walk proudly, smile big, sing out clear and strong, and believe in herself. Then Molly Lou Melon moved to a new town and had to leave her grandma and friends. On the first day of school, Ronald Durkin called her shrimpo, but Molly Lou Melon caught a football, ran under Ronald’s legs, and scored a touchdown. The children were amazed, and Ronald felt foolish. On the next days, Ronald teased her about her teeth, her voice, and her snowflake, but Molly Lou Melon showed her big smile, sang so strongly that Ronald fell back, and made a beautiful snowflake. At the end, Ronald gave her a penny for her tooth, and Molly Lou Melon wrote to her grandma to say her advice was right.

video_title: Ben and Emma's Big Hit by Gavin Newsom | Read Aloud Books for Kids
summary_text: Ben loved baseball and could see shapes all around the field, like the diamond, the pitcher’s mound, and the ball curving through the air. But reading was hard for him because he had dyslexia. In class, Miss Kim helped Ben and the other students by matching letters with sounds. Ben did not like that the letter B sounded different from the way he had learned it before. Reading time made him feel nervous and sick, especially when he saw Emma, who always carried big chapter books. During reading group, Ben could not sound out the words, and when he got stuck again, he ran out of the room. Miss Kim found him by the water fountain, and after he took deep breaths, they went back to class. Ben learned that Emma also could not really read her big books yet, and Miss Kim said learning takes practice. Later, the class helped Miss Kim practice baseball, and she finally hit the ball. Ben saw that everyone must keep trying and can get help from their team.

video_title: The Incredible Shrinking Lunchroom by Michal Babay | Read Aloud Books for Kids
summary_text: Parley Elementary had a lunchroom that was very loud and crowded. Students could not find places to sit, and they wrote to Mrs. Mench, the principal, asking for help. Mrs. Mench thought for a while, then made changes that made the lunchroom even worse. First, she put science projects in the room, so there was less space. Then she moved classroom pets there, and the lunchroom filled with snakes, tarantulas, hamsters, and worms. After that, she brought sports teams inside because it was too hot to practice outdoors. Balls flew, whistles blew, and the room became messy and smelly. The students kept sending notes because they were unhappy. At last, when the heat wave ended, Mrs. Mench moved the sports teams back outside, returned the animals to their classrooms, and put the science projects in the hallways. Then the students had a quiet, roomy lunch and thanked her with chocolate and notes.

video_title: The Incredible Shrinking Lunchroom by Michal Babay | Read Aloud Books for Kids
summary_text: Parley Elementary had a lunchroom that was crowded, noisy, and messy. Students could not hear each other, and lunch was interrupted by the drama club and music club, so they wrote to Principal Miss Mench asking for help. Miss Mench thought about the problem and first put science projects in the lunchroom. This made the room even more crowded, and students had to squeeze between tables and spilled food and juice. They wrote again, and she then moved classroom pets into the lunchroom for a “learning zoo.” A snake escaped, tarantulas molted, hamsters squeaked, and worms looked like spaghetti. The students complained once more. Next, when the weather was too hot for outside sports, she sent sports teams to practice in the lunchroom, which made it even louder and more chaotic. At last, when the heat wave ended, sports moved outside, the animals went back to class, and the science projects were placed in the hallways. The lunchroom finally became quiet, calm, and roomy, and the students thanked Miss Mench.

summary_text: A princess tells how she does almost everything with her pet unicorn. She hears someone say, “Never let a princess paint with her unicorn,” and she feels surprised. She tests it by putting paint on a brush, but the unicorn licks it. Her mom comes down the hall, and the princess thinks she is in trouble. Instead, her mom says she has found her new rainbow unicorn princess dress. The princess sees that the paint made her dress beautiful, and she learns that a little mess can make a magnificent masterpiece.

video_title: A Little Spot of Emotion 8 Book Compilation - SEL Read Aloud - Anger, Happiness, Love, Anxiety
summary_text: A peaceful spot talks to help calm down an angry spot, which means anger. It explains that people can feel anger, sadness, and anxiety, but they feel best when they are peaceful. Angry spots can show up when someone feels frustrated, afraid, or hurt. The peaceful spot teaches a special trick. First, put up one hand and imagine four red spots on the fingers and one green spot on the thumb. Then count the spots from 1 to 4 and tap each one. After that, fill your lungs with peaceful air and coat your spots with love and care. The story then shows this trick being used in different situations. When someone cannot draw the way they want, the angry spot gets big. When a toy is taken, the angry spot gets big again. The trick helps the angry spot get smaller. In the end, the calm child can think clearly, find a missing dinosaur, and see that a spilled painting is really splatter art.

video_title: 🎨I'm NOT Just a Scribble - STEAM Read Aloud - Scribble Series Book 1 - Diane Alber
summary_text: Scribble was a little drawing with crossing, wiggly lines. His tiny loops could make him small, and bigger swirls could make him tall. He could be green, baby blue, or many bright colors, and he liked changing colors as he walked along. One day, Scribble went on a short walk and found a house. He stopped and said hello, and he asked if they could play. The house had never seen anyone like Scribble before. It asked what he was and then said his lines were not straight and his colors were too bright. Scribble asked for a chance, but the house told him to go away. Scribble felt very sad, but he changed his colors and kept walking. Then he met the sun and the clouds, and they also told him to go away. Scribble said that being different did not make him bad. The next day, the house, the clouds, and even Rainbow came back and asked him to play. Scribble forgave them, and they all made beautiful art together.

summary_text: Finn the frog lives in a book and talks to a sick child who visits him. Finn sees yellow boogers and decides the child has a bad cold. Finn eats it and feels better. He thanks the child and says kindness matters more than popularity. At the end, Finn asks for a new photo for his wall of fame and says, “Say flies.”

The story ends by showing that the spots were hard to remove, but they led to art.
