video_title: ❤️A Little Spot of Love - SEL Read Aloud - Diane Alber
summary_text: A little spot of love explains that love is the feeling you get when you care about someone or when someone cares about you. Love can grow big, and that is okay because everyone needs to be loved. The story shows many ways to grow a love spot. Words can help, like saying “I love you” or giving compliments such as “You are smart.” Writing can also help, like making a surprise note or letter. Confidence matters too, because kind words to yourself can help you feel brave, loving, and kind. Actions are another way to show care. Helping someone clean up, listening closely, and spending quality time can make others feel loved. Friendship, gifts, hugs, high fives, fist bumps, waving, and thumbs up can all grow a love spot. The story ends by saying people like different kinds of love, and asks the reader to share their favorite way to grow a love spot.

summary_text: The story is about an egg who says he is a very good egg. He helps by carrying groceries, watering plants, changing tires, and painting houses. Long ago, he lived in a store with eleven other eggs in a carton. Their names were Meg, Peg, Greg, Clay, Shell, Shelly, Sheldon, Shelby, Eggbert, Frank, and other Frank. The other eggs did not follow rules. They stayed up too late, ate sugary cereal, cried, and broke things on purpose. The main egg tried to fix their behavior and keep peace, but he became tired and stressed. One morning, he saw cracks in his shell and learned from his doctor that pressure was hurting him. He decided to leave the carton and go on his own. On the road, he spent time walking, reading, floating in a river, writing in a journal, breathing, and painting. Slowly, his shell healed. Then he went back home, and the other eggs were happy to see him. He understood that the other eggs did not need to be perfect, and he did not need to be perfect either.

summary_text: The story explains that there is a peaceful spot and an anxiety spot. The anxiety spot shows up when a person feels worried, nervous, anxious, or scared. It can appear when trying new things, like playing soccer or taking a test, and it often asks, “What if?” The story says you can answer, “I can do this,” to help turn the anxiety spot into a peaceful spot. Small anxiety spots can help sometimes, but big worries can make a person miss fun things. The story also says anxiety can cause a tummy ache or sweating. Eating healthy food, getting enough rest, and using music, drawing, or writing can help keep anxiety small. When worries grow fast, a child can use a hand trick, say the calming words, and take deep breaths to blow the worry away.

He tries again at home, but he still makes mistakes, like using salt instead of sugar and vinegar instead of water. His cookies turn bitter and his batter turns green. Milo feels like giving up, but he remembers Chef Gustav saying, “Keep trying and you will create the taste of Happiness.” So Milo calms down, makes a to-do list, follows the recipe carefully, and keeps practicing. After many tries, he bakes his 11th batch. Then his mom takes him to a surprise cooking contest. The judge tastes Milo’s cookies and says they are the winner. Milo learns that the secret ingredient is never giving up.

video_title: 👧Mighty Mila - Deaf Awareness, Self-belief, Perseverance, Inclusion - Read Aloud
summary_text:
Mila tells us about her family. She has a big brother named Luca and a little sister named Sophia. Mila has super ears because she uses implants that help her hear big sounds and tiny sounds. Mila thinks she can do many grown-up things by herself, like making her bed and opening snacks. But her mom and dad still help her and tell her to eat broccoli, wear the right clothes, and go to sleep.

Mila decides to prove she is a big kid and tries to do everything alone. She picks her own clothes, puts on a pink headband, and uses tape to fix her sneaker laces. After that, Mila tries to ride her bike without training wheels. She falls and learns it is okay to ask for help. Mommy and daddy help her, and soon Mila rides on her own. Everyone cheers for her.

video_title: 🐶The Trouble With Children (According to Dog) - Read Aloud
summary_text: A dog tells us about life with a human family. The dog says the food is good, the walks are nice, and the house is cozy, but the children are very noisy and rough. They squeeze the dog, ride on its back like a horse, and sometimes kick its food or put dirty toys in its bowl. They also make the dog wear a pink dress with blue polka dots and shiny clips, and they pull the dog’s fur. Then the children come back, and the dog starts to feel different. It likes a scratch on the head, sweet words, cuddles, treats, and belly rubs. The dog notices that the children can be gentle, too. In the end, the dog snuggles in their bed and decides the children can stay. After that, the dog gives simple rules for safe care: be calm, do not sit on a pup, use gentle pats, give treats, watch body language, and never hit or kick a dog.

The child admits no other monster can scare like Gabe, and at last feels ready to sleep.

summary_text: Frank was a frog who wanted to fly. He tried to jump and flap, but he only fell, and the other animals laughed. Frank felt sad. His parents found him and told him that frogs can do frog things, like swim and hop, but not fly like birds. Frank still wanted to fly, so he kept trying. Then he saw a baby bird fall into the water. Frank quickly swam to the bird, lifted her out, and brought her back to shore. The baby bird’s mother was very thankful. She asked Frank if he still wanted to fly, and then she returned with another bird and a twig. Frank held on while the birds carried him high above the trees. He glided and swooped through the sky. After that, Frank went home. He told his parents that birds were flying and he was holding on, but he said he could be a great swimmer. His parents were proud, and Frank joined his friends in the pond.

Keyana loves her hair in every style, especially two ponytails that flap like wings.

summary_text: A hen lays eggs, and after a rooster mates with her, one egg can grow into a chick. The hen sits on the eggs to keep them warm. Inside the egg, the chick has food in the yolk, water in the albumin, and air space for its first breath. Over many days, the chick grows. On day three it has a heart. On day five its head, eyes, tail, wings, and legs begin to form. On day seven it is small but already looks like a chicken. On day ten and day eleven it grows more and can open and close its beak. On day fourteen it gets an egg tooth. On day eighteen it is very big and covered with soft down. On day twenty it breathes and pecks a hole. The next day it hatches, rests, and then the hen covers her chicks. Later the fluffy chicks come out and follow their mother to search for food in the barnyard.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Over and Under The Pond by Kate Messner with art by Christopher Silas Neal
summary_text: Mom and a child paddle over a pond and look down at the water. They see lily pads, reeds, and the sky reflected like a mirror. Mom tells the child that under the pond is a hidden world. As they move along, they pass whirlygig beetles, painted turtles, red-winged blackbirds, and a moose eating water lilies. Under the pond, minnows swim, a brook trout waits, a caddisfly larva builds a home, and beavers dive for roots. They also see a goldfinch getting ready to fly, tadpoles changing into frogs, a great blue heron catching a minnow, a woodpecker searching for ants, an otter looking for mussels, and a dragonfly resting. At the end, they head home while the sun goes down and the pond grows dark.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Frog and Toad Are Friends by Arnold Lobel
summary_text: Frog runs to Toad’s house in spring and knocks on the door. Toad is asleep and does not want to wake up. Frog goes inside, finds Toad in bed, and pushes him out into the bright sun. Toad says he is too tired and goes back to bed. Frog tells Toad he has been asleep since November and says they can have fun in the spring. Toad asks Frog to wake him in half past May, but he falls asleep again. Frog looks at Toad’s calendar and tears off the old months: November, December, January, February, March, and April. Then Frog runs back and says it is May now. Toad checks the calendar, sees the May page, gets out of bed, and goes outside with Frog to see the spring world.

Toad checked the calendar, saw the May page, got up, and went outside with Frog to see spring.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Frog and Toad Are Friends by Arnold Lobel
summary_text: One day in summer, Frog was not feeling well. Toad saw that Frog looked very green and told him to get into bed and rest. Toad made Frog a cup of hot tea, and Frog drank it. Frog asked Toad to tell him a story while he rested. Toad tried to think of a story, but he could not. He walked up and down on the front porch. Then he stood on his head in the house. After that, he poured water over his head. Then he banged his head against the wall. Frog kept asking why Toad was doing these things. Toad said he hoped they would help him think of a story. At last Toad felt terrible, and Frog felt better. Frog said he did not need a story anymore. Then Frog offered to tell Toad a story. Frog told about the frog and the toad, the porch, the head standing, the water, and the wall, and then Toad went to bed while Frog got up.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Frog and Toad Are Friends by Arnold Lobel
summary_text: Toad and Frog went for a long walk across a large meadow, through the woods, and along the river. When they got back to Toad’s house, Toad saw that one button was missing from his jacket. Frog said they should go back and look in all the places they had walked. First they searched the meadow and found a black button, but it was not Toad’s. A sparrow brought a button with two holes, but that was not right either. In the woods they found a small button, then a square button from a raccoon, but Toad said each one was wrong. At the river they found a thin button, and Toad got very upset and ran home. There he saw his own white, four-holed, big, round, thick button on the floor. Toad sewed all the buttons on his jacket and gave it to Frog the next day.

Frog swam fast and made big splashes, and Toad swam slowly and made small splashes. A turtle came by, and Toad asked Frog to tell the turtle to go away so no one would see him when he got out. At last he came out, and everyone laughed, including Frog. Toad said, “Of course I do,” and went home with his clothes.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Frog and Toad Are Friends by Arnold Lobel
summary_text: Toad sat on his front porch and felt sad because it was mail time and he never got any letters. Frog came by and asked why Toad looked sad. Toad said his mailbox was always empty, so waiting for the mail made him unhappy. Frog felt sad with him for a while. Then Frog went home and wrote Toad a letter. He put it in an envelope and asked a snail to take it to Toad’s house. Frog came back and found Toad in bed. Frog told Toad to wait for the mail, but Toad said no one ever sent him a letter. Frog kept looking out the window. Then he told Toad that he had sent the letter himself. Frog said the letter told Toad that he was his best friend. Toad liked that letter very much. Frog and Toad sat on the porch and waited happily. Four days later, the snail brought the letter, and Toad was very pleased.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Words and your heart by Kate Jane Neal
summary_text: This book talks about the heart, the little bit inside a person that makes them who they are. It says words go into our ears and can change how our hearts feel. Some words can help us learn about things, like big or little, or make sounds seem clear. Some words can make people happy and want to sing. But some words can also make people cry and hurt their hearts, like a sharp arrow. The story says words have power. They can cheer up someone who feels sad, help someone who feels weak, and help someone keep going when they want to give up. Words can also make people giggle, grin, and laugh. The book asks us to use our words to take care of each other’s hearts. It says that when we do this, we can help make someone’s world a better place.

summary_text: On a cold day in a little town, Annabelle found a box full of yarn in many colors. She went home and knit a sweater for herself, then one for Mars. She still had yarn left, so she made a sweater for Nate, his dog, and later for her classmates when Mr. Norman said her sweater was a distraction. Annabelle kept knitting and made sweaters for her mom, dad, aunt, Mr. Pendleton, Mrs. Pendleton, Dr. Palmer, little Lewis, and even a hat for Mr. Crabtree. She also made sweaters for dogs, cats, and other animals, and then for things that did not even wear sweaters. People came from far away to see her. An arch duke offered money for the yarn, but Annabelle said no. That night robbers stole the box for him. When the arch duke opened it, he was upset and cursed Annabelle, but the story stops before we learn what happens next.

At school, Mr. Norman said Annabelle’s sweater distracted everyone, so Annabelle offered to knit a sweater for everyone in the class, and then she did, including Mr. Norman. video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: The Moon Seems to Change by Franklyn M. Branley, Ill by Barbara & Ed Emberley
summary_text: Look up at the sky at night and you may see the moon. Sometimes it is big and round, called a full moon. Sometimes only part of it shows, like a crescent moon or a quarter moon. The moon seems to change, but it really does not change shape. It changes because it goes around Earth. As it moves, we see more of the lighted half or less of it. This is called waxing when the moon grows bigger and waning when it gets smaller. Half of the moon is always lit by the sun. The moon goes through phases in the same order again and again: new moon, crescent, first quarter, full moon, third quarter, crescent, and back to new moon. A new moon means we cannot see it. A few nights later, a crescent appears, then the moon grows until it is full, and after that it gets smaller again.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Miss Maple's Seeds by Eliza Wheeler
summary_text: Miss Maple flies home to her tall maple tree. All summer long, she has searched for orphan seeds that got lost during spring planting. She brings them home and learns their names: Poppy, wild rice, maple, water lily, pine, bean, impatiens, apple, raspberry, lupine, sunflower, acorn, corn, pea, lentil, buttercup, tomato, honeysuckle, pumpkin, fern, and more. She tells them, “Take care, my little ones. For the world is big and you are small.” Miss Maple takes the seeds on field trips to the river, the fields, and the forest so they can learn where they may grow. She shows them how to stay away from weedy characters. At night, she reads flower tales by firefly light. In winter, everyone stays cozy and shares maple syrup, corn husks, and fruit rinds. When spring rain comes, Miss Maple says the raindrops help them grow. At last, on a windy May morning, the seeds leave to find roots of their own, and Miss Maple goes on to search for more lost seeds.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Ox Cart Man by Donald Hall, pictures by Barbara Cooney
summary_text: In October, the ox-cart man and his family loaded his cart with the things they had made or grown all year. They packed wool, a shawl, mittens, candles, linen, shingles, birch brooms, potatoes, apples, honey, turnips, cabbages, maple sugar, and goose feathers. He said goodbye to his wife, daughter, and son, then walked with his ox for ten days to Portsmouth market. There he sold all the goods, and then he also sold the boxes, barrels, bag, cart, ox, yoke, and harness. With the money, he bought an iron kettle, an embroidery needle for his daughter, a barlow knife for his son, and wintergreen peppermint candies for the family. He walked home with the kettle and gifts. His family was waiting, and they used the new things right away. That night, he worked by the fire making new harness, a new yoke, and a new cart, while the rest of the family made more things for the next year.

summary_text: A tiny sea snail lived on a black rock with other snails. She looked at the sea and the ships and said she wanted to sail. The other snails told her to sit still and stay put. But the tiny snail wanted to travel, so she climbed onto the tail of a great big gray blue humpback whale. The whale sang to her about ice, coral caves, stars, and waves, and he carried her across the sea. They saw big waves, caves with fish and sharks, and a sky that was sometimes sunny and sometimes stormy. Then the whale lost his way. Fast boats scared him, and he swam too close to shore. The tide went out, and the whale was stuck on the sand. The tiny snail asked him to move, but he could not. She crawled to the school, where children saw her trail and called the firemen. The children helped keep the whale cool, the tide came back, and the whale and snail returned safely. Back on the rock, the snail told her tale, and many snails rode on the whale’s tail.

After a snowstorm, she went outside and saw caribou coming to eat because the snow covered their grass. Then a goose fell from the sky. Babushka found that a hunter had hurt the goose, so she carried it home, fed it, and kept it warm in her best basket. She named the goose Rashinka. As Rashinka grew stronger, she laid eggs and explored the house. One day she knocked over Babushka’s paint jars and then the basket of painted eggs, and all the eggs broke. Babushka and Rashinka were sad. The next morning, Babushka found a new, brightly colored egg in Rashinka’s basket. For 12 mornings, more beautiful eggs appeared. Babushka took them to the festival in Moscow, won first prize, and came home. That night she found one last egg hatch, and the little goose stayed with her always.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: The Tale of Three Trees Retold by Angela Elwell Hunt, Illustrated by Tim Jonke
summary_text: On a mountaintop, three little trees dreamed about what they would become. The first wanted to hold treasure as a beautiful chest. The second wanted to be a strong sailing ship for kings. The third wanted to stay on the mountain and grow tall so people would look up and think of God. Years passed, and the trees grew tall. Then three woodcutters came. The first tree was cut down and taken to a carpenter, who made him into a feed box for animals. The second tree was cut down and made into a small fishing boat. The third tree was cut down too and left in a lumber yard. Later, a baby was placed in the first tree’s manger, a tired traveler calmed a storm from the second tree’s boat, and the third tree became the cross where Jesus was nailed. In the end, each tree learned that God’s love gave it a special purpose.

The second wanted to be a strong sailing ship that carried kings across the sea. The third wanted to stay on the mountain and grow so tall that people would look up and think of God. After many years, woodcutters came and cut down all three trees. The first tree was made into a feed box for animals instead of a treasure chest. The second tree was turned into a small fishing boat and carried smelly fish on a lake. The third tree was cut into beams and left in a lumber yard. Later, the first tree became a manger for a baby, the second carried a traveler who calmed a storm, and the third became the cross for Jesus. In the end, each tree learned that its true purpose was different from what it had first expected.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Where Did My Clothes Come From? By Chris Butterworth Illust by Lucia Gaggiotti
summary_text: Clothes are made from many different things, and each kind is used for a special job. Jeans are made from cotton. Cotton grows on bushes from seeds, with sun and water, then the cotton bowls open and show soft white fibers. People pick the cotton, clean it, comb it, spin it into yarn, dye it blue, weave it into cloth, and sew it into jeans. Sweaters are made from wool, which comes from sheep. The wool is washed, combed, spun, and knitted into warm clothes. Party dresses can be made from silk, which comes from silkworm cocoons. Soccer uniforms are made from synthetic fibers like polyester and nylon, and fleece jackets can be made from recycled plastic bottles. Rain boots are made from rubber from rubber trees. At the end, the story says old clothes can be reused or recycled instead of thrown away.

summary_text: The story explains where many kinds of clothes come from and how they are made. Jeans start as cotton on bushes. The cotton is picked, cleaned in a gin, combed, spun into yarn, dyed blue, woven into cloth, and sewn into jeans. Sweaters are made from wool, which is cut from sheep, washed, combed, spun, and knitted into warm clothes. Fancy party dresses can be made from silk. Silkworms eat mulberry leaves, make cocoons, and the silk threads are unwound, twisted into yarn, dyed, and woven. Soccer uniforms are made from synthetic fibers like polyester and nylon, which begin as chemicals, are pushed through tiny holes, and become yarn and cloth. Fleece jackets can be made from recycled plastic bottles. Rain boots are made from rubber taken as latex from rubber trees, then turned into sheets and boot shapes. The story ends by reminding readers to recycle old clothes instead of wasting them.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: The Tomten by Astrid Lindgren
summary_text: At night, the old farm in the forest is quiet and everyone is asleep except the Tomten. He lives in a corner of the hayloft and walks on small silent feet through the snow. First he visits the cowshed and speaks to the cows in Tomten language. Then he goes to the stable and talks to Stan Stauben, the horse. He visits the sheep and lambs, the chickens in the chicken house, and Caro in the dog kennel. He also looks in at the children’s cot, but the children are sleeping. In the morning, the children see his tiny footprints in the snow. The Tomten returns to his cozy hayloft, where the cat is waiting for milk. Winter is cold and long, but the Tomten keeps walking around the farm every night, and he stays there year after year.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Johnny Appleseed by Steven Kellogg
summary_text: John Chapman was born in Leominster, Massachusetts, in 1774. His early life was hard because his father went to war, and his mother and baby brother died. Later, his father married again, and John grew up in a busy home near an apple orchard. John loved watching apples grow, and he loved the woods and animals. When he was old enough, he went west into the wilderness. He planted apple seeds in the Allegheny Mountains and kept walking through Pennsylvania and Ohio, making more orchards for settlers who would come later. He lived simply, slept in the open, and ate butternuts in winter. People began calling him Johnny Appleseed. He gave help and trees to neighbors and told children stories. During the war in 1812, he ran through the night to warn families about danger. He later moved to Indiana, and in 1845 he became sick in a snowstorm and died in a cabin. People still told stories about him after he was gone.

video_title: 🦬 BUFFALO FLUFFALO - Read Aloud with Ms. Linda | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: There once was a buffalo fluff who was snarly, tough, and always said, “I’m the buffalo fluff. I heave and I huff. Leave me alone because I’ve had enough.” One day, a ram came with a gift: a big floppy wool hat for shade. Buffalo Fluff did not want it and sent the ram away. Then a prairie dog asked him to play in the tubular tunnels, but Fluff said no and told him to go away too. Next, a crow landed on his horn and tried to chat. Fluff still acted grumpy. Then a dark cloud covered the prairie, and rain fell on Fluff. The rain made him small and wet, so everyone could see him. The ram, prairie dog, and crow said he did not need to act tough. Fluff said sorry for being grumbly. In the end, he snuggled with his friends.

summary_text: Buffalo Fluff is an old buffalo who is snarly, tough, and does not want help from anyone. First, a ram brings him a wool hat because he sees Fluff napping in the shade, but Fluff sends him away. Then a prairie dog invites him to play in his tunnels, but Fluff refuses again because he is too puffed up and grumpy. Next, a crow lands on Fluff’s horn and asks to chat, but Fluff says no and acts unfriendly. After that, a dark cloud covers the prairie, thunder crashes, and rain pours down on Fluff’s head. When the others see him wet, they notice that he looks very small without his fluff. Fluff shouts that he is still tough, but the ram and prairie dog tell him he does not need to act tough and that they like him as he is. Fluff admits he is sorry for being grumbly, and the crow says he is huggy and snuggly. In the end, Fluff is happy and snuggles with his friends.

summary_text: A Wildlife Warrior sees the world as big and new, with a fresh adventure each day. The Earth has many animals that need love and care. They learn how animals live, where they live, and what they do each day. They care for animals with fur or scales, big and small. They also watch baby animals grow. The babies become stronger and learn to jump, fly, and move with confidence. Wildlife Warriors learn about deserts, forests, oceans, and jungles, and they protect these places. They help at zoos and at the Wildlife hospital by treating animals with kindness and respect. In the end, they keep learning, observing, and conserving, and the story asks others to come along on the wildlife mission.

summary_text: On the first night of Hanukkah, Ruthie opened a present and got Hanukkah pajamas. She wanted to wear them for all eight nights, and her mom asked her to keep them spotless for the pajama party. Ruthie tried very hard to stay clean, but each night brought a new mess. She made latkes with Sarah, lit the candles, played games, and helped with holiday tasks. On each night, she said her pajamas were still spotless or spot free, even after splashes, glitter, chocolate, and spills. By the last night, Ruthie and her family were ready for the big pajama party. At the family photo, Ruthie spun around and got covered with more spots, smudges, and splatters. She laughed because her Hanukkah pajamas were finally spotted, and the family called it a Hanukkah miracle.

video_title: 🍞 THE BAKERY DRAGON - Read Aloud with Ms. Linda | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: Ember the dragon loved gold and wanted treasure of his own. He saw other dragons with gold, so he tried to get some from villagers. He puffed a big scary flame, but it was only a tiny flame. At dusk, the other dragons flew home with their spoils, and Ember stayed behind. In the foggy village, he saw golden light and thought it was gold, but it was a street lamp and then a window. Ember was tired and curled up in the warm light. Then a storm came. A baker told Ember to come inside and help in the bakery. Ember washed, pushed dough, and used his small flame to light the stove. He watched the dough change into golden bread. Ember took some home and found it tasted buttery, crunchy, and soft. Soon, other dragons wanted a taste. Ember wanted more, and the baker said people did not like dragons who stole. In the end, Ember learned that baking gold was better than taking it, and sharing it was best of all.

video_title: 🐶🐔 AGNES AND THE HEN - Read Aloud with the Author | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: On a little farm behind a cottage lived a big dog named Agnes and a small hen named Rosie. Agnes was strong, wise, and cozy, and she helped keep the chickens safe at night by locking them in their coop. Most hens lived in neat, same-as-every-day ways. They laid eggs in nesting boxes, pecked in straight lines, and slept in a row. Rosie was different. She laid eggs wherever she wanted, followed Agnes around, danced, caught bugs, and slept on a tree branch. After days of rain, Rosie danced so fast in the sunshine that she rolled into a muddy puddle. Agnes helped her up. Later, the other hens looked at Rosie and turned away, and Rosie felt alone. Agnes whispered that being different was not bad. That night, Agnes left the coop latch open by mistake. Foxes came to the farm, but Rosie woke the hens and led them to safety. Then Rosie, the hens, and Agnes howled like dogs, and the foxes ran away.

summary_text: On a little farm behind a cottage lived a big dog named Agnes and many hens. Agnes was strong, wise, and always helped keep the farm safe. She laid eggs when she wanted, followed Agnes around, danced, howled like a dog, and slept in a tree instead of with the other hens. One sunny day Rosie danced so wildly that she rolled into a muddy puddle. Agnes helped her out and brought her back. The other hens stared at Rosie and turned away, so Rosie felt alone. Agnes told her, “not all who are different are lost losing yourself has the greater cost.” That night Agnes forgot to close the latch all the way. Two foxes came, but Rosie woke the hens, led them to safety, and howled like a dog until the foxes ran away. In the morning Rosie saw the hens moving and dancing as they pecked.

video_title: 🐛🦋 WHAT'S INSIDE A CATERPILLAR COCOON? | Read Aloud with the Author | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: Butterflies soar in the sunlight, and moths flutter under the moon and stars. They have lived on Earth since the time of the dinosaurs and are found on every continent except Antarctica. Butterflies and moths are closely related insects. Both can fly, both have antennae, and both are the only insects with scaly wings. They also begin life as wingless, wiggly caterpillars. Their life has four stages: egg, caterpillar, pupa, and adult. This change is called metamorphosis. A baby caterpillar hatches from an egg on a leaf and eats the host plant. As it grows, its hard skin does not grow with it, so it molts and sheds the old skin. Caterpillars spend their time eating and growing, but many predators want to eat them. Some hide with camouflage, some look poisonous, and some use stinky smells or scary tricks. Others spin silk to bungee jump away. When they are big enough, they become a pupa inside a chrysalis or cocoon. Inside, the body changes and a new body with wings is made. Then the adult butterfly or moth comes out and flies.

summary_text: Butterflies and moths fly in sunlight, moonlight, and stars, and they have been on Earth since dinosaurs lived. They are found on every continent except Antarctica. The story explains that butterflies and moths are closely related insects. Both can fly, both have antennae, and both are the only insects with scaly wings. They also begin life as wingless caterpillars. Their life cycle has four stages: egg, caterpillar, pupa, and adult. This change is called metamorphosis. A caterpillar hatches from an egg on a leaf and eats leaves on a host plant. As it grows, it molts because its hard skin does not stretch. The caterpillar spends this stage eating and growing, but it must also avoid predators like birds, lizards, spiders, and wasps. Some hide with camouflage or use spikes, smells, or fake warnings. When it is ready, it becomes a pupa in a chrysalis or cocoon. Inside, its body changes completely, and an adult butterfly or moth emerges with wings.

video_title: 🐛 La oruga muy hambrienta | Spanish Read Aloud Book | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: On a Sunday morning, a little egg rested on a leaf. When the warm sun rose, a tiny caterpillar came out. She was very hungry and looked for food right away. On Monday she ate one apple, but she was still hungry. On Tuesday she ate two pears. On Wednesday she ate three plums. On Thursday she ate four strawberries. On Friday she ate five oranges. Each day she kept eating, but she was still hungry. On Saturday she ate many foods, like cake, ice cream, pickle, cheese, salami, lollipop, cherry pie, sausage, cupcake, and watermelon. That night she had a big stomach ache. The next Sunday she ate one green leaf and felt much better. She was no longer hungry. She had become a big, fat caterpillar. Then she built a cocoon and stayed inside for more than two weeks. After that, she made a hole, pushed out, and became a beautiful butterfly.

video_title: Jamie O'Rourke and the Big Potato - Read Aloud Picture Book | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: Jamie O'Rourke was the laziest man in Ireland, and he would not dig the potatoes. His wife, Eileen, did the planting, watering, and weeding, but then she hurt her back and had to stay in bed. Jamie worried that there would be no food for winter, so he went to church at night. On the way, he found a leprechaun making fairy boots. Jamie caught him and asked for a pot of gold. The leprechaun offered a wish instead, and Jamie wished for the biggest potato in the world. Jamie planted the seed, and a giant potato grew so big that it pushed up the garden shed and part of the cottage. The villagers came to see it and helped dig it out. The potato blocked the road, so everyone cut it up and shared it. All winter they ate the potato, and in spring the villagers promised to help Jamie and Eileen always have food if he did not plant another giant potato.

summary_text: The child says, “This is my body. It belongs to me.” The child learns the names of body parts like belly button, vulva, butt, elbows, penis, and nipples. The child says, “I am the boss of my body,” and talks about doing things that feel good. Grown-ups still make some choices to keep the child safe and healthy, like putting on helmets. When someone says no, or shows no in many ways, we must listen and stop right away. People can change their mind, and their body choices matter.

From the bench, the man will see the boy grow. He will watch the boy learn to ride a bike, run, and fall. He will stay by him and support him when things are hard. The boy will sit on his knee and sometimes cry there. He will also feel happy and sad as he grows. The man will tell him, “I love you,” again and again. The bench will be used for Papa and son to share joys and victories. In the end, the speaker looks out the window with tears of joy at the man and their beautiful boy on the bench, which is now their home.

video_title: The Berenstain Bears and the Spooky Old Tree - Read Aloud Picture Book | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: Three little bears go to a spooky old tree. One bear has a light, one has a stick, and one has a rope. They ask if they dare go in, and they do. Then they climb a twisty old stair. Next they find a giant key and a moving wall, and they go through it into a spooky old hall. There they see a great sleeping bear. The three little bears go over the sleeping bear. After that, they have no light, no stick, and no rope, and they all have the shivers. To get out, they go up a ladder through the floor, down a slide, and out a door. Then they run fast home again, safe at last.

video_title: Breathe Like a Bear - Read Aloud With Author Kira Willey | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: The story explains that mindfulness means paying attention to the present moment, both inside our bodies and around us. It says breathing is the main tool for practicing mindfulness. First, it shows how mindfulness can help with focus, stress, and calm. Then it teaches a game called Rainstorm. Children rub their hands for wind, tap slowly for rain, clap for lightning, stomp for thunder, and then slow down until everything is quiet. After that, it shows Funny Breath, where children sit tall, make bunny paws, and take quick bunny breaths. Next comes Scrunch and Let Go, where children squeeze their toes, legs, belly, arms, hands, and face, then breathe out and relax. It also teaches Hot Chocolate, where children blow on an imaginary cup, and Bear Breath, where children breathe slowly like a bear in a cave. At the end, it asks children to think of kind things they have done and kind things they can do next time.

video_title: Breathe Like a Bear - Read Aloud With Author Kira Willey | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: The story explains that mindfulness means paying attention to the present moment, including what is happening in our bodies and around us right now. It says that breathing is the main tool for practicing mindfulness. The book Breathe Like a Bear shows simple exercises that can help children focus in school, let go of stress, and calm down when they feel hyper or fidgety. The first exercise is Rainstorm. Children rub their hands for wind, tap slowly for rain, clap for lightning, and stomp for thunder. Then they slow down until everything is still and quiet, and they take a long breath in and out. The next exercise is Funny Breath, where children sit up tall, make bunny paws, take quick little breaths, and then let the air out. They can also feel their belly move. The third exercise is Scrunch and Let Go, where children tighten their toes, legs, belly, arms, hands, and face, then breathe out and relax. These exercises help prepare them for calm breathing activities like Hot Chocolate and Bear Breath.

video_title: Dangerously Ever After - Read Aloud Flip-Along Picture Book | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: Princess Amanita loved dangerous things, especially her wild garden full of prickles, nettles, and sharp plants. One day she met Prince Florian, who was looking for a dragon to slay or someone to talk to. He accidentally cut what he thought were grapes, but they were grenades, and they blew a hole in her new wheelbarrow. The next day he brought roses to make up for it. Amanita first thought they were too ordinary, but she discovered the stems were covered with sharp thorns and liked them. She asked for rose seeds, and when they grew, each seed became a pink nose instead of a flower. The noses sneezed all day, made the garden messy, and kept everyone awake snoring at night. Amanita pulled them up and rode off to find Florian, but she got lost in a dark forest. The noses pointed her toward his castle by following the smell of roses. She found Florian, gave him the noses, and they planted them in his garden. Amanita took home nine thorny rose bushes and was pleased because they were dangerous and smelled nice.

video_title: Back-to-School Books for Kids - 60 MINUTES Read Aloud | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: Ricoberto has just moved from Venezuela to a new classroom. At first, the other children do not understand his language, and they laugh until the teacher quiets them. When the teacher says, “From Venezuela,” Ricoberto hears his name and homeland spoken kindly. Later, the teacher asks the class to share what they did last summer. Other children talk about trips to France, Maine, India, Spain, and South Carolina, and they show souvenirs from their travels. Ricoberto remembers staying home, caring for his little sister, making her laugh, hugging her at nap time, and reading books while she slept. He also notices that his lunch and his way of life are different from the others’. At first he feels alone, but later he begins to share his own stories. He tells the class his name is Angelina, and another child says her name is Angelina too. This helps the room feel more open, and Ricoberto starts finding places where he can belong.

summary_text: The story begins with a school day starting. Bells ring, and children hurry in with their pencils sharpened and their things ready. The classroom is a place where everyone is welcome, no matter how they look, what they wear, or where they come from. In class, the children raise their hands, take turns, and share music, art, and stories. At lunch, there are many kinds of bread, and everyone gets food. Then the children go outside to swing and slide together. The day shows that the classroom and school are safe places where people can learn from one another, find talents, and discover the world. When the busy day ends, the children go home to rest and come back ready for a new day. The story ends by saying that everyone has a place and space there, and that being kind and welcoming can help a different person become a new friend.

After she was put back in her carton, Cupcake sneezed frosting and sprinkles on everyone. Milk did not get mad. She said it was okay, and the whole class laughed and got along.

Next, they choose between walking on stilts for a year or jumping on a pogo stick everywhere. Ryan and another child choose the pogo stick because stilts could hit doorways, but Stephen says stilts would make him look taller. Then they choose between being in a row boat in the ocean or on a skateboard in the desert. Some choose the desert, and others choose the ocean, giving reasons about sand, sharks, drifting, and getting to shore. Last, they choose between a laugh like an air horn or a siren, and they all give answers and explain why they picked them.

video_title: IN A JAR by Deborah Marcero  - Read Aloud Picture Book | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: Llewellyn was a collector who kept many things in jars, like buttercups, feathers, and heart-shaped stones. One night, when the sunset made the sky look like tart cherry syrup, he went to the shore with many jars. A girl named Evelyn was there, and Llewellyn scooped some of the cherry-colored light into a jar and gave it to her. Evelyn took it home, and it glowed all night with the memory of the sunset. After that, Llewellyn and Evelyn collected more wonders together, like rainbows, the sound of the ocean, the wind before snow, and the seasons of winter, spring, and summer. Their jars filled Llewellyn’s house. Then Evelyn’s family moved away, and Llewellyn felt very sad and empty. Later, he collected a meteor shower in a jar and sent it to Evelyn. Evelyn sent back sounds, crowds, and bright night lights from her new home. When autumn came, Llewellyn went to collect a jar full of golden leaves for Evelyn, and a boy named Max was there too.

video_title: Laxmi's Mooch by Shelly Anand - Read Aloud Picture Book | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: Lakshmi notices her “much,” the little hairs above her lip, when her friends Zoe and Noah play farm animals at recess. Zoe says Lakshmi looks like a cat because of her whiskers, and Noah agrees. Lakshmi feels shy and spends the rest of the day hiding her face. At home, she tells her mommy and papa about it. Mommy says many women in her family have mooche, or mustaches, and that hair grows on many parts of the body. Papa tells Lakshmi that hair can protect people and keep them warm. They also talk about the hair between her eyebrows and compare it to Frida Kahlo and a caterpillar. That night, Lakshmi dreams of tigers and butterflies. The next day, she chooses to play jungle animals instead of farm animals. She tells Zoe that Zoe has a much too, and they both look in the mirror. Noah asks if he has one, and Lakshmi draws a much on his lip. Soon many children line up to show real or drawn mooches.

video_title: Miss Rumphius - Read Aloud Picture Book | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: The lupine lady was once a little girl named Alice who lived in a city by the sea. She loved listening to her grandfather, an artist, tell stories about faraway places. Alice said she would grow up, travel, and someday live by the sea. Her grandfather told her she must do a third thing too: do something to make the world more beautiful. When Alice grew up, she left home and worked in a library in another city. People called her Miss Rumphius. She traveled to many places, including a tropical island, mountains, jungles, deserts, and the land of the lotus eaters. She met kind people, saw animals, and collected beautiful shells. At the land of the lotus eaters, she hurt her back and decided it was time to live by the sea again. There she planted lupine seeds, and the flowers grew and spread. Soon fields and roads were covered with blue, purple, and rose-colored lupines, and people called her the lupine lady.

video_title: Who Was Ruth Bader Ginsburg? Read Aloud with Author Lisbeth Kaiser | Brightly Storytime Together
summary_text: Ruth Bader Ginsburg learned many things from her mother. She learned to love books, to be kind, and to know that she was important, just like a boy. Ruth grew up seeing that Jewish people and girls were not always treated fairly. She wanted to help others, so she studied hard and went to college. There she learned about lawyers and how they help people speak up for their rights. After college, Ruth became a wife, a mother, and a law student. Some people at law school did not want women there, but Ruth worked very hard. After law school, no law office in New York City would hire her because she was a mother and Jewish, but she did not give up. She became a law teacher and a volunteer lawyer. Ruth went to the Supreme Court to speak about a woman in the air force who was treated unfairly, and the judges agreed the laws should change.

video_title: I'm a Narwhal | Read Aloud Flip-Along Book
summary_text: I am not a unicorn. I am not a fish. I am a narwhal, and I am a kind of whale. My family includes the beluga whale, the dolphin, and the porpoise. I live in the cold Arctic waters with my pod, which means my family. I can dive very deep and hold my breath under the ice for a long time. In spring, narwhals swim to warmer bays. This is called migration. When we get there, we lie on the water and rest. This is called logging. Long ago, people found narwhal horns on the beach and thought they were unicorn horns. My horn is really a big front tooth called a tusk. It grows in a spiral through my upper lip. It helps me taste salt and find food. I can stun cod fish or squid with my tusk and then eat them. I make clicking and knocking sounds, and my family knows what I mean.

video_title: The Night Before Easter - Read Aloud With Author Natasha Wing | Brightly Storytime Together
summary_text: It was the night before Easter, just before dawn. Sister and I were in bed, and our Easter baskets were on the table. We waited and hoped the Easter Bunny would come. Then the hens in the barn made a loud clatter, and I got up to see what was happening. I saw a big fuzzy rabbit with a crook in his ear. He walked on two legs and came to the house with chocolates and striped lollipops. The bunny wore a checkered vest and a bow tie. He filled our baskets with chocolates, chicks, and lots of candy. Some sweets spilled onto the floor. Then he chose eggs and hid them around the house on couches, chairs, the mantle, the bookshelf, and under the stairs. When the rooster crowed, the bunny hurried away in his cart. I read his note: “Happy Easter to all, and to all a great day.”

video_title: The Three Bears | Read Aloud Flip-Along Book
summary_text: There were three bears: papa bear, mama bear, and baby bear. They lived in a little house in the forest. They had three chairs, three bowls, and three beds. One morning mama bear made porridge, but it was too hot, so the bears went for a walk. A little girl named Goldilocks came to their house. She went inside and tried the chairs. The big chair was too hard, the middle chair was too soft, and the baby chair broke. Then she tasted the porridge. The big bowl was too hot, the middle bowl was too cold, and the little bowl was just right, so she ate it all. Goldilocks went upstairs and tried the beds. The big bed was too hard, the middle bed was too soft, and the little bed was just right, so she fell asleep. The bears came home, saw what happened, and found Goldilocks in the baby bear’s bed. Goldilocks woke up, saw the bears, jumped out the window, and ran home.

video_title: Carmela Full of Wishes - Read Aloud Picture Book | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: On her birthday, Carmela wakes up to pancakes with candles and hears her mom sing, “Happy birthday to you.” Her wish has already come true, because she is finally old enough to go with her big brother. They ride through town past the bus stop, the old folks home, the big store, the laundromat, and other places. Carmela jingles her bracelets and imagines many things, but her brother says the sound is annoying. At the laundromat, she picks a dandelion and tries to make a wish, but she does not know what to wish for. Later, her scooter crashes, and her crushed dandelion is beside the drain. Carmela cries because her wish is lost. Her brother takes her back past the shops and tracks to an abandoned farmhouse by the sea. There he tells her to close her eyes and make her wish. Carmela opens her eyes and sees dandelion spores floating in the air like many wishes. Then she follows her brother home, taking off her bracelets.

video_title: Little Tree | Read Aloud Flip-Along Book
summary_text: Once there was a little tree with many green leaves. He stood among other little trees. In summer, his leaves kept him cool. Squirrels climbed his branches and played, and the morning dove sang in him. The little tree thought he would grow big and strong. Then autumn came with cool wind. The leaves on all the trees turned yellow, red, and orange, and one by one they fell. The other animals told little tree to drop his leaves too, but he held them tight because he was not sure what would happen without them. Winter came, and the doe asked why he still had leaves. Little tree kept holding them. Spring came, and the other trees grew bright new leaves. The seasons kept changing, and little tree still would not let go. At last, after another summer and autumn, he saw the other trees growing tall. Then he let his last leaf fall to the ground for the first time.

video_title: The Night Before Summer Camp | Flip-Along Storytime Book
summary_text: The night before day camp, the counselors worked at the town park and tied the canoes by the boat dock. Rick was not happy about camp. In the morning, Mom woke him up, but he hid under the covers and said he did not want to go because he did not know anyone there. Mom told him camp was like a big play time and that it was not an overnighter. Rick said he would try. The bus took him to camp, where he saw many children he did not know and felt lonely. His counselor, Kim, asked him to join the lion cubs and taught the children how to swim. Rick kicked his feet and moved his arms, and Kim said he swam like an otter. Later, the cubs walked on nature trails, saw butterflies, birds, bugs, snakes, and snails, and made little boats from sticks and bark. At lunch, Rick missed his mom and wanted to go home. Kim told him she was nervous too because it was her first job away from home. Rick and Kim held hands, and Rick stayed for the rest of the week. He had fun doing races, crafts, and a play, and by Friday he wanted to come back next summer.

summary_text: Harvey Milk was an ordinary man with a big dream. He wanted everyone, including gay people, to have equality and to live and love as they pleased. Harvey spoke to people about his dream, and in 1977 he became one of the first openly gay people elected to political office in the United States. He and his friends planned marches against unfair laws. Before one march, Harvey asked artist Gilbert Baker to help make a symbol for their group. Gilbert said they needed a flag. Volunteers helped him dye, cut, and sew bright fabric into a flag with eight colorful stripes. On June 25, 1978, the flag flew in San Francisco as Harvey and others marched for equality. Five months later, Harvey and Mayor George Moscone were killed. Many people marched silently with candles. After that, more rainbow flags were made, and the flag became a sign of equality, pride, and hope.

Five months later, Harvey Milk and San Francisco mayor George Moscone were assassinated.
People then marched silently with candles.
After that, more rainbow flags were made, and the flag became a sign of equality, pride, hope, and love around the world.

video_title: The Day You Begin - Read Aloud Picture Book | Brightly Storytime
summary_text: Ricoberto has just moved from Venezuela, and in his classroom he feels different from the other children. When he speaks, some classmates laugh because they do not understand his words. The teacher says his name and homeland in a kind way, and this makes him feel seen. Later, the teacher asks the class to tell what they did last summer. Other children talk about trips to France, Maine, India, Spain, and South Carolina, and they show souvenirs and shells. Ricoberto can only remember staying home, caring for his little sister, making her laugh, hugging her at nap time, and reading books while she slept. He feels empty-handed beside the others. The story also shows other times when he feels left out, such as when his lunch seems strange to others and when he cannot join games. But when children begin to share their own stories, the classroom changes. A girl says she stayed with her sister, and Ricoberto learns her name is Angelina too. The room opens up, and he begins to find new places to belong.

summary_text: Little Red Riding Hood lived with her mother, and her grandmother loved her very much. Her grandmother made her a red velvet cloak, so everyone called her Little Red Riding Hood. On the way, Little Red Riding Hood met a wolf and told him where her grandmother lived. The wolf tricked her into picking flowers while he ran to the cottage. He ate the grandmother, put on her clothes, and waited in bed. When Little Red Riding Hood arrived, the wolf ate her too. Then a huntsman heard loud snoring, came in, killed the wolf, and cut open his belly. Out came Little Red Riding Hood and her grandmother, safe and alive. They thanked the huntsman and ate together.

summary_text: A poor woodcutter lived at the edge of a great forest with his wife, Hansel, and Gretel. When there was almost no food left, the mother told the father to take the children into the forest and leave them there. Hansel heard this and filled his jacket pocket with white pebbles. In the morning, he dropped the pebbles on the path as they walked, and later the children used the moonlight and the stones to find their way home. Soon the family had little food again. This time Hansel tried to drop bread crumbs, but birds ate them. Hansel and Gretel became lost in the forest until they found a house made of bread, pancakes, and sugar candy. They ate from it, but an old woman took them inside. She locked Hansel in a stall and made Gretel work. Gretel pushed the old woman into the oven, freed Hansel, and the children took jewels home.

video_title: 🎾 Iron John—Fairytale Kids Book Brothers Grimm Read Aloud Fantasy Adventure
summary_text: A king had a huge menagerie, but the fiercest creature there was a wild man named Iron John. One day the king’s youngest son, Walter, chased his golden ball into Iron John’s cage. Iron John said he would return the ball if Walter freed him, and he told Walter to find the key under the queen’s pillow. Walter did so, opened the cage, and Iron John escaped with him into the forest. There, Iron John made Walter guard a hidden spring. Walter watched it for years as he grew up. Later, Walter accidentally let a hair, then a finger, and then his hair again touch the spring, and each time it turned gold. Iron John finally sent Walter away with a golden horn. Walter went to a castle, worked in the gardens as Walter-in-the-Mud, and became friends with Elsa. With Iron John’s help, he went to a masked ball, won a tournament, rescued the king’s daughters from robbers, and was healed by Elsa’s tears. He became a prince and took Elsa as his bride.

He stopped Chick Hicks, helped The King finish the race, and returned to Radiator Springs.

video_title: Kamala and Maya’s Big Idea By Meena Harris and Ana Ramírez González
summary_text: Kamala and her sister Maya looked at their building courtyard and imagined a playground there. They told Mommy, and she agreed that it would be nice. Kamala wrote a letter and Maya drew a picture, then they went to ask the landlord. He said no. That night, the sisters asked the other children in the building, and the children also wanted a playground. They wrote to the landlord again, but he said the project would cost too much. He said they could do it themselves if they wanted. The children talked to their parents, but most answers were no. Then Mr. Green offered to help by getting scrap lumber and sand. Soon the children measured, cut, sanded, hammered, and filled a sandbox. Miss Lopez offered old tires for a teeter-totter. More people helped, and the empty courtyard slowly became a playground. Later, Miss Flores found a way to buy an old slide from a school. The children held a potluck and a bake sale to help pay. At last the slide arrived, Kamala and Maya rode it first, and the landlord praised everyone for their work.

summary_text: A fish tells about life in a bowl day by day. At first, the fish swims around the bowl and even thinks about napping, but fish do not sleep, so it keeps swimming. On day 13, it gets a tiny bowl all to itself, but it soon feels lonely and worries about the others. On day 14, everyone comes back together in a big tank, and the fish is happy to be part of a family.

The story ends by saying the spots were hard to remove, but they showed the healing power of art.

She is also told to find people like her and unlike her, say no when needed, color outside the lines, listen to her brave side, and know she can always turn to the book and to the person who loves her.

video_title: Granny Can't Remember Me By Susan McCormick
summary_text: Joey is six years old and has two grandmas. Granny Josie lives in Florida, and Joey takes an airplane to visit her. She has a big yard, a garden, flowers that are not for picking, a pool for grownups, and a cookie door with oatmeal cookies and raisins, which Joey picks out. Joey’s other granny lives two blocks away in a building with a special lock because she may wander and get lost. Granny forgets things like her glasses, pictures, and car keys. She often talks about her big dog, Pickle, who likes balls and swimming. Granny cannot remember Joey’s name, but Joey still tells her about soccer, rockets, dogs, and losing a tooth. Mom says Granny remembers old stories, so she tells Joey about Mom and Uncle Jim when they were little. Joey also hears stories about Granny’s childhood. Pictures from albums help Granny remember the family. At the end, Granny says her very best day was when a little boy was born, and Joey knows she means him.

video_title: All About Weather -  A First Weather Book for Kids By Huda Harajli MA
summary_text: Weather is what the sky and air are like outside. The sky may be blue, the air may feel warm, and the weather can change all the time. Weather helps people decide what to do each day. Weather also changes through the year, and these changes are called seasons. Many places have four seasons: spring, summer, fall, and winter. In spring, the weather is warm and rainy, and flowers bloom. In summer, it is hot and sunny. In fall, the air gets cooler and leaves change color. In winter, the air is cold and there may be snow. Near the middle of the earth, there are two seasons: rainy and dry. Thermometers show how hot or cold the air is. The sun gives light and warmth, and it helps make the weather on Earth.

video_title: The Magic Hat Shop by by Sonja Wimmer
summary_text: One morning, a little hat shop appeared in the town square, and many people stayed away because they did not trust it. The first person to enter was shy Timittim. When he came out wearing a new hat, he stood up straight, looked ahead, and even said hello. After that, more townspeople went in one by one. They came out with hats and seemed changed in good ways. Sad Sally began to smile and laugh again. Mean Morris started leaving his door open and inviting people in for tea and talks. The hatter never spoke much, but he listened carefully and gave each person the right hat. Even the mayor, who called himself the Great Kaczynski, got a hat and felt different and happy. The town wore their hats everywhere. Then a big storm blew through, and all the hats, and the little shop, disappeared. Without the hats, the townspeople felt empty, but Timittim said they did not need magic hats to be themselves. Soon they sang and danced together.

video_title: We Are Water Protectors by Carole Lindstrom and Michaela Goade   Story Time Read Aloud
summary_text: Nakomis tells the child that water is the first medicine and that people come from water. She says water is sacred and that they stand with their songs and their drums. The child hears that the river’s rhythms run through their veins and their people’s veins. Then the story tells of a black snake that will destroy the land, spoil the water, poison plants and animals, and wreck everything in its path. Long ago, people said it would come many years later, and now it is here. Its venom burns the land and makes the water unsafe to drink. The child says they must keep the black snake away from the village’s water and bring the people together to stand for the water and the land. They must also protect the winged ones, the crawling ones, the four-legged, the two-legged, the plants, trees, rivers, lakes, and the earth. The story ends with the people standing as water protectors and saying, “We are still here.”

They do not understand many things and feel afraid to speak. They make many mistakes. Then they become caminantes, walking thousands and thousands of steps across the land. One day, they find a new place that is strange and surprising. In that place, they do not need to speak. They only need to trust, and they do. Books become their language, their home, and their lives. They learn to read, speak, write, and make their voices heard. In the end, they are stories, two languages, lucha, resilience, hope, and dreamers, “sonyadores of the world.”

video_title: Different is Good by Rebecca J. Jackson
summary_text: Ashura loved summertime because the days were long, the world looked golden, and school was out. But he also felt sad because the children at school called him names and made him feel unwelcome. One night, his mother told him to go to the park the next day, and Ashura was scared because he thought the other children would hurt his feelings again. That night, he prayed to the stars for help. A strange purple creature named Cleo came through his window and said the stars had sent him. Cleo promised to go with Ashura to the park. The next day, Cleo showed Ashura many children who were different in skin color, hair, clothes, faith, language, and family. He explained that all of them were special. Ashura listened, played with Bella and her friends, and learned that he belonged too. He went home happy and wished for morning so he could return to the park.

video_title: Fry Bread by Kevin Noble Maillard
summary_text: The story tells about fry bread and how it is made. It starts with simple ingredients like flour, salt, water, cornmeal, baking powder, and sometimes milk or sugar. People mix the ingredients in a bowl and shape the dough with their hands. They make it flat like a pancake, round like a ball, or puffy like a soft pillow. Then the skillet clangs on the stove, the fire blazes below, and the dough is dropped in. The bubbles sizzle and pop as the bread cooks. Fry bread can be golden brown, tan, or yellow, and people eat it with beans, soup, tacos, cheese, vegetables, honey, or jam. The story also says fry bread is shared at weekdays, holidays, dinners, powwows, and festivals. It brings family and friends together.

video_title: That Monster on The Block by Sue Ganz-Schmitt
summary_text: One day, someone moved into vampire’s old house. Monster looked out and hoped the new neighbor would be an ogre, goblin, or dragon. Instead, it was a clown with big shoes, orange hair, and a red nose. Monster called zombie, yeti, mommy, and others to say the new neighbor was a clown, and nobody wanted to welcome him. Clown came around to say hello, but no one answered. He left gifts for the neighbors anyway. Monster still wanted to scare clown away, so at midnight he made loud noises and played spooky music. But clown was not bothered. He was busy helping others, like getting zombie’s cat out of a tree and bringing back mommy’s sheets. Later, clown invited monster to cartwheeling class and helped him practice. Monster saw that clown was fun, and the neighbors gave him a chance. The next day, monster invited clown for scones and tea. Then another new neighbor arrived: a unicorn. This time, monster and the neighbors said, “Welcome neighbor.”

video_title: Clifford's Manners by Norman Bridwell / Children's Story Time Read Aloud
summary_text: Everyone loves Clifford because he has good manners. He says “please” when he asks for something and “thank you” when he gets it. When someone gives him a present, he writes a thank you note. Clifford likes to go to the movies. He waits in line, puts his empty snack bag in the litter basket, says “excuse me” to pass, and never talks during the show. When he needs to sneeze, he uses a handkerchief or tissue. Clifford has many friends, and he shares his toys with them and puts them away when he is done. He plays tennis by the rules, stays calm when angry, smiles when he loses, and does not boast when he wins. He visits his sister in the country by calling ahead, arriving on time, knocking, and wiping his feet. He washes his hands, eats with his mouth closed, helps clean up, and says “thank you” and “goodbye.”

Roy and Silo watch the other penguin families, but they do not have an egg or a baby. One day Roy brings a rock to the nest, and Silo sits on it, but nothing hatches. Then Mr. Gramzy brings them a real egg that needs care. Roy and Silo take turns keeping it warm, turning it, and sitting with it day and night. After a while, the egg cracks open, and a baby penguin comes out. They name her Tango. Roy and Silo feed her, sing to her, and snuggle her. Tango grows strong, swims with them, and the children at the zoo cheer for the family.

video_title: Cami Kangaroo Has Too Many Sweets by Stacy Baver and Rebecca Sinclair / Story Time Read Aloud
summary_text:
All was quiet in the kangaroo house. Mommy was putting baby Wyatt down for a nap, and Cammy Kangaroo was supposed to have quiet time, but she kept thinking about treats. She went to the freezer drawer, took out the ice cream, and carried it to the playroom. She ate too much before Mommy found her. Mommy told Cammy not to sneak treats because sugar can cause cavities and she needed to ask first.

The next day, Cammy looked for more sweets again. She tried the freezer, the pantry, the top of the refrigerator, daddy’s chocolate bars, and even a brownie in the microwave. The dentist gave her a new toothbrush and floss. When Cammy got home, she found Daddy and Wyatt eating ice cream, and Mommy said the family had too many sweets and should start with a healthy dinner.

summary_text: I am Jazz. Jazz loves pink, silver, and green. She likes dancing, singing, backflips, drawing, soccer, swimming, makeup, and pretending to be a pop star. She loves mermaids most of all and sometimes wears a mermaid tail in the pool. Her best friends are Samantha and Casey, and they all have fun together with princess gowns, high heels, cartwheels, and trampolines. Jazz says she has a girl brain and a boy body. When she was little, her mom called her a good boy, but Jazz said, “No, mama, good girl.” Her family was confused because she liked princesses and mermaid costumes, not trucks or superheroes. Jazz kept saying she was a girl and felt unhappy wearing boy clothes. Then her parents took her to a new doctor, who asked many questions and told them the word transgender. After that, Jazz could wear girl clothes to school, grow her hair long, and change her name to Jazz. Some teachers and kids were confused, and some teased her, but the friends who knew her were kind.

video_title: Germs Are Not For Sharing by Elizabeth Verdick & Marieka Heinlen / Children's Story Time Read Aloud
summary_text: Germs are very tiny, so people cannot see them. They can be in the air, in food and water, on the body, and on things people touch. Germs are not for sharing because they can make people sick. When a person coughs or sneezes, the germs can come out. The story says to cover the nose with a tissue and cover the mouth too. If germs get on hands, they can spread when people hold hands, play games, or give high fives. Germs can stay on doorknobs, coins, phones, keyboards, shoes, pets, toys, poles, sponges, and the toilet. They can stay there for up to two hours. To wash germs away, use warm water and lots of soap. Scrub the hands, rinse them, and dry them with a clean towel. Wash hands before eating and after many dirty things.

video_title: Sofia Valdez, Future Prez by Andrea Beaty and David Roberts / Children's Story Time Read Aloud
summary_text: Sophia Valdez was a baby who liked to help. Her Abuelo also helped people in Blue River Creek by doing chores, walking pets, and visiting lonely friends. Each morning, Abuelo walked Sophia to class, and they went home together on Blue River Pass. One day, a pup chased a squirrel and ran away. Sophia and Abuelo followed it up a hill made of trash. The hill broke, and they fell into mud. Abuelo got hurt, and the next day Sophia walked to school alone. She did not like that the hill of trash was still there. Sophia decided to fix it and make a new park. She asked neighbors for ideas and drew a map. Then she learned the town thought she would build it alone. Sophia felt scared and went to city hall. At first, the clerk said she was only a kid and could not build a park. Sophia spoke up, and the mayor let her start a petition. With help from family, neighbors, and school friends, the town built the park together.

video_title: Whoever Heard of a Flying Bird by David Cunliffe and Ivan Barrera / Children's Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Pip lived on an island in the middle of the sea with other birds. They stayed on the ground under a tree and ate seeds and old fruit. Pip wanted something more and wanted to reach high places. First she tried to jump up to a piece of fruit, but she missed. The other birds laughed and said there was no such thing as jumping birds. Then Pip tried running up the tree, but that did not work either. The birds laughed again. After that, she tried flapping her wings, but she still stayed on the ground. That night, Pip sat alone and saw a firefly flying high. This gave her hope. In the morning she tried again. She ran, leaped, and finally flew up to the fruit and took a bite. After that, Pip showed the other birds how to fly, and soon their home was the sky.

video_title: I Will be Fierce by Bea Birdsong and Nidhi Chanani / Children's Book Read Aloud
summary_text: A girl wakes up and says, “I will be fierce.” She gets ready to go outside, puts on her armor, and fills her treasure chest. She goes out to explore new worlds. On the street, she sees dogs on leashes and blows magic bubbles at them. She also sees the older kids waiting for the school bus and the bus itself, which looks like a snake with heads sticking out. When she gets to school, she goes into the elevator while other children walk down the hallway. She goes to the library, where she takes more than five books, even though the sign says only five. Later, she draws a picture of herself riding a giant turtle while other children draw trees and cats. She reaches out to a student no one else wanted to talk to, enjoys the rain while others hide, and then speaks at show and tell. At the end, she rides the bus home with her new friend, rests with her cat, and gets ready for bed, saying she will be fierce again tomorrow.

Now Schmelf travels to bring Hanukkah joy and help children get special gifts.

He saw no stockings, but he saw menorahs, candles, dreidels, gelt, and latkes.
He also saw presents for each night of Hanukkah.
The children’s mother told the story of the Maccabees and the miracle of the oil that lasted eight days.
Schmelf understood and ran back to Santa.
Santa praised him, gave him a new job, and told him to bring magic and joy to Jewish children during Hanukkah each year.
Santa also gave him white and blue clothes, a sleigh, and a Jewish reindeer named Asher.

summary_text: Marcus Geller hears music that no one else seems to notice. He cannot ignore it, so he often tries to play the cello instead. Marcus thinks this may be connected to her younger brother Shane, who played the cello and died when he was 12, the same age Marcus is now. Marcus has heard music since he was little, but when doctors suggested medicine, he kept the music a secret and began copying it on whatever instruments he could find. This made adults notice his talent. Later, his mother brings him a letter from Larkspur Academy for the Performing Arts in New York State. The school invites Marcus to study there and offers to pay all costs. Marcus is surprised, and then he hears an even louder burst of strange music that his mother cannot hear.

video_title: Owl Babies [Children's Storytime | Read aloud]
summary_text: Three baby owls, Sarah, Percy, and Bill, lived with their owl mother in a hole in a tree. One night they woke up and found that their mother was gone. Sarah said she was hunting for food, Percy agreed, and Bill said, “I want my mummy!” The baby owls came out of their home and waited on the tree. Sarah sat on a big branch, Percy on a small branch, and Bill on an old bit of ivy. It was dark in the wood, and they stayed brave while they waited. They moved together onto one branch and thought about where their mother might be. Sarah worried she could be lost, and Percy wondered if a fox got her. Bill still said, “I want my mummy!” Then they closed their eyes and wished for her return. Soon their mother came softly through the trees. The baby owls cried “Mummy!” and flapped and danced. Their mother was back, and Bill said, “I love my mummy!”

summary_text: Deep in the forest, a large crocodile lived in a river. He was selfish and shouted at all the other creatures to stay away. The forest creatures were afraid and went far away to drink and bathe. One morning, the forest heard a loud groaning sound. He ran along the crocodile’s body, went into his mouth, and pulled out a bad tooth. The crocodile’s pain stopped. He thanked the mouse, gave him a nut, and later became his friend. After that, the crocodile invited all the animals to the river, and they came back safely.

The lion still roared, but now he roared with laughter.

video_title: Monkey Puzzle [Children's Storytime | Read Aloud]
summary_text: A little monkey is sad because he cannot find his mum. Butterfly says she will help and asks how big the mum is. The monkey says she is big, bigger than him and bigger than butterfly. Butterfly first shows him a snake, but the monkey says, “No, no, no!” because his mum does not slither, hiss, or curl around eggs, and she has more legs. Then Butterfly shows a parrot, but the monkey says his mum has a nose, not a beak, and she does not squawk or have wings. Next comes a frog, but the monkey says his mum is not green or slimy and she does not croak. Butterfly then thinks the mum is brown and furry, but the monkey says the bat is wrong too. At last Butterfly sees an elephant by the river, and the monkey says that is not his mum either. Butterfly learns that the mum looks like the monkey. Then they go off together to find her hiding place.

video_title: Six Dinner Sid Children's story  Read Aloud
summary_text: Sid was a cat who lived in six houses on Aristotle Street. Each night he went from number one to number six to eat six dinners. He had chicken, fish, lamb, mince, fish again, and beef and kidney stew. The people on the street did not talk to their neighbors, so each one thought Sid was only their own cat. Sid had to remember six names and act in six different ways. He was swanky as Scaramouche, had a job as Bob, was naughty as Satan, silly as Sally, smooched as sooty, and acted rough as Schwartz. One cold day, Sid got a cough and was taken to the vet six times. The vet gave him medicine and then noticed six sick cats in Aristotle Street. He called the owners, and they found out about Sid. The owners were angry and said he could only have one dinner a day. Sid then moved to Pythagoras Place, where everyone talked to each other, so everyone knew about his six dinners and nobody minded.

video_title: The Squirrels Who Squabbled [Children's story | Read Aloud]
summary_text: In a tall forest, autumn came and the air turned cool. Most animals had already stored food for winter, but Cyril the squirrel had not. He had spent the year playing and had no food in his hollow. Then he found one pine-cone with the last nuts of the season inside. Just then, Bruce, who always planned ahead, also wanted the pine-cone because he thought he was one short for his own stores. Cyril and Bruce raced after the cone as it fell from the tree and bounced over bushes and rocks. It landed in the water, and both squirrels followed. A bird swept in and carried the cone away. The squirrels almost fell over the edge, but Cyril grabbed a branch and pulled Bruce to safety. After that, Bruce saw how silly they had been. The two squirrels stopped fighting and began to gather food together, sharing and laughing as friends.

video_title: The Snail and the Whale [Children's story | Read Aloud]
summary_text: A tiny snail with an itchy foot lives on a black rock by the sea. She looks at the ships and says she wants to sail because the sea is deep and the world is wide. The other snails tell her to stay still, but she makes a plan to hitch a lift. One night, a great gray blue humpback whale comes when the tide is high and the stars are bright. The whale sings to the snail and carries her on his tail across the sea. They see icebergs, coral caves, shooting stars, big waves, fish, sharks, storms, and golden sand. Then the whale loses his way and is pushed too close to shore by noisy speedboats. The tide goes out, and the whale is left beached in a bay. The snail cannot move him alone, so she crawls to a school, and children and firemen come to help. The tide returns, the whale is saved, and the whale and snail go back home. After that, more snails climb on the whale’s tail and sail too.

video_title: The Tiger Who Came to Tea [Children's story | Read Aloud]
summary_text: Sophie was having tea with her mummy in the kitchen when someone rang the door. Sophie opened the door and found a big furry stripy tiger. The tiger said he was very hungry and asked to have tea. Sophie's mummy said he could come in. The tiger sat at the table and ate all the sandwiches, buns, biscuits, and cake. Then he drank all the milk and tea. After that, he looked around and ate the supper in the saucepans, the food in the fridge, and the packets and tins in the cupboard. He also drank all the orange juice, daddy's beer, and the water in the tap. Sophie could not have her bath because there was no water. When daddy came home, Sophie and her mummy told him what had happened. Daddy said they should go to a cafe. They put on their coats, walked out in the dark, and ate supper with sausages, chips, and ice cream. They also bought a big tin of Tiger food, but the tiger never came back.

summary_text: A little old lady lived all by herself in a small house with a table, chairs, and a jug on the shelf. She grumbled that there was not enough room.
