video_title: The Highway Rat  [Children's story | Read Aloud]
summary_text: The Highway Rat rode along the highway and stole food from travelers. He stopped a rabbit and took her clover. Then he stopped a squirrel and took his sack of nuts. Next he stopped some ants and took their green leaf. The animals grew thinner, but the Highway Rat grew very fat from eating their food. One day a duck met him on the road. The Rat said he wanted to eat her, but the duck said her sister had tasty food in a cave on the hill. The Rat followed her. When they reached the cave, the duck called out to her sister. The Rat heard a voice promising cakes and chocolates, so he ran into the cave. While he was inside, the duck took his horse and rode away. She returned to her friends, and they shared the food and had a happy feast. The Rat found his way out later and did not rob again. He got a job in a cake shop and swept the floor.

video_title: Greta and the Giants [Children's story | Read Aloud]
summary_text: Greta lived in a beautiful forest. One morning she found many forest animals hiding in the garden. A wolf asked her for help because the giants were breaking the forest and ruining their home. The giants kept chopping down trees to build bigger houses, towns, cities, factories, shops, cars, and planes. Soon there was hardly any forest left, and the animals were scared and had nowhere to go. Greta wanted to help, so the next morning she went to the middle of the forest and held a sign that said, “stop!” At first the giants walked past her. On the fourth day, a little boy joined Greta, and then more people and animals came too. They made a huge crowd and stopped the giants. Greta told them the forest was being damaged and the animals were homeless. Everyone shouted for the giants to stop. The giants were sorry, and after that they slowed down, planted gardens, and helped care for the forest until it became beautiful again.

video_title: Little Red Riding Hood [Children's story | Read Aloud]
summary_text: Little Red Riding Hood was a little girl who loved red clothes. One morning, her mother packed a basket of fresh fruit and asked her to take it to Granny, who was feeling poorly. The wolf asked what she was doing, and Little Red told him about the fruit. He said she should pick flowers for Granny, so Little Red stopped to gather daisies. While she did that, the wolf ran to Granny’s house. He knocked and tried to trick Granny, but Granny saw he was not Little Red and shut the door on his nose. Granny ran for help. The wolf jumped at her, but Granny and a woodcutter burst in and chased him away. Little Red gave Granny the fruit, and they all had breakfast.

video_title: The Not-So-Friendly Friend [Children's story | Read Aloud]
summary_text: A girl was new at school. She wanted to make good friends, so she used the golden rule and treated her classmates the way she liked to be treated. She was helpful, loving, fair, and kind. She shared, took turns, solved problems with words, and gave sweet hugs. Most children liked her, but one kid did not. This kid teased her and acted rude. The girl tried to be a friend, but the teasing made her feel sad. She saw that this was not a true friend, because a friend should not make someone feel small. So she made a boundary. She said she would play if the kid was kind, but if not, she would play with other true friends. She also said the kid could join again when they were ready to be nice. She learned to stand up for herself, stay respectful, and ask a trusted adult for help when needed.

Tomorrow was another day for surfing and fun.

video_title: Pumpkin Soup by Helen Cooper | Read Aloud Educational Picture Book for Children
summary_text: Deep in the woods, an old white cabin stands with pumpkins in the garden. Inside live a cat, a squirrel, and a duck. They make pumpkin soup together: the cat slices the pumpkin, the squirrel stirs, and the duck adds the salt. They eat the soup, play music, and sleep in a quilt made by all three. One morning, the duck wants to be the head cook. He takes the special spoon and says it is his turn to stir. The squirrel and the cat say no, and they fight. The duck is upset and leaves in a wheelbarrow. The cat and squirrel look for him, but they cannot find him. They feel sad and make the soup too salty. Then they search in the dark woods and near a steep cliff. At last they see light in the cabin and find the duck home. They cook soup again, and this time the duck stirs while they stay quiet. The duck teaches the squirrel to measure the salt, and the soup is good again.

summary_text: Deep in the jungle green, the biggest lion said, "Happy Earth Day." But the silliest monkey said, "It's not Earth Day. It's my birthday." Then the crocodile said it was Earth Day and asked everyone to pick up papers and put garbage in a bag. Monkey still said it was his birthday. Next, the giraffe told the animals to recycle bottles, glasses, and cans. Monkey kept saying, "It's not Earth Day. It's my birthday." The hippo asked them to use cloth bags at the store. At the end, monkey whispered to the lion, and the lion said he had made a mistake because his mom had brought a birthday cake for him. Monkey blew out the candles, and all the animals cheered for monkey's birthday and Earth Day.

Finally, Jasper threw it in the toilet. After that, he studied on his own, got a C+, and felt free. The crayon floated away, and then Elliot Pelican found it.

video_title: Love Splat Read Aloud
summary_text: Splat looked in the bathroom mirror on Valentine’s Day and tried to make himself look just right. He had made cards for everyone in his class, and he made a special card for kitten, the cat he liked best. Kitten had snowy white paws and pea green eyes, but every time she saw Splat, she pulled his ears, poked his belly, tied his tail, called him smelly, and ran away. Splat felt sad and kept asking, “Why does she do that?” At school, the class traded Valentine’s cards. Splat carried his little red envelope for kitten, but he was nervous. On the way, he bumped into kitten, and she acted the same way again. Later, Spike saw Splat’s card and showed off his own. Splat threw his card away. But kitten found it in the trash and read, “I like you!” She smiled, sat beside Splat, and gave him a pink envelope with a card that said, “I like you!”

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud | I Love My Curly Hair
summary_text: The girl looks at the other girls at school and sees their long, smooth, straight hair. Her own hair is different. It bounces, twists, and curls. She learns that she got her curly hair from her mom and dad. Sometimes her mom helps her use a comb pick and asks if she wants her hair big or slick. The girl can wear it in many ways, like braided, in a ponytail, or down and bushy. Sometimes she wishes her hair were straight like the other girls, and sometimes other children make fun of her or touch her hair without asking. Then she remembers that her hair makes her unique. She starts to like her curly hair. She wears it for ballet, lets it flow when she rides her bike, and uses gel or cream to smooth frizz. She plays outside, washes her hair with shampoo, bubbles, and water, and feels proud and confident.

video_title: Who Stole MINNIE's Brownies?! | Disney Bedtime Story Read Aloud
summary_text: Minnie Mouse baked a whole batch of butterscotch brownies for Daisy Duck’s party. She put them in tinfoil and carried them in a pink shopping bag to Daisy’s house. At the party, Minnie danced with Mickey Mouse and forgot about the bag. When she remembered, the bag was empty. The brownies were gone, and only crumbs and foil were left. Minnie asked Daisy, Donald Duck, Mickey, and Goofy if they had taken them, but each said no. Goofy had bandages on both thumbs, so he could not have opened the package. Donald said he had smelled the brownies and peeked at them, but he said he did not eat them. Minnie and her friends searched the kitchen and found footprints. The trail led upstairs to Daisy’s bedroom and stopped under Daisy’s bed. Mickey looked under the bed and found Pluto with crumbs on his mouth. Minnie saw that Pluto was the butterscotch brownie thief and said he already had a tummy ache.

summary_text: Rapunzel was alone in the tower with her friend Pascal while Gothal was away. She brushed her hair, painted a new mural, and read her three books. When it got dark, she looked out the window and saw the Moon. It looked like a giant bowl of marmalade, and birds flew across it and made a spooky shape. Rapunzel decided to make a new holiday called marmalade moonight. First, she tried to carve a watermelon into a lantern, but it rolled off the table and broke. Then she played a game with peaches in a tub of water. Pascal used his tongue to pick one up, but Rapunzel could not. She fell into the tub, and the peaches spilled out. After that, she dressed like a ghost and scared Pascal, but then she scared herself when he hid. Rapunzel said sorry and made a witch costume for herself and cat ears for Pascal. At the end, they shared sweet treats together in the tower.

summary_text: Ariel was a young mermaid who loved the ocean. She played hide and seek with her sisters, then swam past the coral reef to look for more places. King Triton saw her and told her not to go beyond the kingdom. He showed her a hungry barracuda and said the ocean could be dangerous. Soon a storm came, so Ariel and her father hurried back to the castle. After the storm, Ariel saw a ship sink in the water. The next day, she swam to the shipwreck with Flounder. She found treasures like a glove, a brush, a mirror, earrings, and a music box. The music box played a song. Sharks came, and Ariel used a rope and life preserver to lift them away. Then Koba, a big shark, chased her. The music from the box put Koba in a trance, and Ariel escaped. Later, Ursula used the music box to control Koba and take Triton’s Trident. Ariel used her mirror to stop Ursula, and Koba broke the box. Ariel returned the Trident, and peace came back.

video_title: ENCANTO: "Antonio's AMAZING Gift!" | Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: Antonio Madrical lived in Casita, a magical house. On his fifth birthday, it was also his gift day. His family gathered at his new bedroom door to see what gift he would get. When Antonio touched the doorknob, a friendly toucan appeared on his arm. This was his gift: he could talk with animals. Abuela Amma hugged him and said she knew he could do it. Antonio’s new room was an endless rainforest. Animals showed him around. He watched sotus run and swing in the trees. A macaw flew with him for a look at the room from above. He even ate a snack with the jikitos. Antonio, who had been shy, began to come out of his shell. He played with his new friends, and they liked being with him. Later, his family came to his room to celebrate. Louisa brought a huge plate of cucatas. Julieta brought repus, and the macaws helped themselves. The family danced, and Antonio fell asleep in his new room with his animal friends.

summary_text: In Santa Cecilia, the Rivera family gets ready for Dia de los Muertos. They make an ofrenda with photos, keepsakes, and food for their family members who have died. He sees Dante and Papita, but they cannot stay in the kitchen. Abuelita is making food for the ofrenda, and Miguel asks what she will make for Papa Hector. Abuelita does not know, so Miguel asks Dante and Papita for help. The two spirit guides take Miguel’s note to Mama Koko and Papa Hector in the land of the dead. Papa Hector writes down his favorite dishes and sends the note back. Miguel gives the list to Abuelita, and she cooks the food in time. That night, the Rivera ancestors cross the bridge and follow the marigold path home. The living and the dead celebrate together, and Miguel plays his guitar while Dante and Papita eat tamales.

The otters have a big family hug, and then everyone hugs Dory, too.

summary_text: It was Queen Anna’s birthday, and the ants on Ant Island brought her many gifts like berries, pine cones, seeds, and grain. Flick did not have a gift yet. But when a door dropped down, he found a sleeping boy in a dark bedroom. Mike tried another door and found another sleeping child. He kept trying, but every child was asleep, so he could not collect any laughs. At the end of the day, Mike felt upset and went home. Celia called him, and he told her work was terrible. They told him they had played a joke by changing his clock, so the children were asleep. Mike realized he had been working so hard that he forgot to have fun. He laughed with his friends, and everyone at Monsters Inc. laughed too.

video_title: Bedtime Stories: Disney Pixar's #ToyStory
summary_text: Andy loved his toys, especially Woody, but he did not know that the toys came alive when people were not watching. On Andy’s birthday, he got a new toy named Buzz Lightyear. When Andy went to Pizza Planet, his mom said he could bring only one toy. Woody tried to move Buzz aside, but Buzz fell out the bedroom window. Later, Buzz joined them in the car, and he and Woody fought. At a gas station they fell out and were left behind. The two toys followed a Pizza Planet truck, got trapped at Pizza Planet, and were captured by Sid, Andy’s mean neighbor. Sid planned to blow Buzz up with a rocket, but Woody and the mutant toys scared Sid away. In the end, Buzz learned he was a toy, he and Woody became friends, and they flew back to Andy’s car just as the moving van was leaving.

summary_text: Wally was a robot who worked on Earth. He packed up trash all day, and he felt very lonely. One day, while he was sorting trash, he found a small plant. That night, another robot came to Earth. Her name was Eve. Wally liked Eve right away and took her to his home. He showed her his treasures and then showed her the plant. Eve took the plant, put it in her chest, and shut down. Later, Eve was taken back to her ship, and Wally went after her. He followed her to the big ship called the Axiom. The captain saw Earth was still full of trash, but Eve saw Wally caring for her. At the end, the ship returned to Earth, Eve fixed Wally, and the robots and humans stayed together on their new home.

Mommy Pig told them to wash their faces because Granny Pig wanted to tuck them in. In bed, Peppa asked for Teddy and George asked for Dinosaur, so Granny Pig found them and tucked everyone in. Peppa and George still were not sleepy, so they asked for a bedtime story. Granny Pig told a story about Princess Peppa and Sir George, but Grandpa Pig and then Daddy Pig tried to finish it, and the story kept going into a party. At last Mommy Pig took over, and Peppa whispered the story softly until she and George fell asleep. Then the grown-ups fell asleep too.

video_title: Town mouse and country mouse. Children’s bedtime story read aloud in an English accent.
summary_text: Pippen was a little brown country mouse who lived in a house in a hedge. In spring, he listened to birds sing, and in summer, he ate wild strawberries and cut grass for his winter bed. One cold day, his cousin Toby Town Mouse came to stay. Pippen gave Toby soft moss to sit on and took him to smell the flowers, but Toby said the seat was too damp and sneezed at the flowers. That night, Toby did not like Pippen’s nuts and berries and said the country was horrible. The next day, Toby took Pippen to the town on a train. In town, Pippen saw tall buildings, noisy streets, and busy cars. Toby showed him his house under the floor, and they ate a feast in the dining room. Then a cat came, and the mice ran away. Pippen wanted to go home. At last, he returned to his hedge and slept in his warm hay bed.

video_title: Monsters Love Underpants | A Bedtime Story read aloud in British Accent
summary_text: Monsters love to creep around and look scary, but they love underpants even more. They like pants of all kinds, with patterns, shapes, and styles. Some monsters walk through dingy dungeons and find squeaky armor pants. Some come from a steamy swamp and fill pants with gooey slime, but the pants get slippery and slide down. Wild mountain monsters grab frozen pants and run away in the night. Sea monsters wear pants with jewels from treasure chests on a pirate ship at the bottom of the ocean. Spiky space monsters wave and roar when bright bloomers float out from deep space. One monster has pants that are too small and wishes they were scratchy. On Saturday night, the monsters meet in a secret cave for a disco rave and dance the monster bop. When someone shouts, “Stop!”, they hurry home before daylight so no one will see them. The story ends by warning that a monster might be under your bed trying on snazzy pants.

video_title: Jack and the Beanstalk. Ladybird read it yourself book read aloud in an English accent.
summary_text: Jack and his mother were very poor, and they had only one cow. Jack’s mother told him to sell the cow and bring back the money. On the way, Jack met a man who had no money, but he offered Jack five magic beans for the cow. Jack took the beans home, but his mother was angry and threw them out of the window. The next day, Jack saw a giant bean stalk growing up to the sky. He climbed it and found a giant castle. A giant woman hid him in a cupboard when her giant husband came home. The giant counted his money and fell asleep. Jack took the money and climbed down to his mother. Jack climbed the bean stalk two more times. Each time, the giant brought something special: a Magic Hen that laid golden eggs, and then a magic Harp that played music. Jack took them too. At last, Jack ran down the bean stalk, his mother cut it down, and the giant was gone. Jack and his mother were no longer poor.

video_title: Can Kristoff Fix the Magical Crystal?! Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: Kristoff and Sven were visiting the trolls and helping harvest mushrooms. After a long day, they sat by the campfire with Boulda and the other trolls. Then Boulda saw that her favorite crystal was going dark. She said Grandpy had given it to her, and she needed to recharge it before the northern lights faded. Kristoff said he and Sven would fix it. In the morning, they went to Arendelle and found Anna, Elsa, and Olaf in the library. Elsa read a book that said crystals could be re-energized where lights wake the sky, where sky touches the earth, and where waters run long. The friends went on a long trip to Oplating Mountain. They climbed cliffs, walked along the fjord, and camped for the night. When the northern lights appeared, they saw glowing colors inside the rocks. They tried to reach the crystals, and Anna touched Boulda’s dark crystal to one in the rock. It glowed again, but the next morning it faded. Back in Troll Valley, Anna placed the crystal in Boulda’s hands, and it glowed brightly again. Boulda said they had worked together, and Kristoff said they did it because she was family too.

Anna looked out the window and saw three children building a toboggan in the snow. Kristoff then told Anna that when he was a child, he did not have many friends, and he had never been able to join the ice games because only humans were allowed and a team needed three people. Anna felt sorry for him and told Elsa. Elsa was glad when Anna suggested that the three of them form a team and take Kristoff to the games. They packed quickly and traveled to the glacier for the ice games. There, Elsa promised not to use her magic. She won the first contest by carving an ice statue with a hammer and chisel. Anna and Kristoff later entered couples ice skating and came in third place. The next day, the three of them raced in the big toboggan event, but the children from Arendelle won. Kristoff said it was still good because he finally got to compete and had friends he could count on.

video_title: Walt Disney's FROZEN! Babysitting the Troll Tots - 5 Minute Read Along Bedtime Stories
summary_text: Anna, Kristoff, and Sven babysat the troll toddlers while Boulda and grandpappy went to a magical prophesying convention. The grown trolls told old stories, then left the little trolls with berries, leaf changes, and bedtime plans. But the troll toddlers escaped and ran, climbed, and swung everywhere. Anna and Kristoff tried to help them calm down, but the toddlers stayed wild. Anna gave berries, Kristoff checked their leaves, and they still would not sleep. Then Olaf came to help. Anna fell into the berry basket, and the toddlers licked the purple berry juice from her face. After that, the toddlers ate, got clean, and felt sleepy. Olaf talked about summer, and Anna asked Kristoff and Sven to sing a lullaby instead. Kristoff played his lute and sang a soft song. Soon the troll toddlers fell asleep. When Boulda and grandpappy came back, they saw the babies sleeping and said Anna and Kristoff did a great job.

video_title: 5 Minute Read Along Bedtime Stories: Walt Disney's FROZEN! Elsa's Gift

Elsa was happy because her ice magic was under control and the Kingdom's Gates were open. Anna pulled Elsa away so they could finish getting ready. Elsa worked on the banquet room, then wanted to make something special for Anna. With Olaf's help, she went to the kitchen to make cookies. Anna came to the door, but Elsa told her not to come in so the surprise would stay hidden. Elsa and Olaf made the cookies, and Elsa also made Anna's favorite punch. When Anna came back again, Elsa asked her to leave. Kristoff saw Anna was upset and told Elsa that Anna really wanted time with her sister. Elsa went to Anna in the snowy courtyard, and they had a big snowball fight. After that, they got ready for the ball. At the party, Anna saw the cookies, punch, and ice sculpture. Elsa said she made them for her, and Anna said the best gift was being with Elsa. The sisters went to enjoy the party together.

video_title: MOANA The Ocean Chooses a 3-Year Old | Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: Grandma Tala tells the children about Maui, the Heart of te fiti, and the danger beyond the reef. Tui, Moana’s father and the village chief, comes in and says no one should go outside the reef. The children get scared when monster pictures fall down, but Moana watches the ocean with wonder. She slips away to the beach and sees a baby sea turtle blocked by birds. Moana uses a palm frond to help the turtle reach the water. Then the ocean opens a path for her and gives her shells to follow. Deep in the water, she finds a glowing green spiral stone. Tui sees Moana near the water and carries her back to the shore. He tells her the sea is dangerous and says she is the next great chief. Later, Grandma Tala quietly picks up the stone and keeps it safe for Moana.

She says someone will one day go beyond the reef, find Maui, and return the Heart to save everyone. Tui, the village chief and Moana’s father, stops the story and says no one should go outside the reef because it is safe inside. There she helps a baby sea turtle cross the sand by holding a palm frond over it until it reaches the water. After that, the ocean parts and leads her to a trail of shells. Deep in the lagoon, the ocean gives her a glowing green spiral stone. Tui finds her, takes her back to shore, and tells her she is the next great chief, but she must learn where she belongs. Grandma Tala later picks up the stone and keeps it. Moana then spends time with her parents, learns about sharing, and watches the village before hearing the waves call her again.

video_title: MOANA The Missing Boat | Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: Moana leaps onto the giant crab Tamatoa and takes back Maui’s fish hook. She gives it to Maui and tells him to run. Moana also shows him the True Heart of te fiti, then tricks Tamatoa by swapping the heart with a rock and rolling the rock into the crevice. Tamatoa gets angry and crashes through the wall, which opens a way out. Outside, Maui turns into a fish and then back into a human, and Moana keeps helping him as they escape. A geyser shoots them up into the air, and Tamatoa falls upside down while his treasures spill out. The sea monsters rush in and take the treasure. Moana and Maui return safely near Spire Island. Maui thanks Moana, but Moana sees that their boat is gone because Hey Hey pecked the rope and let it drift away. Moana gets upset, then sees the island is dark and dead. She tells Maui her island is dying and she must restore the heart. A broken kamakura boat drifts by, and Moana says they can use it to get her boat. She encourages Maui, and he gets ready to help her.

video_title: MOANA Story of the Greedy Fisherman | Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: In a village lived three siblings: Taotai, Lalalagi, and Masina. Taotai had their father’s fishing boat and went out on the lagoons to fish. Lalalagi and Masina kept the house neat and helped him, but Taotai became resentful. He decided not to share his fish. He caught only a few fish for himself, slept in the boat, and brought little home. Lalalagi and Masina were left hungry. After many days, Lalalagi asked to go with him and learn to fish, but Taotai refused and said the boat was his. The villagers saw how he treated his siblings. An elder told him to share, but he laughed. Then the villagers shared food with Lalalagi and Masina. The two siblings worked with an elderly neighbor in his taro fields and learned to plant taro. They also made a net and caught birds for food. Later, storms kept Taotai from fishing. Lalalagi and Masina shared their food with him, and Taotai promised to teach them to fish when the storms ended. After that, they shared food and lived happily.

summary_text: In a village lived three siblings: Taotai, Lalalagi, and Masina. Taotai had their father’s fishing boat and went out on the lagoons every day. Lalalagi and Masina kept the house neat, but Taotai became resentful and refused to share his fish. He often came home with only a few fish and said he needed them all for himself. The younger brother and sister went hungry, but they did not fight with him. Later, Lalalagi asked to go fishing too, but Taotai said no. The villagers saw how badly he treated his family and shared food with Lalalagi and Masina instead. The siblings worked hard for a kind neighbor in his taro fields and learned to grow taro. They also made a net to catch birds and shared bird meat with the neighbor. When storms stopped the fishing, Taotai had no food. He got sick after eating an unripe sweet potato. Lalalagi and Masina made him soup and shared their food with him. Taotai felt ashamed and promised to teach them fishing after the storms. Then the three siblings lived together in harmony.

video_title: MOANA Her First Leadership Test! | Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: At dawn, Tui wakes Moana and tells her the Village Council will happen today. Then he says she will lead it. Moana feels happy because she wants to show she can be a good chief. Her mother, Cena, helps her get dressed in a special red and yellow dress and puts a headdress on her head. Moana also greets Pua, her pig, before going to the council house. The drums beat, and the people gather on their mats. Tui gives Moana the battle ax, and she begins to speak. A villager asks about Hey Hey the rooster, and Moana answers. Then a farmer shows rotted taro roots, and Moana says they should separate the bad crops and find a new field. Next, a fisherman says there are fewer fish in the lagoon. Moana looks at the map and says they should fish beyond the reef. Tui says no one goes beyond the reef, and he gets angry. Moana is upset and leaves the council house.

video_title: MOANA The Story of the Kakamora | Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: One day, the kakamura appeared on the horizon in strange canoes covered with mist. At first, voyagers only saw their boats in the distance. When people got closer, they saw the tiny kakamura jumping around on decks made from many found objects. The creatures wore coconut shells on their bodies and painted faces on the shells. They often argued, stole shells, and played tricks on one another, so the men liked watching them. Then the kakamura attacked. They hid their canoe in thick fog and came close without being noticed. Their boat split into many boats and surrounded the voyagers. Spears fell on the men’s canoe, drums sounded loudly, and kakamura warriors jumped aboard with sharp claws and scary faces. They took the treasures and left the boat broken. The voyagers went home shaken and warned others, but later travelers were also attacked.

video_title: The Haunted House (1981 Disney Fisher-Price Read-Along)
summary_text: One night Mickey, Donald, and Pluto drove on a dark road in the woods. Their old car stopped because it ran out of gas. Mickey and Donald walked to find help and saw a spooky old house. They went to the house, and Pluto saw three shadows in a window. The door opened by itself, and they went inside. A painting made a wall spin around, and Mickey, Donald, and Pluto fell into a secret passage. There they saw three ghosts. Pluto found a door in the floor, and they fell into a basket. summary_text: The book begins with a talking owl telling the reader not to turn the page. The owl says the first page was opened by accident and asks again and again for the reader to stop. When the reader turns more pages, the owl gets upset and says it will tell the reader’s parents. It even asks for punishment and says no dinner and no books. The reader keeps turning pages anyway, so the owl cries and says it will do anything, even give gold or a flying car. At the end, the owl says a terrible witch will turn it into a frog if the last page is reached, and it thanks the reader when the end is finally opened.

They decorated Little Tree, put Tiny Star on top, and Santa came. Santa said Little Tree was the most beautiful Christmas tree in the forest and left the forest animals’ presents under it.

summary_text: One sunny summer afternoon, Dora and Boots were exploring the farm when they heard Mommy Pig calling for help. Mommy Pig said her three little piggies were missing. Dora, Boots, and Mommy Pig went to the barn, but the door closed and they had to find another way in. They crossed the duck pond by finding the key in a nest with four eggs, then unlocked the gate and crossed the bridge. Next, they followed piggy footprints at a fork in the path and reached the corn maze. A scarecrow told them to take the amarillo, or yellow, path. They followed it to the barn, stopped Swiper when he tried to swipe, and then found all three piggies inside. Mommy Pig hugged her babies, and the piggies gave Dora and Boots apples to say thank you.

summary_text: Peter Clinton came to the Brown Detective Agency and asked Encyclopedia to help him. Peter had a chance to trade his bicycle for a Civil War sword, but he wanted to know if the sword was real and if it really belonged to Stonewall Jackson. Encyclopedia agreed to take the case and went with Peter to the Tigers Clubhouse behind Mr. Sweeney’s auto body shop. There, Bugs Meanie showed the sword and said it had belonged to General Jackson. Encyclopedia read the words on the blade and learned that the sword was presented to Thomas J. Jackson by his men after the First Battle of Bull Run in 1861. Bugs tried to make the trade sound important, but Encyclopedia said the sword did not belong to General Stonewall Jackson. Peter then knew he should not trade his bicycle for it.

summary_text: One bright day, Jim pansy woke up and thought everything was wrong. The sun was too bright, the sky was too blue, and the bananas were too sweet. Norman said it was a wonderful day to be grumpy, and Jim felt a little better.

video_title: We don't eat our classmates, animated#readaloud #bedtimestories #storytime #kindergarten #toddlers
summary_text: Penelope Rex was a little T-Rex who felt nervous about starting school. Her mom bought her a backpack with ponies on it, and her dad packed 300 tuna sandwiches and apple juice in a pony lunchbox. On the first day, Penelope saw that all her classmates were children, and she ate them because she thought children were delicious. Mrs. Noodleman told her, “We don’t eat our classmates,” and made the children come back. Penelope tried to be friendly, but the other children stayed away from her because they were scared. At home, her dad asked if she had eaten her classmates. Penelope said she had, and her dad told her that children are the same on the inside and that friends should not be eaten. The next day, Penelope ate more classmates until everyone ran away. Then she met Walter the goldfish. After Walter tried to bite her finger, Penelope learned what it felt like to be a snack. She stopped eating children, and after that she played, ate lunch, and made friends.

summary_text: One morning Bella woke up to Bob crawling in her room and licking her jewelry, so she shouted, “Get out of my room!” That began her “no no no” day. Later, Bella got upset when her cookie broke, would not let Sasha and Bob play princesses, and was grumpy at ballet class, where Mrs Clark and Miss Louisa could not practice. On the way home, Bella lay on the sidewalk and shouted. At supper, bath time, and tea time, she did not like the peas, the cold bath, or the toothpaste, and she kept throwing things. At bedtime she rolled around and said, “No bed!” But after a story with Mommy, Bella grew tired, said sorry, and went to sleep.

After that, Hao puts honey on Bruce, and bees chase him and sting his bottom. Bruce falls down a hill, and his basket tumbles after him. Bruce says spring stinks because of all these bad things. At the end, Hao shows Bruce her new friend, a skunk, and Bruce says the skunk stinks too.

summary_text: On a rainy day, the little princess paints a picture of her family. She paints her dad the king, her mom in a purple dress, and herself in the middle holding their hands. She has a crown too. While she paints, she uses a glass of water for cleaning her brushes, but she knocks it over by mistake. Blue paint spills everywhere, and the picture becomes a messy blur of colors. The maid cleans up the mess and says everything is okay. The princess wants her mom, but it is the maid beside her. Then her mom looks at the wet picture and says it is wonderful because it looks like a rainy day. She hangs it up. Later, when the rain stops, the princess goes outside to play on the seesaw. She hurts her knee and her teddy bear flies away. She goes to the doctor, who puts smelly medicine on her knee and bandages it. The princess cries for her mom while she waits to get better.

Her mom gives her a backpack with ponies on it, and her dad packs 300 tuna sandwiches and apple juice in a pony lunchbox.
On the first day, Penelope is surprised to see that her classmates are children.
She eats them because she thinks children are delicious.
Mrs.
Noodleman tells her, “We don’t eat our classmates!” and makes Penelope spit them out.
Penelope feels sad because her classmates are dirty, scared, and do not want to play with her.
At home, her dad asks if she ate her classmates and tells her that children are the same on the inside, but they should not be eaten.
The next day Penelope tries again, but she keeps eating classmates until they run away from her.
Then she meets Walter the goldfish and asks him to be her friend.
After she learns what it feels like to be someone’s snack, she stops eating children.
Penelope and the other children play together, have lunch together, and become friends.

video_title: My Teacher Is a Monster Read Aloud | Funny Kids' Story Time | Preschool kindergarten by Peter Brown
summary_text: Bobby had a big problem at school. His teacher, Miss Kirby, seemed like a monster to him. Bobby threw a paper airplane in class, and the other children saw him. Miss Kirby stomped, roared, and called him Robert, which was Bobby’s long name. Bobby spent his free time in the park, trying to forget school. One Saturday, he found Miss Kirby in the park wearing a hat. He wanted to hide, but he said hello. A wind blew her hat away, and Bobby jumped and caught it before it fell in the water. Then they sat by the ducks and quacked with them. Miss Kirby changed more and more as they spent time together. Bobby took her to his favorite spot on the rocks, and she gave him paper to make a paper airplane. Bobby flew it outside, and it soared high. By lunchtime, Miss Kirby looked normal again. Bobby was not scared anymore, and they said goodbye until Monday.

video_title: Dragons love tacos read aloud, learn to read- #bedtimestories #storytime #toddlers
summary_text: A boy finds dragons in his room and counts many of them. The dragons are on the dresser, the bookcase, the bed, the floor, the lamp, and in the sky. The boy and the dragons talk about why dragons love tacos. They look at taco ingredients like peppers, tomatoes, onions, cheese, beef, beans, tortillas, lettuce, and salsa. The dragons say they like tacos, but they hate spicy salsa. The boy reads a book about keeping salsa mild. The dragons also dress up for parties, go to pool parties, and dance with accordion music. The boy makes many tacos so there will be enough for a big taco party. Dragons come to Robbie’s house for the party and eat the tacos. Then they find spicy jalapeno salsa, and the dragons breathe fire. The fire burns the house. After that, the dragons help Robbie rebuild the house, and they celebrate with more non-spicy tacos.

video_title: OFFICER BUCKLE AND GLORIA - Caldecott Medal Book by Peggy Rathmann | Read-Aloud
summary_text: Officer Buckle knew many safety tips in Naville. He wrote them on his bulletin board and shared them at Naville School, but the children did not listen. Sometimes they even snored. Then the police department got a dog named Gloria. Gloria went with Officer Buckle to school, and he showed that she obeyed his commands. When he gave safety tips, the children began to watch Gloria and listen to him. They laughed, clapped, and cheered. Officer Buckle was surprised, and after that speech there were no accidents. The next day the students sent him a big envelope full of thank-you letters with drawings of Gloria. One letter from Claire said that he and Gloria made a good team. Soon many schools called and asked Officer Buckle to come with Gloria. He gave speeches at 313 schools, and children listened each time.

video_title: OFFICER BUCKLE AND GLORIA - Caldecott Medal Book by Peggy Rathmann | Read-Aloud
summary_text: Officer Buckle knew more safety tips than anyone in Naville, and he kept each new one on his bulletin board. He gave safety speeches at Naville School, but the students never listened, and sometimes they even snored. That changed when the police department bought a police dog named Gloria. Gloria went with Officer Buckle to the school, and when he said, “Gloria sit!” she sat down. The children became interested as Officer Buckle shared tips like keeping shoelaces tied, wiping up spills, and never leaving a thumbtack where someone might sit on it. They laughed, clapped, and cheered, and there were no accidents after the speech. The next day the police station received many thank-you letters, including one from Claire. Soon other schools asked Officer Buckle and Gloria to come speak, and they visited 313 schools. Later, after a television appearance, Officer Buckle stopped giving speeches when he thought no one listened to him. When Gloria came alone to Naville School, everyone fell asleep. Afterward, the school had a terrible accident with banana pudding, and the students sent more letters. Claire wrote again, saying Gloria missed him. Officer Buckle then learned his best safety tip: always stick with your buddy.

video_title: Mr. Willowby's Christmas Tree - by Robert Barry | Read-Aloud
summary_text: Mr. Willowby got a big, green Christmas tree by special delivery. He wanted it in the parlor corner, but it was so tall that it bent into the ceiling. Baxter the butler cut off the top. Mr. Willowby was happy and began trimming the tree. Baxter gave the top to Miss Adelaide, who liked it but cut off the top again. The little treetop was left outside, and Timm the gardener took it home. His wife thought their house was too small, so she cut off the top too. Barnaby Bear found it next and brought it home for Mama Bear. Little Bear said it would not hold a star, so Mama Bear cut off the top again. Later, Frisky Fox found the tree top, took it home, and then Benjamin Rabbit found it outside the fox den. Benjamin and his family celebrated around it, but Mrs. Rabbit saw it was too tall and cut off the top. At last, Mistletoe Mouse found the smallest piece and took it home. Mrs. Mouse put a cheese star on top, and it was just right.

video_title: THE TRUTH ABOUT DRAGONS - written by Julie Leung & illustrated by Hanna Cha | Read-Aloud
summary_text: A child sets out on an epic quest to learn the truth about dragons. The child puts on a favorite cloak and sturdy boots and goes into a deep forest on a crisp day. The child follows a brook past gnarled groves, crunchy oak leaves, and tall trees. The child must be careful of hob goblins under mossy bridges and glowing Willow the Wisps that try to lead travelers away. The child finds a yellow cottage in a swamp and meets a wise woman. She serves a warm drink and says dragons are fearsome, fire breathing, and live deep underground with treasure. Then the child travels to another forest with green bamboo and misty mountains. The child follows nine-tailed fox footprints and, if lost, can ask the white rabbit on the moon for help. The child reaches an airy palace and another wise woman says dragons are majestic, live in the sky and rivers, and can bring rain and floods. In the end, the child learns both truths about dragons and that both journeys can be taken.

video_title: IN NOVEMBER - by Cynthia Rylant & illustrated by Jill Kastner | Read-Aloud
summary_text: In November, the Earth grows quiet and makes a white winter bed for flowers and small creatures. The trees stand bare like sticks and bones, with no leaves, and they stay still. Some birds fly away, and some birds stay. The birds that leave have long journeys ahead, and the birds that stay must get ready for cold days and save every berry they can. Animals sleep more because the air is chilly. Cats huddle in barns, mice pile up under logs, bees hide in deep holes, and dogs lie near the fire. November food smells like squash, pumpkin, and cinnamon. People carry pies to each other’s homes, sit by crackling wood stoves, and drink cider. On a special November day, they travel far to share a meal and give thanks. At Winter’s Gate, the stars are sharp, the sun appears only sometimes, and the world waits quietly for spring.

video_title: Leaf Man - by Lois Ehlert | Read-Aloud (Daytime & Bedtime Versions)
summary_text: Leaf Man used to live near the speaker in a pile of leaves. One day, the wind blew him away. The speaker last saw Leaf Man going east, past the chickens, toward the marsh, and over the ducks and geese. Then he blew over fields of pumpkins and winter squash and flew past the turkey, potatoes, carrots, and cabbages. After that, he went out of sight. The speaker wonders if Leaf Man is now drifting west over orchards or prairie meadows, or maybe moving along a lake, river, or mountains. The story says a leaf man must go where the wind blows. No one knows where Leaf Man will land, because only the wind knows. The story ends by telling the listener to listen for a rustle in the leaves, because Leaf Man may be waiting to go home with you.

video_title: TOO MANY PUMPKINS - by Linda White & illustrated by Megan Lloyd | Read-Aloud
summary_text: Every spring, Rebecca Estelle planted carrots, beans, tomatoes, peas, corn, and rudabagas, but never pumpkins. When she was a girl, her family had been very poor, and she had eaten pumpkins for a whole month. After that, she never wanted to see a pumpkin again. One autumn day, a pumpkin fell from a truck and smashed in her yard. Rebecca Estelle covered it with dirt and tried to forget it. But in spring, pumpkin vines grew at the edge of her yard. She ignored them, cut them down, and shut her curtains, but the vines kept growing back. She stopped using the front door and did not look at the vines all spring and summer. Then, one autumn day, she saw that pumpkins had covered her whole yard. Rebecca Estelle decided to give them away. She made pumpkin pies and many pumpkin treats, carved jack-o-lanterns, and called the town to come. Everyone came, ate pumpkin food, and left with pumpkin gifts. Rebecca Estelle kept only a few seeds for next spring.

video_title: HALLOWEEN NIGHT - By Marjorie Dennis Murray & Illustrations by Brandon Dorman | Read-Aloud
summary_text: On Halloween night, many spooky creatures were busy in the house. Bats flew by the walls, spiders came out, and the witch stirred a brew by the fire. video_title: Pumpkin Soup - written and illustrated by Helen Cooper | Read-Aloud
summary_text: Deep in the woods, an old white cabin held three friends: a cat, a squirrel, and a duck. The cat sliced the pumpkin, the squirrel stirred the water, and the duck added the salt to make pumpkin soup. They ate the soup, played music, and slept in a quilt made by all three. One morning, the duck woke early and wanted to be the head cook. He took the squirrel’s spoon and said he should stir the soup. The squirrel and cat said no, and they all had a big fight. The duck packed a wheelbarrow and left. The cat and squirrel looked for him in the pumpkin patch and in the dark woods, but they could not find him. Their soup became too salty, and they cried. At last they found the duck back at the cabin. They cooked together again, and the duck stirred while the others let him help. The soup was good, and peace returned to the cabin.

video_title: Weslandia - By Paul Fleischman Illustrated by Kevin Hawkes | Read-Aloud
summary_text: Wesley was unhappy because he did not fit in with the other people in his town. He did not like pizza, soda, or football, and he refused to shave half his head like the other boys. He had no friends and was often chased by tormentors. One week at school, he learned that wind can carry seeds far and that each civilization has a staple food crop. After school ended, he decided to use that knowledge for a summer project. He planted a patch of ground in his yard and waited. The wind helped plant the seeds, and soon seedlings grew. The plants grew very tall and made fruit, juice, roots, and leaves that Wesley used for food and drink. He also made a hat, robe, oil, games, and a new way of counting. He named his land Weslandia. By the end of summer, Wesley had created his own civilization, and when he returned to school in September, he had many friends.

video_title: Bats at the Beach - By Best-Selling Author & Illustrator Brian Lies | Read-Aloud
summary_text: When the sun slips down, bats wake up and fly out of their barn, cave, and rafter. They call to each other and say the moon is perfect for bats at the beach. Soon they pack buckets, towels, blankets, books, and other things, then fly over the dark trees to the ocean. They land on warm sand and set up their blankets. The bats play games, bury friends in sand, make sand caves, and race on the waves. At lunchtime, they eat beetles, ants, milkweed bugs, crickets, moths, and other bug treats. Later, their stomachs hurt, so they go to the snack bar for dessert. The old bats sing bat songs while the little bats rest. Then the sky turns purple and the sun begins to come up. The bats say goodbye, pack their things, and fly home before day. They curl up in their home and dream about the moon weather.

video_title: WHERE THE WILD THINGS ARE - Caldecott Medal Book by Maurice Sendak | Read-Aloud
summary_text: Max wore his wolf suit and made mischief. His mother called him a wild thing, and Max said, "I'll eat you up." So she sent him to bed without supper. In his room, a forest grew. The walls turned into the world, and an ocean came by with a private boat. Max sailed far away to where the wild things are. The wild things roared, gnashed their teeth, rolled their eyes, and showed their claws. Max said, "Be still," and looked into their yellow eyes without blinking. The wild things became afraid and made Max king. Max said, "Let the wild rumpus start!" Then he sent the wild things to bed without supper, and he felt lonely. He smelled good things to eat far away, so he gave up being king. The wild things asked him to stay, but Max said no. He sailed home through the night and found his supper waiting, still hot.

She changed the towels by cutting them, dusted the furniture with dusting powder, drew the drapes by making a picture, and put the lights out by taking out the bulbs. When the Rogers came home, they saw the strange results. Mrs. Rogers was angry and nearly fired Amelia Bedilia, but Mr. Rogers tasted the lemon mering pie and loved it. The Rogers decided to keep Amelia Bedilia, and Mrs. Rogers learned to say things more clearly.

video_title: Possum Magic - written by Mem Fox & illustrated by Julie Vivas | Read-Aloud
summary_text: Deep in the Australian bush, two possums lived together. Their names were Hush and Grandma Poss. Grandma Poss could do bush magic. She made wombats blue, cucuras pink, dingo smile, and emus shrink. Her best magic made Hush invisible so snakes could not see her. But one day Hush said she wanted to know what she looked like, so she asked Grandma Poss to make her visible again. Grandma Poss looked in all her magic books, but she could not find that spell. The next day, she remembered that the magic had something to do with food, so they left the bush and traveled across Australia. They ate many foods, but Hush stayed invisible. In Darwin they ate a Vegemite sandwich and Hush got a tail. In Perth, pavlova made her legs and body appear. In Tasmania, a lamington made her visible from head to tail. After that, Hush stayed visible, and once a year she ate those foods again to keep it that way.

video_title: HELLO LIGHTHOUSE - Caldecott Medal Book by Sophie Blackall | Read-Aloud
summary_text: On a tiny island at the edge of the world, a lighthouse stands on a high rock and sends its light to the sea. A new keeper arrives to take the place of the old one. He polishes the lens, fills the oil, trims the wick, winds the clockwork, paints the rooms, writes in the log book, and listens to the wind. He drinks tea, fishes for cod, and writes letters to his wife. Soon the tender brings supplies and his wife comes too. He shows her the round rooms, and they set the table for two. Then thick fog comes, and a bell rings to warn ships. One dark night, a boat crashes on the rocks, and the keeper pulls three sailors from the water and wraps them in blankets.

video_title: The Yellow Bus - by #1 New York Times Bestselling author Loren Long | Read-Aloud
summary_text: A bright yellow bus spent her days driving and carrying people from one important place to another. Every morning, children climbed in with pitter patter, giggle giggle, and patter sounds, and the bus felt happy. Then a new driver came and took the bus on unfamiliar roads. The children still climbed in with shuffle, clunk, and creak sounds, and the bus still carried them and felt joy. After a long time, another new person drove the yellow bus into the city, parked her in a quiet spot, and walked away. No one came for a while, and the bus stayed empty and still. One cold night, people climbed in and huddled together, making rustle and bump sounds. Later, the bus was taken by a truck across a bridge, through the country, and to a farm in a valley. There, more animals came in with clip clop and maaah sounds. Then the farmer gathered them and took them away. The farm became quiet. Soon the river rose, and then swimmers came in with swish and swoosh sounds, and they filled the yellow bus with joy.

At Easter, the Easter rabbit found Hoppy and praised his special work. Hoppy rode with him to hide the eggs for children to find.

video_title: The Emperor's New Clothes | Read-Along | 1977 Scholastic Record & Book | Vintage Children's Story
summary_text: An emperor loved new clothes and spent his money on them. Two men came to town and said they were weavers who could make cloth so special that only smart people and good workers could see it. The emperor believed them and gave them money, gold thread, silk thread, and a room in his palace. The men only pretended to weave. When the emperor sent his chief minister and then his second chief minister to look at the cloth, both men could not see anything, but they lied and said it was beautiful. At last the emperor went himself and also saw empty looms. He still pretended he could see the cloth and gave the men medals. The men later pretended to make a suit for the parade. On parade day, they dressed the emperor in invisible clothes. The people praised the suit until a little child said the emperor had nothing on. Then everyone shouted that he had nothing on, but the emperor kept walking in the parade.

summary_text: Mira lived in a gray city and loved to doodle, draw, color, and paint. When she saw blank paper, she thought, “Hmm… maybe.” She gave little gifts to people on her way to school, like an apple for Mr. Henry, a flower for Ms. Lopez, a songbird for Mr. Sax, and a red heart for the policemen. On the way home, she taped a glowing sun on a wall, and the city became a little less gray. The next day, Mira met a muralist with paintbrushes. He asked what she saw, and he said, “Maybe something beautiful.” He painted the wall, and Mira joined in with bright colors. Soon Mr. Sax and many others came to paint, dance, and make music. Even the policeman asked to paint too. They colored walls, benches, utility boxes, and sidewalks. At the end, everyone rested, and the artist said they were all artists and the world was their canvas.

video_title: All Ages Storytime: Juneteenth for Mazie
summary_text: Maisie wants to play outside, eat a cookie, and stay up late, but Dad keeps saying no because it is getting dark and bedtime is near. Maisie feels grumpy and tells Dad she cannot go where she wants, have what she wants, or do what she wants. Dad tells her that tomorrow they will have a celebration. He says they will celebrate her great great great grandpa Mose and Juneteenth. Dad explains that Grandpa Mose worked in the fields until sunset and had to keep going because the masters would not let the slaves quit. The slaves thought about freedom, prayed for it, and made plans for a better future. Later, a brave president’s proclamation was read in Galveston, Texas, and Grandpa Mose heard cheers, saw happiness, and felt pride. The people danced and celebrated into the night because they had found freedom.

summary_text: A poor miller had a beautiful daughter and boasted about her to the king. He said she could spin gold out of straw. The king wanted to see this, so he brought the girl to the palace and put her in a room full of straw. He told her to turn it into gold by morning. The girl could not do it and cried. Then a little man came and offered to help if she gave him her necklace. He spun the straw into gold. The king saw the gold and brought her to a bigger room with more straw. Again the little man helped, this time for her ring. The king then took her to an even larger room and said she could become his wife if she spun all the straw. The little man asked for her first child, and she agreed. Later, after she became queen and had a baby, the little man returned. He said she could keep the child if she guessed his name. On the third day, she learned his name was Rumpelstiltskin. When she said it, he was angry and disappeared into the ground.

Then he took it home and saw that it was a golden egg. He sold it for a lot of money. The next morning, the goose laid another golden egg, and this happened every day. summary_text: Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail, and Peter lived with their mother in a sand-bank under a big fir-tree. One morning Mrs. Rabbit told them not to go into Mr. McGregor’s garden, because their father had an accident there. She went to the baker’s and bought bread and currant buns. Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail went to gather blackberries, but Peter went into Mr. McGregor’s garden. He ate lettuces, beans, radishes, and parsley. Then Mr. McGregor saw him and ran after him. Peter lost his shoes, got caught in a gooseberry net, and left his jacket behind. He hid in the tool-shed, jumped into a can, sneezed, and ran out a window. At last he found the gate, escaped home, and flopped down tired and wet. His mother gave him chamomile tea and put him to bed, while the other little rabbits had bread and milk and blackberries.

video_title: Kindness Makes Me Stronger by Elizabeth Cole | Read ALOUD Books for Children
summary_text: Little Nick was very happy when summer vacation began. He went to his grandparents’ farm and hugged Grandma and Grandpa. After breakfast, Nick asked to go outside to play. Soon he saw Duck, Sheep, Cow, and Pig having a loud argument. They were upset because they would not share toys, a ball, or mud, and they were saying unkind things to each other. They said hello, smiled, and said sorry when needed. By the end of the day, everyone was happier, and Duck thanked Nick for being a good friend.

video_title: The Emperor's New Clothes READ ALOUD book for Children - Classic Tales for Kids
summary_text: Many years ago, an emperor loved fine clothes more than anything else. He did not care about hunting, plays, food, or wine. One day, two swindlers came to town and said they were master weavers. They told the emperor they could make a magical cloth that only intelligent people could see. The emperor gave them gold and sent his prime minister to check on their work. The prime minister saw nothing, but he lied and said the cloth was beautiful. He even gave the swindlers more money. Then the emperor visited the room himself and also saw nothing. Afraid of seeming stupid, he praised the cloth and ordered a suit. Soon the swindlers pretended to dress him, and he marched through town while everyone pretended to admire his clothes. At last, a child shouted that the emperor had nothing on. The crowd agreed, and the emperor knew he had been tricked.

video_title: Inch by Inch by Leo Lionni - Read Aloud Books for Children
summary_text: One day, a hungry robin saw an inchworm on a twig and wanted to eat him. The inchworm said, “Don’t eat me! I am useful. I measure things.” The robin asked him to measure his tail, and the inchworm said it was five inches long. The robin liked hearing that, so he flew with the inchworm to measure other birds too. The inchworm measured the flamingo’s neck, the toucan’s beak, the heron’s legs, the pheasant’s tail, and the whole hummingbird. Then one morning the nightingale met the inchworm and asked him to measure his song. The inchworm said he could not measure songs. The nightingale said to do it or be eaten for breakfast. The inchworm tried, and while the nightingale sang, he measured and measured until he inched away out of sight.

George did not like that exhibit, so he went outside into the sunlight. There he saw penguins swimming and flying through the water. George went into the penguin exhibit and copied the penguins. The penguins ran out, and one baby penguin fell into the water. George climbed the rope and swung over the beluga tank to save the chick. The director thanked George and made him an honorary staff member.

video_title: Flat Stanley and the Haunted House - Stories for Kids
summary_text: Stanley Lambchop lived with his mother, father, and little brother Arthur. Stanley was flat because a bulletin board had fallen on him, and he liked being flat. Stanley, Arthur, and Mrs. Lambchop went to Stanley School for a Halloween party. Arthur wore a monster costume, and Stanley wore a blueberry pancake costume. Mr. Lambchop tied Stanley to the car roof rack, and they went to the school gym. The gym was full of pirates, witches, and fairies, and Arthur wanted to see the haunted house. Inside, they saw a ghost and a sneezing werewolf, but Stanley said it was not scary. Outside, they found their neighbor Martin Tibbs crying because a bully had stolen his giant candy corn prize from the limbo contest. Stanley had an idea. He put on Arthur's monster costume, went to the bully, and Arthur spoke to him. Stanley stayed very still until the bully got scared and ran away, leaving the candy corn. Martin got his candy corn back. Then Mr. and Mrs. Lambchop saw them, and Mrs. Lambchop said they had been scary. Everyone wished each other Happy Halloween.

summary_text: Phyllis was a groundhog who liked to wake up in February, go outside, and play in mud and water. Her mother and aunties often said, “That’s Phyllis.” In summer, Phyllis picked blackberries and said that when she grew up, she wanted to be Punxsutawney Phil. The others laughed because Phil was a fellow. One February morning, Phyllis woke early and felt that spring was coming early. She tried to wake Uncle Phil, but he kept sleeping. The other groundhogs said Phil Jr. or Pete should do the job, but Phyllis said she could do it. At last, they dumped snow on Uncle Phil and woke him up. Phyllis went with him outside and showed him the melting snow, running brook, singing chickadees, and warm spring air. Uncle Phil finally agreed that spring was coming early. Then he said he would retire and choose Phyllis to be the next Punxsutawney Phil.

video_title: 'The Man on the Tip' Read By Hayley Mills | Halloween Ghost Stories
summary_text: One Saturday morning in Manchester, a film crew came to Moss Row tip, a big broken piece of land near Aras. They brought lorries, cameras, lights, cabins, and many men dressed like old soldiers for a television film about the Battle of the Somme. They used fake gunfire, smoke, and explosions, and the actors kept charging up the ridge and falling down. The narrator watched all day. Then Grandad came home and stopped in shock when he saw the battle. He had been in the real war, and the noise and sights upset him. Mum explained that the war had been horrible and that Grandad had lost friends. That night, Grandad looked out at the tip again and heard a weak cry. He and the narrator went onto the tip, found a mud-covered man in a crater, and helped him back. Grandad carried him home. The next day, the tip was ordinary again, but the narrator never forgot how much the war had meant to Grandad.

video_title: 🪨 Kids Book Read Aloud: RICKY, THE ROCK THAT COULDN'T ROLL by Mr. Jay and Erin Wozniak
summary_text: Over the lake and past the bay was a green grassy hill where the Rocks played. They raced to the top and rolled down again. The Rocks included Kip, Chester, Marvin the boulder, Ignatius, the Pebbles, Kai, Maya, Stu, Parker, Grumpy Old Albert, Gabby, Lisi, and Emma. All of them were round and could roll, except Ricky. Ricky was flat on one side, so he could not roll like the others. His friends asked him to come roll, but Ricky said he could not. Marvin carried Ricky to the top of the hill and pushed him down, but Ricky only slid. Then the Rocks glued rubber balls onto Ricky, but he only bounced. They kept trying, but nothing worked, and Ricky felt sad and sat aside. His friends did not give up. Stu saw the rain and had an idea. They carried Ricky to the lake, covered his flat side with mud, shaped it into a round mound, let it dry in the sun, and wrapped vines around him. After that, Ricky tried again and finally rolled down the hill with his friends.

People share pies, sit by warm stoves, drink cider, and travel far on a special November day to share a meal and give thanks for food and babies. Then they go home as winter begins.

video_title: SPOOKLEY THE SQUARE PUMPKIN 🎃 A Halloween Story About Courage & Kindness Kid's Book Read Aloud
summary_text: In a pumpkin patch, a little pumpkin named Spooky was born. He was not round like the other pumpkins. He was square, and the other pumpkins teased him because he could not roll. Spooky wished he could be like them. Then Halloween was almost here, and a big storm came. The wind tossed the round pumpkins around and broke their vines. Spooky stayed safe because he was square. When the fence broke, three pumpkins rolled into the bay. Spooky tipped and flipped until he fit in the gap and stopped the pumpkins from going farther. The pumpkins shouted hooray. After the storm, the farmer saw Spooky holding the broken fence. He knew Spooky had saved the day. The next year, the farmer planted Spookley’s seeds, and many pumpkins grew in many shapes and colors. Every Halloween, people come to see the special pumpkins and remember not to judge by how something looks.

While the other pumpkins were round and could roll, Spookley was square and could not move.
The other pumpkins teased him because of his shape, and he wished he could be round too.
Then Halloween came, and a strong storm blew across the bay.
The round pumpkins rolled everywhere, and some even snapped loose from their vines.
Spookley was scared, but his square shape helped him stay in place.
When the fence broke and three pumpkins rolled into the bay, Spookley tried hard, tipped and flipped, and finally blocked the gap in the fence.
He saved the day, but then many pumpkins piled on top of him.
The farmer found him the next morning and realized Spookley had protected the patch.
After that, the farmer planted Spookley’s seeds everywhere, and the patch grew pumpkins of many shapes and colors.
Every Halloween, people came to see them, and the story showed that you cannot judge a pumpkin by its cover.

Then his mom takes him to a cooking contest, where Judge Gustaf tastes Milo’s cookies and names him the winner. Milo learns that never giving up is the secret ingredient.

He also keeps an emergency kit ready with things like a parachute, bug spray, gloves, a hard hat, soap, and sardines. video_title: 🖌️ Kids Book Read Aloud: SCRIBBLE STONES by Diane Alber
summary_text: One happy gray stone lived in a pile with many other stones. He waited while the other stones were picked for different jobs, and he hoped he would have a purpose too. At last, he was chosen and placed on a desk beside a big cup. He thought he might help, but he was only a paperweight. Then bright scribbles came by and made art on the paper. The paper stack got taller and taller, and the scribbles cried because they had used all the paper. Stone did not want them to be sad, so he rolled down and asked if they could use red, yellow, and blue. The scribbles liked his idea and painted on him. More stones came, and soon Stone was picked again. He became a small gift that could brighten someone’s day. After that, scribble stones traveled everywhere and helped many people feel happy.

On Christmas morning, Splat thought Santa had not come, but his family jumped out and gave him a really big present.

video_title: ⛄ SNOWMEN AT NIGHT What Do Snowmen Do When No One is Watching? Funny Kids Book Read Aloud
summary_text: One wintry day, a child made a snowman that was very round and tall. The next day, the snowman looked different. His hat had slipped, and his arms drooped down. This made the child wonder what snowmen do at night. The child thought snowmen might slide off the lawn, down the street, and into the park when it gets dark. In the park, snowmen gather in a circle and wait for the others. They drink ice-cold cocoa made by snowman mothers. Then the snowman games begin. They race, skate on the pond, and do tricks on the ice. Sometimes they giggle, act like clowns, and bump into each other until they all fall down. They gather snowballs and play baseball under the moonlit sky. Then they have a big snowball fight. After that, they go sledding down the hill. At the end, they are tired and sleepy, so they gather their things and go home.

video_title: 💻 Kids Book Read Aloud: A LITTLE SPOT LEARNS ONLINE by Diane Alber
summary_text: Spot helps children get ready for online learning. He says virtual class is like school, but it happens on a computer at home, where the teacher and classmates can see and hear each child. Spot tells them to wear comfortable, appropriate clothes, not pajamas, and to eat before class so their stomachs do not grumble. He says eating during class can distract everyone, and snack time will come later. He tells children to be organized, keep a water bottle and school supplies nearby, and go potty before class starts. Spot also says to sit in a chair, find a quiet place, and put toys and food away. Pets should be in another room. He reminds children to join early, check the computer, camera, and microphone, and be ready to listen, watch, and raise a hand when they want to speak.

summary_text: The story begins with a speaker saying, “My face is shiny,” and getting ready to move from head to toe. The speaker asks, “Can you do it?” and then shows many body moves. At the end, the speaker asks if the listener can do the moves too, says, “Yes, you can,” and finishes by saying, “Move yourself from head to toe. See you next time.”

People saw the baby bird and were amazed. They sent Horton home happy.

video_title: 🐞 The Grouchy Ladybug! By: Eric Carle, Read Aloud kids book.
summary_text: At night, fireflies danced in the dark. In the morning, the Sun came up, and a friendly ladybug found some aphids for breakfast. Then a grouchy ladybug flew in and wanted the aphids too. The two ladybugs argued, and the grouchy one said it would fight anyone. So the grouchy ladybug went off to look for bigger and bigger animals. At 6 o'clock it met a yellowjacket. At 7 o'clock it met a stag beetle. At 8 o'clock it met a praying mantis. At 9 o'clock it met a sparrow. At 10 o'clock it met a lobster. Then it met a skunk, a bull, a snake, a hyena, a gorilla, and an elephant. Each time, the other animal was bigger or stronger, and the grouchy ladybug flew away. At 5:15 it met a whale and held on to its tail. The whale slapped it across the sea and land. At 6 o'clock the grouchy ladybug came back home. The friendly ladybug still had aphids left, and the tired grouchy ladybug thanked it. Then the fireflies woke up and danced around the moon.

video_title: My First Chinese New Year. By:  Karen Katz. Read Aloud kids book.
summary_text: The family gets ready for Chinese New Year. They decorate the walls with red paper cutouts and say red brings good luck and happiness in China. The sister and child push away the bad luck from last year so good luck can come in. Dad and the child buy plum and Christmas pumps, and the candy bars remind them that new things have grown. Grandpa and the child make headholsters to honor their ancestors. They add boats filled with tangerines and oranges, which stand for money and good luck. Mom buys brand new clothes, and the child adds a little dress to the bucket. Then everyone gets a haircut so they can start the year fresh and green. After that, the family begins cooking for the big feast. Grandma and the child make a special soup for good health, and later the child will put out the dumplings on New Year’s Eve. Girlfriends, cousins, uncles, and everyone else come to the big round table. They eat soup, chicken, whole fish, parmesan, and sweet rice pudding. On New Year’s day, the family shares more good luck. Then they go to the Chinese New Year parade in Chinatown. They watch the lion dancers, drummers, symbol clashes, clothes, paper launchers, and finally the dragon, which is a sign of good luck. At the start of spring, they hug and wish each other happy new year.

It says noses can be found on many kinds of heads and can come in different colors and sizes, such as blue, pink, red, long, and strong. The story also says a person sees a new kind of nose and that noses can be useful for making holes in trees, roofs, and barber balls. Some noses can even be used like horns or to make boom sounds. But the story also says noses are not always fun, because they sniffle and get built by far. Then it asks the reader to imagine having no nose. Without a nose, a person could never smell a rose, pie, or chicken, and could not smell anything at all. It also says glasses would fall off, so having a nose matters.

video_title: Pete the Cat and the Tip-Top Tree House. By: James Dean. Read Aloud kids book.
summary_text: Pete the cat built a tree house and called his friends to come play. When they arrived, they said it was great, but it was too small. Pete said he would fix it, and then he started building a bigger tree house. Kelly, Smarty, and others helped him. Together, they made a tower for Petey’s tea house. Marty said, “Let’s have a tree house party!” Pete and his friends got to work. They filled the tree house with fun places and games, like a bowling alley with 20 lanes, a pool, a movie theater, a skate park, a climbing wall, and an ice rink. When the party began, Pete showed each friend a place to play. Then he asked if everyone was there. His friends said they were all there to play with each other. Pete called everyone to the jungle gym, and they all climbed down. His friends said the tree house was amazing, and Pete said he was glad it brought them together.

video_title: 👾 Don't Push the Button! Read Aloud for Kids.
summary_text: A person sees something new and pretty and wonders what will happen if it is pushed. One voice says no, but another says no one is looking. The person gives it one little push, and then it changes. It turns yellow. It is pushed again, and now it is yellow and polka dot. It is pushed twice, and then there are two of it. It is pushed many more times, and things get very strange. Then the story says to scratch Larry’s tummy to make him normal again. After that, Larry is much better. The person says not to push the button again, but it was fun. Then the person thinks about brushing it just a little more.

video_title: Pink Is Not a Color by Lindsay Ward. Read Aloud for Kids.
summary_text: The primaries are getting ready for the rainbow extravaganza. Pink wants to help, and the others explain that it is a party to celebrate all the colors in the rainbow. Pink is surprised because Pink is not a rainbow color. The primaries tell Pink that it is still okay to come. Pink says it may be hard to make it because there are many things to do, like coloring dinosaurs and race cars and baking cupcakes. Then Pink starts to wonder what Pink is if Pink is not in the rainbow. Pink talks with other colors and learns that some colors are tints, like colors mixed with white, and some are shades, like colors mixed with black. Pink still feels confused and goes to Gray. Gray says Pink is a color too. Gray takes Pink to see more colors, and Pink learns that sunrise and sunset colors are important and special. Pink finally understands that Pink is a happy color too. Pink comes to the party with friends and cupcakes with extra sprinkles, and everyone celebrates all the colors together.

video_title: A Green, Green Garden: Little Critter : A Springtime Book For Kids (My First I Can Read) Read Aloud
summary_text: It is time to plant the garden. We go to the garden store, and it has everything we need. Mom buys seeds, and Dad buys baby plants. Dad rents a plow from Mr Pinky. At home, Dad plows the garden, and we pick up stones and clumps of grass. Then we plant the seeds and the little plants. I get tired and want to rest, but Dad says we must water each plant. So we water, weed, and wait. We do this every day. Later, I learn more about gardening at school. We make a compost heap from old leaves and stuff. We buy worms for the garden and good bugs that eat bad bugs. Deer eat some of the garden, and Blue wants to protect it. In the end, the garden grows green, yellow, orange, and red, and we have a great dinner from the garden.

video_title: Pete the Cat: Rock On, Mom and Dad! Read Aloud Kids Book
summary_text: It is Monday morning, and Pete the Cat is late for school because his alarm did not go off. Dad makes him breakfast, Mom packs his backpack, and Pete still makes the bus. Pete thinks about all the things Mom and Dad do for him. Mom helps him practice baseball, and Dad takes him to guitar lessons every day. Pete sees that he has never really said thank you. He wants to surprise them with something special. He thinks about breakfast in bed, flowers, cleaning the house, mowing the lawn, and changing the oil in Dad’s car, but he wants to do something they will never forget. Pete asks his big brother Bob for help. Bob says it does not matter what Pete does, but how he does it, if it comes from the heart. Pete gets an idea. He writes Mom and Dad a song and sings it to them. The song says he loves them with all his heart, and it is the best surprise ever.

video_title: How to Relieve Stress and Anxiety. Mindfulness in The City. From the Book: The Spaces in Between.P2
summary_text: In a busy city, a person may feel worried, noisy, or overwhelmed. The story shows many simple ways to feel calmer. In the morning, the person can take deep breaths in through the nose and out through the mouth. They can send friendly wishes to a friend or family member, such as wishing them happiness or wellness. They can stretch their body like a dog waking up, and they can look for flowers, birds, and other nature in the city. They may notice smells like coffee, bread, or grass. The person can also draw a picture, listen to calming music, eat a healthy snack slowly, write in a diary, or talk with a parent, teacher, or friend. At the end of the day, sleep and rest help the brain relax.

video_title: How Rocket Learned to Read by Tad Hills. Read Aloud Kids Book
summary_text: Rocket loved to play outside. He chased leaves, chewed sticks, and listened to birds sing. Every fall morning, he rested under his favorite tree. One day, a little yellow bird surprised him and called him her student. She showed him a sign and invited him to class. Rocket did not know how to read, but he stayed. The bird read a story about an unlucky dog named Buster who lost his favorite bone. Rocket listened closely and wanted to know the end. The next morning, he came back early. The bird gave him a name tag and taught him letters, sounds, and words. Each day he learned more, and each afternoon she read stories. When the weather turned cold, she flew away and told him not to forget that words are built one letter at a time. Rocket practiced all winter. When spring returned, the bird came back. Rocket learned more words, read more stories, and heard the story of Buster finding his bone.

The next day, JoJo changed the sign above her bed and was glad she did.

After that, the witch and her friends made a new broom with seats and a nest, and they all flew away together.
