video_title: The Berenstain Bears Count Their Blessings. Read Aloud Kids Books
summary_text: Mama Bear let Sister Bear go to Lizzy’s house and Brother Bear go to cousin Freddy’s house. Mama knew they would come home talking about all the things their friends had that they did not have. Sister Bear liked Lizzy’s many Barbie dolls, and Brother Bear liked Freddy’s many video games. Then a storm came. The Cubs ran home just before the rain started. They began to complain again about Lizzy’s Barbie dolls and Freddy’s games. Mama Bear told them to stop and to count their blessings. She showed them the warm house, their family, and their love for each other. Papa Bear made a fire in the fireplace, and Mama made cocoa. The family stayed safe and cozy while thunder and lightning filled the sky. Papa explained how to count the seconds between lightning and thunder. When the storm ended and the lights came back on, Sister Bear said she was counting her blessings. The story ends with the family thinking about gifts for birthdays and Christmas.

video_title: All My Stripes A Story for Children with Autism. Read Aloud Kids Books
summary_text: Zayn ran home feeling upset and told Mama about his bad day at school. In art class, the teacher started a hoof painting project. Zayn did not want paint on his hoves, so the teacher gave him a paintbrush. The other zebras laughed because they did not understand. In math class, the fire alarm rang, and Zayn hid under a desk, screaming and covering his ears. The class left without him, and firefighters found him. After lunch, some classmates talked about a video game, but Zayn did not know how to join in. He talked about the game, but the others did not hear him, and they left for science class. In science, the teacher gave each student a planet to draw, but Zayn made his own. Later, he looked for a boat in the classroom after the teacher said, “Whatever floats your boat.” Zayn cried and asked why people only saw his autism stripe. Mama showed him many other stripes he had, like pilot, caring, honest, and curious. Zayn felt better and loved himself again.

video_title: Curious George Goes Camping Read Aloud Kids Books
summary_text:
George was a good little monkey, and he was very curious. One weekend, he went camping with the Man with the Yellow Hat. The man unpacked the gear, and George looked at the tents. Then the man asked George to help put up their tent and to fill a bucket with water at the pump. George loved marshmallows and wanted to help.

George filled the bucket, but on the way back he saw a camper pour water on a campfire. George did the same to another fire, and the camper chased him. The Moon is Earth’s only natural satellite, and it circles Earth every 27.3 days while also spinning once in that same time. Because of this, Earth always sees the same side of the Moon, while the Moon appears to change shape through its phases. The Moon is smaller than Earth and has weaker gravity, so things weigh less on it. It also helps keep Earth from wobbling and pulls on the oceans to create high and low tides. People have walked on the Moon, leaving footprints and objects behind. The Moon says it is always with Earth, day and night.

video_title: My Way to Making Friends: Children’s Book about Friendship, Inclusion and Social Skills. Read Aloud
summary_text: Melissa was a quiet and shy little girl. She often felt lonely and had trouble making friends. One day, she saw children playing in a sand pit and wanted to join them, but she was too shy to go. Then a girl invited her to help build a sand castle, and Melissa had fun. But when the rival team won, Melissa felt upset. She ruined the castle and went home. That night, Melissa hugged her teddy and went to sleep, saying her teddy was the only friend she needed. In her dream, she traveled to a jungle and met a giraffe who told her that she could make many friends. Melissa still did not know how, so the giraffe showed her different ways, like saying hello, asking a name, or inviting someone to play. Melissa tried these ways with zebras, a monkey, and a lion. She learned to talk, share, help, and play with others. In the end, she woke up, went to the park, and made many friends.

Then the wind went ooh and the light went out. Zoe dropped her basket in fright, and the other pumpkin told her it would be all right. In the end, the five little pumpkins stayed together and shared their Halloween fun.

summary_text: Finn the frog lives in a book and talks to a sick kid who comes to read. Finn sees that the kid has a runny nose, sneezes a lot, and has yellow boogers, so he says the kid has a nasty cold. Finn gives the kid medicine and makes the kid take a spoonful. Then Finn starts to feel sick too, because he got the cold from the kid. He tries human medicine, but it makes him look like a cherry. Next, Finn tries a pump on his arm, but it only makes his head feel like a balloon. The kid gives Finn herbal tea, but Finn is allergic to honey and gets blue spots. Finn feels worse and says human remedies are not right for him. Then he takes a bath and the kid adds Epsom salt. Finn feels better for a moment, but then gets a rash. At last, the kid makes fly soup, just like Finn’s mom used to do. Finn eats it, feels better, and thanks the kid for helping him.

summary_text: The story is told by a pie who says he is humble and usually stays in the background. His best friend is Jake, a cake who gets attention at school, sports, and parties. At a birthday party, Jake talks to everyone while the pie helps by cleaning, serving food, and watching the children. One day, their science teacher, Mr. Barryman, lets the class choose lab partners for a project. The pie and Jake work together at first, but then Jake becomes busy with many activities and keeps missing the project work. The pie does most of the work alone and feels overwhelmed. Finally, the pie tells Jake that he needs help. Jake listens, says sorry, and helps finish the project. Their presentation goes well, Mr. Berryman praises their teamwork, and the classmates are impressed. The pie learns that being humble does not mean staying silent, and he can ask for help and speak up for himself.

video_title: A Loud Winter's Nap. Read Aloud Kids Books
summary_text: Tortoise was ready for his long winter nap when Robin came and asked him to join a singing class. Tortoise said no because he wanted to sleep, and he said tortoises do not like winter. He moved to a quieter place, but Rabbit soon asked him to make ice sculptures. Tortoise said no again and packed up. Then Squirrel invited him to a snowball fight, and Tortoise got angry because he still wanted to sleep. He moved higher and higher to find a quiet place, but winter kept following him. At last, Tortoise found a flat piece of wood behind a small tree. When he sat down, he was sent sliding on a sled and then across the ice. He smiled, giggled, and joined his friends skating, sliding, and spinning all night. By the end, Tortoise saw that winter could be fun too.

video_title: FIONA’S LUCK read aloud – St. Patrick’s Day Read Aloud | Bedtime | Storytime | Kindergarten
summary_text: Long ago, luck was easy to find in Ireland because the leprechauns made it. Then the big folk came, and the leprechaun king worried they would take all the luck. The leprechauns used golden nets to sweep up the luck and store it in an oak chest. But they took too much, and Ireland became unlucky. Hens laid no eggs, cows gave no milk, and potatoes rotted. A woman named Fiona knew the leprechauns had the luck, so she bought a cow and chickens and planted potatoes. Each day she showed milk, eggs, and potatoes to her neighbors, and people thought she had lots of luck. The leprechaun king brought Fiona to his throne room and tested her with shells, a harp, and chess. Fiona lost each test and said she had no luck. Then she wished for a hole in the chest. Luck spilled out, and Fiona returned home as luck flowed freely in Ireland again.

video_title: PERFECTLY PEGASUS read aloud | A Children‘s Story about Friendship read along | Kids Picture Book
summary_text: Nimbus was born high in the sky. She had wide feathered wings and loved the clouds, but sometimes the sky felt empty. When that happened, she traced pictures in the stars and dreamed of having company. One night, a wishing star shot across the sky, but Nimbus did not have time to make her wish. She flew down to the place where the star had fallen. On the ground, she met a sparkling creature named Kelp. Nimbus told Kelp about her search, and Kelp wanted to help. Nimbus looked high, and Kelp looked low, but they did not find the star. Then Kelp asked his friends for help. His pointy friends searched everywhere, but the star was still missing. Nimbus thanked them and flew back to the sky. There, she saw that her new memories and new constellations made the sky feel less empty. She thought her wish may have already come true.

video_title: MY TINY TEMPER by Christopher Fequiere read aloud | Kids Picture Book about controlling their temper
summary_text: The child has a tiny temper that follows everywhere and grows when parents say no. In the morning, the parents say there is no breakfast until teeth are brushed, and the child says okay. Then Dad says no playing until homework is done, so the child puts the game away. video_title: STACEY’S EXTRAORDINARY WORDS by Stacey Abrams – A Kids Read Along Picture Book about Perseverance
summary_text:
Stacy loved words. She liked reading, writing, spelling, and learning unusual words from the dictionary. She kept a special notebook for extraordinary words and practiced them carefully. Words made her feel understood, especially when she felt quiet, clumsy, grumpy, or anxious. One day her teacher, Mrs. Blakesly, asked her to stay after class and gave her a spelling test with a big red 100. Then Mrs. Blakesly told Stacy that she would be in the spelling bee with Jake. Stacy knew Jake was a bully who used words to hurt other students, and she hoped she could be braver at the contest.

Stacy studied all week. At the county library, she took her place onstage and spelled word after word correctly. Soon only Stacy, Jake, and one other girl were left. The other girl missed her word, and then Jake kept spelling correctly too. Stacy finally misspelled instantaneous and lost. Jake won first place, and Stacy got second. Jake was rude, but Stacy told him he should be courteous. Her mother reminded her, "Only fail if you stop," and Stacy remembered perseverance. She decided she would keep learning words and try again tomorrow.

video_title: TURKEY'S VALENTINE SURPRISE read aloud – Kids Funny Valentine’s Day Story read along | Picture book
summary_text: On Valentine’s Day at Farmer Jake’s Farm, Turkey finds a card from a secret admirer and feels very happy. He decides to make secret valentines for his friends and deliver them in disguise. First he dresses like a cat and tries to put a card in Rooster’s box, but Rooster catches him and reads the card. Then Turkey dresses like a dog for Horse, but Horse quickly knows it is Turkey too. Next Turkey dresses like a toad for Cow, but Cow sees him as well. Turkey feels sad because his surprise plans keep failing. Cow helps him deliver cards to Sheep and Pig in the barn, and they all like the valentines even after they know who sent them. Turkey still wants one secret surprise, so he sends pizza to the Valentine’s dance and slips away unseen. Everyone enjoys the pizza, and Turkey smiles because this surprise stays a secret.

video_title: TIM O’TOOLE AND THE WEE FOLK – St. Patrick’s Day Read Aloud | Bedtime | Storytime | Kindergarten
summary_text: Tim O’Toole and his wife Kathleen lived in Donegal and were very poor. Their house had no food left, and Kathleen told Tim to go find work. Tim walked all over the county, but no one would hire him. At last he rested by a road and heard music from a hollow in a hill. He looked down and saw the wee folk singing and laughing. Tim asked for their treasure, and they gave him a little gray goose that laid golden eggs. On his way home, Tim stayed with the McGoons and told them about the goose. While he slept, they swapped it for an ordinary goose. Tim later got a magic tablecloth from the wee folk, but the McGoons stole that too. After Tim told the wee folk what happened, they gave him a green hat. Tiny men jumped out of the hat and beat the McGoons until they returned the goose and tablecloth. Tim and Kathleen used them to get food, and their home was comfortable again.

video_title: ACORN WAS A LITTLE WILD – Fall Autumn read aloud | Funny | Kindergarten | Storytime or bedtime story
summary_text: Acorn was a small wild acorn who jumped off the tree before the others. Oak warned, “Don’t do that! Squirrels will get you!” But Acorn did not listen. He rolled in the sun and wind and even teased the squirrels. Soon a squirrel caught him and carried him up a tree. Acorn liked the fast climb, but he did not like when the squirrel tried to nibble him. Then a dog came, and the squirrel was distracted and dropped Acorn. Acorn fell down the tree and rolled down the hill again. Later he sat in the grass while rain pounded on his shell. After more time, another squirrel found him and buried him deep in the ground. At first this was not fun, but worms wiggled by and tickled him. In the dark, Acorn changed and grew. He pushed up through the ground and became an oak tree. He kept growing for many years and stayed a little wild inside.

video_title: If You Give Moose A Muffin (Kindness & Patience) #educational #toddlers #kindergarten #kidsbooks
summary_text: If you give a moose a muffin, he will want jam too. Then he will eat the muffin and ask for another, and another, until they are all gone. He will ask for more muffins, so you must go to the store for muffin mix. He will go with you and feel the chilly air, so he will ask to borrow a sweater. summary_text: In January, hermit crab says he has grown too big for his little shell. He feels safe in his shell, but the open ocean feels scary without a house to hide in. He looks for a new home and, in February, finds a big, strong shell. It feels just right. In the next months, he meets many sea friends and asks them to live on his shell. In March, a sea anemone joins him. In April, a starfish helps decorate. In May, a coral helps make the house more beautiful. In June, a snail helps clean. In July, a sea urchin comes to protect the house. In August, they travel through dark seaweed and cannot see well. In September, a lantern fish lights the way. In October, pebbles build a wall around the shell. By November, the shell feels small again, but hermit crab loves his friends like family. In December, a smaller hermit crab moves in. The next January, hermit crab leaves and finds another big empty shell.

video_title: The Jelly Donut Difference Sharing Kindness with the World (teaches sharing, caring) Kids Read Aloud
summary_text: On a cold winter morning, Dexter ran downstairs to eat his mom’s bacon and cheese bread pudding, but his twin sister Leah got the first bite again. Later, when Mama and Papa were busy cooking for a big dinner, Dexter and Leah helped in the kitchen. Papa found out they had no eggs, so he sent the twins to Ms. Marvis’s house to get some. At Ms. Marvis’s home, Dexter noticed it felt very quiet and lonely. On the way back, he and Leah talked about how their house was always full of people, and they asked their parents to invite Ms. Marvis to dinner. That night, Ms. Marvis shared stories about living in Poland and making punchki, jelly donuts made in winter. The next day, Papa used her recipe, and the twins helped make punchki to give to Ms. Marvis. They later built a snow family in her yard, and Ms. Marvis wrote a thank-you letter saying their kindness made her feel special.

video_title: I Walk with Vanessa-A Story About a Simple Act of Kindness (compassion, friendship) Kids Read Aloud
summary_text: A girl sees another girl being bullied. She stops and thinks about how the hurt girl might feel. Then she decides to do something kind. She can be extra friendly, include the girl in games, and not join in when others are mean. The story says that even small actions can help a lot. If the bullying is still happening, the girl can tell a trusted grown-up. The story explains that telling is not tattling. Tattling is getting someone in trouble, but telling is getting someone out of trouble. The story also says kindness can spread. When one person does a kind thing, other people may do kind things too. The girl shares her ideas with others and invites them to help.

summary_text: One summer, a boy was happy with his new tree house, his sister away at camp, and his baseball team. Then Jeremy Ross moved next door to Stanley, the boy’s best friend. The boy did not like Jeremy because Jeremy laughed when he struck him out in baseball and invited Stanley to a trampoline party but not him. The boy made an enemy list and put Jeremy on it. His dad said he knew a way to get rid of enemies and began making something called Enemy Pie from an old secret recipe. The boy thought the pie would be disgusting, but it smelled and looked good. Dad said the boy had to spend a day with Jeremy and be nice to him for Enemy Pie to work. The boy played bikes, trampoline, lunch, basketball, boomerang, and games with Jeremy. By dinner, Jeremy was no longer felt like an enemy. Dad served the pie, but the boy stopped Jeremy from eating it. Then he saw Dad already eating it. The pie was delicious, and Jeremy became a friend.

Thomas must go to the dairy for milk and then to the farm for butter. At the dairy, Thomas is told to go very slowly with the milk churns. Thomas meets Emily and races her. The churns shake and the milk turns almost to butter. The factory manager sends Thomas back for more milk. Then Sir Topham Hatt says the children will have no cakes. Thomas goes back carefully, but he has a better idea. He goes fast with the churns to the bakery. The baker looks inside and finds butter enough for the cakes. Sir Topham Hatt says Thomas saved the party, and Thomas is the guest of honor. The children cheer for Thomas.

summary_text: It was springtime on the island of Sodor. The engines worked in the sunshine. Sir Topham Hatt came to Tidmouth Sheds and said the new Sodor museum would open soon. He said important people would visit. Gordon said all the engines would get a repaint. Toby heard James and Thomas talk about the repaint, but Toby was not told. Toby worried all night. He thought he might be old and be put in the museum. He did not ask Sir Topham Hatt. Instead, Toby tried hard to be useful. He helped Emily, pulled Annie and Clarabelle, and moved coal and stone for James and Percy. Toby worked all day and got very tired and dirty. Then he had an accident and his axle and cow catchers broke. Sir Topham Hatt told Toby he was not going into the museum. Toby was special and useful. Toby was repaired, polished, and then he took the visitors to the museum for the grand opening.

summary_text: One morning Sir Topham Hatt came to Tidmouth Sheds. He told the engines that a new engine had arrived on the island. His name was Neville, and everyone must make him feel welcome. Neville was going to the broken bridge. Thomas realized the story was wrong. Neville was in danger on the bridge, so Thomas pulled him back to safety. Thomas said sorry for believing silly stories, and Neville was very happy.

video_title: I Will Take a Nap! (laughter, relatable moments, heartwarming twist) Kids Picture Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Gerald is tired and cranky, so he says he will take a nap. He likes naps and hopes for good dreams. Piggy hears him and asks what he is doing. Gerald says he is trying to nap because he feels cranky. Piggy says a nap helps when someone is cranky, and Gerald agrees. Gerald says sorry to Piggy because he feels very cranky. Piggy says she feels cranky too and may need a nap. She decides to nap with her special buddy, Gerald. They get ready and say, “Ready to nap. Ready to nap. Sleep tight.” Then they sleep and snore. After the nap, Gerald wakes up and feels rested, not cranky. Later, Piggy asks how Gerald is enjoying his nap, but Gerald says he is not napping and is floating with a turnip head. Piggy and Gerald both talk about floating and having turnip heads. In the end, Piggy says hello to Gerald and asks if he had a good nap, and Gerald says he sure did.

summary_text: Pete the Cat wakes up early and sees the sun and birds. His friend Vinnie the Velociraptor shakes the bed and says it is a perfect day for a picnic. Pete and Vinnie decide to invite everyone. Pete visits Ethel the Apatosaurus in a tall tree and invites her to bring a big salad. Then he finds T-Rex by the river and invites him to bring his guitar. T-Rex says he can also bring Al the Allosaurus with drums. Pete asks Terry the pterosaur for a ride to the picnic, and he invites Skip the stegosaurus too. On the way, Pete meets Trinny the Triceratops, who is playing hide and seek, and she joins the picnic. At the picnic, some friends start to argue, so Pete sings and plays guitar. Soon everyone is happy again, eats salad, and plays hide and seek. Pete says it is the best picnic ever.

video_title: Chocolate Milk, Por Favor! (kindness knows no language barriers) Kids Picture Story Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Johnny saw a new boy named Gabe walking into school with his mother. Gabe cried and held her hand. Johnny thought Gabe was a baby. In class, the teacher told everyone to help Gabe because he did not understand their words yet. Johnny did not want to share with him and called him “Cry Baby.” At lunch, Gabe asked for chocolate milk in a different language, and another child helped him. Johnny said Gabe was not like the others because he could not order lunch. At recess, Gabe did a tricky soccer move that Johnny had tried for weeks. Gabe joined the team, and the other children were kind to him. By the end of the week, Johnny was alone at lunch while Gabe played with many friends. Gabe showed Johnny the soccer move, over and over, until Johnny finally did it. Johnny then understood how hard it was for Gabe to learn a new language. The next day, Johnny smiled, said hi, and gave Gabe chocolate milk. They both smiled and became friends.

video_title: The Pout-Pout Fish Goes to School (world of learning adventures) Kids Picture Story Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Mr. Fish went to school for the first time and got a kiss from his parents before he swam inside. He rushed in but got lost. The bigger fish knew where to go, but Mr. Fish did not. He looked into a classroom and tried to write his name, but he could not do it. He looked into another room and tried to draw a rhombus, but he could not do that either. Then he tried math, and he could not do that too. Mr. Fish felt sad and said school was too hard, so he tried to leave. Then Miss Hewitt, his teacher, spoke kindly to him and said he did not need to know things before learning them. She said she was there to help and that he belonged. She took him to the class for brand new fish. The class learned together, and with help, they listened and tried. Mr. Fish smiled and stayed with his class, knowing he could learn.

Feeling upset, he decided to leave school and said it was too hard. Then Miss Hewitt, his teacher, spoke kindly to him. She told him he did not need to know everything yet, that she would help him learn, and that he belonged. She took him to the classroom for brand new fish. There, she and the class said they were smart, could learn, and belonged. With Miss Hewitt’s help, Mr. Fish tried again, succeeded, and ended the day swimming happily with his class.

video_title: I Am Invited to a Party! (surprises, humor, true essence of friendship) Kids Picture Book/Read Aloud
summary_text: Piggie shows Gerald an invitation to a party from Mo Willems and asks him to go too. Gerald says he has never been to a party, but he will go with Piggie. Next, Gerald thinks it might be a pool party, so they get ready again and say they will make a splash. After that, Gerald wonders if it could be a costume party, and they get ready one more time. At last, Gerald asks if they can go. Piggie says yes, they are ready now. But when they arrive, they are surprised. It is Gerald who does not know parties. They say, “Party, party,” and then it is morning, and they say goodbye.

Love is brown because sometimes love stinks. Love is gray because love can be small and soft or big and strong. Love is white because sometimes love is hard to see. Love is green because love is helpful. Love is yellow and orange because love is sunny and warm. Love is blue because sometimes love is stormy. Love is pink because love can be silly. Love is peach because sometimes love can hide. Love is black because love is not always bright and colorful. At the end, the story says love is every color.

video_title: Measuring Penny (mathematical adventure, educational and fun) Kids Picture Story Book Read Aloud
summary_text: When the child gets home, Penny the dog jumps all over them, and they realize Penny can be used for homework about measuring. Penny is a Boston terrier, and the child compares her size with other dogs at the park. They measure noses with inches, tails with dog biscuits, ears with cotton swabs, paw prints with centimeters, and height with inches, feet, and yards. Penny is one inch long in the nose, one dog biscuit long in the tail, one swab long in the ears, three centimeters wide in the paw print, and 18 inches tall. Then the child checks how high the dogs can jump, and Penny jumps as high as the child’s waist. The child also uses a seesaw to compare weight and later weighs Penny on a scale at home. Penny weighs 16 pounds.

Since there is no scale in the park, the child uses a seesaw to compare weight. Later, at home, Penny is weighed at exactly 16 pounds and gets water and food. The child also learns about Penny’s schedule, how long it takes to care for her, how fast she runs, the temperatures she likes, and how much she costs. In the end, the child says Penny is worth a lot and might be renamed Million.

Everyone was happy, and Mr. Fish felt merry too.

He fell asleep, woke up ready for more fun, and finished his trip by thinking about what he had learned and the friends he met. He sang that it was nice to be back home.

He started early, but soon he saw a flashing orange sign. An array offered him a local map, and Mr. Fish thanked them and kept going. He went around a roundabout and stayed on his way. Then he became hungry. An eel told him about a diner on the next street, and Mr. Fish found it and ate there. After that, a crab saw that his luggage was overflowing and helped him fix it at a rest stop. At the lodge, Mr. Fish unpacked, but then he saw that he had forgotten his snoozy snuggly. He felt sad and wanted to go home. Then he remembered a loving message from far away, fell asleep, and woke up ready to keep going. He had more fun, saw more sights, and met new friends. At the end, he knew that bumps and detours are part of a trip, and he was glad to be back home.

summary_text: Mr. Fish went to school for the first time. He got a kiss from his parents and felt excited, but then he got lost in the big school. Other fish knew where to go, but Mr. Fish did not. He looked into a classroom and tried to write his name, draw a rhombus, and do long division, but he could not do them. He felt sad and said he was not smart and did not belong. Then he hurried toward the exit. Miss Hewitt, his teacher, spoke kindly to him and told him he did not need to know everything yet. She said she would help him learn and that he could do it. She took him to the class for brand new fish. There, Miss Hewitt helped the students, and they listened and tried their work. Soon everyone could do it. Mr. Fish felt happy, and he swam with his class, saying they were smart, could learn, and belonged.

summary_text: When Mr. Fish was very small, he went to school for the first time with a kiss from his parents. At first, he rushed in and got lost while the bigger fish found their lockers and classes. Mr. Fish looked into a classroom where the class was writing, but he could not print his name. He felt sad and swam down the hallway. Then he found another room where the class was drawing shapes, but he could not make a rhombus. After that, he saw a math class, but he could not do long division either. He decided school was too hard and started to leave. Then Miss Hewitt, his teacher, spoke kindly to him and said he did not need to know things he had not learned yet. She took him to the brand new fish classroom. There the class listened, tried, and learned together. In the end, Mr. Fish was happy, and he and the class said they were smart, could learn, and belonged.

video_title: Pout-Pout Fish Collection #1 | Kids Picture Story Book | Read Aloud-American English- Listen & Learn
summary_text: Deep in the ocean, Mr. Fish and his pals were playing at the park on a warm, gentle day. They laughed and felt happy. Then a shark came along and made mean noises. He said, “Move aside micro fishies!” and later, “I’m the boss of this game!” Mr. Fish felt scared and did not know what to do. The friends tried to play again, but the shark came back and stole a guppy’s lunch. He said, “Fear the Finn!” Mr. Fish felt upset and worried. After the shark left, Mr. Fish thought about what could help. He remembered that words can make a difference, and his voice is strong. He turned back and spoke to the shark about the bad things he had done. Mr. Fish told him to leave until he was ready to be kind and respectful. Then the friends were no longer scared, and they played together again. The park filled with happy play, and they remembered to be kind, be fair, and speak up when something goes wrong.

summary_text: On a warm day in the ocean park, Mr. Fish and his friends were laughing and playing. Then a shark came swimming in and told them to move aside. He showed his teeth, used mean words, and scared the small fish. Mr. Fish felt afraid and did not know what to do. The friends tried to play again, but the shark returned and kept being rude. He shouted that he was the boss and even stole a guppy’s lunch. Each time, Mr. Fish and the others shrank back in fear. After the shark left, Mr. Fish thought about what had happened. He realized that words can make a difference and that his voice was strong too. He turned back, faced the shark, and spoke up. He told the shark that his actions were mean and that he needed to leave until he could be respectful. The friends stood together, and the park became happy again.

summary_text: Deep in the water, there lives the Pout-Pout Fish. He has a glum face and says he spreads the “dreary wearys” everywhere. First, a clam comes by and tells him to turn his frown upside down. The fish says that is just the way he is. Then a jellyfish floats in and asks him to smile and be friendly, but the fish still says he cannot change. Next, a squid swims up and tells him to show some joy and hope. The fish again says he is a Pout-Pout Fish and will stay glum. After that, an octopus tells him his sulking is not nice, but the fish still feels the same. Then a bright silver fish comes along. She does not speak. She kisses his pout and swims away. The Pout-Pout Fish is surprised, and then he says he was wrong. He becomes a “kiss-kiss fish” and says he will spread cheery cherries all over the place.

video_title: Ride, Fly Guy, Ride! (laughter, unexpected twists, joy of exploration) Kids Picture Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy, and Fly Guy could say Buzz’s name. One day Dad asked who wanted to go for a ride, and Buzz and Fly Guy said they did. The family buckled up and drove with the windows down. Buzz stuck his hand out like an airplane, but a strong wind blew Fly Guy out of the car and into a passing truck. Buzz shouted, “Follow that truck!” Fly Guy then bounced from the truck to a motorboat, from the boat to a circus train, from the train to an airplane, and then toward a rocket. Buzz kept calling for each vehicle to be followed. At last, Buzz and Dad landed the rocket and raced into space to find Fly Guy. Dad said they had not really gone to space. Then they rode home, and Fly Guy said, “More rides.”

In the end, Dad and Buzz went home, and Fly Guy said, “More rides.”

video_title: Are You Ready to Play Outside? (joy of shared playtime w/friends) Kids Picture Story Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Piggy asks Gerald if they are ready to play outside, and both say yes. They plan to run, skip, and jump all day. Then a drop falls, and it starts to rain. The rain gets heavier and heavier, and Piggy is upset because they cannot play outside. Gerald stays with Piggy while it keeps raining. Then they see others having fun in the rain, so they decide to try splashing too. Soon they are running, skipping, and jumping in the rain, and Piggy says he loves the rain and hopes it rains all day. But then the rain stops, and Piggy is sad again. Gerald tells Piggy not to worry and says he has a plan. He says, “Rain elephants make the best friends.”

video_title: The Pout-Pout Fish and the Worry-Worry Whale (empathy, overcoming anxiety)Kids Story Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Mr. Fish was happy because he was going to a party with a gift. On the way, he met Willa Whale, who looked worried. Willa said she did not want to go because she thought many things might go wrong. She worried it might be too crowded, that no one would play with her, and that she would not know what to say. Mr. Fish listened and told her that worry tells stories that are not always true. He asked her to take a big breath and choose one small thing to try. Willa decided she could try just the beginning of the party. Together, they kept walking. Willa breathed, talked with Mr. Fish, and felt calmer. At the party, she found a quiet place, watched her friends, and played a little. Later, when it was time to sing, Willa worried again. She chose to try one note and hum if needed. She sang, the others joined in, and Willa enjoyed the party.

video_title: Prince Fly Guy (combines humor, fantasy, fun filled & engaging) Kids Picture Story Book Read Aloud
summary_text: A story begins with an ugly troll, then a smelly pig herder, but Buzz does not like those ideas. He says a handsome prince is better. The handsome prince goes to the Dark Castle, first walking, then riding, then flying there. At the Dark Castle, Buzz says the prince eats cold porridge, but that is not right either. Then Buzz says the prince rescues a beautiful princess. Soon, a giant who lives in the Dark Castle chases the prince and the princess and knocks them to the ground. The princess throws her crown, and it hits the giant on the nose. Boink! The giant falls down and runs away, saying, ouch, ouch, ouch. After that, the prince and princess fly home. They make matching crowns and live happily ever after. Buzz says, “Oh the end,” and he likes his fairy tale.

video_title: Pete the Cat and the Cool Cat Boogie (captures determination) Kids Picture Story Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Pete the cat was learning a new dance called the cool cat Boogie. Grumpy toad came by and told Pete he was dancing all wrong. Pete felt sad and walked away. That night, he could not sleep because he wondered if his dancing was bad. He decided not to give up. Pete practiced again and asked squirrel, Gus, and Turtle how to dance. Each one showed him a different move, but Pete made mistakes and stepped on toes, bopped a nose, and fell over Turtle’s shell. After each try, Pete walked away and kept trying again. At last, Wise Old owl watched from his tree and told Pete that it did not matter how he moved as long as he was being himself. Owl said that when Pete heard a groovy beat and felt happy in his feet, he should dance, dance, dance.

They contact the United States Embassy in Nairobi. Soon an American diplomat comes by Jeep and sees a big ceremony with dancers, singers, and many cows. The Messi give 14 blessed cows to help heal the sorrow in America.

video_title: The Man Who Walked Between the Towers (Remembering The Twin Towers Before 9/11 Tragedy) Read-Aloud
summary_text: Once there were two tall towers in New York City. Philippe was a young street performer. He rode a unicycle, juggled balls and torches, and loved to walk on a rope. When he saw the two towers, he wanted to stretch a wire between them and walk on it. He knew people would say no, so he made a secret plan. One August evening, Philippe and friends brought rope and cable into the South Tower and waited until night. At midnight, they shot a line across to the other tower and tied the strong cable between the roofs. When the sun came up, Philippe put on black clothes and took his balancing pole. He stepped onto the wire and walked high above the city. Police came and shouted, but Philippe kept walking back and forth for almost an hour. Then he returned to the roof and gave himself up. The judge later told him to perform in the park for children.

The paper is a treasure map with a trail ending in an X, so Captain Pete and first mate Cali set sail for secret Island. As they race over the waves, a giant sea monster appears and splashes their ship. The crew gets scared, but Captain Pete plays his guitar, and the monster stops and follows the beat. Then a storm comes, and the ship is tossed by the waves. Captain Pete asks the sea monster for help, and the monster lifts the ship and pushes it through the storm. At last, the crew reaches secret Island and finds grumpy toad with a pile of treasure. He says treasure is no fun if it cannot be shared with friends. The pirates load the treasure, invite the sea monster to join them, and sing together as a complete crew.

video_title: Super Fly Guy (hyperbole, puns, slapstick humor, & silly drawings)Kids Picture Story Book/Read Aloud
summary_text: A boy named Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy, and Fly Guy could say Buzz’s name. One day Fly Guy went to school with Buzz. He learned reading, phonics, and art. At lunchtime, Fly Guy liked the lunchroom very much. He liked the dirty dishes, the smelly mop, and the garbage cans. There he met the lunch lady, Roz. Roz said there were no flies in the lunchroom, but Fly Guy said her name, and Roz saw that he was smart. She gave him chicken bones, fish heads, and sour milk, and Fly Guy was happy. Then Roz’s boss saw the flies and fired her because the children could not eat in a room full of flies. The next day Miss Muzzle became the new lunch lady, but she made burnt peas and turnips, so no one wanted to eat. Buzz made a plan. After Fly Guy caused trouble in the lunchroom, the boss fired Miss Muzzle. Roz came back, called Fly Guy a Super Fly Guy, and made him special garbage soup. Everyone was happy again.

video_title: Apples for Everyone (a seasonal treasure) Kids Picture Story Book | Read Aloud
summary_text: Each year, apple trees bloom in orchards and backyards. Bees buzz from blossom to blossom, and then the petals fall to the grass. Small fuzzy bumps grow into baby apples. The apples get bigger and change color into red, green, yellow, and sometimes speckled or striped fruit. Their branches become heavy, and some apples fall to the ground and rot, helping feed the tree. In fall, Harvest Time comes, and apples are ready to pick. People find them in grocery stores, farmers markets, and roadside stands, or pick them from trees. Apples are eaten fresh, dipped in caramel, baked into pies, cooked into applesauce, crushed into juice, or warmed into cider. Apple trees have grown in America for many years. Johnny Apple Seed, also called John Chapman, walked through the wilderness planting apple seeds. Apple seeds are found in the core, and when an apple is cut crosswise, it makes a star shape.

video_title: Apples: New and Updated (undeniably delicious🍎educational treats) Kids Picture Story Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Apples grow on apple trees, and apple trees grow in many places around the world. Long ago, colonists brought apple seeds and small trees from England to America. As people moved west, they carried apple seeds too. In the early 1800s, John Chapman traveled through Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Indiana planting apple seeds and giving seeds and seedlings to settlers. People called him Johnny Appleseed. In spring, apple blossoms bloom on the trees. Insects or wind carry pollen from one blossom to another so apples can grow. The blossoms die, the apples grow through summer, and then they ripen in fall. Workers pick ripe apples by hand during harvest time. Some apples go to stores, and some are made into juice, cider, jelly, and applesauce. In winter, the trees become bare and dormant until spring comes again.

Apple trees need pruning, fertilizing, and care to grow good fruit.

video_title: A Big Guy Took My Ball! (emphasizing friendship & problem-solving) Kids Read Aloud- William & Sarah
summary_text: A child finds a big ball and has fun with it. Then a very big guy, Gerald, takes the ball away. The child feels upset and says the big guys get all the fun. The child thinks about how big Gerald is and wants the ball back. Gerald tries, but he cannot get it back from the even bigger guy. The child says thank you when the little ball is found, but it is not the big ball. Gerald then says he is so big that no one will play with him, and little guys have all the fun. At the end, the child asks Gerald to play whale ball. Gerald asks what whale ball is, and they say they do not know yet. They say they can make it up together and have big fun with a little help.

video_title: The Seasons of Arnold's Apple Tree (learn about nature, creativity) Kids Picture Book | Read Aloud
summary_text: Arnold climbs high into his apple tree, and it is his secret place. In spring, he watches buds grow into apple blossoms. He sees bees gather nectar, and he makes a swing, a blossom wreath, and a flower arrangement with his family. In summer, the tree has big green leaves. Arnold builds a tree house, rests in the shade, and watches tiny apples grow bigger. He even juggles some green apples. In fall, the tree has red apples and golden leaves. Arnold gathers leaves for his tree house and picks apples into a basket. He and his family make apple pies and fresh cider from the apples. On Halloween, Arnold decorates some of the biggest apples. In winter, snow falls. Arnold hangs popcorn and berries for the birds, builds a snow fort, and makes a snowman. When the snow melts, spring comes again.

video_title: The Little Old Lady Who Was Not Afraid of Anything (fearless attitude & ingenious solution)Kids Book
summary_text: One windy afternoon, a little old lady left her Cottage and walked into the forest to gather herbs, spices, nuts, and seeds. It grew dark on the way home. On the path, she met two big shoes that went “clump clump,” then a pair of pants that went “wiggle wiggle,” then a shirt that went “shake shake.” She kept walking and found two white gloves that went “clap clap” and a tall black hat that went “nod nod.” Near her Cottage, she saw a very big orange pumpkin head that went “boo boo.” The little old lady ran home and locked her door. Inside, she sat by the fire until there was a knock on the door. She opened it and saw all the things again, standing together. She was not afraid. She spoke to the pumpkin head, and it looked happier. The next morning, she saw the clothes and pumpkin head in her garden, and they scared the crows away.

summary_text: In the morning, Mommy says the child is going to be the king of kindergarten. The child washes, gets dressed, and eats breakfast with Mommy and Daddy. Mommy and Daddy say the child is growing up. Then a big yellow Carriage takes the child to a grand Fortress, which is the school. At the Towering doors, the child remembers to hold the head high and smile. The teacher welcomes the child and says good morning. The child says the name proudly and sits at the Royal seat. The other children wave, and the child waves back. In class, the teacher talks about rules, shapes, the alphabet, and numbers, and reads a book about trucks, trains, and tractors. At recess, the child asks Marie to play, and she says yes. Marie helps save the kingdom from a fire breathing dragon in the cafeteria. The child also shares chocolate pudding with Howie. After rest time, the children sing, dance, and bop. The child goes home happy and looks forward to tomorrow.

video_title: The Smallest Girl in the Smallest Grade (empathy, kindness, for what’s right (Kids Book | Read Aloud
summary_text: Young Sally McCabe was the smallest girl in the smallest grade, and most people did not notice her. But Sally noticed many things at school. She saw an abandoned kite stuck in a tree, the janitor’s 27 keys, wildflowers changing, a dog howling, and stray cats meeting in the church parking lot. She also saw children being treated badly, like Tommy Torino getting tripped, Kevin McEwen being pushed off a slide, and Billy being dragged away by his father. Sally watched the hurtful words and mean actions around her. Then, on February 3rd at 11:29, Sally stepped out of the lunchroom line and said she was tired of seeing this terrible stuff. At first, some people laughed. Then many others, including the principal Claire, stood up with Sally and raised their fingers in the air. After that, the world went back to normal, but people noticed small kind acts more, like opening doors and making room. Everyone remembered that Sally had paid super extra special attention.

video_title: Stumpkin (teaches children about acceptance, empathy) Kids & Family Picture Story Book | Read Aloud
summary_text: A few days before Halloween, a shopkeeper put pumpkins on the shelves outside a little shop in a big city. A girl came to look at them. She picked up one pumpkin and carried it away. The other pumpkins worried about their friend, then saw him across the street, high up as a Jacko Lantern. He had triangle eyes, a nose, and a big smile. The pumpkins were happy for him and dreamed that they might become jackolanterns too. Then one pumpkin saw something sad. He had lost his stem and was now just stumpkin, a stemless pumpkin with a little stump. Still, stumpkin was a nice pumpkin, orange like a traffic cone and round like a basketball. video_title: 3 Creepy Books By Aaron Reynolds | Kids & Family Picture Story | Read Aloud-American English
summary_text: On Thursday, Jasper rabbit needed new underwear. Mom took him to the underwear store and picked up plain white packages, but Jasper saw a pair of creepy underwear and wanted them. Mom said they were too creepy, but Jasper said he was a big rabbit now, so Mom bought one pair. That night Jasper wore them to bed. In the dark, the underwear glowed a ghoulish greenish glow, and Jasper could not sleep. He changed into plain white underwear and hid the creepy pair in the laundry hamper. The next day the creepy underwear were back on him, so he threw them in the garbage. After school, Jasper heard scratching at his dresser and found the underwear back again. He mailed them to China, but the next morning they returned with chopsticks. Jasper used his mom’s sewing scissors, then later buried the underwear deep in a hole at Creek hanger Hill. At the end, Jasper bought creepy underwear again all by himself and was not scared.

summary_text: Jasper Rabbit was having a hard time at school. He was failing math and spelling, and only art was going well. Then he found a purple crayon that was pointy, perfect, and seemed happy to see him. One night he was too tired to study for a spelling test, but when he picked up the crayon, he suddenly spelled every word right and got an A+ with a sticker. Later, the crayon helped him with math homework and a surprise quiz, and Jasper saw strange purple words appear on his things. The crayon also made his poster contest art into a better picture, but Jasper did not like how creepy it felt. He tried hiding the crayon, melting it, and throwing it away, but it kept coming back. Finally, Jasper threw it into the toilet. After that, he studied on his own, did not use the crayon, and got a C+ on his spelling test. He felt free, and the crayon drifted away until Elliot Pelican found it.

Every November, they made him practice dance steps and football moves because they believed he might be chosen for something special. Turk’s brother, Runt, kept warning that turkeys were chosen to be eaten, but no one listened to him. Two days before Thanksgiving, Madame Waddell came to choose a turkey for Swan Lake. Turk danced beautifully, but then Runt acted wild and chased her away, so she left without picking anyone. The next day Coach Giblet came to choose a turkey for a football team. Turk played hard, but then Runt acted sick and sneezed, and the coach drove away because he thought the birds were too sick. On Thanksgiving morning, a little old lady came in a car and wanted Runt for dinner. Turk saw the danger, worked with Runt, and they acted so strange that the lady left. The family then shared a thankful feast, and Runt warned that they still were not safe from holiday dinners.

summary_text: The story talks about many farm animals and what they eat. A baby cow is called a calf. Cows eat grass, clover, and hay. A baby horse is called a foal. Horses eat grass, hay, corn, oats, fruits, and vegetables. A baby pig is called a piglet. Wild pigs eat leaves, roots, fruit, and rodents. A baby sheep is called a lamb. Sheep eat mostly grass, plants, and seeds. A baby chicken is called a chick. Chickens eat grass, bugs, fruit, vegetables, and even table scraps. A baby goat is called a kid. Goats eat shrubs, trees, hay, and grains. The story also shares fun facts. Cows can smell things far away. Horses sleep standing up. Pigs cannot sweat. Sheep have rectangular pupils. Chickens bathe in dirt.

video_title: One Vote, Two Votes, I Vote, You Vote #kids #story #books #reading #learning #inspiration #readaloud
summary_text: Voting is a way people choose something and use their own voice. People vote for a class president, a snack, a class trip, or a class pet. They can vote with a raised hand, on paper, or with thumbs up or thumbs down. If people do not vote, they lose their say. In big elections, people choose the President and Vice President every four years. They also elect senators, Congress people, mayors, and sheriffs. The story explains that the United States is a democracy, so the people help govern the country. It also tells how voting rights changed over time. Black men could vote in 1870, women in 1920, Native Americans in 1924, and 18-year-olds in 1971. Adults 18 and older must register to vote. Political parties, like Democrats and Republicans, help choose candidates. Candidates campaign, give speeches, and try to win voters’ trust.

summary_text: It snowed all night on Sodor, and in the morning everything was white. Sir Topham Hat asked Thomas to take firewood to the stations. He asked Gordon to take trucks to the docks. Sir Topham Hat told Gordon that the snow was slippery and said to take the long way around the hills. Gordon did not listen. He said he was strong and could go over any hill. Thomas was careful, but Gordon went straight on. On one hill, Gordon slid fast. Then he came to a bigger hill, and a giant snowball grew behind him. Thomas came up the hill and was pushed back by the snowball. Gordon could not stop it. Thomas was knocked off the rails. Gordon felt sorry and asked Rocky to help. Rocky lifted Thomas back on the tracks. Then Thomas and Gordon delivered the firewood to all the stations, and they went around the hills together.

Then everyone in Tidmouth came to give gifts and sing carols at the Christmas party.

summary_text: At the end of a busy day on Sodor, Thomas told James and Percy a bedtime story about Jack and the beanstock. The next day, Thomas carried a load of beans from the farm. Diesel 10 rushed around a bend, hit Thomas, and left him tipped over with beans spilled on the ground. Then a tiny leaf grew fast into a giant beanstock with tracks going up it. Thomas climbed and climbed to the top and found a big world above the clouds. He saw a castle, a giant, and a little gold engine. The gold engine said she was taken from her home and wanted to go back. Thomas offered to take her to Sodor, but he ran out of coal. She gave him golden coal, and they sped away. The giant and Diesel 10 chased them, but Thomas and the gold engine got back down to Sodor. Then James and Percy helped push Thomas, and when Thomas woke up, the beanstock was gone. Thomas found a piece of gold coal in his hopper and wondered if it had all been a dream.

summary_text: One day Percy rushed into the shed and told Thomas he had seen a monster in the forest. Percy said monsters were very big animals with very big teeth, and they ate engines. Thomas felt scared, but he still had work to do. Then Thomas saw the big animal in the forest and thought it was a monster. He raced back to Percy and said he had seen it too. Soon Sir Topham Hat came and asked Thomas to bring a special load from the forest. Thomas was worried, but he went back. There he saw the same animal again. His driver told him it was not a monster. It was a model of a dinosaur for Sodor's new dinosaur park. Harold the helicopter helped lift it, and workers guided it onto Thomas's flatbed. Percy saw it and called it a monster too, but Thomas explained it was a dinosaur model. Thomas carried it to the park, where children waved. Sir Topham Hat praised him, and the dinosaur was placed where everyone could see it.

Thomas told everyone, and Sir Topham Hat explained that it was Great Waterton, a town that had been lost when the springs ran dry and people moved away. Sir Topham Hat put Thomas in charge of repairs and of checking the old tracks. Thomas worked hard, but he went too fast on the old line and toppled off the track. Harvey put him back, and Thomas went to the works. While he was away, Stanley took over the work. When Thomas returned, Sir Topham Hat said Stanley would stay in charge and Thomas would help him. Thomas tried to prove himself by shunting freight cars and then chasing an old freight car into Morgan's mine. The car disappeared, and Thomas got lost in the mine. Stanley searched for him, found him, and pulled him back onto the track. Then Stanley broke a valve, and Thomas pushed him home. In the end, Great Waterton was repaired in time for Sodor Day, and Thomas and Stanley were both praised.

summary_text: Docks was always busy, and Cranky the crane worked there day and night. He never got a nap, so he was always cranky. One morning he unloaded pipes from a cargo ship and put them into trucks. Salty said hello, but Cranky snapped at him. Then Bill and Ben came to work, and Cranky shouted at them too. Salty said Cranky was lonely and offered to keep him company by telling a story. Cranky did not want to listen. He dropped the pipes, and they rolled into a big shed. Crash! The shed fell down, and Bill, Ben, and Salty were trapped. The Fat Controller came to the docks and saw the mess. He told Cranky he had made a terrible mess and must wait until Harvey could clear it up. All night, Salty told stories. In the morning Harvey came and cleared the mess. Cranky felt better and promised to be kind. He worked carefully and said please and thank you, but later he became cranky again.

summary_text: One morning Sir Topham Hat spoke to James and said that if he could not behave, his red coat would be taken away and he would be painted blue. James felt cross. He was rough with the coaches and called, “Come along, come along!” The coaches grumbled and squealed. James had to fetch his own coaches, and he thought this was unfair. He bumped the coaches hard onto the train and made them groan. Then he had to take them to a different platform where people stayed far away. James felt lonely and wanted to show that he could pull the coaches well. When the guard blew his whistle, James started off with a big jerk. He went too fast, and then the train began to slow down because the brake pipe was leaking. The driver and guard found a hole. They fixed it with newspapers and a leather bootlace from Jeremiah Jobling. After that, James pulled the train safely and was careful never to bump coaches again.

summary_text: One morning, Sir Topham Hat spoke severely to James and warned that if he could not behave, his red coat would be taken away and he would be painted blue. After that, James pulled the train safely, and he became sadder and wiser and never bumped coaches again.

summary_text: The ballots were counted, and Splat the cat became the new student body president. At first, he gave a speech and promised new pencils, better fish food for the class goldfish, and quieter quiet reading time. But at lunch, he heard classmates grumbling that they did not want the new pencils, and his afternoon felt rough. Mrs. Wimpy Dimple told Splat to think about what the kids really wanted and to share new ideas the next day. That night, Splat thought hard on the bus and at the dinner table. The next day, he made big promises about race cars for school, pizza and ice cream every day, and robot teachers to do homework and tests. Mrs. Wimpy Dimple later explained that Splat could not promise things he could not keep. She told him to look for something he could change. Splat then suggested fixing up the school library, and everyone painted, sorted books, and set up displays. The library project was a big success.

summary_text: Autumn was one of Splat’s favorite seasons. Mom Splat helped him rake leaves, and Splat and Seymour made a huge pile. Splat got excited and sent the leaves flying everywhere. Then Mom Splat had an idea. She told Splat to go to Farmer Patch’s pumpkin patch and pick a pumpkin to decorate for the porch. Splat took his wagon and went with Seymour. At the pumpkin patch, he saw a scary scarecrow, got lost in a hay bale maze, and tasted fresh apple cider. He looked for the perfect pumpkin and kept choosing ones that were too small, not round enough, or not orange enough. At last, he found a big, round, orange pumpkin. It was perfect, but it was too big for the wagon. Splat rolled it home, but it ran away down a hill. He chased it, steered it with his feet, and brought it through the front gate. The pumpkin stopped, and Mom Splat said it was perfect.

summary_text: A calerie pear tree lived for more than 20 years on the World Trade Center Plaza in New York City. On September 11, 2001, the Twin Towers fell near her and covered her with debris. For a month, she lay under smoking rubble. Then workers saw a few green leaves showing through the gray ash and concrete. They carefully uncovered the tree and found that many branches were gone, only a few roots were left, and her trunk was burned and scarred. Still, the leaves gave them hope. The workers took her by truck to a nursery. The tree felt scared as the city grew smaller behind her. At the nursery, workers put her in rich soil and fertilizer. Richie, a city parks worker, touched her trunk and said he would help her heal. The tree felt sad, but she began her long recovery.

summary_text: At the end of a busy day on Sodor, Thomas told James and Percy his favorite story, “Jack and the beanock.” Percy wished a magic beanock would grow on Sodor, and James wondered if giants liked railway engines. The next day Thomas was carrying beans when Diesel 10 crashed into him. Thomas tipped over, and beans spilled on the ground. Then one bean began to grow. It grew into a huge beanock with railway tracks winding up to the top. Thomas was brave and climbed the tracks. At the top he found a magical world above the clouds, with a castle and a giant. He also met a small gold engine who wanted to go home. Thomas shared her gold coal, and they ran away together. Diesel 10 chased them, but they escaped back to Sodor. Then Thomas and his friends pushed against the beanock, and Thomas woke up. Percy and James were there, and Thomas found a piece of gold-colored coal in his hopper. He wondered if it had all been a dream.

video_title: The Couch Potato | Kids & Family Together Picture Story Books Time | Read Aloud
summary_text: The story is about a potato who calls himself a couch potato. He loves sitting on his couch and uses many gadgets to stay comfortable. He has screens for shows, messages, video games, and even a live stream of his best friend, Spud. One day, a new video camera arrives, but then the power goes out. With nothing else to do, he opens the curtains and takes his dog, Tater, for a walk. Outside, he sees bright sunlight, fresh air, birds, a park, a hill, and a big tree. He sits there and watches the sky and sunset. When he gets home, the power is back on. He uses his couch gadgets again, but then he thinks about how much time he spent sitting there. After that, he decides to go out more often. He starts biking, hiking, swimming, playing board games, and spending time with friends.

summary_text: Santa is getting ready to leave on Christmas Eve. The toys are packed, the tree lights glow, and the stockings are full. video_title: Red & Lulu by Matt Tavares #kids #story #books #christmas #kidslearning #reading #readaloud #family
summary_text: Red and Lulu lived happily in their evergreen tree. Their nest was safe in the branches, and the tree kept them cool in summer and cozy in winter. In winter, people decorated the tree with lights and sang, “Oh Christmas tree, oh Christmas tree, thy leaves are so unchanging.” Red and Lulu loved to listen and sometimes sang too. One cold morning, Red went to find breakfast while Lulu stayed in the tree. When Red came back, the tree was gone. It had been cut down, placed on a big truck, and driven away with Lulu inside. Red flew after it, but he could not catch up. He searched for days in a strange place and felt tired and hungry. Then he heard the song again and followed it to Lulu. Later, workers took the tree away again, and Red and Lulu stayed in a new home in a park. Every year, they still visit the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree and listen and sing.

summary_text: Red and Lulu lived happily in their evergreen tree. It kept them safe, cool in summer, and cozy in winter. They loved winter best because people decorated the tree with lights and sang songs about it, especially “Oh Christmas tree, oh Christmas tree, thy leaves are so unchanging.” One cold morning, Red went to find breakfast while Lulu stayed in the tree. When Red returned, he saw that the whole tree had been cut down and strapped to a truck. He heard Lulu singing inside as the truck drove away. Red chased the truck, but it was too fast, and he lost sight of the tree. For days he searched a strange new place and felt tired and hungry. Then he heard the song again, flew toward it, and found Lulu. Later, workers took the tree away once more, and Red and Lulu stayed behind. They made a new home in a park. Every year, they return to listen to the singing at the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree.

The gingerbread man popped off the pan and ran through the hall, saying he wanted to be with the children. He met the coach, who helped when his toe came off. The art teacher sent him to the principal. Principal Peacock showed him a missing poster from room 23. At last, the class came back, cheered, and made him a gingerbread desk, chair, and house. He stayed with them and looked happy.

summary_text: In the wild wild west, a Rancher and his wife lived on a ranch. Every morning, the Rancher fed the cattle and saddled his horses, while his wife baked breakfast biscuits. One day, she got tired of biscuits and made gingerbread dough instead. She cut out a gingerbread Cowboy with boots, a hat, and a big belt buckle, then gave him raisins, candies, and nuts for eyes, mouth, and vest. She put him in the oven to bake. When the Rancher peeked inside because he was hungry, the gingerbread Cowboy jumped out and ran away. He laughed, “Giddy up giddy up as fast as you can. You can't catch me. I'm the gingerbread man.” He ran past a Road Runner, havelinas, longhorn cattle, and Cowboys, and each one wanted to catch him or eat him. At the river, a coyote offered help. The coyote carried him across, then tricked him, tossed him up, and swallowed him. That was the end of the gingerbread Cowboy.

summary_text: A cookie lives in a bakery near a river and tells about feeling unsure at school. The cookie goes to a gingerbread house school with kind Miss biscotti, but does not raise a hand, finishes tests last, and often makes mistakes. One day Miss biscotti gives the class a homework task: make something completely original. The cookie tries cooking, building, and sculpture, but each idea fails. Then the cookie watches the rain on the river and gets an idea to write a poem called “my crummy days.” The cookie writes it and feels proud. The next day, the cookie reads the poem aloud to the class. The other children listen, nod, laugh at the funny parts, and clap at the end. Miss biscotti says the poem is completely original. After that, the cookie feels more confident, starts speaking up, and learns that being smart can mean many different things.

They put on red boots and mittens, catch flakes on their tongues, and roll down hills. The snow gives them angels and new friends. While snow is here, people are told to notice how beautiful the world is, then go home, make something warm to drink, and read, play, or talk. Snow falls while flowers, the sun, and green gardens sleep.

video_title: A Picture Book of Martin Luther King, Jr.(Ordinary People Change the World) Kids & Family Read Aloud
summary_text: Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta, Georgia, on January 15, 1929. He grew up with his father, who was a pastor, his mother, who had been a teacher, and his sister Willie Christine and brother Alfred Daniel. As a boy, Martin liked baseball, football, basketball, riding his bicycle, and singing in his father’s church. One day, two friends said they could not play with him anymore because they were white and he was black. Martin cried and did not understand why skin color mattered. His mother explained that black people had been treated unfairly for a long time. Martin learned to read at home and read books about black leaders. He finished high school early, went to Morehouse College, studied in Boston, and married Ketta Scott. Later, as a pastor in Montgomery, he led peaceful protests after Rosa Parks was arrested. He helped lead the bus boycott, the March on Washington, and other peaceful protests. In 1964 he won the Nobel Peace Prize. In 1968 he went to Memphis to march for fair pay, and there he was killed.

video_title: The Youngest Marcher (1963-a Young Civil Rights Activist) Inspiring Kids/Family  Picture Story Book
summary_text: Audrey Fay Hendrix lived in Birmingham with her Mama C, Daddy, and family. When Mike, also called Martin or Dr. King, visited, the family served him a big meal, and the grown-ups talked about segregation laws that kept black and white people apart. Audrey spoke up because she wanted to eat inside Newberries, sit downstairs at the Alabama, and use the same schools and stores as white children. Mama told her to hush, but Audrey kept listening to meetings at Fred’s church, where people sang, shared stories, and heard Mike say segregation was wrong. Mike asked people to protest and fill the jails, but many adults were afraid. Then Jim said children should go instead. Audrey said she wanted to go to jail, and her parents let her join the protest. She marched from 16th Street Baptist Church, was arrested, and spent days in juvenile hall with hard beds, little food, and strict guards. After more children were arrested, the jails filled up, the protests worked, and Birmingham later ended segregation laws.

summary_text: Audrey Fay Hendrix lived in Birmingham with her Mama C and her family. When Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., whom they called Mike, visited, they shared big meals at the Hendrix home. At supper, Audrey heard adults talk about segregation, but she also spoke up about wanting to eat inside Newberries, sit downstairs at the Alabama, and use the same school books and movie seats as white children. Mama told her to hush, but Audrey knew the unfair rules well. On Monday nights at Fred’s church, she heard freedom songs and testimonies about injustice. When Mike preached that segregation was morally wrong, he told people to disobey unjust laws and fill the jails. At first, the grown-ups would not volunteer. Then Jim Bevel said the jails should be filled with children. Audrey said she wanted to go to jail, and Mama let her go. She was arrested, held in juvenile hall, and treated harshly. After several days, the jail filled up, the children’s protest helped change Birmingham, and later the city removed segregation laws.

In the end, he says only a brilliant child may make the perfect trap, and maybe next year someone will catch him.

summary_text: Jamie oor lived in Ireland and was very lazy. His wife, Eileene, planted, watered, and weeded the potatoes, but Jamie would not help dig them up. One day Eileene hurt her back and had to stay in bed. Jamie became worried because there would be no potatoes for winter. At midnight he went to church, but on the hill he heard singing and tapping. He found a leprechaun making fairy shoes. Jamie grabbed him and asked for a pot of gold, but the leprechaun offered a wish instead. Jamie wished for the biggest potato in the world. The leprechaun gave him a seed. Jamie planted it, and a huge potato grew so big it pushed up the garden and part of the cottage. The villagers came, helped dig it out, and shared the potato. In spring Jamie kept one potato eye, but the villagers promised to give him food if he did not plant it again.

summary_text: St Patrick's Day is celebrated on March 17th. It honors St Patrick, a man from Britain who lived many years ago. As a boy, he was taken to Ireland and made a slave. He herded sheep and prayed for help. After six years, he escaped and went back to Britain. There he thought and prayed, then went to France to study religion. In 432, the Pope named him Patrick. He became a priest and then a bishop. Bishop Patrick returned to Ireland, preached to the people, and built churches and schools. People trusted him because he was kind. He cared for the Irish people for the rest of his life. He died on March 17th in 461, and later the Catholic Church made him a saint. Today people celebrate with church, green clothes, shamrocks, cards, music, dances, parades, and Irish food. Some people also remember stories about snakes, a cloak, poison, and a shamrock.

Dolly wanted to go far in life and become a star. Soon, she sang on TV with a famous entertainer. After many years, Dolly decided to sing on her own and make her own music. Song after song, she won many awards. Dolly also tried new sounds with different singers. She wore dazzling wigs and costumes. Dolly gave to others too. She opened a theme park in her hometown and a library that travels all over the country. Dolly became a real-life legend with a heart as big as her dreams.

video_title: When Penny Met POTUS (combines humor, curiosity, imagination runs wild) #kids #story #books #reading
summary_text: Penny thinks today will be her best day ever because she gets to work with her mom at the Big White House. Her mom has an important job, and her boss is called Pus, which Penny says like POTUS. Penny imagines that Pus has Secret Service agents, an airplane, and a chef who makes Pus sandwiches. She practises what she will say when they meet. When Penny arrives, she asks when she can meet Pus. Her mom says maybe later because she must make phone calls. Penny cannot wait, so she quietly leaves the office to find Pus by herself. She asks people around the Big White House if they have seen Pus. One man and one woman say no. Then Penny asks another woman, and her mom comes looking for her. Penny learns that the woman is PODUS, the President of the United States. Penny is surprised to find that PODUS is a human, just like her.

video_title: Secret Pizza Party (humorous brilliant plan, delightful escapades) #kids #story #books #reading
summary_text: A poor raccoon wants pizza very much, but he does not know how to ask politely. Someone says pizza is wonderful and suggests a secret pizza party at the raccoon’s house. The pizza party is kept secret so it can feel special. The raccoon is told to call the pizza man and ask for the best pizza pie. Then the raccoon worries that the delivery guy may know him from posters and chase him with a broom. He tries to act calm and follows a sneaky route past the broom factory, the broom Enthusiast Club, and the raccoon sniffing broom Bots. But the bots are there, so he runs fast. At last, the raccoon and the others make it home, block the doors, and open the pizza box. They have a secret pizza party and try to stay quiet, but the pizza makes them so happy that they forget to be secret.

summary_text: Taylor Allison Swift was born on December 13, 1989, in West Reading, Pennsylvania. She grew up with her mom, dad, and little brother Austin. The family loved to read, visit new places, and play outside. Taylor especially loved Christmas because her family lived on a Christmas tree farm. At Christmas, her dad mowed the fields on a tractor, and Taylor picked praying mantis egg pods off the trees so no bugs would surprise people. As a child, Taylor tried many things like riding horses, acting, and writing poetry. Then she learned to play guitar and found what she loved most. Taylor wanted to go to Nashville, Tennessee, because she liked country singers Faith Hill and Shania Twain. When she was 11, her mom took her and Austin there. Taylor visited music offices and gave out CDs. Later, RCA Records wanted to work with her, and her family moved to Nashville. Taylor made albums, sang her own songs, and became a big music star.

summary_text: An old lady swallowed a daisy. She was not lazy. She swallowed the daisy to brighten the clover. Then she swallowed a butterfly. She did not sigh. She swallowed the butterfly to rest on the daisy. The daisy stayed to brighten the clover. After that, she swallowed a bird. It was not absurd. She swallowed the bird to glide with the butterfly. The butterfly rested on the daisy, and the daisy brightened the clover. Then she swallowed a pot. Believe it or not, she swallowed the pot to carry the bird. Next she swallowed some gold. It was shiny gold, and she swallowed it to fill up the pot. The bird, butterfly, daisy, and clover were all part of the chain. At the end, she swallowed a fiddle. The old lady started to dance, a wee little leprechaun joined her, and she giggled so much that out popped a rainbow. Happy St Patrick's Day!

summary_text: Brian was a leprechaun who liked to be alone. He lived under the ground in a quiet place. Then a man named Shawn McDonald built a stone cottage right over Brian’s home. Brian used magic to scare Shawn, but it did not work. So Brian made a door under Shawn’s bed and came out at night when it rained. Shawn could not sleep, and Brian whispered, “It’s only the cat under the bed.” Shawn soon guessed there was a leprechaun there. He put food under the bed, and Brian ate it. Later, Shawn got poor, and Brian left gold coins on the kitchen table. People in the village heard stories and thought Shawn had a chest of gold. Two robbers came to steal it. They tied Shawn up and looked under the bed. There they saw a wild cat, and they ran away. Shawn was free, and Brian and Shawn lived well and happily.

summary_text: Oi was a leprechaun who lived in the basement of a house in Chicago. He sat by his pot of gold and sometimes sang and read newspapers. Michael McKeever lived in the house with his mother and father. On St Patrick’s Day, Michael found that his old baseball shoes were too small and broken. He could not ask for new shoes because his family had little money. His mother asked him to get a big pot from the basement. There Michael saw Oi in the recycling bin beside the gold. Michael and Oi talked. Michael told Oi that his dad had lost his job, the hot water tank was broken, his mother’s bike was broken, and he needed new shoes. Oi would not give him any gold, and they argued. Later Michael’s father said he believed their luck would change, and Michael felt better. That night Oi remembered that he had been a cobbler in Ireland. The next morning, Michael found a new pair of green baseball shoes with gold shamrocks and strong spikes. They were very lucky shoes.

summary_text: Audrey Fay Hendrick lived in Birmingham with her mama and daddy. When Mike, also called Martin or Dr. King, came to town, her family cooked ribs, greens, sweet potato, and hot rolls. Audrey listened when grown-ups talked about segregation, which kept black and white people apart. When the grown-ups would not go, Jim said children should go. Audrey raised her hand and said she wanted to go to jail. Her mama said okay, and Audrey went with other children to protest.

Today people celebrate with church, green clothes, shamrocks, cards, songs, dances, parades, and food.

summary_text: It was the night before St Patrick’s Day, and Tim and Morin decorated the den from floor to ceiling with streamers, rainbows, and shamrocks. They also made traps with gold charms and rings because they hoped to catch a leprechaun and find his pot of gold. The children went to bed thinking about golden coins. In the morning, Dad played bagpipes, Mom made green eggs, and sang. Then the children heard a noise and ran to the hallway. They found a big mess and muddy footprints on the floor. Morin told Tim to be quiet and said they must keep looking at the leprechaun, because if they blinked, he would disappear. The footprints led under Tim’s bed and past the closet. Soon they heard giggling inside a trap. There was a tiny leprechaun in green clothes, holding something shiny and golden. Tim and Morin walked up to him and stared right into his eyes. Then they asked him to tell them where the gold was.

Joe studies inventors too, like the people who helped create ice cream cones and Unsticks. In the end, Joe says he has worked hard all summer and is excited for the special trip to the top of Ice Cream Peak.

summary_text: There was once a triangle that was always busy. It held up roofs, supported bridges, made music in an orchestra, caught the wind for sailboats, and could also be slices of pie and halves of sandwiches. Its favorite thing was to fit into the shape people made when they put their hands on their hips. The triangle liked to hear the latest news and tell it to its friends. One day, the triangle felt bored and said there must be more to life. It went to the local Shape Shifter and asked for one more side and one more angle. Poof! The triangle became a quadrilateral. The quadrilateral was happy with its new jobs, like being a baseball diamond, a checkerboard space, a screen, or a window frame. Its favorite thing was being the pages of a book. But after a while, it also grew dissatisfied and went back to the Shape Shifter for another change.
