summary_text: A square had four equal sides and four matching corners, and it was happy. On Monday, it was cut into pieces and poked full of holes, so it changed into a fountain that babbled and giggled and clapped. On Tuesday, it was torn into scraps, so it became a garden. On Wednesday, it was shredded in strips, so it became a park. On Thursday, it was shattered, so it became a bridge. On Friday, it was snipped into ribbons, so it became a river. On Saturday, it was crumpled and ripped and wrinkled, so it became a mountain. On Sunday, the square waited and waited for something else to happen, but nothing did. Its sides felt confining and its corners felt rigid and cramped. Then it changed into a window that looked out on the mountain, the river, the bridge, the park, the garden, and the fountain.

summary_text: Nikki spent one summer at her Grandma’s cottage in the North Woods after her dad drove away to work at the plant. Nikki felt sad at first because there were no other kids and no TV. She gave Nikki chores like stacking firewood, cleaning gutters, and fixing the truck. Then she taught Nikki to fish for bluegills near the lily pads. Nikki did not catch anything at first and thought the river had no fish. The next day, while waiting on the dock, Nikki found an old raft floating toward her with drawings of animals on it. Grandma helped her use the raft, and many birds and animals came close. Nikki began to draw what she saw. She spent the summer exploring, swimming, and learning about the river. On her last day, she helped a deer fawn stuck in mud, drew it on the raft, and Grandma painted over the drawing so Nikki would always be part of the river.

summary_text: The story tells about a child growing up in the mountains with grandfather and grandmother. Grandfather came home in the evening from the coal mine covered in black dust, but his lips were clean, and he kissed the child on the head. Grandmother cooked hot cornbread, pinto beans, and fried okra, and once took the child through the grass to the Johnny house at night. The family walked across the cow pasture and through the woods with towels to swim in a dark, muddy swimming hole, where they sometimes saw snakes. On the way home, they stopped at Mr. Crawford's for white butter. They also pumped water from the well, heated it, and filled round tin tubs for baths. Afterward, they stood by the old black stove while grandmother heated cocoa. On Sundays they went to church in the schoolhouse, and sometimes the congregation walked to the swimming hole for baptisms. The child’s cousin Peter was baptized there, and grandmother cried.

summary_text: The leaves had always lived in the trees, swaying in the green. Then the wind blew colder, and the leaves felt that something new was coming. Bir liked the crisp breezes. Oak came down more slowly. Maple stayed up the longest, then pulled loose and fell too. On the ground, the leaves saw boots, rakes, gutters, and dogs. A girl found them, held them close, and listened as they spoke. Fall felt new again.

video_title: Chairs on Strike (powerful lesson about kindness and respect) #toddlers #kindergarten #stories #kids
summary_text: The chairs tell about how people sit on them in many rough ways. Kids sit pretzel style, sit down hard, lean back until the chairs fall, drag them by their backs, swing them around, and smear food on them at lunch. The worst part is when someone sits on a chair and lets out a fart. One day, the chairs decide they have had enough. They gather in the classroom at night and write a strike letter to the teacher. They say they want respect and kindness before they go back to work. In the morning, the children cannot find their chairs and must stand in class all day. They can still do their schoolwork, but they do not like it. Then the children write letters back, saying they are sorry and will treat the chairs better. The chairs read the notes, return to the classroom, and the children keep their promise.

After that, Mary Ellen liked reading very much.

summary_text: Every spring, Rebecca Estelle planted vegetables for winter, but she never planted pumpkins because she hated them. When she was little, her family had almost nothing to eat except pumpkins, so she never wanted them again. One autumn, a pumpkin fell from a truck and smashed in her yard. Rebecca Estelle covered the mess with dirt and tried to forget it. In spring, she found pumpkin vines growing where the smashed pumpkin had been. She cut the vines down, but they grew back. So she stopped looking at the front yard and ignored the vines all spring and summer. Later, when she finally saw the yard again, it was full of pumpkins. Rebecca Estelle decided to give them away. She made pies and many pumpkin treats, then carved jack-o'-lanterns to make people come. The town came, ate pumpkin food, and took pumpkins home. In the end, only a few seeds were left, and Rebecca Estelle saved them for next spring.

video_title: Sick Simon by Dan Krall (Personal Health & Hygiene) #toddlers #kindergarten #education #kidsbooks
summary_text: On Monday, Simon had a cold, but he still wanted the best week ever. He kissed his family, ate his favorite breakfast, and rode the bus to school. Simon loved school, and math was his best subject, so he joined in a lot. On Tuesday, he took care of Mr. Warbles, the class chinchilla, shared snacks, and did show and tell. On Wednesday, he went on a field trip. On Thursday, recess was fun, and on Friday, he looked forward to a big kickball game. On the bus ride home, Simon heard germs talk to him. They said they spread sickness when people do not wash hands or cover mouths. Simon then covered his mouth when he sneezed and coughed, used a tissue, threw it in the trash, and washed his hands with warm, soapy water. The germs went away. Simon rested all weekend, drank lots of fluids, and by Monday he felt good again and was ready to go back to school.

video_title: Pete The Cat - Firefighter Pete Children's Read Aloud Story Book For Kids By James Dean
summary_text: Principal Nancy tells Pete and his class they are going on a class trip. They ride a bright yellow bus to the firehouse. Pete and the other kids see the big red firehouse, two fire trucks, and the firefighters’ tools. The firefighters show the children around and let them ring the brass firebell and slide down the pole. Then the kids try on firefighter gear. Pete puts on black overalls, tall boots, a yellow jacket, and a black helmet. The gear is very heavy, and he can barely move. The children also look inside a fire truck. Cie honks the horn, and Pete turns on the sirens and lights. Then the fire alarm rings. The firefighters hurry to get ready, jump into the truck, and drive to a fire in town. They connect the truck to the hydrant, use the hose, and spray water on the fire. Pete helps aim the hose. When they hear grumpy toad on the roof, they raise a ladder and help him climb down. The fire goes out, everyone is safe, and the firefighters tell Pete, “Good job, Pete!”

summary_text: On Halloween, Charlie Brown raked leaves while Snoopy played in them. Lucy came with a football and asked Charlie Brown to kick it. But when he ran up to kick the ball, Lucy pulled it away again, and Charlie Brown fell hard. Inside, Linus wrote a letter to the Great Pumpkin and told Charlie Brown that the Great Pumpkin rises from the pumpkin patch on Halloween night with toys for children. Lucy laughed at Linus, but Sally listened and wanted to wait with him in the pumpkin patch. Linus mailed his letter with help from his blanket. Later, the children wore costumes, went trick-or-treating, and then went to Violet’s Halloween party. Charlie Brown got a rock, Lucy got candy, and Linus stayed in the pumpkin patch with Sally, waiting for the Great Pumpkin.

summary_text: Elsa says she is royal, neat, and purple. Anna says she likes color, noise, and shine, and her words are pink and crowded. When they were little, the sisters were close. Elsa wished for a sister more like herself. Anna liked fun and play, while Elsa wanted a sister who would climb trees with her and study geometry with her. The pranksters agreed to slow down in town, and everyone enjoyed the day together.

summary_text: Today, the friends are fishing. One friend catches a fish, but then they see a balloon in the sky. It looks like Donald’s balloon, and there is no pilot. The friends want to catch it before it floats away. Their boat gets stuck in the middle of the lake, so they ask the turtles for help. The turtles bring a sail, and the friends use it to get back to shore. Then they get into their van and follow the balloon. The balloon floats farther away, so they go to the clubhouse and use the mouse spotter to look for it. Donald spots the balloon, but it flies away again. Turtles brings the tune plane, and the friends chase the balloon. It goes higher and higher and into outer space. Then Toodles brings a rocket ship. The friends blast off into space, find Donald’s balloon, and grab it before it gets away again.

A dragonfly flies by, and Blue begins making boats, stacking stones, and building dams. She also joins Dad at Daddy Day Spa, where Bingo puts mud on Dad's face and Blue brings more mud. At the end, Blue knows the creek is beautiful.

Mowgli did not want to leave, so he ran into the jungle. There he met Baloo the bear, then was taken by King Louie and the monkeys. Bagheera and Baloo rescued him, and after a fight with Shere Khan, Mowgli used fire to scare the tiger away. In the end, Mowgli saw a girl at the water hole, followed her to the man village, and went there to live.

video_title: 🐘🎪 Kids Read Aloud Books : Disney Dumbo
summary_text:
One morning, storks flew over the circus with baby bundles. Mrs. Jumbo looked up and waited for her baby, but at first no bundle came to her. The next day, the circus train moved on. Then Mr. Stork came late and gave Mrs. Jumbo a bundle. Inside was a baby elephant with big blue eyes. Mrs. Jumbo named him Jumbo Jr. When the baby sneezed, his ears opened very wide. The other elephants laughed and called him Dumbo. Mrs. Jumbo loved her baby and held him close.

Later, some boys teased Dumbo in the tent. Mrs. Jumbo got angry and threw straw to make them leave. The ring master took Mrs. Jumbo away and locked her in a wagon. Dumbo cried for his mother. Then Timothy the mouse came and became his friend. Timothy made a plan to help Dumbo and his mother. Dumbo later flew through the air with a magic feather, then learned he did not need it. He could fly by himself. After that, Dumbo became famous, and Mrs. Jumbo was freed. Dumbo was happiest when he was back with his mother.

Joy then suggested making an origami figure. Anxiety folded paper too, and when she worried it might be crushed, Sadness helped her think of a plan. Anxiety felt better, yawned, and kept folding until everyone went back to bed.

The wolf huffed and puffed, but he could not blow it down. He climbed down the chimney and fell into boiling water. After that, the three pigs stayed safe in the brick house.

summary_text: On a beautiful spring morning, the animals in the forest came to see a new baby deer. Thumper called for friend owl, and everyone gathered around Bambi and his mother. There, Bambi met Faline and played with her until a loud noise scared the deer away. Bambi got lost, but the Great Prince of the forest helped him return to his mother. After that, the forest became peaceful again. Bambi later learned about winter, the loss of his mother, love for Faline, the forest fire, and the birth of his twins with Faline.

At first she left them alone, and they played by themselves. But they soon learned that playing alone was not as fun as playing together. Boo found a photo of himself and P, and both felt sad and cried because they missed their friend. Ellie saw this and pushed the wall Far Far Away. Then P and Pocoyo saw each other again and ran to hug. They learned that making up is better than being angry.

Then a dinosaur spoke to him and said it would like to play with Danny too. The dinosaur let Danny ride on its back, and they went into town. They stopped at red lights, walked by a dog, and moved carefully so they would not bump houses and stores. They saw buses, buildings, and a ball game. Danny and the dinosaur also went to the zoo, but everyone came to look at the dinosaur instead of the animals. Danny then found his friends, and the children asked for rides. The dinosaur gave them rides, played hide and seek, and was found many times. At the end, Danny and the dinosaur said goodbye. The dinosaur went back to the museum, and Danny went home alone after a wonderful day.

Marshall put the cards on Rubble’s digger, and the pups went to find Mr. Postman. They passed a spooky old house and heard a scratch, so they ran away. In town, they gave Mr. Postman the cards. Mayor Goodway said Adventure Bay was the friendliest town. Then Mayor Humdinger came from Foggy Bottom with a kitten and more cards. The kitten threw the cards, and Mayor Humdinger said Adventure Bay was not the friendliest anymore. He challenged Adventure Bay to a Friendship Day contest. The pups delivered cards all over town. Chase helped with a big cake, Rocky fixed the cake after it tipped, and Skye and Chase helped with balloons and bunnies. In the end, the pups found Miss Marjorie and Maynard the raccoon at the spooky house, and everyone met at Town Hall for a big party.

video_title: 🧌🛸 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney World Off Reading Star Wars : Death Star Battle
summary_text: Luke, Han, and Princess Leia escaped from Darth Vader and brought secret battle plans to the Rebel base on Yavin IV. The plans showed that the Death Star had one small weakness deep inside a trench. The Rebel Pilots got ready to attack, but Han Solo first decided to leave because he thought the plan was foolish. Luke felt sad, and he missed Obi-Wan Kenobi. Then Luke flew with R2-D2 and the other x-wing pilots toward the huge Death Star. The ship’s cannons and Darth Vader’s tie fighters attacked them. Some pilots missed the target, and Leia and C-3PO worried on Yavin IV because the Death Star was getting close. Luke heard Obi-Wan’s voice telling him to use the force. Han returned and helped Luke by chasing away Vader. Then Luke closed his eyes, used the force, and fired into the weakness. The Death Star exploded, and the rebels hugged and celebrated their victory.

The map could help Leia find her brother, Luke, a great Jedi Knight. Poe told Lor to hide and gave the map to BB-8 so the First Order could not take it. The First Order captured Poe and took him to Kylo Ren. Kylo Ren wanted the map and was angry when Poe did not have it. Poe said BB-8 had the map. FN2187 freed Poe, and they escaped together by stealing a TIE fighter. They flew into space, got away from the First Order ship, and Poe named his new friend Finn. Poe then flew back toward Jakku to find BB-8.

video_title: 🏰🌪️ Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney’s Tangled
summary_text: Rapunzel lived in a tall tower with her very long, magical hair. Every day, Mother Gothel called, “Rapunzel, let down your hair!” and Rapunzel pulled her up. Mother Gothel used the magic in Rapunzel’s hair to stay young and pretty. Rapunzel did not know that Mother Gothel had taken her from the King and the Queen. Rapunzel only had one friend, a chameleon named Pascal. On her birthday, Rapunzel watched sparkling lights rise into the sky and wished to see them. Just before her 18th birthday, Flynn, a thief, climbed into her tower while running from Maximus, a horse from the royal guard. Rapunzel asked Flynn to take her to the lights. They traveled together, met friendly people in a pub, escaped from Maximus, and reached the kingdom. There, Rapunzel saw the lanterns, learned she was the Lost Princess, and later went back to the tower. Mother Gothel hurt Flynn, but Rapunzel’s magic saved him. Rapunzel went home to her real parents, the King and Queen.

video_title: 🦆 Kids Book Read Aloud: One Duck Stuck by Phyllis Root
summary_text: One duck gets stuck in the muck down by the Deep green Marsh. The duck calls for help. First, two fish Tales swim to the duck, but there is no luck, and the duck stays stuck in the squishy fishy Marsh. Then three moose munching on Spruce plod over, but the duck still cannot get out. Four crickets chirping in the thickets leap to help, then five frogs hopping on logs, six skunks climbing over trunks, and seven snails making slippery Trails. Each time, the duck stays stuck deep in the muck. Next, eight possums nibbling on blossoms, nine snakes leaving little wakes, and ten dragonflies zooming through the skies come to help. At last, all of them work together. Splish bump bleep plop plunk slush swash link zing. The duck gets out of the muck and says, Thank you!

Then Elsa woke Anna up and told her she would have a very special birthday. Elsa made new dresses for both sisters and led Anna through Arendelle to find presents. Anna found a bracelet, an Olaf cuckoo clock, sunflowers, a family portrait, silk stockings, and a fishing pole. Elsa kept sneezing, and tiny snowmen kept popping out, but Anna did not see them. In the village, a children’s choir sang for Anna, and more little snowmen ran around. Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf tried to keep the cake safe. Elsa gave Anna one last gift at the Clock Tower, but Elsa became very sick and nearly fell. Anna helped Elsa to bed. Elsa said sorry, but Anna said the day was wonderful. At the end, everyone sang happy birthday in the courtyard, and Olaf brought the little snowmen to the Ice Palace.

Then he heard steam and saw a train outside his house. A conductor invited him aboard the Polar Express and took him to the North Pole. Many children in pajamas rode with him, sang Christmas carols, and ate candy. The train raced through dark forests, high mountains, icy plains, and a frozen desert until it reached the North Pole, a city full of toy factories and elves. At the center, Santa chose the boy for the first gift of Christmas. The boy asked for a silver bell from Santa’s sleigh. Santa gave him the bell, but it fell through a hole in the boy’s pocket on the way home. On Christmas morning, his sister Sarah found the bell in a box with a note from Mr. C. The boy could hear the bell, but others could not. As years passed, only he could still hear it.

video_title: 🧪⚗️ Kids Book Read Aloud: Pete the Cat and the Supercool Science Fair
summary_text: Pete the Cat could not wait for Friday because his school was having a science fair. Pete had never been a scientist before, and now he could try. His teacher put the students into groups, and Pete worked with Cali, Gus, and Squirrel. They talked about many ideas, like a mini submarine, a giant tree, and an invisible guitar. Then Gus suggested making a volcano, and everyone liked that idea. At Pete’s house, they checked a big book of experiments and gathered glue, water, newspaper, paint, a plastic bottle, vinegar, baking soda, and dish soap. Pete and Gus mixed the glue and water, while Cali and Squirrel tore newspaper strips. They made a sticky volcano, but the brown paint was really blue. They decided to keep it blue and tested the lava. The volcano erupted and made a big mess. On Friday, their blue volcano amazed the class, and glitter lava burst out at the fair. Pete said science is hard work, but a good team makes it easier.

video_title: 🎄Kids Book Read Aloud: Oh, the Places You'll Go! by Dr.Seuss
summary_text: The story tells a child that today is their day and they are off to great places. The child has brains in their head and feet in their shoes, so they can choose where to go. As they keep going, they may fly high, join the High Flyers, and take the lead. But sometimes they will not be first, and sometimes they will get hung up, left in a Lurch, and fall into a slump. They may come to a place with no signs and feel confused about which way to go. They may also find the Waiting place, where everyone is just waiting for things. The story says they will escape that place, keep moving, face scary things, and go on until they succeed and reach their mountain.

When the work was done, they went home and said good job to the boy.

The truck tries to move, but the gears grind, the engine roars, and it cannot go even one inch more. The truck calls for help. First, a car full of travelers comes by, and the car and truck try to pull together, but the dump truck still will not move. Then a van driven by a moving man arrives, but that does not work either. Next, a Jeep, then a bus full of youngsters, all try to help, and each time the truck stays stuck. At last, a tow truck comes with a mechanic. The mechanic hooks up the truck, and at once the dump truck is free. Then the car, van, Jeep, and bus all move on, and the dump truck rolls away to deliver its load.

video_title: 🐯Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney Princess : Jasmine the Matchmaker
summary_text: One morning, Jasmine and Raja rode in their Royal Coach through Agrabah. They stopped at a big colorful tent and saw a sign for a circus. The next day, Jasmine went with Aladdin, and Raja came too. At the circus, Raja watched all the acts, but he did not look happy. Then the circus owner announced Malika the star of the show, and Raja saw a beautiful tigress. Raja loved Malika right away. After the show, Jasmine asked to meet Malika backstage, but the circus owner said she was needed for the circus. Raja went home sad. Jasmine tried to cheer him with food, a new bed, and other tigers, but nothing worked. Later, the circus owner came to the palace with Malika and said she was in love too. He gave her to Jasmine, and Raja was happy again. Jasmine then moved the circus to a park next to the palace, and everyone celebrated.

video_title: 🐛 Kids Book Read Aloud: Pete the Cat and the Cool Caterpillar by James Dean
summary_text: Pete goes on a bug safari with his friends to look for bugs. Cali finds a tiny black ant building an ant hill. Gus sees a round red ladybug in the mint patch with nine spots. Marty spots a big black spider that caught a fly. Then Pete finds a green caterpillar in a flower pot and says he will bring it home to show Mom and Dad. At home, Mom and Dad help Pete make a home for the caterpillar in a big jar. Dad makes little holes in the lid, and Pete adds leaves and a twig. The next morning, the caterpillar is gone, but Mom and Dad show Pete that it is inside the jar as a pupa. Pete waits while Cali, Gus, and Marty visit and ask if it has come out yet. One day, the pupa wiggles, cracks open, and a butterfly comes out. Pete, Mom, Dad, and his friends watch it fly away. Pete says they should find a new caterpillar.

video_title: 🐢 Kids Book Read Aloud: Franklin Goes to School by Paulette Bourgeois
summary_text: Franklin could count by twos, tie his shoes, zip zippers, and button buttons, but he felt worried about his first day of school. He woke up very early and told Godi his fish, “It’s my first day of school.” He packed his new pencil case with a ruler, a pencil, an eraser, and 12 colored pencils. Then he woke his parents and said he could not be late. His mother and father told him it was too early and made him a good breakfast. Franklin said his tummy felt like it had jumping frogs. On the way to the bus stop, he wanted to go home. His parents hugged him and showed him his friends waiting for the bus. On the bus, Franklin and the other children worried, too. At school, Mr. Owl welcomed them, showed them where to go, and gave them fruit. Franklin learned, drew, built with blocks, sorted money, and asked Mr. Owl to help him read his favorite book. He had a wonderful day. When he got home, he had forgotten his jumpy tummy and gave his parents two pictures and big hugs.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: I Need My Monster by Amanda Noll
summary_text: The child found a note saying Gabe had gone fishing and would be back in a week. The child wanted a monster under the bed to help with sleep, so the child knocked on the floorboards and waited. First came Herbert, who had a soft voice, no claws, and did not seem scary enough. Then came Ralph, who had neat fur and shiny claws with nail polish, but he also was not scary enough. Next came Cynthia, a girl monster with sharp claws and a slimy tail, but the child said a boy monster was needed. After that came Mac, who had scruffy fur, claws, and a long tongue, but he still did not feel right. Then Gabe came back from fishing. Gabe had green ooze, a spiked tail, and scary claws. The child said no other monster could scare like Gabe. Gabe stayed under the bed, and the child pulled up the blanket and got ready to sleep.

video_title: Kids Book Read Aloud: Goodnight, Little Bear by Igloo Books
summary_text: The first snow fell, and Mommy bear told little bear it was time to hibernate. She said hibernate means to find a cozy place and sleep all winter. Mommy bear made a bed of dry leaves in a cave under a rock. Little bear lay down beside her, but he could not sleep. He felt something was missing, so he got up quietly and walked into the dark forest. He saw wood cutters carrying heavy wood. When they saw him, they shouted, “Help a bear!” and ran away, leaving their wood behind. Little bear kept walking. Soon he found a small wooden house by a frozen pond. Inside was an old lady. She did not shout. She said, “Come in. Come and warm yourself by the fire.” She stroked his head, gave him honey, washed him, and then gave him a teddy bear. Little bear went back to Mommy bear and slept with the teddy bear at last.

video_title: 🐼 Kids Book Read Aloud: Panda Bear, Panda Bear, What Do You See? by Eric Carle
summary_text: A panda bear asks, “What do you see?” The bald eagle answers that it sees a water buffalo charging by. The water buffalo sees a spider monkey swinging by. The spider monkey sees a green sea turtle swimming by. Then the green sea turtle sees a macaroni penguin strutting by, and the macaroni penguin sees a sea lion splashing by. Next, the sea lion sees a red wolf sneaking by, and the red wolf sees a whooping crane flying by. The whooping crane sees a black panther strolling by, and the black panther sees a dreaming child watching over it. At the end, the dreaming child sees all the animals together: panda bear, spider monkey, green sea turtle, red wolf, whooping crane, bald eagle, water buffalo, macaroni penguin, sea lion, and black panther. They are all wild and free.

summary_text: There were three brothers called the Billy Goats Gruff. They wanted to cross a brook and go up a hillside with thick green grass. Then Middle Billy Goat Gruff crossed. The troll woke up again and again wanted to eat him. The middle goat said to wait for his bigger brother, and the troll let him pass. Last came Big Billy Goat Gruff. He was so heavy that the bridge shook. The troll tried to stop him, but Big Billy Goat Gruff rushed at him, and the troll fell into the water. Then all three goats ate the grass on the hillside.

summary_text: A donkey worked for a farmer for many years, but he wanted to leave and see the world. The farmer did not like this, but he finally let the donkey go. The donkey walked toward Bremen because he had heard about music there and wanted to be a street musician. On the way, he met an old dog who was tired from running. The donkey invited the dog to join him, saying they could make music together. Soon they met a sad old cat who wanted to see the world too, and she joined them. Then they found a rooster on a farmyard gate, and he also came with them. That night they could not reach Bremen, so they found a house, scared the people inside with their loud music, and ate the supper left behind. Later, an uncle came to check the house, but the animals frightened him away, and the family ran off too. The four animals stayed in the house and were safe there.

She had done all the work, so she ate the bread all by herself.

video_title: PJ Funnybunny's Bag of Tricks | READ ALOUD book for kids 🐰💫
summary_text: One day Mr. Funny Bunny brought home a surprise for PJ: a magic kit. PJ thanked his dad and opened the box. Inside were a magic wand, a red scarf, a top hat, and a magic book. He also read his mother’s mind, made Honey Bunny’s doll float, and made Pot’s Pig’s candy bar disappear. When his family and friends wanted other things, PJ got mad and said he would do the biggest trick of all. Then he disappeared. Grandma and Grandpa came, and everyone looked for PJ. At last, his top hat hopped, PJ jumped out, and the Funny Bunnies were glad to see him. It was his best trick of all.

summary_text: Simon the squirrel bounces around under his tree and looks for acorns to save for winter. He gathers nuts, but when his friends start playing, he joins them and says he will collect the nuts another day. The warm autumn days pass, and a chilly wind begins to blow, but Simon does not stop to prepare. Then winter comes quickly. Snow falls, the ground gets covered, and Simon realizes he does not have enough food. He feels cold, scared, and alone, and he calls for help. A blue feathered bird and wise friend Olly come to him. Olly helps Simon calm down, breathe, and look around. Simon learns he can be strong. He digs in the snow, finds the buried acorns, and carries them home. In the end, Simon has enough food for winter and feels proud.

video_title: A Day at the Farm || Read-Aloud for Kids
summary_text: Mother duck takes her ducklings to meet the lamb and the falls. Mother horse watches while they all make friends. A brown and white dog looks after the animals at the farm. He watches the cow and her calves as they come to see the little fall in the field. The farmer feeds the hens corn at feeding time, and the other animals are hungry too. The goat eats hay, and baby goats, called kids, play games with the piglets. The chicks want to play, but they are too small. The sheepdog looks after the sheep in the meadow and teaches her puppies. The animals watch the ducklings learn to swim. Later, the piglets roll in the mud while the others watch. Then the lambs and baby donkeys wait for a drink of water from the pond. At the end, the foal and the kids slide by the pond, the ducklings rest, and the cats climb the tree.

video_title: Little Larks 1 - Belief - Meet Me at the Moon
summary_text: Beneath the shade of the boa Bob tree, little one sang the calling song, and Mama came with a loving muzzle. Mama said the land was dry and she must climb the highest mountain to ask the skies for rain. Little one did not want Mama to go. Mama told little one to listen for her sound on the wind, to feel her love in the warmth of the Sun, and to look at the brightest star at night. She said they would meet at the moon where the sky touches the earth. Then Mama left. Each night little one looked at the brightest star and each day listened to the wind and felt the Sun. After many days, rain came, but Mama did not return. Later, little one saw the moon, sang the calling song, and the moon made a path. Mama answered, and they found each other again.

summary_text: There was a red crayon who went to school. His teacher asked him to draw a red strawberry, but he could not do it well. His grandparents also tried to help when he made a self-portrait for parents’ night, but he still had trouble. The other crayons and art supplies gave advice too. They said he was broken, too tight, not sharp enough, or lazy. The masking tape and scissors even tried to fix him, but he still could not draw the way they wanted. After that, he made many blue things, like bluebells, blueberries, a blue whale, and blue jeans. Everyone was happy with his work, and he kept making more blue pictures.

summary_text: A long time ago in Africa, Navarro lived in a village with his two beautiful daughters, Manyara and Niasia. Manyara was often mean to Niasia and said she would one day be queen, while Niasia stayed kind and worked in her garden. One day a messenger came from the king’s city and said the king wanted a wife. Navarro prepared to send both daughters, but Manyara tried to go first. On the road, she met a hungry boy, an old woman, and a grove of laughing trees, but she was rude and did not help them. Niasia later met the same boy and gave him food, gave the old woman seeds, and was polite to the trees. When the party reached the city, Manyara ran out in fear and warned Niasia about a monster. Niasia went inside and found Nyoka, the garden snake, who changed into the king and chose her as his wife. Manyara became a servant in the queen’s household.

video_title: Little Larks 12 - Personal Leadership - The Most Magnificent Thing
summary_text: A girl and her best friend do many things together. One day the girl decides to make the most magnificent thing. She hires an assistant, gathers supplies, and starts working. She tinkerers, hammers, measures, saws, glues, twists, and paints, while her assistant helps by pouncing, growling, chewing, circling, and tugging. But each time they finish, the thing is wrong. It is square, round, fuzzy, long, short, rough, smooth, big, small, and even smells like stinky cheese, but it is still not magnificent. The girl gets angrier and works faster until she hurts her finger and shouts that she quits. Her assistant takes her for a walk. As they walk, she sees that some parts of her wrong things are actually good. By the end of the trail, she knows how to make it right. She works carefully again, and this time she makes the most magnificent thing.

video_title: The Elephant and the Blind Men: A Powerful Lesson on Perspective  | learn english through story |
summary_text: In a small village, six Blind Men heard that a huge elephant had come to town. They had never met an elephant before, so they went to learn about it by touching it with their hands. The first man touched the side and said the elephant was like a wall. The second touched a tusk and said it was like a spear. The third touched the trunk and said it was like a snake. The fourth touched a leg and said it was like a tree. The fifth touched an ear and said it was like a fan. The sixth touched the tail and said it was like a rope. Soon they began to argue because each one thought only his answer was right. A wise old man came and told them they were all correct. He explained that each man had felt only one part of the elephant, so each description was only part of the whole. The Blind Men stopped arguing and understood that they had to listen to each other to see the full truth.

She entered it in a school contest, read it to her class, and won first place. Lily hugged Percy and said, “We did it together!”

summary_text: In a quiet countryside, an old woman named Mrs. Aara lived in a peaceful cottage. One day, Clara came to her gate feeling sad and full of worry about her past. Peter Pan and Tinkerbell came to the nursery to find Peter’s lost shadow. Wendy woke up, sewed the shadow back on, and said she had to grow up the next day. Peter did not want her to leave, so he invited Wendy, John, and Michael to fly to Neverland. They used a wonderful thought and pixie dust, then flew to the island. There they saw Mermaid Lagoon, the Indian camp, and the Jolly Roger. Captain Hook wanted to catch Peter Pan because Peter had beaten him in a sword fight and a crocodile had eaten Hook’s hand. Peter and Wendy tried to rescue Tiger Lily, who had been kidnapped by Hook. Later, Hook trapped Tinkerbell, tricked her, and learned Peter’s hideout. In the end, Peter saved Wendy and the others, Hook fell into the water, and the children flew home to London.

video_title: Up Read Along Storybook: Watch Dug in HD
summary_text: Doug, Carl Fredrickson, and Russell went looking for a place to camp for the night. Doug, who could talk with humans by a special collar, found a clearing with trees and a nice view. Carl and Russell set up the tents, cooked dinner, and roasted marshmallows. When it was bedtime, Russell saw paw prints near the campfire. Carl said he would keep watch, and Doug promised to stay awake too. Doug sat by the tents like a guard. He scared a squirrel, tripped Russell’s tent rope, and later a bat made him spill the lemonade. Then Doug heard scratching and found a raccoon stealing food from the picnic basket. Doug tugged the sausages away and chased the raccoon off. He saved breakfast and felt proud. By morning, Carl saw the mess, found Doug asleep, and told him, “Good dog, Doug!”

summary_text: Mirabel Madrigal lives with her family in the magical Encanto. Long ago, Abuela Alma and Abuelo Pedro fled danger, and Pedro was lost. A miracle came from Abuela’s candle, and the Encanto grew. Abuela says the family must keep earning the miracle. Everyone has a gift except Mirabel. At Antonio’s fifth birthday, he gets the gift to talk to animals. Mirabel walks him to his door, and the family is happy for him. Then Mirabel sees cracks in the house. She tries to warn everyone, but the cracks disappear, and no one believes her. Her mother comforts her, and Abuela worries that the magic is fading. Mirabel finds Bruno’s broken vision, helps him finish it, and learns she must talk to Isabela. Isabela shows she can grow prickly plants too. The cracks grow worse, the candle goes out, and the family loses their gifts. Abuela later tells Mirabel that Pedro’s love made the miracle. Mirabel returns home, and the family works together to rebuild the Encanto.

video_title: All By Myself by Mercer Mayer - Little Critter - Read Aloud Books for Children - Storytime
summary_text: The child gets out of bed all by himself. He buttons his overalls and brushes his fur and shoes. He pours juice for his little sister and helps her eat breakfast. He pulls a duck for her, drives his truck, and rides his bike. He gives a drink to his bear, kicks his ball, and rolls on the ground. He pounds with his hammer and sails his boat. He looks after his little sister and helps Dad trim a bush or ice a cake for Mom. He looks at a book and finds a mouse picture. Then he puts his toys away, gets into his pajamas, and brushes his teeth. At the end, he cannot go to sleep without a story. Good night.

video_title: Just a Mess by Mercer Mayer - Little Critter - Read Aloud Books for Children - Storytime
summary_text: Today, the child could not find the baseball mitt. The child looked in the tree house, under the back steps, and asked mom. Mom said to try the room. In the room, the child saw a big mess. Mom said it was time to clean the room, and the child asked for help. Mom said, “You made the mess, so you can clean up the mess.” Dad was busy in the yard, the little sister said, “No way,” and the baby did not understand. So the child cleaned alone. The child put things in the closet, clothes in the drawers, games straight, books away, and the rest under the bed. Then the bed was made. The child vacuumed the floor because mom said no to washing it. At the end, the child looked for the missing pillow and found the baseball mitt on the other side of the bed.

video_title: The New Potty by Mercer Mayer - Little Critter - Read Aloud Books for Children - Storytime
summary_text: The boy says he is a big boy and knows how to use the potty. He wears underpants with skateboards on them. His little sister is still a baby and wears diapers. He likes to play with her, but sometimes she smells funny, and Mom changes her diaper. One day, Mom says it is time for little sister to use a potty. They go to the store and buy a pink potty chair. At home, the sister wants to carry it in, but she cries and will not sit on it. Mom says she is scared. The boy sits on the potty first, and then his sister is not scared. He gives her a book, and she does not want to get off. She sits on the potty in the downstairs room, at dinner, and even near her bed at night. In the morning, she uses the potty, gets new underpants, and later has an accident in the sandbox. The next time, she uses the potty the right way. Everyone is proud.

video_title: Just Me and My Puppy by Mercer Mayer - Little Critter - Read Aloud Books for Children - Storytime
summary_text: The child wanted a puppy just for himself, so he traded his baseball mitt for one. His baby sister liked the puppy right away, and Mom and Dad were surprised. They said he could keep the puppy if he took care of him himself. So the child feeds the puppy every morning, puts on the leash, and takes him for walks. He teaches the puppy to heel, sit, stay, play dead, roll over, and fetch. The puppy still needs practice, but he learns many things. The puppy also helps around the house. He is a good guard dog, brings in the paper for Dad, and stays with the child while he does homework. When the puppy gets dirty, the child gives him a bath and dries him off. Then they get ready for bed together.

video_title: Just Me and My Mom by Mercer Mayer - Little Critter - Read Aloud Books for Children - Storytime
summary_text: Just me and my mom went to the city. Mom gave me money to buy train tickets, and I wanted to help her get on the train, but the steps were too high. Mom helped me instead. Then the conductor came, and the tickets were gone, so Mom paid him more money. The city was busy, and I held Mom’s hand. We went to the Museum of Natural History and saw rooms full of old dinosaur bones. I picked up a little dinosaur egg to show Mom, but someone took it away. I tried on costumes for Mom, and a museum guard did not like that. Next we went to the aquarium and saw fish and seals. Mom got mad because she could not find me. I ran to the front to see the seals better. We also went to an art museum, had lunch, bought a hot dog, and went to a store where I tried on clothes. We took a taxi back to the train station, and Mom bought the tickets this time. We went home, and I stayed awake almost all the way.

video_title: Halfway Herbert by Francis Chan - Children's Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Herbert Halwe was known as Halfway Herbert because he did many things only halfway. He brushed only part of his teeth, did half his homework, answered only half the test questions, ate only part of his meals, and listened only halfway to his soccer coach. One day, Herbert tried to ride his bike with only one shoe tied. His shoelace got caught in the wheel, and he crashed into his dad’s car. His bike bent, his leg hurt, and the car got dented. When his dad asked what happened, Herbert told only half the truth. Then Mr. Rug, the next door neighbor, called and said he saw the crash. Herbert’s dad explained that half the truth is a whole lie and that Jesus wants people to follow him with their whole hearts. Herbert prayed for help, and God gave him the Holy Spirit. After that, Herbert finished things, listened well, and obeyed better.

video_title: The Story of St. Nicholas by Cheryl Odden - Children's Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Nicholas was born in Lysia to rich parents, but when he was still young, both of them died and left him their money. Nicholas decided to use it to help poor people. He heard about a father who had three daughters but did not have enough money to help them marry. At night, Nicholas secretly climbed the house and threw a bag of gold into the daughters’ room three nights in a row. On the third night, the father stayed awake, caught Nicholas, and learned it was a young man helping them. Nicholas asked him not to tell anyone, and the father promised. Later, Nicholas traveled to the Holy Land, prayed in Bethlehem and in Jesus’ empty tomb, and then returned by ship. A storm came, Nicholas prayed, and the sea became calm. When the ship reached Meera, the church leaders chose Nicholas to be bishop.

video_title: A Little Prairie House by Laura Ingalls Wilder
summary_text: Laura traveled across the giant Prairie in a covered wagon with her paw, ma, big sister Mary, little sister Carrie, and their bulldog Jack. They were looking for a place to build a house. One morning Laura and Mary woke before the sun, ate cornmeal mush, and helped ma wash the dishes. Then paw drove the wagon until he stopped and said this was the place for their house. Paw and ma unloaded the wagon while Laura, Mary, and Jack watched. Paw then drove away to bring back logs from the creek bottom. Laura felt frightened without the wagon, but she helped ma while Mary watched baby Carrie. For many days paw hauled logs and made piles for the house and stable. When there were enough logs, paw and ma began building the house together. Later paw met Mr. Edwards, who lived across the creek. Mr. Edwards came to help finish the house, and he and paw worked fast, cut a door and windows, and then stayed for supper. That night paw played his fiddle, Mr. Edwards danced, and the family sang under the big moon.

video_title: A New Coat For Anna by Harriet Ziefert - Children's Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Winter came, and Anna needed a new coat because her old blue coat was too small. Her mother had once hoped to buy one after the war, but the stores were still empty and there was no money. So Anna's mother thought of a way to trade special things for what they needed. First, she and Anna went to a farmer and asked for wool from his sheep. The farmer said they must wait until spring, so Anna visited the sheep often, asked if their wool was growing, fed them hay, and gave them hugs. In spring, the farmer sheared the sheep, and Anna's mother traded a gold watch for the wool. Then they traded a lamp to an old woman for yarn, red lingan berries made the yarn red, and a weaver traded cloth for a garnet necklace. At last a tailor made the coat, and Anna wore it home. At Christmas, the helper trades were remembered, and everyone shared cake and joy.

video_title: MICKEY MOUSE's Book of Cars and Trucks | Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: Marty and Ferdy had homework. They needed to write a report about their favorite car or truck. Uncle Mickey said he could help. He took the boys in his new convertible and drove them around town. They saw a mail truck, a garbage truck, a backhoe, and a dump truck. They also saw a cement mixer. Then they passed a supermarket and saw a soda truck, a dairy truck, and a bakery truck. At the firehouse, the firefighters let the boys sit on a hook and ladder truck. Next they went to the racetrack and saw Formula One racers and hot rods. On the highway, they saw road workers, a truck with asphalt, and a steamroller. Then Mickey’s car stopped because it had no gas. A police car called for a tow truck, and an ice cream truck gave the boys ice cream. The tow truck took the car to a gas station. The mechanic filled the tank, and the next day the boys wrote about Uncle Mickey’s car.

summary_text: Donald Duck took pizzas out of the oven when Huey, Dewey, and Louie came into the kitchen. Donald had made different pizzas: pineapple and sardines for himself, pepperoni for Daisy, and sausage for the boys. He told them not to touch the pizzas and went to get Daisy. While they were gone, a shaggy brown bear came to the house. He smelled the pizzas, crawled through the open window, and ate Donald’s pineapple and sardine pizza because it was just right for him. Then he sat on the couch, tried Daisy’s chair, and finally rocked in Donald’s favorite rocker until it tipped over. After that, he went upstairs, tried the boys’ beds, and fell asleep in Donald’s bed. When Donald, Daisy, and the boys came back, they saw the eaten pizzas and the mess. Donald followed the clues upstairs and found the sleeping bear. Soon Charlie from Charlie’s Pizza arrived, said the bear was his pet, and took him home. Charlie then gave Donald and the others three big hot pizzas as a reward.

Pluto sniffed the ground and ran after a smell, pulling Mickey along. Pluto found a bone near Butch, a big Bulldog, and took it. Butch woke up and chased Pluto. Two men came and said they hid a package of jewels there. Pluto woke up, grabbed the package, and Mickey found him. The police caught the thieves, and Mickey got the reward. Pluto got a new collar and a bone.

video_title: MICKEY MOUSE and the Pet Shop | Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: Mickey Mouse loves animals, so he agrees to watch Mr. Palmer’s pet shop for one night. Mr. Palmer leaves and says he will be back tomorrow afternoon. Mickey looks at the animals, but one little puppy keeps whimpering. Mickey takes the puppy out, but the puppy runs to the fishbowl, knocks it over, and sends the fish flying. Mickey catches the fish and puts it in a new bowl. Then a customer comes in, and Mickey forgets to lock the kennel door. The puppy gets out again and frees the mice, so the customer runs away. Mickey puts the pets back and locks the kennel this time. That night the puppy howls, so Mickey lets him sleep under the covers. In the morning the shop is messy, and Mickey finds the puppy in the basement. Mickey cleans up, and the puppy helps him sweep and dust. Mr. Palmer returns, gives Mickey his paycheck, and thanks him. Mickey takes the puppy instead of the money and names him Pluto.

video_title: MICKEY MOUSE and the Lucky Goose Chase | Bedtime Story for Kids
summary_text: Mickey Mouse, Minnie, Morty, and Ferdy went to the farm to get Sweetheart, the boys’ pet calf, ready for the county fair. Commander, a big goose, kept following them and causing trouble. The boys washed Sweetheart, combed her coat, polished her hooves, and oiled her halter until she was ready. Then they loaded Sweetheart onto the truck, and Commander climbed on too. At the fair, Commander pecked Mickey’s shoe and knocked over a bucket of water. The next morning, Sweetheart was missing from her stall. Mickey, Minnie, Morty, and Ferdy searched all over the fairgrounds, but they could not find her. Then they heard Commander squawking near a cotton candy stand, and he led them to Sweetheart. She was covered with grain and molasses from the feed room. Mickey and the others washed her and brushed her again. They hurried Sweetheart to the judging area just in time, and she won first prize in the calf contest. Minnie gave Commander a blue ribbon too.

summary_text: Kanga told Ru that his babysitter would be Pooh while she went shopping and to dinner with Aunt Satie. Ru did not want to be babysitted. The friends thought there were no more months, but Christopher Robin said there would be a new year with new months and new calendars for everyone. The friends were glad and celebrated the New Year together.

Then the friends started a new game, and Piglet began counting.

summary_text: One sunny spring day, Tigger and Rue bounced to Christopher Robin. Christopher Robin told them that tomorrow was Mother’s Day. Roo wanted to give Mama, Kanga, something extra special. Eeyore’s kite was missing its tail, but Roo found it and gave it back. On festival day, the wind was very weak, and the kites would not fly well. The friends went off to do other things until the wind returned. Later, strong wind blew through the wood, and the friends hurried back to the festival. This time, the wind lifted them and their kites high into the air.

He tells the readers that being thankful can help them feel confident and can help other people feel loved. In the end, the others start their own list and say Thanksgiving might be pretty great after all.

video_title: 📚 THE GIRL WHO MAKES A MILLION MISTAKES - Kids Books Read Aloud
summary_text: This is Millie, and she makes lots of mistakes. She spills milk, uses too much toothpaste and glue, spells banana wrong, and runs too fast. Millie wants to be a top athlete, so she enters a hurdle race. At the start, she forgets to tie her shoelaces, and one shoe comes off. Then she forgets to jump and breaks the first hurdles. Her mom shouts, “Jump, Millie, jump!” Millie starts jumping, but she jumps so high that she crashes into a tree and loses a tooth. Stuck in the tree, she calms herself, says she is strong, and finds a way down by tying branches together with her shoelaces to reach a parachute. The next morning, she practices jumping, breathing, and telling herself she can do it. On race day, she jumps over the hurdles, finds her lost tooth, and keeps going. She trips again, but then she grabs her tooth and wins the race.

video_title: 📚 THE GIRAFFE WHO FOUND ITS SPOTS - Kids Books Read Aloud + PRINTABLE WORD SEARCH
summary_text: A giraffe felt sad because he stuck out everywhere he went. He tried to fit in with other animals so he could make friends. He showed the monkeys his tail, but they swung away. He showed the cheetahs his spots and fast running, but they ran away. He showed the ostriches he could stick his head in the sand, but they flapped away. He showed the elephants he could curl like them, but they did not want him. He showed the rhinos his horn, but they charged into him. He showed the flamingos he could stand like them, but they flew away. The giraffe said it was hopeless and asked why no one liked him. Then someone told him to stop trying to be someone else and to be himself. He was told that being different made him special. He went to a big party at night, and when it got dark, he reached the branches overhead so moonlight could shine down. The animals loved the bright party and said it was the best party ever because of him.

video_title: 📚 A LITTLE SPOT OF ANXIETY - Kids Books Read Aloud
summary_text: The story explains that there is a peaceful spot and an anxiety spot. The anxiety spot shows up when someone feels worried, nervous, anxious, or scared. It can grow bigger when a child tries something new, like playing soccer for the first time or taking a test. When this happens, the story says to answer the worry with, “I can do this.” Small anxiety spots can sometimes help keep a child safe, but big worries can make it hard to enjoy good things. The story also says anxiety can cause a tummy ache or sweating. To help keep anxiety from growing, children should eat healthy foods, get enough rest, and use music, drawing, or writing to share their worries. If anxiety grows fast, the story teaches a trick: imagine gray spots on the fingers and a green spot on the palm, say, “I can do this. I can be calm,” then take a deep breath and blow the worry away.

summary_text: Mrs. Poodle had four puppies named Fifi, Fufu, oo la la, and Gaston. She taught them to sip, yip, walk with grace, and look pretty and pink. When spring came, Mrs. Poodle took her puppies to the park. There she saw Mrs. Bulldog with her puppies, Rocky Ricky Bruno and Antoinette. The mothers soon saw that there had been a mix-up. Gaston and Antoinette traded places because each one fit better with the other family. At first, both puppies had trouble in their new homes. The next day, the mothers met again at the park, and Gaston and Antoinette switched back. After that, the two families met every afternoon. The poodle puppies learned to be rough, and the bulldog puppies learned to be tender. Later, Gaston and Antoinette had puppies of their own and taught them to be whatever they wanted to be.

video_title: March Book Madness 2024 - Not Quite Narwhal
summary_text: Kelp was born deep in the ocean. He was a narwhal, but he was different from the others. His tusk was shorter, he liked different food, and he was not a very good swimmer. His friends did not mind, so Kelp did not mind either. Then a strong current swept him away. He wished he could swim better and found himself near land. On a cliff, he saw a sparkling creature that looked like him. Kelp swam to shore and tried walking on land for the first time. It was hard, but he kept going until he reached the forest. There he met land narwhals, who were unicorns. They showed him that his tusk was called a horn, gave him unicorn delicacies in cones, and taught him to gallop. Kelp had fun, but he missed his ocean friends. He said goodbye and returned home. His narwhal friends welcomed him back and told him they already knew he was a unicorn. Kelp felt happy, but he still remembered the unicorns and wondered if he had to choose between them.

video_title: March Book Madness 2024 - Rescue & Jessica
summary_text: A pup named Rescue was training to help people, but his trainer told him he was not meant to be a seeing eye dog. Rescue felt sad and worried, because his family had always helped people. He learned to be a service dog instead, wearing a blue cape and staying by his partner’s side. He also learned to open doors and do many helpful jobs. In the city, a girl named Jessica was in a hospital after her legs were badly hurt. Doctors removed part of her left leg, and later she had to use a wheelchair and a prosthetic leg. She practiced hard, but she felt sad and unsure. Then Jessica saw another service dog named Ciri and decided to apply for a dog of her own. Soon Rescue got a new red cape, and he met Jessica. They spent weeks together in the country, and Rescue showed her what he could do. After they returned to the city, they worked together every day. When Jessica later lost her right leg too, Rescue helped her start again, and they learned together step by step.

video_title: March Book Madness 2024 - This Very Tree
summary_text: A tree stood in a busy plaza below two tall towers. It gave people shade, birds a place to rest, and flowers that showed spring was coming. The tree liked the city, the wind, and the rain on the concrete. Then one ordinary morning, something bad happened. The tree waited alone in the dark and hot place for weeks. When people found it, the tree saw that the city had changed. The tree was taken on a truck to a quiet nursery in a faraway park. There, people cared for it all winter, and its leaves came back. Birds visited, and a dove made a nest in its branches. After many years, the tree grew strong again and was moved back downtown. It saw a new plaza with many trees and empty spaces where the towers had been. The tree was planted in one empty space. Now it gives shade and hope, and it still blossoms first each spring.

video_title: March Book Madness 2024 - Beneath
summary_text: Finn was in a horrible mood, and Grandpa wanted to talk with him. Finn said Grandpa would not understand, but Grandpa asked him to go for a walk. Finn agreed, though he said he would stay under here. Grandpa promised to remember to think of what was beneath. As they walked into the forest, Grandpa showed Finn how there are things under the parts we can see, like tree roots under the ground and the water under a boat. He said that sometimes things that look still can have a lot happening below. Grandpa also said that some things are a mystery, like a nest or a baby on the way. He explained that beneath what is outside, there can be growing, changing, or hidden feelings inside plants, animals, and people. Finn listened and began to want to know more. Grandpa said everyone is more than what you see, and sometimes the person who seems not to understand knows exactly how you feel. At the end, they walked home, climbed the hill, and looked at the stars.

summary_text: When the Berlin Wall rises suddenly, 12-year-old Gera’s family is split apart. Gera, her mother, and her brother Fritz live on the Eastern side with the Soviets. Her father and middle brother are stuck in the West after going there to look for work. Gera watches the wall even though it is dangerous, and she thinks about Freedom, which is forbidden. She sees East German soldiers with guns watching their own people so no one can escape. Gera, her family, and their neighbors feel trapped in their city. Then Gera sees her father on a viewing platform on the western side of the wall. She sees him make a strange dance and thinks he is sending a message. Gera believes he wants her and Fritz to dig a tunnel under the wall and escape East Berlin. But if they are caught, they could die. Gera must decide what to do in a place where no one can be trusted.

video_title: March Book Madness 2025 - Wings of an Eagle
summary_text: Olal Lakota Native American boy grows up on Pine Ridge reservation with his family. He remembers cold winters, shared homes, and a giveaway where people bring gifts to share. After his mother dies, his father tells him to step inside a circle and says he must dig deeper and keep going. The boy works hard, runs from bullies, and thinks about stories of Native Olympians. He sweeps floors, builds grain elevators, and goes to Haskell Institute, where he is first told he is too slow for track. He keeps training with cans of concrete and later earns a team jersey. He wins records and dreams of the Olympics, but his body feels weak in races. A coach gives him honey, which helps. He gets a college scholarship, faces unfair treatment, and keeps running. After medical help, new training, and more hard work, he goes to Tokyo. There he gets shoes, runs the 10,000 meter race, and wins the gold medal. At the end, he is honored with songs, drums, a feather headdress, and a new name.

video_title: March Book Madness 2025 - Magic Ramen
summary_text: After World War II, Momo fuku Ando walked home through the ruins of Osaka, Japan. He saw a long line of hungry people waiting in the cold for ramen soup, and he could not forget them. He decided that food would be his life’s work. Over the next years, he made salt, dried fish, and nutritious food for sick people. Then one business deal failed, and he became poor again. He dreamed of a new kind of ramen that would be tasty, healthy, and easy to make. In his backyard shed, he mixed and tested flour, salt, water, eggs, milk, spinach, soup, and many cooking methods, but the noodles kept failing. One night he watched his wife make tempura and saw how hot oil made tiny holes in batter. He fried his noodles, then added hot water. At last, instant ramen worked. Ando and his family made and sold it, and many people were able to eat it.

video_title: March Book Madness 2025 - Amy Wu and the Perfect Bao
summary_text: Amy can do many things, but she cannot make the perfect bow. Her mom, dad, and grandma make soft, fluffy bow that Amy loves to eat. Amy tries to make bow, but her first ones are too empty, too full, or leak. She watches her family, but her bow still do not turn out right. Then Amy has an idea. She whispers to her grandma, and Grandma cuts the dough into smaller pieces for Amy’s small hands. Amy rolls the dough, adds the right filling, and pinches it shut. Soon she makes many perfect bow. After the bow are steamed, Amy sees that her perfect bow are soft, fluffy, and delicious. She eats them, and she also eats one that is not perfect. It tastes good too.

video_title: March Book Madness 2025 - More Than Words
summary_text: Nathan does not say much when his classmates talk in class. He listens while they call out answers and say things like “Hey,” “that’s mine,” and “vanilla please.” Even when he is quiet, Nathan has many thoughts. He thinks about puddles outside and about digging in the schoolyard. The story shows that people can share what they feel in many ways, not just with talking. Tomorrow uses words to say when she is happy or sad. Meline shows feelings with her face. Lon and Carlos write. Carlos uses Braille. McKenna types, Raheem spells, and Fatima and Mato use sign language. Other children point, press, sing, make sounds, repeat words, move, play, build, wear special clothes, paint, draw, dig, search, and create new things. video_title: The Best Nest: A Tale of Roosting Rivalry. Written & Illustrated by J. C. Perry
summary_text: In a tree by an old stone wall, two birds named Peter and Paul built nests. Paul looked at Peter’s nest and wanted to know whose was best. Paul said he had soft feathers in his nest, and Peter said he had strong sticks from a vine. Paul got upset and made his nest stronger with mud while Peter was away. Then Peter made his nest into a veranda with a straw roof. Paul made his nest into a fortress with a drawbridge, turrets, and cannons. Peter then built a hot tub, a home cinema, and a games room, with a ferris wheel, merry-go-round, and log flume outside. A storm came, and both big nests were too heavy. They fell apart and landed in a broken, soggy pile. An owl took Peter and Paul into her tree trunk home, gave them food and drink, and kept them dry. After that, Peter and Paul built a smaller home together in a hollow tree and welcomed other animals there when rain flooded their homes.

video_title: Mark the Shark  Written by Richie Dean
summary_text: Mark was a hammerhead shark in Bubbleton. He was big and had sharp teeth, but he was gentle and shy. The people in the village were afraid of him and closed their shops when he swam by. One day, Mark saw a lonely little plant pot outside a shop. The shopkeeper was so scared that he told Mark to take it and go away. Mark did not want to hurt anyone. He paid for the plant and took it home. Mark cared for the plant every day. Soon it grew into a big Christmas tree. Mark decorated it with bright coral. The lights and colors made his house glow. The fish in Bubbleton came to see the tree. Mark asked them to help decorate, and they brought lights and seaweed decorations. More fish came, and they all said hello to Mark. After that, decorating Mark’s Christmas tree became a yearly event, and the village learned not to judge him so quickly.

His father asked questions, and Kevin said he could kick his feet while Sammy tied him up. The next day Kevin tried the swings, but Sammy chased him away again. Kevin went home and talked with his father, who asked what Kevin could do if Sammy dug a hole. Kevin said he could kick dirt back in. The next day Kevin tried the monkey bars, but Sammy stopped him again. Kevin went home, climbed a tree, and told his father that Sammy would nail up the house. Kevin and his father laughed, and Kevin said they could walk out the other door. The next morning Kevin returned to the playground and went to the sandbox. Sammy shouted threats, but Kevin answered back. They both dug tunnels until their heads bumped. Then they started planning a fort together.

video_title: The Selfish Crocodile By Faustin Charles Illustrated By Michael Terry
summary_text: A big crocodile lived in a river deep in the forest. He was selfish and shouted that the river was his. He told all the forest animals to stay away or he would eat them. Because of this, the river had no fish, tadpoles, frogs, crabs, or crayfish, and the animals went far away to drink water. One morning, the forest heard a loud groaning sound. The animals saw the crocodile lying on his back in pain and holding his swollen jaw. They watched from far away and did not help. Then a little mouse came to the crocodile. The mouse climbed onto him, went into his open mouth, and pulled out a bad tooth. The crocodile felt better at once. He thanked the mouse, gave him a juicy nut, and promised to help with his teeth. Soon they became friends. The crocodile invited all the animals to drink and bathe in the river, and the river filled with life again.

Tim got scared, and then everyone heard a noise. It was only Norman snoring. The family laughed until morning, when Tim fell asleep and Jim finally did too.

video_title: This Little Explorer: A Pioneer Primer
summary_text: Many little explorers went on big adventures. Leif Erikson was a Viking who sailed to North America and was the first European to land in America. Marco Polo went to China with his dad when he was a teenager. He rode camels, saw wild animals, met a rich Emperor, and later wrote a book about his travels. Christopher Columbus sailed from Spain on the Nina, the Pinta, and the Santa Maria in 1492. He wanted to reach Asia, but he landed in America instead. Ferdinand Magellan showed that the world was round by sailing around it. These explorers traveled on oceans and across lands to find new places and learn new things.

At his house, he lit a lamp, and a small spider inside asked for peace, so Uncle elephant turned the lamp off and they ate supper. The child felt sad looking at a family picture, so Uncle elephant wore all his clothes at once and made them both laugh. He wrote a song for the child, and later a telegram said mother and father had been found. Uncle elephant took the child home, and they said goodbye after one last song and piano music.

That does not work either, because one friend is very big and could take all the cookies. The friends get nervous, and one starts breaking things. When they count the cookies again, the pieces keep getting smaller and smaller. Soon there are many cookie pieces, but still only four friends. The friends worry because the cookies are almost crumbs. At last, one friend says to take one piece at a time. Each friend takes three pieces, and everyone gets the same amount. They are happy because they did it: equal cookies for all.

video_title: Grumpy Monkey
summary_text: One wonderful day, Jim pansy woke up and thought everything was wrong. The sun was too bright, the sky was too blue, and the bananas were too sweet. Jim did not know what was happening. Norman from next door said Jim might be grumpy, but Jim said he was not. On his walk, Jim met Marabou, then lemur, then snake. Norman kept saying Jim was grumpy, and the others pointed out Jim’s hunched body, bunched eyebrows, and frown. Jim tried to fix these things by loosening up, raising his brow, and smiling, but he still did not feel happy inside. Many animals asked Jim to sing, swing, roll, stroll, lie in the grass, stomp, take a bath, hug, laugh, nap, eat, jump, sit in the sun, and dance. Jim did none of it. He shouted, stormed off, and felt sorry. Then Jim found Norman again. Norman was grumpy too because he had danced with porcupine and got hurt. Jim asked if Norman was okay, and Norman said he would feel better soon. Jim said he was still grumpy too, and Norman said it was a wonderful day to be grumpy. Jim agreed and felt a little better.

video_title: The Little Butteryfly That Could
summary_text: A little butterfly wants to reach a group of migrating butterflies and find the flowers, but the trip is 200 miles long. The butterfly worries about flying so far and asks if it can take a plane, a hot air balloon, or a blip, but the answer is no. It remembers life as a caterpillar, when it built a chrysalis, waited, and then started the journey with friends. Now it is lost and alone, and it fears storms and animals like snakes, birds, dragonflies, frogs, and spiders. A whale also appears, and the butterfly jokes about living in its stomach, but the whale spits it out. The butterfly keeps hearing, “Keep trying,” and starts flying again. It travels mile by mile, though wind blows it back and it feels discouraged. At last, after 200 miles, it reaches the flowers and says it can do many things when it believes in itself. Then it is told to eat up before going dormant for winter.

video_title: A Tale of Two Kitties: Finding a Home
summary_text: Taco was a cat who lived a happy life with his humans in a warm house with good food and love. When he was a tiny kitten, a man threw him from a car near a Mexican restaurant, and Taco got stuck in a bush. He cried in the rain and cold until two big hands came through the bush and picked him up. A girl hugged him, and the humans took him home. They made him a cozy bed and fed him from a bottle until he grew strong. As Taco got bigger, he became a brave cat who went on many adventures, like walking outside, visiting the lake, wearing costumes on Halloween, and helping with Christmas. When Taco was 17, his humans brought home Bean, a dirty yellow kitten from under a dumpster. Taco hissed at first because he did not want to share. Then the girl reminded him how he had been saved too. Taco understood, shared a toy with Bean, and decided to be a good big brother.

video_title: The Itchy Book
summary_text: A dinosaur reads a sign that says, "Dinosaurs do not scratch." Soon he feels itchy and wants to scratch, but he tries to stay tough. A bee stings him, and he still looks at the sign. Other dinosaurs also feel itchy. They all say they are tough dinosaurs and do not scratch. They try many things to make the itch go away, like a feather, grass, an ant, a wool sweater, dandelion seeds, dry leaves, a straw hat, daisies, a caterpillar, sand from the beach, hair from a haircut, and a cat log. Then a turtle moves and shows more of the sign. The rest of the sign says, "Dinosaurs do not scratch alone." The dinosaurs scratch and feel better. In the end, they learn that the sign was right, and one dinosaur says he has an itch too.

video_title: A Little SPOT of ANGER
summary_text: A peaceful spot explains that it can help calm an angry spot, which means anger. It says people also feel sadness and anxiety, and everyone has these feelings inside. The story says feelings can get too big, and then people do not feel good. When anger shows up because someone feels frustrated, afraid, or hurt, the peaceful spot teaches a special trick. First, hold up a hand and imagine four red spots on the fingers and one green spot on the thumb. Then count the spots from one to four, tapping each finger, and one more tap. After that, fill your lungs with peaceful air and coat the spots with love and care. The story shows this trick in different situations, like when a child cannot draw the way they want, when someone takes a toy, when a dinosaur goes missing, and when paint spills. Each time, counting and breathing help the angry spot get smaller, so the child can calm down and think clearly.

video_title: Yertle the Turtle
summary_text: On the far away island of Salamasand, Yertle the Turtle was king of a small, clean pond where the turtles had plenty to eat and were happy. But Yertle wanted to see more and be higher than everyone else. He ordered nine turtles to swim to his stone and stand one on top of another, making a nine-turtle stack for his throne. Yertle climbed up and bragged that he could now rule cows, mules, a house, a blueberry bush, and a cat. Then Mac, the turtle at the bottom, said his back, shoulders, and knees hurt. Yertle did not listen and ordered many more turtles to pile up. Mac and the others obeyed, and Yertle rose even higher. Mac asked for rights and food, but Yertle shouted back. When the moon rose, Yertle wanted to go higher still. Then Mac burped, the throne shook, and Yertle fell into the pond. Yertle became king of the mud, and all the turtles were free.

In social studies, English, phys ed, and art, every subject becomes another math problem. Mrs. Fibonacci also shows different ways to count, like counting by twos, and talks about number patterns on other planets. By the end of the day, the class is still working on cupcake fractions, and the narrator says being allergic to cupcakes so everyone else can have one.

The man with the yellow hat and the director put the puppies back. Then George opened another door and found the missing puppy. Everyone was happy, and the director gave the puppies and their mother a snack.

video_title: How Do Dinosaurs Stay Friends?
summary_text: A dinosaur and his friend have a terrible fight. The story asks many times if the dinosaur will do mean things, like write a bad note, ruin a towel, tear a book, throw a lunch box, kick a bike, or tell lies. But the dinosaur does not do these things. Instead, he sends a nice note and takes most of the blame. He is surprised to find that his friend does the same. Then the dinosaur invites his friend over to share and play. He lets his friend choose the first toys. He also brings a toy dragon and knight to school with a card that says he does not want to fight. Later, he gives his friend cookies he helped his mom bake. He wraps up a favorite bear with a bow and brings it as a gift. In the end, the friends make things right and stay friends with good hugs and more.

She hit every target with her arrows, ran faster than the others, blocked arrows with her bracelets, and won the last sword fight. When she showed her face, her mother was surprised and proud. Diana left Paradise Island in her invisible jet and lived in Washington DC as Diana Prince. She worked for the government and rushed to help when a bridge was about to fall and when a tiger was stolen from the zoo. She used her strength, her speed, and her lasso to save the day.

video_title: Big Dog Little Dog
summary_text: Fred and Ted were friends. Fred was big and Ted was little. Fred had money, and Ted did not. When they walked in the rain, Fred got wet and Ted stayed dry. Fred played the flute, and Ted played the tuba. Fred ate spinach, and Ted ate beets. Fred painted the house green, and Ted painted it red. One day they drove away in their cars. Fred had a green car and drove slowly. Ted had a red car and drove fast. They came to a sign and chose the mountains. In the mountains, Ted skied all day and Fred skated all day. At night they were sleepy and stayed in a small hotel. Fred was upstairs, and Ted was downstairs. They did not sleep well. In the morning, they walked and talked. A bird said Fred should sleep downstairs and Ted should sleep upstairs. They changed beds and slept well. The story ends by saying big dogs need big beds and little dogs need little beds.

video_title: Duck and Hippo In The Rainstorm
summary_text: Duck knocked on Hippo’s door and asked him to walk in the rain. Duck twirled her umbrella and said, “It’s spring, spring, spring!” Hippo was worried about the weather, but Duck said he could come if he shared her umbrella. Hippo put on his big rubber boots and went outside. At first, there was no room for Hippo. He tried walking in front of Duck, and then behind her, but that did not work. Then Duck stood on Hippo’s feet while Hippo held the umbrella, and that worked just fine. They jumped in puddles, splashed through mud, and dropped a stick into the creek. Duck wanted to sail down the creek, so Hippo helped her into the water. Again, there was no room for Hippo, so Duck sat on Hippo’s lap. They swirled around boulders and a crocodile, then twirled into a pond. Duck could not find Hippo, but Hippo was under her, and Duck was sitting on his head. At the end, they went home, shared the umbrella again, and Hippo invited Duck in for tea.

video_title: Pinkalicious Fairy House
summary_text: It was spring, Pinkalicious’s favorite season. She loved the cotton-candy sky at sunset and the garden full of blossoms. She believed fairies came to the yard and made the plants grow with fairy dust. One spring, she decided to build a house for the fairies so she could see them. Peter helped her gather twigs, leaves, and shells. Together they made a little house in the garden, added buttercups around the door, and made a shell path. Pinkalicious also made a pond, a boat, and a slide. She watched and waited, but the fairies did not come. Peter tried to cheer her up, but Pinkalicious still wanted to see them. Then she thought the fairies might come at night, so Mommy and Daddy let her and Peter camp outside. She left honeysuckle and berries for the fairies and stayed awake as long as she could, but she fell asleep. In the morning, the flowers were blooming and the snack was gone. Pinkalicious saw bright morning light and knew the fairies had come.

summary_text: This book goes through the alphabet and shows many insects and other small creatures. A is for ant, a hard worker that carries heavy things.
