video_title: It's Not Easy Being a Bunny
summary_text: Pj was a funny bunny, but he felt very sad. He did not like being a bunny. His mother made him eat cooked carrots every day, he had many brothers and sisters, and his ears were very big. One day Pj left home. He said he wanted to be a bear, so he lived with the bears. But when the bears slept all winter, Pj could not sleep, and life there was not exciting. Then Pj wanted to be a bird and went to live with the birds, but he did not like trying to fly. After that he tried being a beaver, but beavers worked very hard and Pj did not like work. He tried being a pig, a moose, a possum, and a skunk, but each time he found something he did not like. At last Pj decided he really wanted to be a bunny. He hurried home, and his family was happy to see him. Pj ate his cooked carrots, played with his brothers and sisters, and was glad to be a bunny again.

video_title: Paddington Bear in the Garden
summary_text: One morning Paddington went into the Browns’ garden with paper and pencil and made a list of the nice things about being a bear and living with the Browns. He wrote about having his own room, a warm bed, and marmalade for breakfast. He soon remembered another very nice thing: the garden. The Browns’ garden was quiet and lovely, but it took hard work to keep it nice. Mr. Brown mowed the lawn, Mrs. Brown weeded the flower beds, and Mrs. Bird helped too. Mrs. Bird suggested that Jonathan, Judy, and Paddington each have a piece of the garden. Mr. Brown agreed, and the children began their work. Paddington bought a garden book, looked at the building site, and accidentally left his marmalade jar on a platform. Builders poured concrete over it, but when the jar came back, Paddington found a way to use the broken concrete. He made a rock garden, won praise, and later received a gold star from Mr. Lionel Trug on National Garden Day.

Back in the warm cozy lair, Bear’s friends begin to worry because he is late and the storm is getting worse. Mouse, Wren, and the other friends decide to search for him. Badger lights a lamp, and the whole group goes out together through the wet weather. They call for Bear until they hear him. When they find him, they gather around and give him bear hugs. Later, everyone stays close together, and Bear tells stories while his friends fall asleep safely.

video_title: The Story About Ping
summary_text: Ping was a young duck who lived with his big family on a wise-eyed boat on the Yangtze River. Every morning they crossed a little bridge to the shore to look for food, and every evening they went back to the boat. Ping always tried not to be last, because the last duck got a spank on the back. One evening Ping was busy catching a little fish and did not hear the call. His family crossed the bridge without him. Ping hid in the grasses so he would not be last, but the boat sailed away in the dark. In the morning Ping was alone and swam down the river to find his family. He met strange fishing birds and ducked underwater. Then he found crumbs leading to a houseboat, where a boy grabbed him. The boy’s family took Ping onto the boat, but later the boy set him free. Ping swam back just as his family returned, and he was spanked for being last. At last he was home again.

He said he would run away tomorrow if he was still mad.

video_title: Caps For Sale

He walked through town calling, “Caps! Caps for sale!” One morning, nobody wanted to buy any caps. The peddler grew hungry, so he went for a walk in the country and came to a big tree. He sat down, leaned back, and fell asleep. When he woke up, his caps were gone. He looked all around, then looked up into the tree. Monkeys were sitting in the branches, and each monkey wore a cap. The peddler shook his finger and stamped his feet, but the monkeys copied him. At last he threw down his own cap. Then all the monkeys threw down the caps too. The peddler put them back on his head and walked back to town calling, “Caps! Caps for sale!”

Then his friend told him that not everything is a race and that some things should be savored. Straw had not thought about that before. That night, after bedtime story, Straw talked about the strawberry swirls in the whipped cream and the rainbow inside a tiny bubble. He stayed in bed and thought about the day until he fell asleep. After that, Straw still sometimes wanted to be first, but most of the time he wanted to make good things last.

video_title: The Rabbit Listened Lesson & Activities | Guided Reading Discussion Questions
summary_text: Taylor decided to build something new, special, and amazing. Taylor felt proud, but then everything came crashing down. The chicken came first and said to talk about it, but Taylor did not want to talk, so the chicken left. Then the bear came and said to shout about it, but Taylor did not want to shout, so the bear left too. The elephant came and said to remember how things were, but Taylor did not want to remember, so the elephant left. The hyena wanted to laugh, the ostrich wanted to hide, the kangaroo wanted to throw it all away, and the snake wanted to knock down someone else’s stuff. Taylor did not want to do any of that. Soon Taylor was alone. Then the rabbit came close and sat quietly with Taylor. Taylor asked the rabbit to stay. The rabbit listened as Taylor talked, shouted, remembered, laughed, and made plans to build again.

Grumpy Toad showed Pete cool blue magic sunglasses and said they help you see things in a whole new way. Pete put them on and looked around. He saw the birds singing, the bright sky, and the shining sun, and he felt all right. Pete thanked Grumpy Toad and kept going. Soon he met Squirrel, who was mad because he only found one acorn. Pete shared the cool blue magic sunglasses, and Squirrel felt all right too. Then Pete met Turtle, who was frustrated because he was upside down. Turtle wore the sunglasses and felt all right. Next Pete met Alligator, who was sad because no one wanted to play. Alligator wore the sunglasses and felt all right. Then Pete fell, and the sunglasses cracked. Wise Old Owl told Pete he did not need magic sunglasses to see things in a new way. Pete looked around and saw the good in the day, and everyone felt all right.

video_title: The Invisible Boy - Read Aloud By Mr. Joshua Brooks
summary_text: Brian is a quiet boy in Mrs. Carlotti’s classroom, and many kids do not notice him. Nathan talks too loudly, and Sophie whines, so they get most of the attention. At recess, Micah and JT pick kickball teams. The best players and their friends are chosen first, and Brian is left waiting. JT says there are enough players and suggests playing in the cafeteria instead. Later, the class talks about Madison’s birthday party, and everyone says they had fun. Brian was not invited. While the others play games and read, Brian sits alone and draws dragons, pirates, aliens, and superheroes. On Monday, a new student named Justin arrives. At lunch, the kids laugh at Justin’s Korean food, bulgogi, but Brian does not laugh. The next day, Brian leaves Justin a note saying the bulgogi looked good. Justin thanks him, and later he says Brian’s drawing is cool. In class, Justin and Emilio let Brian join their project group. At lunch again, Justin calls Brian over to sit with them, and Brian is no longer left out.

Dad has already made breakfast, Mom has packed his backpack, and Pete will still make the bus.
Pete thinks about how much Mom and Dad do for him every day.
Mom helps him practice baseball, and Dad takes him to guitar lessons.
Pete realizes that he has never really said thank you.
He wants to surprise them with something special, so he thinks about making breakfast, picking flowers, cleaning the house, mowing the lawn, or changing the oil in Dad’s car.
None of these feels big enough.
Pete asks his big brother, Bob, what to do.
Bob says it is not about what you do, but how you do it, and that if it comes from the heart, Mom and Dad will love it.
Pete gets an idea and does what he does best: he writes Mom and Dad a song.
In the song, he tells them they are the best and that he loves them with all his heart.
It becomes the best surprise ever.

video_title: Little Critter: I'm Sorry - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook - NO ADS
summary_text: Little Critter says, “I’m sorry” many times after he makes mistakes. He knocks his sister off her bicycle by accident, leaves her jump rope at the park, uses his brother’s blanket as a Super Critter Cape, and gets it dirty. He also pulls down a curtain during hide and seek and knocks over books while reaching for his favorite book. Mom helps him put the books back. Then he wakes the baby when he forgets to play quietly, and Mom tells him to play outside. He still makes more mistakes, like forgetting to close a window, getting tackled in Mom’s garden, not emptying his pockets before Mom washes his pants, and making a mess in the bath. Later, he takes apart his sister’s dollhouse and cannot put it back together. At the end, Mom says that sometimes saying “I’m sorry” is not enough, and Little Critter learns he must be more careful.

Seven uncles come with eight jugs of cold lemonade. Nine aunties bring cheesecakes. Then 11 nephews, 12 sweet potato pies, 13 nieces, and 14 fresh honeydews arrive. Last come 15 hungry grandkids. Everyone rushes in for the feast, and the house becomes too full. The walls budge, and there is no more space. So someone says to move the big dinner outside. Everyone carries the food, tables, and chairs into Grandma’s wide backyard. Then the family eats there, and Grandma’s backyard is the perfect place for the meal.

summary_text: It was Halloween in the jungle, and Jim Panzee and his friends walked in the dark to find treats. The trees looked strange, and Jim heard knocking sounds. Porcupine said there were many night noises and told Jim not to be scared. Then the friends heard creepy cackling, and they thought about who was behind a tree. It was hyena, who gave them treats. Later, something slimy wrapped around Jim’s leg. Warthog shouted, but it was arvar, who also gave treats. The friends kept walking, but the wind, the dark, and the smells made the night feel spooky. Then they met Polecat, who sprayed a very stinky liquid and scared them away. After that, Jim heard more knocks and saw glowing eyes. He felt too scared and cried out. A little voice explained that the noises came from a small animal looking for bugs. Jim learned that everyone feels scared sometimes. Then the friends shared Halloween treats and played a game of scaring one another.

video_title: Ish - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook
summary_text: Ramon loved to draw anytime and anywhere. One day he drew a vase of flowers, but his brother Leon looked over his shoulder and laughed. Ramon felt so upset that he crumpled the picture and threw it away. After that, he kept trying to make his drawings look right, but nothing seemed good enough. Many months passed, and Ramon filled many sheets of paper with crumpled drawings. At last he put down his pencil and said he was done. Then his sister Marisol watched him. Ramon told her to go away, but she picked up one of his crumpled papers and ran to her room. Ramon chased her there and stopped when he saw the drawings on her walls. Marisol showed him one of her favorite pictures and said it looked “face-ish” and “vase-ish.” Ramon looked closely and began to see all the drawings in a new way. He started drawing freely again, making “ish” drawings and “ish” words, and he was happy to create once more.

The man laughed, hugged Olaf, and then climbed back up the chimney. Before he left, he said, Merry Christmas to all and to all a good night.

video_title: Where Do Babies Come From? - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook
summary_text: A baby starts growing inside a mother’s body. When a woman has a baby growing inside her, she is called pregnant or expecting a baby. The baby grows in the womb, which is below the stomach and keeps the baby safe. To begin a baby, two things are needed: a sperm from the father’s body and an egg from the mother’s body. When the sperm and egg come together, a tiny seed may start to grow in the womb. The baby gets food from the mother through a special tube called the umbilical cord. This cord helps the baby grow bigger. Babies usually grow for 9 months. When the baby is ready, it is born through the birth canal. After birth, the umbilical cord falls off and leaves a belly button.

summary_text: Slowly, slowly, slowly, a sloth crawled along a branch in a tree. Slowly, slowly, slowly, the sloth ate a leaf, fell asleep, and then woke up. All day long and all night long, the sloth hung upside down in the tree. Even when it rained, the sloth stayed there. One day, the howler monkey asked, “Why are you so slow?” The sloth did not answer. Then other animals came and asked why the sloth was so quiet and so boring. The anteater asked too, and the jaguar asked why the sloth was so lazy. The sloth thought and thought for a long, long time. At last, the sloth said it was true that it was slow and quiet, but it was not lazy. The sloth said it liked to live in peace and do things slowly, slowly. Then the sloth yawned and said, “That’s just how I am.”

After that, the crayon drew many blue things, like bluebells, blue jeans, and blue whales. People were happy with his work, and he started making bigger and better pictures, including a green lizard. In the end, he was working on a big new project and enjoying a perfect day.

video_title: Our Skin - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook
summary_text: Our skin is beautiful, strong, and important just the way it is. Skin gets its color from something called melanin inside our bodies. Melanin helps protect skin from the sun. Some people have more melanin and some have less, so skin can be many shades from dark to light. The story says color words like black and white are sometimes used to describe people, and there are many groups of people in the world, like black, indigenous, asian, white, arab, pacific islander, african american, latinx, and biracial. Color does not tell us what a person is like on the inside. A long time ago, some white people made up the idea of race and said white people were better. That was not true or fair. When people believe this story and make unfair rules, that is called racism. Racism can happen in big ways and small ways, but people can work for racial justice by telling the truth, speaking up, and changing unfair rules.

video_title: Owl At Home - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook
summary_text: Owl was at home by the fire on a cold, snowy night. He ate buttered toast and hot pea soup. Then he heard loud banging at the front door. Owl opened the door, but no one was there, only snow and wind. After it happened again, Owl thought the poor old winter was knocking and wanted to be kind. He opened the door very wide and invited winter in to warm itself by the fire. But winter rushed into the house, blew Owl against the wall, and put out the fire. Snow whirled through the rooms, the window shades flapped, and the pea soup turned into hard green ice. Owl told winter to go away. Winter rushed out and slammed the door. Owl made a new fire, the house became warm again, the snow melted, and the pea soup turned soft once more.

summary_text: Al was in bed and was ready to blow out the candle and sleep. Then he saw two bumps under his blanket at the bottom of the bed. He looked, but he could only see darkness. Al could not sleep because he worried the bumps might grow bigger while he slept. He moved his right foot on the bump on the right, and then he moved his left foot on the bump on the left. He pulled off all the covers and saw that the bumps were gone. He only saw his own two feet. But then he got cold, so he covered himself again. The same two bumps came back. Al cried that he would never sleep. He jumped on the bed, and the bed came falling down. Then he ran downstairs and sat in a chair near the fire. He decided to leave the bumps on the bed and sleep there instead.

summary_text: Owl takes a kettle from the cupboard and says he will make tear water tea. He sits very still with the kettle on his lap and begins to think of sad things. He thinks of chairs with broken legs, songs with forgotten words, books with torn pages, clocks that have stopped, mornings nobody saw, mashed potatoes left on a plate, and pencils that are too short to use. As he thinks, Owl cries, and big tears fall into the kettle. He keeps crying until the kettle is full. Then he says, “That does it.” Owl stops crying, puts the kettle on the stove, and boils the tears for tea. He fills his cup and says the tea tastes a little salty, but tear water tea is always very good.

summary_text: One night, Al went down to the seashore and sat on a big rock. The sky was dark. Soon a small piece of the moon came up over the sea, and then the whole round moon shone brightly. Al watched it for a long time and said that if he looked at the moon, the moon must be looking back at him too. He said he would come again, but then he had to go home. As Al walked along the path, he looked up and saw the moon following him. He told the moon to stay over the sea, but it kept coming. He climbed a hill and shouted, “Goodbye, moon!” Then the moon went behind some clouds and disappeared. Al felt sad, went home, put on his pajamas, and got into bed. Soon the moon came back from behind the clouds and filled the room with silver light. Al saw the moon through the window and felt happy again.

video_title: Mouse Soup - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook
summary_text: A weasel caught a mouse and brought him home to make mouse soup. The mouse said the soup would not taste good unless it had stories in it. The hungry weasel agreed, and the mouse told four stories. First, bees landed on his head, and he led them through mud until they flew away. Then two large stones wondered about the other side of a hill, but a mouse showed them it was like their own side. Next, a mouse could not sleep because ten crickets chirped too loudly, so he told them to go away. Last, an old lady found a thorn bush in her chair, and a policeman helped her water it until it grew leaves and roses. After the stories, the weasel ran outside to find bees, mud, stones, crickets, and a thorn bush for the soup. He was stung, scratched, and tired, and when he returned, the pot was empty. The mouse had escaped home, lit a fire, eaten supper, and finished his book.

summary_text: Leila was happy that Ramadan was starting, because for the first time her mom said she could fast all month. The next morning, she woke up before sunrise, ate pancakes, and prayed with her mom before school. Her mom gave her a note for Mrs. Penworth, but Leila forgot to hand it over. On the bus and in class, she worried that no one knew about Ramadan. At lunchtime, she did not eat and felt hungry while other children shared food. She left the cafeteria and went to the library, where Mrs. Carmen listened to her. Leila explained that she was fasting and missed her friends, Hen and Ishrat. Mrs. Carmen told her to write her thoughts down, so Leila wrote a note and a poem about Ramadan for Mrs. Penworth and gave them to her. The next day, Mrs. Penworth praised her poem, said fasting was special, and invited her to share it with the class and spend lunch in the library.

video_title: The Story of Ruby Bridges - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook
summary_text: Ruby Bridges was born near Tyler Town, Mississippi. Her family was very poor, and when her father lost his job, they moved to New Orleans. Ruby’s father worked as a janitor, and her mother cared for the children and worked at night. In New Orleans, Black children and white children went to separate schools. In 1960, a judge said four Black girls could go to white schools. Six-year-old Ruby went to William Franz Elementary School. On her first day, angry people stood outside and shouted at her. Federal marshals walked with her to keep her safe. Ruby went into school alone with her teacher, Mrs. Henry, and she kept learning every day. One morning she stopped and prayed for the people in the mob. Later, more children came to the school, and the mobs gave up. Ruby finished school, graduated from high school, and later started the Ruby Bridges Educational Foundation.

He looked at many trees, big and small, crooked and straight, until he found one that was just right. The tree had a strong brown trunk and green branches that waved in the cold December wind. Dragon could not cut down such a lovely tree, so he came back with colored lights and Silver Bells to make it even prettier. That night, he looked at his shining tree and thought it was perfect. Later, Dragon made a candy wreath from Old Wire and chocolate candy, but he kept eating the candy when pieces fell off. Soon he shook the wreath until every piece fell off, and he got a tummy ache. Dragon also bought clip-on mittens so he would not lose them, but then he lost his coat. At Christmas, Dragon bought gifts for himself, but he gave them away to hungry raccoons, a cold Rhino, and two sad birds. When he got home, his sack was empty, and he slept under his warm quilt.

video_title: Ice Cream Face - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook
summary_text: The child in the story loves ice cream and wants it after lunch. The child sees many ice cream faces, like the nose licker, the dribbler, the side swiper, the biter, the bearded lady, and the bearded baby. Waiting in a long line is hard, and the child makes a waiting face while thinking about how good the ice cream will taste. When the ice cream comes, the child’s face turns drippy and sweet. Then the ice cream is eaten too fast, and the child gets a brain freeze face, so the child slows down and licks it more carefully. After that, the ice cream starts to melt into soup, and the child has a sad face. At the end, a door is closed, then ice cream faces are seen all around again, and the child shares scoops. The story ends by showing that ice cream is sweeter when it is shared.

video_title: Chicka Chicka Boom Boom - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook
summary_text: A told B, and B told C, that they would meet at the top of the coconut tree. Then D, E, F, and G joined in, and soon H, I, J, and K were climbing too. More letters kept coming, and the tree got crowded. L, M, N, O, P, and then Q, R, S, T, U, and still more W, X, Y, and Z rushed to the coconut tree. The letters piled up so high that everyone wondered if there would be enough room. The whole alphabet climbed together, and the adults came to help after the big pileup. Some letters got hurt or twisted, and others were tangled, looped, or bent. Then P, Q, R, S, and T appeared, followed by U, V, W, X, Y, and Z, and they wiggled free as the sun went down. At the end, the moon came out, A got out of bed, and said he would beat everyone to the top of the coconut tree again.

He compares himself to many good things in nature and in life, like gravity, moonbeams, a cinnamon roll, a cool breeze, and a paper airplane. He says he is brave when he falls while skateboarding and gets back up again. He is curious, smart, and always learning, like someone looking through a microscope or telescope. He also says he is kind and polite, helps his grandmother, and blesses strangers who sneeze. He enjoys music, sports, and fun times with others. In the end, he says he is a brother, son, nephew, cousin, grandson, and friend. He says he is real, he will not answer to any name that is not his own, and he is worthy of success, safety, kindness, happiness, and love.

At the end, Mama Bear sees all the animals, including her baby bear, looking at her.

summary_text: The story explains hijab, a head scarf worn by many Muslim women. In Islam, people are asked to dress in a modest way. Many women wear hijab to cover their hair, and often their ears, neck, and chest. They may wear it because they want to show their faith, feel close to God, or follow what they believe their religion asks. Women may put on hijab when they go to work, school, or play sports in public. At home, they may uncover their hair with close family members or with other women and girls. Some young girls practice wearing hijab, but most do not wear it all the time until they are older. The story also says that some observant Muslim women do not wear hijab, but may still cover their hair when they pray or visit a mosque.

video_title: THE HALLOWEEN TREE - A kids Halloween read aloud | Children's Bedtime Storytime picture book
summary_text: At a Christmas tree farm, many young trees dreamed of becoming a family’s Christmas tree. One little tree did not. He grumbled that he did not like lights, decorations, or people, and he did not want to leave his spot. As he grew, his branches became twisted, and his needles turned brown and fell off. Then the farm closed, and houses were built nearby. Soon children came to play. Ben, Sarah, and Tomas climbed the tree and used it as a pirate ship, a fort, a spaceship, and even a dragon. In winter, the children stopped playing outside, and the tree stood alone. Then it saw a Christmas tree in the window and wished for lights, decorations, and people. The next year, the children played in it again. Later, when the parents wanted to cut the old tree down, the children saved it by decorating it for Halloween. The tree became a Halloween tree and was happy.

He grumbled that he did not like lights, decorations, or people, and he refused to leave his spot. As he grew, he became twisted and gnarled because his needles turned brown and fell off whenever he thought about being decorated. Eventually, all the other trees were sold, the farm closed, and houses were built nearby. Children began playing on the tall tree, first climbing him like a pirate ship and then using him as a fort, a spaceship, and even a dragon. In winter, the children stopped coming, and the tree saw a Christmas tree in the window of Sarah and Ben’s house. The next year, the children played in him again until Halloween came. When their parents wanted to cut him down, the children saved him by decorating him with Halloween lights and decorations. The tree then realized he liked lights, decorations, and people, and he became a Halloween tree.

video_title: SIR SIMON: SUPER SCARER - A kids Funny Halloween read aloud | Kids Bedtime Storytime picture book
summary_text: Sir Simon is a ghost who likes to scare things and shows off his business card. He has haunted a forest, a boat, and a bus stop, and now he is being moved to a house. Simon explains that ghosts have many chores at night, like stomping in the attic, flushing toilets, hiding things, and standing in the window. He also says he has hobbies like cross stitch and learning French. At the new house, Simon sees Grandma and Grandpa moving in. Then he meets Chester, a child ghost who just moved there with his grandma. Chester wants to be a ghost too, so Simon tells him how to look spooky and gives him a schedule. But Simon really wants Chester to do the chores while he goes off. Chester tries the tasks, but he is not very scary and gets confused. Later, Simon feels bad and helps Chester with human chores like vacuuming and laundry. In the end, Simon and Chester learn they are both better at being friends than at being ghosts or humans.

video_title: HOW DOES SANTA GO DOWN THE CHIMNEY? |  Christmas Read Aloud  | Read Aloud
summary_text: The story asks many funny questions about how Santa gets into a house on Christmas Eve. It wonders if he goes down the chimney head first, feet first, or if he gets stuck and needs help from the reindeer. It also asks what happens if there is no chimney. Maybe Santa knows about the key under the flower pot, or maybe he can slide under the door, come through the pipes, or fit through a mail slot like a letter. The story imagines Santa with dogs too. It says he might carry treats, know their names, and let them lick his beard. It also asks how Santa can see in the dark and whether he uses special goggles. In the end, the tree lights help Santa see as he tiptoes inside, leaves presents, gets a kiss from the dog, takes a cookie, and goes away. Santa goes up the chimney the same way he comes down.

video_title: It’s Not Little Red Riding Hood | Ms. Ocasio Reads… | Story Time | Bed Time Read Aloud For Kids |
summary_text: Little Red Riding Hood lived with her family in a cottage near the woods. Her grandmother loved her very much and sent her a red cape with a hood. One day, Grandma became ill, so Little Red’s mother packed a basket of food and asked Little Red to take it to Grandma’s house. Little Red walked through the woods by herself. Halfway there, the Big Bad Wolf came out of the trees and asked where she was going. Little Red told him she was bringing food to her sick grandma. The wolf told her to pick flowers, then ran ahead to Grandma’s house. He knocked on the door and pretended to be Little Red. When Little Red arrived, she noticed Grandma looked strange. The wolf tricked her into talking about Grandma’s ears, eyes, and teeth. Then the Woodsman came to rescue them. In the end, Grandma felt better, and everyone shared ice cream sundaes at Grandma’s shop.

video_title: The Magician's Hat | Ms. Ocasio Reads… | Story Time Bed Time Read Aloud For Kids | Full Story
summary_text: At Varaha family fun day at the library, children enjoyed scavenger hunts, storytelling, and reading rallies. Then a magician came with a big hat and a bag of tricks. He bent a spoon, made cards float, pulled a coin from a puppy’s ear, and made a banana disappear. He told a story about coming to the library as a child and finding a special book about magic. As he read, he learned that books are magic because they can take readers to new places. After that, he wanted to become a magician and got his magician’s hat. Later, he asked the children what they wanted to be when they grew up. Amy said she wanted to be a dentist, Matt said he wanted to be a famous football player, and Ryan said he wanted to be a dog. Each child reached into the hat and found a book about the dream they truly wanted. The magician said the magic comes from their dreams and from reading.

video_title: Pete the Cat: The First Thanksgiving | Ms. Ocasio Reads… | Story Time | Bed Time Read Aloud For Kids
summary_text: Pete felt nervous when he played a pilgrim in his class Thanksgiving play. His friend Callie told him to do his best, and Pete tried. He wore a pilgrim hat that his mom made for him and stood at the front of the cardboard Mayflower. The story then told about the pilgrims who left England in 1620 to begin a new life. Their trip on the big ship was long, rough, and dangerous, and many got very sick. After 65 days, they saw land and were happy. The pilgrims landed at Plymouth Rock in Massachusetts and worked hard to grow food, find water, and build homes. Their first winter was hard. In spring, Squanto and other Native Americans helped them grow corn, beans, and squash. By fall, the pilgrims had food to share and invited the Native Americans to the first Thanksgiving. Pete finished his play, then later at dinner he asked everyone to say what they were thankful for.

video_title: Books About Big Feelings for Kids | Ms. Ocasio Reads...LIVE BIG with CATCH-M | Full Story Read Aloud
summary_text: Ketchum opened his eyes and found only darkness. He felt alone and scared, and his shadow thoughts followed him. He cried and prayed for help and for a brave heart. Then his heart whispered, “Believe you’re extraordinary.” Ketchum listened, took slow breaths, and imagined a wonderful world. He held his heart, smiled, and said, “Yes, I am extraordinary.” His heart spoke again and told him to love himself. Ketchum took breaths full of love, and his lonely shadow thought went away. He felt happy and bright like a star. Then he hugged his shadow thoughts, and they made colorful rainbows together. His heart told him to do good and share love’s wondrous power. Ketchum agreed. Soon, many Ketchums were shining and sharing love everywhere, and they said no one would ever be alone in the dark.

video_title: Give Bees a Chance | Ms. Ocasio Reads… | Story Time | Bed Time Read Aloud For Kids
summary_text: The story says there are about 25,000 kinds of bees. It then explains the three types of honey bees in a hive: queens, drones, and workers. There is only one queen in each hive. The queen is a large female bee, and her job is to make baby bees. Drones are large male bees. There are about three to five hundred drones in a hive, and they do not have stingers. Their job is to find a queen to mate with. Workers are the biggest group, with about 30,000 to 80,000 in a hive. They are small female bees with stingers. Workers do many jobs. They gather nectar, pollen, and water, make honey, feed baby bees, build and protect the hive, and make royal jelly for the queen.

summary_text: The story begins with someone saying they love honey, but they would still miss bees if bees were gone. It explains that bees do much more than make honey. Bees help flowers by carrying pollen on their fuzzy bodies. When a bee visits one flower and then another, the pollen falls onto the next flower. This helps plants grow fruits and vegetables. A single bee can visit over 1,000 flowers in one day, so bees help a lot of food grow. The story then says bees are disappearing because of pesticides, parasites, not enough bee-friendly flowers, and pollution. Because of this, people need to help bees. In the end, the speaker changes their mind and says they do not want bees gone. They can help by planting bee-friendly flowers and by staying calm and not getting too close to bees.

video_title: A Bad Case of Stripes | Ms. Ocasio Reads… | Story Time | Bed Time Read Aloud For Kids | Full Story
summary_text: Camila Cream loved lima beans, but she did not eat them because her friends did not like them. On the first day of school, she worried about what to wear and tried on 42 outfits. When she put on a red dress, she saw that her whole body was covered with stripes. Her mother kept her home, and Dr. Bumble said she could go to school the next day. At school, the children laughed and called out different colors and shapes, and Camila kept changing into them. The principal said she had to stay home because she was too distracting. Her parents called more doctors, but the specialists and experts could not find a cure. News reporters came, and many helpers tried to fix her, but each one made her look even stranger. Finally, a kind old woman offered her plain lima beans. Camila admitted she really loved lima beans, ate them, and the stripes disappeared. After that, she ate lima beans whenever she wanted and never got stripes again.

video_title: If I Ran the Rain Forest | Ms. Ocasio Reads… | Story Time | Bed Time Read Aloud For Kids
summary_text: The Cat in the Hat takes Sally on a trip to the rain forest. He says the rain forest is steamy and wet because lots of rain falls there near the equator. He also tells about other kinds of rain forests, like seasonal rain forests, cloud rain forests, and mangrove rain forests. Then he explains that rain comes from transpiration, when plants give off water and warm air makes clouds. The Cat says the rain forest has four floors. On the top floor, very tall emergent trees grow, with buttress roots to hold them up. Harpy eagles and macaws live there. On the next floor, the green canopy is full of animals like howler monkeys, sloths, toucans, orchids, and tree frogs. Hummingbirds help flowers by carrying pollen. The understory is dark and has spider monkeys and ocelots. The forest floor is full of leaves, insects, snakes, jaguars, and people who have lived there for many years. In the end, the Cat says many trees are being cut down and asks people to save the rain forest.

Pig three bowed, warned the wolf, and showed strong ninja moves.
She split a stack of bricks, and the wolf got scared and ran away.
The pigs were happy and went back to school to keep learning.

video_title: Adventures at Lake Omigosh | Ms. Ocasio Reads | Kids Read Aloud | Bedtime Story for Kids | Storytime
summary_text: Every summer, children came to Camp Horizon on Lake oh my gosh in New Hampshire. Felix and Harry had gone there for many years and liked swimming, diving, horseback riding, horseshoes, and board games. One day after lunch, they decided to take a rowboat out on the lake. The camp rules said to wear life preservers, stay where the camp could still be seen, and never go out in bad weather. Felix and Harry were in a hurry, so they forgot the life preservers and rowed away from shore. Soon the wind pushed them farther out, and they could not get back. It got dark, cold, and rainy, and the boat rocked hard. Then the boat broke apart, and the boys fell into the water. They were tired and could not see the shore. Just when they were sinking, something lifted them up and carried them back to land. When they looked back at the lake, they thought they saw a huge turtle with a long neck diving under the water.

video_title: RAMADAN by Hannah Eliot  | Kids Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Ramadan begins when the crescent moon first appears in the sky. It lasts for one whole month. During Ramadan, Muslims think about what is important, feel thankful, and help other people. They eat and drink only when it is dark outside before the sun comes up. Each day they have a big meal called sahoor to get energy. In the evening, when the sun goes down, family and friends gather to break the fast. They eat a date first, then share a meal called iftar. People still go to work, school, and play, but they also spend time with family, pray, and do good deeds. When the crescent moon appears again, Ramadan ends. Then people celebrate for three days with a feast called idolfitter, also called the sweet festival. They eat, pray, and give gifts.

video_title: Ruby's Worry  😖 😫 😩|  Kids Story Read Aloud
summary_text: Ruby loved being Ruby. She liked swinging high and exploring faraway places, even the bottom of the garden. One day, Ruby found a small worry. At first she barely noticed it, but each day it grew bigger. It was there at breakfast, at school, and at bedtime. No one else could see it, so Ruby tried to act normal. But the worry stopped her from doing the things she loved. Ruby began to worry about the worry, and it grew enormous. It filled the kitchen, the school bus, and the cinema. Ruby thought she might never feel happy again. Then she saw a boy sitting alone in the park with a worry beside him. Ruby talked to him, and his worry shrank. Ruby talked about her own worry too, and it got smaller and smaller until it was gone. Ruby felt like herself again, and later worries did not stay for long.

Then Bruce’s empty lunchbox was found with two rare cobblestone tiger beetles in it. Since these beetles lived in the forest, the land had to be protected. The factory was stopped, and the forest became Bruce Wildland Park.

In the morning, William saw happy families and a gift from the night gardener. Later, the leaves changed, fell, and the topiary disappeared, but the town and William were changed by what had happened.

The insects returned to the garden, and Spider was left alone. Then Spider looked at the stars, spun high in the flowers, and more wonders fell from the sky.

Dung beetle tried to roll it, and stink bug said it must have grown from the ground.
Then the wise grasshopper said it was not of Earthly Origins and might be a fallen star, a comet, or a small planet.
Luna Moth knew it was actually a magical Chrysalis that needed warmth, but it did not hatch.
In the morning, spider said it belonged to him because it had fallen into his web.
He built Wonderville to show it off and sold tickets.
Many insects visited, but the spider kept raising prices and grew rich.
Then a five-legged creature stole the wonder and took it back to the sky.
After that, the garden changed, the insects returned, and the spider was left alone.
Later, he looked at the stars, understood what he needed to do, and waited patiently until more wonders fell from the sky.

summary_text: Mortimer was lonely because he did not have a sweetheart before Cupid’s ball. He tried to win girls over in many ways. He read advice books, walked his dog, exercised at the gym, and took ballroom dancing lessons, but nothing helped. Then Mortimer placed a newspaper ad saying he was tall, dead, handsome, and wanted someone who liked graveyards, horror films, and Voodoo. On Saturday, he bought a new suit at the funeral home, fixed his hair, and went to Cupid’s ball. He waited by the punch bowl, but every girl ran away when he smiled. As the room emptied, Mortimer started to leave. Then he heard a crash and saw a beautiful girl named Mildred on the floor. She asked if she was too late, and Mortimer said she was right on time. They danced by moonlight and fell in love.

summary_text: Hamlet the pig leaned over a fence and looked at the other pigs in the mud. He asked his mother and father to read a new book to him, but his father only asked if it was a cookbook. Hamlet then showed his mother his notebook and said he had written poems. His sister and brother laughed at him because he wore a clean shirt and wrote poems. While everyone laughed, the farmer walked away from supper, and the pigs rushed across the Mud Hole shouting, “Supper! Supper! Supper!” Hamlet did not feel hungry. He noticed mud on his favorite shirt and walked away by himself. Near the farmer’s pond, he watched the rising moon and wrote more poems in his notebook. When he looked into the pond, he saw his twin reflection, whom he called Eggs. Hamlet read poems to Eggs, and the reflection seemed to answer. Then the moon and clouds changed, the reflection faded, and Hamlet heard small voices say they liked his poems and wanted him to read to them.

summary_text: Lil tells us about her dad, Bill. Bill likes many kinds of food and says, “just try it.” Lil likes only a few foods, like vanilla ice cream, pizza, rice, grilled cheese sandwiches with no crust, and french fries. Then mustard gets on the food. Bill reminds her of their one rule: try things once. After Bill washes his shirt, Lil learns she did try the mustard and liked it. She then wants to try more new things.

The pigs also play bad music, choosing sad country songs instead of marching band music. Finally, they would not hold the giant balloons, so the balloons might drift away. Because of all these problems, the story says a pig parade is a terrible idea.

This year, Bruce’s family had an idea. They decided to act out a scary story called the legend of Soggy Hollow. They got dress-ups and asked friends to help. Then the story began. Long ago, a soldier lost his horse and became known as the Horseless Horsemen of Soggy Hollow. Later, a school teacher named Bruce moved to town. He was kind and gave students treats, sang, and danced, and he liked Miss Camila van muffl. One night, he went to ask her to marry him, but he got scared on the way. Miss van muffl said yes, and Bruce was happy. Then the Horseless Horsemen came close, and Bruce ran through the woods. After the chase, Bruce gave out candy, Camila said, “My hero,” and the old story was still told on cold nights.

When Alice spoke up, the cards flew at her, and she woke up on the riverbank beside her sister.

video_title: 🦖 Goldilocks and the Three Dinosaurs 🦕 by Mo Willems 📚 Kids Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Papa Dinosaur, Mama Dinosaur, and a visiting dinosaur from Norway live in a house with three bowls of chocolate pudding. They make their beds, set their chairs, and cook the pudding, then go away and leave the house unlocked. Soon, Goldilocks comes by and walks into the strange big house. She smells the pudding and climbs a tall ladder to reach it. She eats the first bowl, which is too hot, the second bowl, which is too cold, and the third bowl, which is just right. Then she sees three chairs, but all of them are too tall. After that, she goes to the bedroom and finds the beds are also too big. Goldilocks realizes this is not a bear’s house. She runs out the back door. Then the three dinosaurs rush back, but Goldilocks is already gone. The story ends with the dinosaurs disappointed and the house still needing the back door locked.

In the end, the pirates danced and took treasure home, and they learned to check that their pants elastic is in place.

Finn looked out at the sea and remembered the magical place.

He got salmon, honey, and eggs, and he went home to cook. But the fire in his stove went out, so he went to get more wood. When he came back, he found that the eggs had turned into goslings. Bruce did not want goslings. He took them back to their nest, but Mrs. Goose was away. The goslings followed him home, and Bruce could not make them leave. As time passed, the goslings grew up. In winter, Bruce and the geese packed bags, took a bus, and migrated to Miami together. Now they spend winter at the beach.

Penelope felt sad and thought she was not right for the job. Then she stopped and remembered that not all library voices are quiet. She got a new idea, went back to work, and soon students came to listen. In the end, Penelope smiled and invited everyone to come back for Penelope story time the next day.

Kelp then wondered if he had to choose between the sea and land.

video_title: Farmhouse
summary_text: At the end of a road by a glittering stream stood a house where 12 children were born and grew up. They learned to crawl in the front hall, stood on the wooden stairs for pictures, and had their heights marked on the wall. They played, lied about the cat, and were scolded. In the serious room, men were comforted and the organ was played. The children read books about planets and stars, dreamed of Mars, kept secrets, and collected toys, feathers, bones, and movie stars. They worked hard, too. They milked the cows in the barn, fed calves, cleaned stalls, fished in the stream, picked apples, and brought mud into the house. They helped their mother, set the table, cared for a sick younger child, and sewed and darned their clothes. Spring always came, and rain leaked through the roof. As the children grew up and left, the youngest one finally went away too. Then the house leaned, rotted, and slowly fell apart.

summary_text: Papa Pig and Rebecca love playing mermaids. Rebecca says she wishes she were a mermaid with a shiny tail. summary_text: Miguel Rivera lived in Santa Cecilia with his big family, including Mama Coco. On Dia de los Muertos, his family remembered relatives who had died. Miguel and his dog Dante tried to go to a talent show, but Dante knocked down the family ofrenda. Miguel saw a photo and learned that Mama Coco’s papa was Ernesto de la Cruz. Miguel’s abuelita broke his guitar, so Miguel went to Ernesto’s tomb and took his guitar. Then he found himself in the land of the dead. He met Mama Imelda, who would not bless him to be a musician. Miguel traveled with Hector to find Ernesto. Ernesto was happy to see Miguel, but Miguel learned Ernesto had stolen Hector’s songs. Ernesto threw Miguel and Hector into a pit. Hector told Miguel about the song “Remember Me.” Miguel returned home with Mama Imelda’s blessing and sang to Mama Coco. Mama Coco remembered her papa, and the family saw that music could bring them together.

summary_text: One fine morning, Chicken Little went out to the woods. An acorn fell on her head, and she thought the sky was falling. She got very scared and said she must go tell the king. On the way, she met Henny Penny, then Goosey Loosey, then Ducky Lucky, and then Turkey Lurkey. Each bird asked how she knew, and Chicken Little said a piece of the sky fell on her head. The other birds became worried too, and all five hurried to tell the king. Then they met Foxy Loxy. He said they should hide in his den while he went to tell the king. The birds followed him inside. summary_text: Lacey Walker liked to talk and talk all the time. Her mom, teacher, brother, and dad all told her to stop talking and listen, but Lacey kept talking. On the way to school, she noticed her friend Nadine told funny jokes. At school, Lacey finished her work and got a gold star for listening. That night, she watched a monster movie with her brother and liked it. She got ready for bed on time, and her dad had time to read two extra books. The next morning, Lacey got her voice back. She talked on the way downstairs, then ate breakfast while her family talked and she listened.

summary_text: Jojo was lonely because she did not have any friends. She saw that Mama duck had ducklings, White kitty had friends, and even the little birds stayed close together. She asked, “Mr. snowman, will you be my friend?” The snowman said yes and told her his name was Puddles. Puddles said he was made with friendship snow and would teach her how to be a good friend. When spring came, Puddles had to go away and told Jojo to keep a heart and remember she was a good friend. Jojo later made new friends, including black kitty and Ned, and Puddles returned every winter.

Little Bear said they had not caught anything, but Dad bear explained that fishing was not only about catching fish. He hid in the bushes and shouted, and the children laughed. They kept playing this trick on each other many times, and Mr. Malouf stayed silly even when he was old.

video_title: 👻 Gustavo the Shy Ghost 🎃 Kids Book Halloween Read Aloud Day of the Dead SEL Short Story
summary_text: Gustavo was a ghost who liked normal ghost things, like passing through walls, making objects fly, and glowing in the dark. But most of all, he loved playing the violin. He also loved Alma, the prettiest monster in town. Gustavo was very shy, and making friends scared him. He tried to get close to the other monsters, but they could not see him. Gustavo wanted to be part of something and to make a friend. So he wrote a letter inviting all the monsters to his violin concert at the Day of the Dead party next full moon at the cemetery. When the night came, Gustavo worried that no one would come. No one was there, so he played by himself. The music made him happy, and he glowed. Then the monsters arrived late and said they had gotten lost while getting flowers. They heard his music and saw his glow. They loved the concert and asked him to hang out. After that, Gustavo’s life changed, and everyone saw how he helped and protected his friends.

After recess, they said goodbye, and Mrs. Hartwell went back to her empty room with Daisy and said she would miss the children too.

video_title: 🤣 Don't Touch That Flower! 🌼 Kids Book First Day of Spring Changing Seasons Read Aloud Short Story
summary_text: One spring day, Squirrel hears a cuckoo call, a bumblebee buzz, and sees a swallow flap by. Bird tells Squirrel these are signs that spring has arrived. Then Squirrel finds a small yellow flower growing between Bird’s tree and Squirrel’s tree. Bird says new flowers are also signs of spring. Squirrel likes spring now and says the flower is his because it is closer to his tree. The next morning, Squirrel worries that wind will blow the flower away, so he tries to protect it. After that, he worries it will get wet, but Bird says flowers need water to grow. The next day, Squirrel shouts at a bee, thinking it is eating the flower. Bird explains that the bee is collecting nectar and that the flower is a wildflower for everyone to enjoy. Squirrel still tries to keep it safe. Later, the flower looks unwell, and Bird says it needs air, light, and space. That night, Squirrel worries, and by the next morning, many flowers have grown. Bird and Squirrel see that there are enough flowers for everyone.

At last Lisa takes him back to his burrow, where he falls into a deep winter sleep and dreams of winter.

Fletcher tried to help by tying a leaf back on with grass and then pushing it onto a twig, but the leaf still fell. The next day, a strong wind blew. Fletcher chased leaves as the squirrel took some for a nest and the hedgehog took some to keep warm. Fletcher cried out that they were stealing the leaves. Fletcher found one last leaf, held it through the wind, and carried it home when it came off. In the cold morning, he saw the tree covered with shining icicles and knew it was beautiful in winter too.

video_title: ❤️ Love in the Library 📚 Kids Book Asian American Heritage Short Read Aloud Story
summary_text:
Tama did not like the desert, but she walked to the library every day in Minidoka. She worked there because she loved books. George came to the library each morning and returned the books he had borrowed. Tama and George had lived in Minidoka for a year. Tama had been sent there with many Japanese Americans from the West Coast, including babies, children, and older people. Life in the camp was hard, with heat, cold, mud, and no privacy. Tama did not know when she would leave, so she kept working and watching the days pass.

Some days many people came to the library, and some days, especially when it snowed, almost no one came. Tama felt constant worry and fear, but the books and George were constant too. One day Tama said she felt sad and confused. George told her there was a word for that: human. Tama felt better and less alone. Later, Tama and George married, had a son in Minidoka, and hoped for the best. Tama wrote that the miracle was in people who believe in change, beauty, and hope.

video_title: ☺️ Alma and How She Got Her Name—Kids Book Hispanic Heritage Read Aloud Short Story
summary_text: Alma Sofia Esperanza José Pura Candela thinks her name is too long and says it never fits. Her daddy asks her to come close and tells her the story of each name. Sofia was her grandmother, who loved books, poetry, jasmine flowers, and her family. Esperanza was her great-grandmother, who wanted to travel and kept her heart with her sailor son. José was Alma’s grandfather, an artist who painted daily life and taught his son to see and love their people. Pura was her great-aunt, who believed ancestors stay near and tied a red string around Alma’s wrist to keep her safe. Candela was her other grandmother, who always stood up for what was right. Then Daddy says Alma was chosen just for her, and she is the first and only Alma. Alma listens to all the stories, then says her name fits her just right and that she has a story to tell.

video_title: 🪨 Stone Soup 🥣 Kids Book Fun Read Aloud Sharing Generosity Short Story
summary_text: Three monks named Hok, Lok, and Siew walked down a mountain road and talked about happiness. They came to a village where people were tired, scared, and did not trust one another. The villagers shut their windows and would not answer the monks’ knocks. Siew said they would show the village how to make stone soup. The monks made a fire, filled a pot with water, and put in three smooth stones. A little girl watched them and helped find the stones. When she told her mother, the mother gave the girl a bigger pot. Soon the other villagers came out to watch. The monks talked about salt, pepper, carrots, onions, and more. Each time, someone ran to get an ingredient and put it in the soup. At last, everyone shared rice, buns, tea, cakes, and more. They ate together, told stories, and let the monks sleep in their homes. In the morning, they said goodbye, and the villagers said sharing had made them richer.

video_title: 📕 Petunia—Kids Book Silly Goose Funny Read Aloud Story by Roger Duvoisin
summary_text: Early one morning, Petunia the silly goose walked in the meadow and found a Book. She had seen a Book before under Bill’s arm, and she remembered hearing that Books are precious and that the one who loves Books is wise. Petunia thought that if she carried the Book and loved it, she would become wise too, and no one would call her silly again. So she took the Book and went off with it. She slept with it and swam with it, and soon she became proud. Her neck stretched longer and longer. The other animals saw her with the Book and believed she was wise. They asked her for advice, and Petunia liked giving it, even when no one asked. She gave wrong advice to King, Ida, Noisy, Straw, and Cotton, and each one had trouble because of what she said. At last, the animals opened a box of candies, and it exploded. Then Petunia saw the Book open and noticed she could not read the words. She understood she must learn to read to be truly wise.

summary_text: One early morning in the meadow, Petunia the silly goose found a Book and thought that owning and loving it would make her wise. She carried it everywhere, slept with it, and swam with it. As she grew prouder, other animals began to believe she was wise and asked her for advice. Petunia gave answers even when no one asked, but her advice was often wrong and caused trouble. She told King the rooster that his comb was fake, which made him stop singing proudly. She counted Ida’s chicks wrong and worried Ida. She tried to smoke Noisy the dog out of a rabbit hole, and he got hurt. She almost pulled Straw the horse’s teeth to stop his toothache, so he said nothing about it again. She also made the animals climb on each other to rescue Cotton the kitten, but they all fell. At last, Petunia read a box of firecrackers as candies, and they exploded. Then she saw she could not read the Book and decided she must learn to read to become truly wise.

video_title: 👧🏾 Areli is a Dreamer—Kids Book Read Aloud Hispanic Heritage Immigrant Story
summary_text: At Abuela’s house in Mexico, Areli loved Saturdays with family, sunshine, games of al escondite, and chasing chickens. On Sundays, she and Alex waited for the phone to ring so they could talk to Mamá and Papá in America. Mamá and Papá said they were trying to bring the children to live with them. But years passed, and they did not come back for birthdays, Día de los Muertos, or Navidad. One day Alex packed a suitcase and left for Nueva York first. Later, Areli started kindergarten and learned new things at school. Then Abuela told her that it was Areli’s turn to leave. Areli said goodbye to her cousins, friends, mountains, and chickens. A kind man took her to America. There, Mamá and Papá cried and hugged her, and Alex was happy to see her. New York was bigger and louder than Mexico, and Areli had to learn English and face teasing at school because she was born in Mexico and was not yet a citizen.

video_title: 🌼 Carmela Full of Wishes—Kids Book Hispanic Heritage Read Aloud Short Story
summary_text: On her birthday, Carmela rode her scooter with her big brother through their town. They passed the greenhouses, the Laundromat, the bodega, the pharmacy, and other busy places. Carmela wore her birthday bracelets, and they jingled as she moved. Her brother did not want her to follow him, and he kept telling her she was annoying. Carmela found a dandelion and wanted to make a wish, but she did not know what to wish for. She helped her brother with the laundry and kept imagining many things, like candy, her mom in a hotel bed, and her dad getting his papers fixed. Then her brother went into a friend’s house, and Carmela sat on the curb. She thought about turning him into animals and looked at the dandelion again. On the way home, she fell and crushed the dandelion. Her brother helped her, then took her to an abandoned farmhouse near the sea. He told her to close her eyes and make her wish. When she opened them, she saw white spores floating in the air like wishes. He said not to tell the wish, and Carmela took off her bracelets and went home with him.

video_title: 🐟 A Different Pond—Kids Book Asian American Heritage Short Read Aloud Story
summary_text: Before sunrise, Dad wakes the child quietly so Mom can keep sleeping. Dad has already made sandwiches and packed the car. The child helps carry the tackle box, and they drive through dark, quiet roads to Lake Street to buy minnows at the bait store. Dad says he has a second job and must work that morning, so they still need to fish for food because everything in America costs a lot of money. At the pond, Dad holds the child’s hand and says, “Step where I step.” The child makes a small fire from dry twigs and lights it with one match. Dad asks the child to put a minnow on the hook, but the child says no because the fish is small. Dad is not upset. He tells about fishing in Vietnam with his brother, who did not come home from the war. Soon Dad catches crappie, and the child helps put them in the bucket. They go home with enough fish for dinner.

video_title: ☺️ Amy Wu and The Perfect Bao—Kids Book Asian American Heritage Chinese Lunar New Year Read Aloud
summary_text: Amy can do many things, but she cannot make the perfect bao. Her mom, dad, and grandma make soft, fluffy bao that Amy loves to eat. Today, Amy wants to make the best bao ever. Her dad makes the dough in the morning and kneads it. Amy helps, and the dough rises and gets bigger. Her mom makes the filling with garlic, mushrooms, pepper, salt, and ginger. Then everyone starts making bao. Amy’s first bao is too small, and her second is not quite right either. It is hard to know how much filling to use and how to pinch the dough shut. Amy watches her family make bao and tries to copy them, but her bao still leak or have holes. Then Amy has an idea. Her grandma cuts the dough into smaller pieces for Amy’s small hands. Now Amy can roll, fill, and pinch the bao better. She makes perfect bao, and later they are steamed and eaten.

video_title: 🦋 Eyes that Kiss in the Corners—Kids Book Asian American Heritage Short Read Aloud
summary_text: The child tells us about eyes that kiss in the corners and glow like warm tea. At first, the child says some people have big eyes and long lashes, but their own eyes are different. The child’s eyes are like Mama’s. When Mama comes home from work, her eyes crinkle into crescent moons. She hugs the child, tickles them, and tucks them into bed at night. The child also says Mama’s eyes are like Amah’s eyes. Amah’s eyes do not work like they used to, but she can still see into the child’s heart and read the child’s mind. Her eyes hold many stories, and the child imagines Guanyin, the Monkey King, lychee trees, and mountains by the sea. The child then says Amah’s eyes are like Mei-Mei’s eyes too. Mei-Mei waits at the window, smiles with two teeth, and follows the child around. In the end, the child says their own eyes are like all of theirs and are beautiful.

video_title: 🐯 Little Sambha and the Tigers—Kids Book Short Fable Read Aloud
summary_text: Little Sambha lived with his mother, Maata, and his father, Baapa. Maata made him a red coat and blue trousers. Baapa bought him a green umbrella and purple shoes with crimson soles and linings. Little Sambha put on his fine clothes and went for a walk in the jungle. There he met many tigers. Each tiger said it would eat him up, and each time Little Sambha gave away one of his things to stay safe. He gave away his coat, then his trousers, then his shoes, and then his umbrella. After that, he had nothing left and cried. Soon he heard a loud noise and saw the tigers arguing about which one was the grandest. They fought, rolled, and spun around the tree until they melted into a pool of butter. Baapa took the butter home, Maata made pancakes, and the family ate a big supper.

video_title: 🍦One Morning in Maine ☺️ Kids Book Read Aloud Classic by Robert McCloskey
summary_text: One morning in Maine, Sal woke up and remembered that she was going to Buck's Harbor with her father. She got ready and helped little Jane dress too. In the bathroom, Sal found that one of her teeth was loose. She ran to her mother, who told her that loose baby teeth fall out when a child grows up and that a new tooth will grow in later. Sal learned that when a tooth comes out, it can be put under a pillow for a secret wish. After breakfast, Sal worked with her father on the beach, digging clams. She showed her loose tooth to fish hawks, a loon, a seal, and seagulls. While she was helping dig, her tooth dropped out in the mud and she could not find it. Later, she found a gull feather, made her secret wish on it, and went with her family to Buck's Harbor. There, a spark plug came out of the boat motor, and Sal gave her wish to Jane. After errands and ice-cream cones, Sal went home happy and said they would have clam chowder for lunch.

video_title: 🐑 A New Coat for Anna—Kids Book Read Aloud Short Story
summary_text: Winter came, and Anna needed a new coat because her old blue one was too small. Her mother had once hoped to buy one after the war, but the stores were still empty and there was no money. So Anna’s mother used family treasures to trade for what they needed. The snow says hello to the storm and howls. Then morning comes. The orange hills glow, and the early light shines on everything. The snow begins to melt in the sun and turn to slush. Soon the winter thaw brings new leaves, waking animals, bright flowers, blue water, running brooks, and green grass. Robins come back, the petals bloom, the fish wake up, and streams run down the hills. In the end, winter is gone, and spring arrives.

summary_text: Cassie Louise Lightfoot is eight years old and lives with her family in a building roof she calls Tar Beach. One night she lies on the roof and looks at the stars, the skyscrapers, and the George Washington Bridge. She remembers that Daddy worked on the bridge and told her it is the longest and most beautiful bridge in the world. Cassie says she can fly, and she thinks that if she flies over something, it can be hers forever. She wants the bridge to be her prized possession. Daddy also works on a new Union building, but he cannot join the union because Grandpa was not a member. Cassie thinks that if she flies over the building, it can belong to Daddy. Then he would not have to work so hard, and Mommy would not cry when he looks for work. On Tar Beach, Mommy cooks peanuts and chicken, Daddy brings watermelon, and the Honey neighbors play cards. Cassie plans to fly with Bibi to the union building, because anyone can fly if they have somewhere to go that they cannot reach any other way.

summary_text: At night, the moon rises and the Flying Fox wakes up to look for food. It is a bat, not a fox. Flying foxes sleep in the day and fly at night. They like fruit, especially ripe figs, and they also lick nectar from flowers. The pollen sticks to them and helps plants grow. The story then tells about Stellaluna, a baby fruit bat who gets lost one night when an owl swoops down. She falls into a forest and lands in a bird nest. The baby birds are surprised. Stellaluna is hungry, but she does not want the bugs the bird mother brings. Later she eats a grasshopper. She learns to live like the birds, but she still hangs by her feet. When she tries to fly like them, she feels clumsy and flies away by day. At last, other bats find her and show her she is a bat. Stellaluna brings the birds to meet her bat family, and they stay friends even though they are different.

video_title: Rechenka's Eggs STORY
summary_text: Babushka lived alone in a little house in the country and was known for painting beautiful eggs. Every year, her eggs won first prize at the Easter Festival in Moscow. One day after a snowstorm, she went outside to feed the wild caribou and saw a goose fall from the sky. She put the goose in a basket lined with a warm quilt and named her Rashenka. Babushka cared for Rashenka, and the goose grew strong. Rashenka laid an egg each morning, but one day she jumped on Babushka’s work table and knocked over the basket of painted eggs. The eggs broke, and both Babushka and Rashenka felt sad. The next morning, Babushka found a shining egg in Rashenka’s basket. She cooked the egg for breakfast and admired its beauty. Soon she had enough eggs for the festival, where the judges chose her eggs as the most beautiful. Babushka won first prize, a feather bed quilt, and went home happy. Later, she found a new egg in Rashenka’s basket and saw that it was hatching. A special gosling came out, and Rashenka stayed with Babushka.

summary_text: Ancient Egypt was a long country with the Nile River running through it. The people buried their dead and hoped to live forever. They believed that after death, a new life would begin, and they would live in their tombs as they had on earth. To do this, the body had to be preserved. A body that was dried so it would not decay was called a mummy. At first, the hot, dry sand of Egypt dried bodies naturally. Later, embalmers learned to mummify bodies in a careful process that took 70 days. They removed the organs, covered the body with Natron, and let it dry. Then they cleaned it, added oils and spices, wrapped it in linen strips, and placed a portrait mask on the head. Artists and carpenters made coffins and sarcophagi, and the tomb walls were painted with scenes from Egyptian life. Finally, a funeral procession carried the mummy to the tomb, where it was sealed inside forever.

video_title: Lemonade For Sale STORY
summary_text: The Elm Street kids club felt sad because their clubhouse was falling down and their piggy bank was empty. Matthew said they could sell lemonade to make money. Danny said they should sell many cups each day for a week, and Sherry said she would make a bar graph to keep track. On Monday, the children set up a stand. Petey, Meg’s pet parrot, squawked, “lemonade for sale,” and the children made and sold lemonade. Sherry filled in the Monday bar. On Tuesday they sold more cups, and the bar went higher. On Wednesday even more people came, and the sales grew again. On Thursday, hardly anyone stopped, because people were watching a juggler named Jed. Sherry saw what was happening and made a plan. On Friday Jed juggled next to their stand, Petey called out the same words, and many people came. The children sold lots of lemonade and earned enough money to rebuild their clubhouse. They asked Jed to join the club, and he said yes.

video_title: Borreguita and the Coyote STORY
summary_text: Borreguita was a little lamb who lived on a farm at the foot of a mountain. One day her master tied her to a stake in a field of red clover. While she ate, a coyote came and said he would eat her. Borreguita told him she was still too thin, and he should come back when she was fat. The coyote agreed and left. Later he returned, but Borreguita tricked him again. She told him about cheese, and at night she led him to the pond. He saw a round shape in the water and thought it was cheese, but it was only a reflection. When he jumped in, the image broke and he got wet, while Borreguita escaped. The next day she fooled him again by pretending to hold up a mountain under a rock ledge. Coyote helped by holding it up with his own feet, and Borreguita ran away. At last, Borreguita tricked him one more time and knocked him back, so Coyote never bothered her again.

The wise shaman saw that Little Gopher had a special gift and told him his path would be different from the warriors. When Little Gopher went to the hills alone, he had a dream vision. A young Indian maiden and an old grandfather came to him and gave him tools for painting. The maiden showed him a pure white buckskin and told him to find one like it. After the dream ended, Little Gopher made brushes and paints and began painting hunts and visions. He found a white buckskin, but he could not make the colors of the sunset. One evening, a voice said he would find the colors because he had been faithful. The next night, sunset-colored brushes appeared, and he painted quickly. In the morning, the brushes had grown into bright flowers, and the people gave him a new name: He who brought the sunset to the earth.

video_title: Mufaro's Beautiful Daughters STORY
summary_text: A long time ago in Africa, Mufaro lived with his two daughters, Manyara and Nyasha. Both girls were beautiful, but Manyara was often mean and told Nyasha that one day she would be queen and Nyasha would be a servant. Nyasha stayed kind and worked in the garden. One day she found a small snake named Nyoka and welcomed it. Soon a messenger said the king wanted to see the most beautiful and worthy daughters in the land so he could choose a queen. Mufaro told both girls to get ready. That night Manyara left early, but she was rude to a hungry boy, an old woman, and laughing trees. In the morning she was missing, so the others followed her path. Nyasha gave food to the boy, seeds to the old woman, and the trees bowed to her. At the city gate, Manyara ran out in fear after seeing a monster. Nyasha went inside and found Nyoka, who changed into the king and chose her to be his wife. A great feast was held, and Mufaro was glad that Nyasha became queen.

summary_text: The Gruffalo tells his child about the Big Bad Mouse and says the mouse is strong, scary, and has a long tail and fiery eyes. In the end, footprints lead back to the Gruffalo cave, and the Gruffalo’s Child is less bored and less brave while the Gruffalo still snores.

Then even more snoots need boops, including sitting, standing, and upside down snoots. The boops continue all around until every snoot is booped. The story ends with clapping and hoorays, but then it says there is one more snoot that needs a boop.

video_title: I Can Handle It Read Aloud
summary_text: Sebastian says he can handle anything. He tells about many times when he feels hard feelings. When his best friend is mad, Sebastian feels sad, but he can give a hug, try to make him laugh, or draw a picture. When adults do not listen, he feels frustrated, and he can say, “Excuse me,” write a letter, or tell someone else. When his sister bothers him, he feels mad, and he can ask her to stop, move away, or make a joke. When he cannot find his shoe, he feels annoyed, and he can look for it or wear another pair. When he wants a pet but cannot have one, he feels disappointed, and he can pretend, make a pet, or play with a friend’s pet. Sebastian also feels ashamed, upset, discouraged, cranky, and miserable at other times, but he finds ways to handle each problem. In the end, he says he can handle all of these feelings.

video_title: Otis and the Tornado Read Aloud
summary_text: Otis and the little calf liked to play Follow the Leader with all the Farm Friends. They marched around the apple tree, the barn, the hill, the pond, the cornfield, the meadow, and Mud Creek. Everyone played together except the bull. The bull lived alone in a pasture and scared the other animals. Otis once brought him a red apple and asked him to play, but the bull snorted, glared, and charged at the fence, so Otis stayed away from him after that. One day a storm came. The sky turned green, the wind stopped, and the farmer shouted that a tornado was coming. Otis opened the stalls and let the calf, pig, sheep, horse, and cow out of the barn. Then he heard the bull crying in his pen. Otis rushed back, broke the gate, and led the bull to Mud Creek. The animals hid there until the tornado passed. After the storm, the farm needed repairs, and the bull joined the other animals in Follow the Leader.

video_title: The Dot Read Aloud
summary_text: Art class was over, and Vosi still had a blank paper. Her teacher looked at it and said it was a polar bear in a snow storm. Vosi said she could not draw. Her teacher told her to make a mark and see where it takes her. Vosi made a strong dot on the paper. Her teacher looked closely and told her to sign it. Vosi said that maybe she could not draw, but she could sign her name. The next week, Vosi saw her dot hanging above her teacher’s desk in a gold frame. Vosi wanted to make a better dot, so she used watercolors to paint yellow, green, red, and blue dots. Red and blue made purple. She kept making more dots, big and small, and even made a dot by not painting one. At the school art show, a little boy said he could not draw. Vosi gave him a blank paper and told him to show her. When he drew a shaky line, Vosi asked him to sign it.

video_title: The Little Old Lady Who Was Not Afraid of Anything Read Aloud
summary_text: A little old lady who was not afraid of anything went out from her cottage one windy afternoon to gather herbs, spices, nuts, and seeds in the forest. She stayed out so long that it became dark. On the path home, she met two big shoes that went clomp clomp. She told them to get out of her way and kept walking. Then she met a pair of pants that went wiggle wiggle, a shirt that went shake shake, two white gloves that went clap clap, and a tall black hat that went nod nod. Each time, she said she was not afraid and walked faster. Near her cottage, she found a very big orange pumpkin head that went boo boo. This time she ran home and locked her door. Later, she opened the door and saw all the things again. The pumpkin head said they came to scare her, but she was not afraid. She whispered to the pumpkin head, and the next morning the pumpkin head and the other things were in her garden, scaring away the crows.

video_title: Shark Lady Read Aloud
summary_text: Eugene loved the aquarium on Saturday. She watched the glittery fish and, most of all, the sharks. She pretended to swim like them and wanted to know what it would be like to live under the sea. In the summer, her mother took her to the beach in Atlantic City, and Eugene dove into the water. She imagined sharks, sea stars, and ocean currents, and she saw sharks as beautiful. Since the sharks were only in her mind, she decided to learn all she could about them. Eugene read books about whale sharks, nurse sharks, tiger sharks, and lemon sharks. She joined the Queens County aquarium society and filled her notebooks with shark drawings and facts. Her mother also gave her a small aquarium, and Eugene kept fish and snails in her room. As she grew older, people told her to stop thinking about sharks, but Eugene studied zoology, became a scientist, found new fish, saw a wild shark, and later trained sharks. In the end, she proved sharks are smart and should be protected and loved.

video_title: Click, Clack, Moo Cows That Type Read Aloud
summary_text: Farmer Brown has a very strange problem. His cows find an old typewriter in the barn and begin typing all day. Farmer Brown hears, “click clack moo, click clack moo, clickity clack moo,” and then sees that the cows really are typing. The cows send him a note asking for electric blankets because the barn is cold at night. Farmer Brown says no. Then the cows go on strike. They put a sign on the barn door that says there will be no milk. The next day they send another note saying the hens are cold too and want electric blankets. Farmer Brown still says no, and now there are no eggs either. Farmer Brown gets angry and writes back that he wants milk and eggs. Duck carries the message to the cows. The cows meet and send back a deal: electric blankets for the typewriter. Farmer Brown agrees and leaves the blankets outside. But the next morning, Duck brings him a new note. The ducks now want a diving board for the pond.

summary_text: A dinosaur stays safe all day at home, at school, and at play. He does not climb too high, jump on his bed, race his bike without a helmet, or be rough with the cat. He does not stand on chairs when Mama says no. He does not run down the stairs or jump from the rooftop. When he crosses the street, he holds Mama’s hand tight and watches for the light. When he eats, he is careful with forks, knives, and spoons. He does not go with strangers. When he swims with friends, he stays where Papa can see him. He wears a good helmet on his bike and takes water on a long hike. In playtime, he knows how to dial 911. The story ends with a big roar to stay safe and play safe, little dinosaur.
