video_title: Storms Read Aloud
summary_text: Storms happen in the atmosphere, the blanket of air around Earth. When the air changes fast and hard, we call it weather, and very violent weather is a storm. Thunderstorms are powerful storms that can bring huge amounts of rain, hail, lightning, and thunder. They begin when warm, wet air rises from the ground and meets cool, dry air. Tiny water drops form clouds, and the cloud can grow very tall and wide. Inside the storm, water drops bump together and grow bigger. Then heavy rain or hail falls, and strong winds blow up and down inside the storm cell. Some thunderstorms stand alone, but many join in a squall line. Thunderstorms help move heat high into the sky and bring water to dry land. They can also make hail, strong gust fronts, and dangerous lightning that can start fires and hurt people.

video_title: Storms Read Aloud
summary_text: The story explains that the atmosphere is always moving, and its violent changes are called storms. It begins with thunderstorms, which are powerful electrical storms. Warm, moist air rises, cools, and forms puffy clouds that grow into tall thunderheads. Inside the storm, droplets join together, rain or hail falls, and strong updrafts and downdrafts make a storm cell. Many storm cells can line up in a squall line, and each cell dies when cold wind pushes the rain outward and cuts off the rising warm air. Thunderstorms help cool the Earth, clean the air, and carry water to dry places. The story then describes hail, gust fronts, lightning, and thunder, and explains how to count seconds between flash and sound to judge distance. It also gives safety rules for lightning and tornadoes, and ends with hurricanes, the deadliest storms, which form over warm seas, bring storm surges, and are tracked by satellites and radar.

video_title: The Worrysaurus Read Aloud
summary_text: Worry Saurus woke up, brushed his tiny teeth, washed his top and tail, and packed a little bag of snacks. He set off along the golden sand, thinking about a picnic he had planned. Soon, his busy head started to worry. He wondered if he had enough food and drink, and he thought about getting lost or having a fall. Then a lizard skittered by and shouted that a storm was coming. Worry Saurus felt scared and said he was not ready for rain. The sky was still blue and the sun was shining, but his happy picnic thoughts were gone. He remembered what his mommy said: if it is not a happy ending, then it has not ended yet. He took out his little tin with special things inside, like Teddy Ned, a pebble, and a letter. Holding them helped him feel better. He calmed his busy brain, shared his picnic with the lizard, and they laughed and had fun in the sun.

video_title: Trick ARR Treat Read Aloud
summary_text: The pirate Chief shuts the door and gives the gang rules for Halloween. They must be home by dark, and they must not smile or be sweet. Gabby, Pete, Tim, and the other pirates say they are brave and fierce. They go down dark streets, house to house, stomping, clomping, and shouting, “We be Pirates! Trick our treat!” Charlotte Blue Tongue, Rude Renit, and Dreadful Davey ask for loot and treasure. The pirates stick out their tongues and make loud pirate sounds. Then they hear panting and slurping. They keep sneaking and peeking for more treats. Charlotte Blue Tongue says she wants her belly filled, and the others say silly pirate things. Suddenly, the pirates see a scary sea serpent in the Halloween dark. They get frightened and yell at it to go away. But the Beast is not there to fight. He runs faster than the pirates because he wants to share the feast. The pirates run through the park and find a party on a gangplank, where scoundrels are playing games and laughing. Then everyone gets to eat and enjoy the booty.

video_title: Abuela Read Aloud
summary_text: Abella is the narrator’s grandma. She speaks mostly Spanish, and she and the narrator go places together. One day they go to the park and see many birds around the bread they bought. Abella imagines the birds lifting her up so she can fly. The narrator calls to her, and Abella answers and leaps into the sky. They fly over the city, parks, streets, buses, factories, trains, and the Sea. They see ships, fruit from Abella’s home country, and the Statue of Liberty. Abella remembers coming to this country for the first time. They fly to the airport, then to Tio Pablo and Tia Alisa’s store for lemonada. They rest in the clouds, look at shapes in the sky, and fly over their house and the building where the narrator’s father works. At the end, they return to the park by the lake, and Abella invites the narrator on another adventure.

video_title: My Parents Think I'm Sleeping Read Aloud
summary_text: The child says parents think they are sleeping, but they are not. Under the covers, they read poems and stories, shine a flashlight, and play with a model rocket kit. At night, the child hears many loud sounds and imagines ogres, tigers, monkeys, elephants, pigs, dinosaurs, and a poltergeist army, but it is only the alley cat chorus outside. The clouds that looked like silent sheep in the day seem like smoky wolves at night, and then the child tells how night is all around and must be slept through until day comes back. The child also sees a spooky shadow on the wall and feels afraid to close their eyes. Later, the child thinks about how colors disappear at night and return at dawn. The story also shows the child lying in bed, dreaming of a forest, thinking of chocolate cake, listening to rain, and finally noticing the very still night, the moonlight, and the special lamp before staying awake and trying hard to sleep.

video_title: Good Night, Body Read Aloud
summary_text: The speaker talks kindly to their body before sleep. They ask the body to get the last wiggles out by curling up tight like a hedgehog and opening wide like a starfish. Then they climb into bed and imagine it is a tree house, safe and calm. The speaker says hello to each part of the body one by one: head, mind, face, eyes, mouth, shoulders, arms, hands, fingers, heart, lungs, belly, hips, legs, feet, and toes. Each part is asked to be soft, still, stretchy, or gentle in a special way. The heart says, “you’re loved, you’re loved,” and the lungs breathe in air and let it go back out. At the end, the speaker asks the body if it is ready for sleep and says, “Good night body. Good night dear friend. Thank you for being my home.”

video_title: I Am Love Read Aloud
summary_text: The story begins when the speaker sees someone in a storm of hurt, unfairness, anger, and sadness. The sky grows dark, and the speaker listens with a hand on the heart to find the answer. The speaker says love is compassion and tenderness. Love can listen without speaking, stay close, hug, hold, and say everything will be all right. Love is also gentle words, gratitude, and taking care of the body and mind. In the middle, the speaker says love can help someone share what is important, understand that no one is perfect, and try to make things better when something is wrong. Love can also remember people who were loved before and notice small kind acts like a smile or helping hand. At the end, the speaker says all creatures share the world and the same Stardust. When clouds come for others and for the speaker, the heart leads the way, and love helps everyone weather the storm and Light Up the Sky together.

video_title: I'm Fast! Read Aloud
summary_text: A freight train races toward Chicago. At first, one train says, “First one to Chicago wins!” The other train says it must load its freight first. It loads lumber, bricks, a gondola, a steel coil car, a gas tank car, and a gravel bin. Then it opens the hatch, checks the hopper catch, and goes fast. The train carries a freezer car full of ice cream bars and sees cold mountain ahead. It takes an auto rack through a tunnel and out into the snow. It pushes through and keeps going. It also carries a boxcar full of food like wheat, eggs, tomatoes, peppers, and cheese. Trucks ride on piggyback cars, and cattle stand on the track, so the cows move out of the way. The freight cars roll on the side track and the train wins the race to Chicago.

Then it opens the hatch, the hopper catch, and the throttle goes up. The train says, “Ready, set, roll!” It races ahead carrying a freezer car full of ice cream bars. The train goes past a cold mountain, takes a shortcut through rock, and rushes through a tunnel from the dark into the snow. It keeps moving fast, even when the track is hard. Later, it carries a boxcar full of boxes with wheat, eggs, tomatoes, peppers, and cheese. It also tows trucks on piggyback cars. When cows block the track, they move aside. The freight cars call out their names, and the train moves onto the side track, slows down, and wins the race to Chicago. At the end, the train invites red to take the train back.

video_title: Skippyjon Jones In The Doghouse Read Aloud
summary_text: Skippy John Jones made a very big artwork on the newly painted hall walls, and Mama June Bug Jones was upset. She told him to drop the crayon and said he was not a chihuahua, but a naughty Siamese cat who needed a time out. Mama put him in his room and said she would get him a fat mouse with butter and cheese if he thought Siamese and stayed out of his closet. But Skippy John Jones was already thinking of bouncing and of being a chihuahua. He bounced high and low, missed the chair, and landed in a pile of stuffed animals. Then he put on his mask and cape and used a Spanish accent to sing about Scapito Fresquito. Mama and the girls watched TV, but Skippy John Jones was not thinking Siamese. He went into his closet and found a place full of chihuahuas and his old amigos, the lost Chimichangas. They told him a Babalito was in their house, and they rolled him into a three-bean burrito. They took him to the doghouse, where he fought the Babalito, stuffed the little bubbly toe into his pants, and brought him down. Then Skippy John Jones went back to his room, wrapped in his blankie, talking to his bobble head and still thinking Chihuahua.

video_title: The Tub People Read Aloud
summary_text: The tub people were seven wooden figures who stood in a line on the edge of the bathtub: father, mother, grandmother, doctor, policeman, child, and dog. Every bath time, the father played sea captain and took the mother, grandmother, and child for rides on the floating soap. The policeman and doctor had water races, and the child cheered. When bath time ended, they always lined up again. One evening, the water rushed down the drain too soon. The soap spun in a whirlpool, and the child was carried away. The father could not save him. The mother looked into the drain, and all the tub people felt sad. That night and the next night, they called for their child, but he did not answer. Later, a big man fixed the drain and pulled the child back out. The tub people smiled, but the child was put into a tool box. After that, they waited until they were moved to a new room and placed on a soft bed, where they became seven again and played new games together.

summary_text: A lonely prince wanted to marry a girl, but his mother, Queen Larena, wanted a very special wife for him. One day a maiden came to the castle and asked to stay. The prince liked her right away and said he would marry her. Queen Larena wanted to test the girl, so she put a tiny pea under many mattresses and blankets on the bed. The girl slept in the bed, but it felt lumpy and hard. In the morning, Larena asked how she slept. The girl said she slept on a heart lumpy bed. The prince was happy because the girl had passed the test. He asked her to marry him, and they had a royal wedding in the castle. The queen did not know that the prince had helped the girl by putting pitchforks and stones in the bed.

video_title: Animals In Winter Read Aloud
summary_text: The days grow short and the nights grow long. It gets cold, and winter is coming. Leaves fall from the trees, and there are no berries or seeds left. Birds and animals get ready in different ways. Bluebirds and Orioles fly south to warm, sunny places with food. In spring, they fly back north. Monarch butterflies also migrate. They gather in a tree by the hundreds, stay there all night, and fly south in the morning. Some bats go south, but some stay in caves and hibernate all winter without eating. Woodchucks hibernate too. In fall, a woodchuck eats grass, twigs, and leaves, grows fat, and sleeps in a long tunnel for many months. Some animals, like pikas and squirrels, store food for winter. Other animals must hunt all winter for food. When spring comes, the days grow longer and the weather gets warmer.

video_title: I Am Enough Read Aloud
summary_text: The story says, “I am enough.” It tells about a child who is like many things in nature and life. The child is like the sun, and shines. The child is like a voice and sings, like a bird and flies, like trees and grows, and like mountains and stands strong. The child also fights like a champ, loves like a heart, climbs like a ladder, and rises like the air and wind. The child pushes, pulls, pours, and falls like rain. The child dreams like the moon, learns like a student, swells like water, and burns like fire. Even in winter, the child keeps trying. Sometimes the child cries, but still tries again. The story says people do not have to be the same. They may look different and sometimes disagree, but they all have worth. In the end, they should live with love, help each other, stay together, and remember: “I am enough.”

Miss Nelson asked them to settle down, but they did not listen. The next morning, Miss Nelson did not come to school. The children were glad at first and thought they could misbehave even more. Then a stern new teacher came in an ugly black dress. She called herself Miss Viola Swamp. She made the children open their arithmetic books, do their work, and have no Story Hour. She gave lots of homework and warned them to be quiet and still. After many days, the children missed Miss Nelson and tried to find her. They asked Detective Mick Smog, but he was not much help. They also went to Miss Nelson’s house, but no one answered. At last, when they thought Miss Nelson was gone forever, she came back. The children were happy to see her, and they quickly behaved well during Story Hour. Miss Nelson smiled and kept her little secret.

summary_text: Skeleton woke up with the hiccups. He took a shower, brushed his teeth, polished his bones, carved a pumpkin, and raked leaves. Then he played with a ghost. video_title: Leaves Read Aloud

In spring, he woke with wide eyes. He felt the sun and saw little buds on the bare trees and tiny leaves opening. He cried, “Welcome!” and thought the leaves welcomed him.

video_title: The Koala Who Could Read Aloud
summary_text: Kevin was a koala who liked to stay high in his tree. He liked to cling, nap, and eat leaves. He thought the ground below was too fast, too loud, and too strange, so he did not want to try new things. One day Wombat called up to him and asked him to come down and play. Then Ruse and the dingos also invited him. Kevin said no and stayed in his tree. Days and weeks passed, and Kevin kept still while the others played below. Then one day he heard a tapping sound and saw a crowd under the tree. They told him to jump and said they would catch him. Kevin was scared and said he could not let go. But then the tree came down with a crash. Kevin loosened his paws one by one and found that he felt light, safe, and happy. Wombat held out a paw, Dingo asked him to play, and Kevin said yes. After that, Kevin was ready to try something new.

video_title: Miss Nelson Has A Field Day Read Aloud
summary_text: For some weeks, Horse Beasts Medley School felt sad and gloomy. The Smedley tornadoes did not win games, did not score, and kept horsing around. Miss Nelson worried about them, and Mr. Blandsworth said they needed a real expert. One day Coach Armstrong was laughing too hard, so Miss Nelson took him home in a taxi for a long rest. After that, the school said he had the measles. The children talked at Lulu’s and said they needed someone tough like Viola Swamp, the meanest substitute in the whole wide world. Miss Nelson heard this, went home, found an ugly black sweat suit, and made an important phone call. The next day, a lady named Viola Swamp came to coach football. She made the team work hard with leg raises, fast running, and tough rules. In just a few days, the team got much better. When Coach Armstrong came back, the players looked great. On Thanksgiving Day, the tornadoes beat the werewolves 77 to 3, and everyone celebrated with hot dogs.

video_title: Ballet Stars Read Aloud
summary_text: Today is ballet show day. The children dress up in sparkly ribbons, ballet shoes, bright white tights, and new tutus. They do stretches, bends, and warm-ups with their ballet friends. They make ballet arms and ballet feet, point their toes, and bring their fingers together. Then they go across the floor. They run three steps and jump on four. Their families and friends come to watch the show. When the music starts, the dancers find their places and smile. They twirl like snowflakes, sway like trees, and dance in twos and threes. In two rows, the ballet dancers do turns on tippy toes. At the end, they bow to the left and below, and send kisses to the right. Everyone is a ballet star tonight.

video_title: 🏹🔥The Rough-Face Girl🔥🏹Native American Cinderella Read Aloud for Kids
summary_text: Long ago, by Lake Ontario, there was a great wigwam where an invisible being lived with his sister. Many women wanted to marry him, but his sister said only someone who could see him could become his wife. In one village, a poor man had three daughters. The two older girls were cruel to their youngest sister and made her sit by the fire until her hands, arms, face, and hair were burned and scarred. The older sisters tried to marry the invisible being, but his sister asked them questions about his bow and sled runner, and they guessed wrong. Then the rough-faced girl asked for beads, buckskin, and moccasins, and she made her own dress from birch bark. People laughed at her, but she kept walking. The sister of the invisible being saw her kind heart, answered her questions, and welcomed her. The invisible being arrived, married her, and after she bathed in the lake, her scars disappeared and her beauty returned.

summary_text: On Christmas Eve, long ago, a boy from Finmark was traveling to Oslo with his ice bear. He saw smoke from a hut and went toward it because he was cold and hungry. Inside the hut, Kyrie was warming food on the fire. There was sausage, fish, buns, cakes, porridge, and apple cider. Kyrie had been afraid because trolls had come in past years and eaten the Christmas meal. Her father had gone up the mountain to watch for them. The boy came inside, and the ice bear slept under the stove. Soon they heard knocking at the door and more loud banging. The boy pushed a chest in front of the door and locked the windows. Then the trolls broke in through the cellar trapdoor. They ate the food and made a big mess. A little troll woke the ice bear by poking his nose with sausage. The bear chased the trolls away. Later, Kyrie's father came home, and they all ate porridge. One year later, a little troll saw Kyrie and asked about the sleeping cat, and Kyrie said it had grown into a big cat with seven kittens, so the troll ran away.

Luc placed the weeds by the manger, and they changed into shining red stars.

At the Christmas program, Ruthie was the Heavenly Angel. At the end, Papa returned in an army uniform and hugged Ruthie, Mama, and the tiny angel.

video_title: The Three Little Grouches|Sesame Street|Books for Kids
summary_text: There were three little grouches on Sesame Street: Oscar the Grouch, Zoe the Grouch, and Elmo the Grouch. Oscar put yucky fish and one rotten banana on his trash can. Zoe put old socks and two rotten bananas on her trash can. Elmo put stinky cheese and three rotten bananas on his trash can. The smell was so bad that Super Grover noticed it and said it was a super stinky mess. One day, while the three grouches were playing, a big Snuffleupagus came by. He huffed and puffed and blew Oscar’s trash, Zoe’s trash, and Elmo’s trash all the way to the garbage truck. Oscar shouted after the truck. Zoe and Elmo liked their clean trash cans and thanked Snuffleupagus. Then Zoe and Elmo ran off to get bananas that were not rotten. Oscar stayed behind and grumbled. In the end, two little grouches went away, and one little grouch was left.

video_title: The Empty Pot!
summary_text: In a small village near the Moroccan desert lived a young potter named Amir. His father made famous pots, but Amir wanted to make the most beautiful pot of all. He worked hard, used gold dust, and put his shiny pot in the town square. People admired it for a while, but an old herb seller said beauty alone would not last. A desert fox and a bird found that the pot was empty, and soon the wind made it tip over and crack. Amir made another pot with jewels and silver, but it was empty too. A sandstorm blew it away. Then the old herb woman told Amir that a pot must have a purpose. Amir made a simple clay pot, filled it with water, and left it for travelers. People came to drink, and his father said the pot now shone from the inside out. Amir understood that kindness mattered more than glitter.

video_title: the Fly in the Vase!
summary_text: In the grand city of Lu Yang, a boy named Chen Yu worked in Master Lao’s pottery shop. Master Lao made beautiful porcelain vases for the emperor. One day, Master Lao was asked to make a vase for the emperor’s spring festival and told Chen Yu that patience and honesty were important. That night, Chen Yu secretly tried to finish the vase. He painted on it, but he made a mistake and damaged it. He hid the vase and ran away. In the morning, Master Lao found the damage, and Chen Yu said nothing. Later, Chen Yu tried to fix the ruined vase by himself, hoping to show his skill. The repaired vase looked nice, but he used the wrong gold paint. At the spring festival, the vase cracked and the dragon paint peeled. The emperor was upset, and Master Lao’s shop was sealed. Chen Yu went to the emperor and told the truth. The emperor spared him and made him work in the palace store room for a year. After that, Chen Yu returned to Master Lao, learned to be honest, and later became a famous craftsman.

video_title: The Boy Who Never Gave Up
summary_text: Eli sat on a park bench in Sakura Park and watched the skateboarders move fast under the cherry blossoms. He wanted to skate like them. For his birthday, his grandmother gave him a skateboard with a dark blue deck and bright orange wheels. At first, the board felt wobbly, and Eli fell many times. His knees got bruised and his elbows got bandages. He sat on the curb and said he might not be meant to do it. Then Ren, an older boy, stopped beside him. Ren said everyone falls and told Eli to bend his knees and not stand so stiff. Eli tried again and rolled for a few seconds before falling into the grass. After that, he practiced every day after school. He kept falling, but he got up faster each time. Later, Ren helped him learn the Ali trick. Eli tried many times and failed, but then he followed Ren's timing and jumped. The board and Eli went up together, and he landed it. Ren cheered, and Eli smiled and rolled away, ready to keep trying.

video_title: Leo and the Wise Old Mechanic
summary_text: In Ridgeville, a boy named Leo loved building things. He worked hard on a go-kart called the Comet for the annual Ridgeville Derby. Leo was sure his design was perfect, but the steering kept getting loose after every turn. He tried many times to fix it with bolts and new parts, but nothing worked. Leo’s father saw his frustration and told him to visit Mr. Pinto, an old man who knew a lot from experience. In Mr. Pinto’s small garage, Leo showed his blueprints and used big words, but Mr. Pinto looked at the kart, wiggled the wheel, and found the problem. He gave Leo a small rubber washer and told him to place it in the right spot. Leo did, and the steering became strong and steady. At the Derby, the Comet raced fast and won. Leo learned that talent helped build the kart, but experience helped it succeed.

video_title: The Boy Who Asked Why ?!?
summary_text: In a quiet fishing village by the sea, a boy named Keon asked many questions about everything. He asked why the sea was blue, why fish sparkled, and why thunder sounded angry. The villagers laughed kindly and told him he asked too many questions, but Keon did not stop wondering. One morning, the sea became rough and dark. The fishermen were worried and said the winds were strange. Some thought a sea monster might be in the water. Keon did not want to believe a story without knowing the truth. He took his grandfather’s old compass and a tiny boat and sailed into the unknown sea. The sky grew heavy and the waves rose high, but Keon kept going. After many hours, he saw something big under the water. It was not a monster. It was a blue whale. The whale rose beside his boat and told Keon that the moon pulls the water and the wind moves the tides.

On summer evenings they would chase fireflies or sleep in the woods under the stars. At the beach they would play all day, and on Halloween they would trick or treat and bring home candy. At the end, the child hopes the snow is magic and the snowman stays all year.

video_title: The Stranger by Chris Van Allsburg
summary_text: Farmer Bailey was driving home when he hit something in the road. He thought it was a deer, but it was a man lying there. The man woke up scared, tried to run, and fell down. Mr. Bailey helped him into the truck and took him home. Mrs. Bailey made him comfortable on the parlor sofa, and Katie saw that he wore strange leather clothes. The doctor said the man had lost his memory and had a bump on his head. He stayed with the Baileys, and they gave him clean clothes, dinner, and work in the fields. He learned quickly and never seemed tired. He watched the geese fly south and looked worried when he saw the green trees around the farm while trees to the north had already turned red and orange. Soon he became upset, left in his old clothes, and disappeared. After that, every autumn the trees around the Bailey farm stay green for a week, then turn bright overnight, and the farmhouse windows show the words, “See you next fall.”

Every autumn after that, the trees around the Bailey farm stay green longer, then change overnight, and frost on the windows says, “See you next fall.”

video_title: Brave Irene
summary_text: Mrs Bobbin was very tired and had a bad headache, but she finished sewing a beautiful gown for the duchess. Her daughter Irene wanted to help, so she packed the dress in a big box, dressed warmly, and carried it out into the snow. The wind was strong and kept pushing her, but Irene kept going because the gown had to reach the palace. The wind tore the box open, and the dress flew away. Irene searched for it, fell into the snow, and became lost as night came. At last she saw the light of the palace below. The box turned into a sled, and Irene slid down until she found the gown caught in a tree. She put it back in the box and brought it to the palace. The duchess and servants cheered, and Irene stayed there for dinner. The next morning, Mrs Bobbin found Irene returning in a sleigh, safe and smiling, with gifts and a note from the duchess.

video_title: The Widow's Broom by Chris Van Allsburg
summary_text: Mr. Spivy was angry and scared when he saw the broom acting in strange ways. He called it wicked and told others it was dangerous. But the broom kept working hard on the widow Mina Shaw’s farm. It swept the road and even played the piano with one note at a time. One day, two of the Spivy boys and their dog bothered the broom on the dirt road. The boys kicked stones into its path, called it names, and tapped it with sticks. The broom finally turned and knocked both boys down. When the dog chased and bit at it, the broom was still not harmed. That evening, Mr. Spivy and three other men came to the widow’s house with rope and a stake. Mina said they should take the broom away. The men tied it up, burned it, and turned it to ashes. After that, people found the dog safe in a tree, and life seemed normal again.

video_title: 📚Harold and the Purple Crayon by Crockett Johnson, children’s story read aloud
summary_text: One evening, Harold decided to go for a walk in the moonlight. There was no moon, so he drew one with his big purple crayon. He also drew a long straight path and a field, then a small forest with one tree. The tree was an apple tree, and Harold drew a scary dragon to guard the apples. The dragon frightened Harold, and he soon found himself over his head in an ocean. Harold made a trim little balloon, and the moon went with him as he sailed away. After landing on a beach, he made a picnic with nine kinds of pie. He shared the leftover pie with a hungry moose and a porcupine. Then he made a hill into a mountain, fell, and made another balloon and basket. He made a house, then a city of windows, and asked a policeman for help. At last he remembered his bedroom window was always around the moon. He made his bed and fell asleep.

video_title: 🚌The Magic School Bus, Inside the Human Body, children’s story, read aloud.  By Joanna Cole
summary_text: Miss Frizzle showed the class a film strip about the human body, and the children knew another strange adventure was coming. The next day, she made them do an experiment and then took them on a class trip to the Science Museum to see how food gives the body energy. They rode in the old school bus and stopped at a park for lunch. When it was time to leave, Arnold was still at the picnic table eating cheesy wheezys, so he stayed behind. Miss Frizzle pressed a strange button, and the bus began shrinking and spinning. The class landed inside a human body and traveled down the esophagus into the stomach, then into the small intestine. Miss Frizzle showed them how food moves into the blood through tiny villi. The children rode red blood cells through the blood, into the heart, up to the brain, and along the nerves and muscles. At the end, they were blown back to school through Arnold’s nose.

They learned they were inside a human body, first going down the esophagus and then into the stomach, where food was mashed and mixed with digestive juice.
The bus then moved into the small intestine, where food molecules entered the blood through tiny villi.
The class traveled through blood vessels, the heart, and the lungs, saw red and white blood cells, and visited the brain and spinal cord.
They finally returned to school when Arnold blew his nose, and Miss Frizzle had them draw a chart of the human body.

video_title: 🎃🍁Pumpkin Jack, written and Illustrated by Will Hubbell, children’s story read aloud with music
summary_text: Tim carved his first pumpkin and named the Jack-o-Lantern Jack. He liked Jack very much and kept him for a while, but Mom said the pumpkin would rot and needed to go outside. Tim carried Jack to the garden and left him there. As the days passed, Jack changed. He got wrinkled, then moldy, and then flat. Winter snow covered him, and Tim forgot about him. Later, when the snow melted, Tim found only a little pumpkin skin, a stem, and some seeds. He covered the remains with dirt and said goodbye. In spring, a green sprout grew where Jack had been. Tim watered it and watched it grow into a pumpkin vine. Yellow flowers came and went, and then a small green pumpkin appeared. By Halloween, the pumpkins were orange, and Tim made one into a new Jack-o-Lantern and welcomed Jack back.

video_title: 🎧💥Too Much! An Overwhelming Day for help supporting children with sensory needs, story read aloud
summary_text: An alarm clock beeps, and the child feels upset by the loud sound and bright sunlight. Washing is hard because the washcloth feels rough and the water is cold. At breakfast, the child does not want crunchy food and chooses soft bananas instead. Then the child gets dressed, but the shirt has a sharp, itchy tag and the coat feels too tight. At the playground, friends crowd close, someone hugs the child, and everything feels too loud, too bright, too itchy, and too tight. The child does not want to play because it all feels like too much. Later, the child asks for a gentle hug and feels brave. The child learns to say what is needed, like quiet time, a dark place, a soft shirt, and personal space. With deep breaths and a held hand, the child feels thankful and calm.

video_title: 🎄🎅🏿❄️Fletcher and the Snowflake Christmas, by Julia Rawlinson, children’s story read aloud withmusic
summary_text: On a bright Christmas Eve, Fletcher the rabbit saw that the rabbits had moved to a new burrow. He worried that Father Christmas would not find the new home. Fletcher began to collect sticks and make a trail of arrows through the wood. Squirrel saw him and helped. Soon birds came down from the trees, and then the mice joined in too. Together, they finished the trail to the rabbit’s new burrow. The rabbits’ home was warm and smelled like blackberry pie. The friends sat by the fire, ate pie, and sang Christmas songs. Then snow fell softly, and the arrows disappeared. Fletcher became worried again. He asked everyone to stay awake and help Father Christmas find the burrow. But one by one, the animals fell asleep. Father Christmas came anyway. The next morning, the rabbits were happy because Father Christmas had found them, and all their friends came to share the bright, warm burrow.

video_title: Storytime! ~ Disney's MOANA Read Aloud ~ Story Time ~  Bedtime Story Read Along Books
summary_text: Moana of Montenui loved the ocean. She liked Grandma Tala’s stories, especially the one about Maui, who stole the heart of Teiti and upset nature. Moana’s father, Chief Tui, said the ocean was dangerous, so people could not sail past the reef. But Moana felt close to the ocean. The ocean gave her a special gift, and Grandma Tala picked it up and said it was the heart of Teiti. When Moana was 16, Grandma Tala showed her hidden canoes and told her it was time to learn who she was meant to be. Grandma Tala asked Moana to find Maui and restore the heart. Moana set sail with the heart in her necklace. A storm came, and she washed up on an island where she met Maui. Maui took her boat, but the ocean made sure Moana went with him. Maui said he would help if Moana helped him find his magic fish hook. They faced the Kakamura and went into Lowa Tha. Moana tricked Tola, the crab monster, and got the fish hook back. Maui taught Moana to wayfind by using the sun, stars, moon, and ocean current. Grandma Tala’s spirit came back and told Moana to know who she was meant to be. At Teiti, Moana gave the heart to Teay, who became Teiti again. The world was balanced, and Moana returned home as a daughter, a leader, and a wayfinder.

video_title: St Patrick's Day ~ Pete the Cat  THE GREAT LEPRECHAUN CHASE  Read Aloud ~ StoryTime
summary_text: Tomorrow is Saint Patrick’s Day, and Pete’s teacher, Mr. G, teaches the class about leprechauns. He says the only time you can catch one is on St. Patrick’s Day, and a leprechaun brings good luck. Pete gets an idea. He opens a leprechaun catching business called Pete’s Lucky Leprechaun Catchers. On St. Patrick’s Day, Pete sets up his stand. Squirrel comes first and wants a leprechaun for a test. Pete follows a rainbow and finds Clover by a pot of gold, but Clover is too fast and escapes in green smoke. Gus comes next and wants good luck for a band recital. Pete plays music, and Clover dances closer, but then Clover spins Pete around and ties him up with a rope. Later, Kelly wants a leprechaun for a tennis match. Pete sets a trap, but Clover finds candy, and the trap is empty. Pete follows the candy to Clover’s hideout and catches him. Clover says luck comes from friends helping each other. Pete lets him go and helps Squirrel study, Gus rehearse, and Kelly practice. All of them do well, and Pete learns that making luck by helping is better than catching it.

Farmer Dale drove the crowded truck into town, and the rooster crowed a happy cheer.

Soon he reached a drawbridge, but it was up because the dump truck had made it rise. Beach balls were in the water below, and Milly saw a pattern: small, small, big. When one big ball was missing, Milly made a new big ball so UmiCar could bounce across. UmiCar lowered the bridge for the other racers. Later, the dump truck spilled soapy water on the road, and UmiCar skidded. Geo fixed his broken steering wheel with shapes. Near the end, the team counted to ten, UmiCar went faster, passed the dump truck, and won the race. He shared his balloons, and the dump truck said sorry.

video_title: THOSE DARN SQUIRRELS FLY SOUTH  Read Aloud ~ Bedtime Story Read Along Books  ~ Kids Books Read Aloud
summary_text: Old man Bookwire lived by a beautiful forest, but he was a grump. He scolded fireflies, clouds, and lilacs. In summer, he painted the colorful birds in his yard, and sometimes he painted squirrels by accident. Then fall came, and the birds flew south for the winter. Bookwire thought he would be alone, but the squirrels had built flying machines and followed the birds. They flew in gyrocopters, gliders, and a zeppelin. The birds waved goodbye, and the squirrels flew after them. They traveled through night, rain, and turbulence until they reached a warm beach in Santa Vaca. There they had a fiesta, swam, ate mangoes, and danced. Later, Bookwire got a phone call from Santa Vaca. He missed the birds and squirrels, so he drove his old car to the beach. The squirrels hugged him, and he laughed for the first time in a long time. He painted the birds there, but the hot sun made him too tired. The squirrels gave him water, and everyone drove home together.

In the end, the frog hears that it is good to be a frog and that he should be happy he is not a fly.

Then Turkey became a ballerina and went to Farmer Jones’s house, but Jones’s daughter sent him away. After that, he dressed as a pirate and tried Farmer Fred’s house, but he was turned away again. Next, he wore a superhero costume and went to Farmer Anne’s house, but she said no treats for turkeys. At last, Mabel Mayberry saw Turkey in a new costume and thought he looked marvelous. She gave him all the rest of her treats. Turkey was happy, and he said it was the best Halloween ever.

video_title: Thanksgiving Stories ~ FRANKLIN'S THANKSGIVING Read Aloud ~  Bedtime Story Read Along Books
summary_text: Franklin loved Thanksgiving. He liked pumpkin fly pie, cranberry jelly, and making holiday crafts. Most of all, he liked when Grandma and Grandpa came for dinner. But one day a postcard came. Grandma and Grandpa could not come this year. Franklin felt sad and grumbled. His family still worked hard to bring in the harvest. Franklin helped pick apples, make applesauce, dig vegetables, and gather berries and nuts. At school, Franklin learned about early settlers and invited Mr. Al and his mother to dinner. Then Franklin’s mother invited the Bear family, and Franklin’s father invited Mr. Mole. Franklin also invited the Moose family. On Thanksgiving morning, everyone came, but too many guests arrived for the table and there was no room inside. Franklin saw what to do. The family and all the guests carried food, tables, and chairs outside and ate in the field. Everyone had a happy Thanksgiving, and Grandma and Grandpa later called to hear all about the new tradition.

video_title: THE NIGHT BEFORE THANKSGIVING Read Aloud ~ Thanksgiving Stories ~  Bedtime Story Read Along Books
summary_text: The night before Thanksgiving, the family got ready for a big meal. Mom baked three pies: pecan, pumpkin, and apple surprise. The children went to bed thinking about turkey legs. The next morning, they watched the parade on TV. Relatives came by taxi, airplane, train, and car. The children helped set up the tables with silverware, chairs, and the kids’ table. The turkey went in the oven. More cousins arrived, and the children greeted them by name. They played in the room, made pilgrim hats and shoe buckles, and performed a skit. Uncle Norm called to say he was stuck in a storm. Later, Mom cooked yams, cranberry jelly, and honey baked hams. The children played outside and got hungry. When the timer rang, the turkey was done. Dad dropped it, but the children caught it on a platter. Grandpa told them to carve it. Uncle Norm arrived, and everyone sat down to eat. They were thankful to be together, and the next day they ate leftover food.

summary_text: Kitty is hungry, so someone gives her fish, but Kitty does not want fish. Then she is offered beef, moose, walrus, and even a turnip, but Kitty still says no. Kitty wants candy. She has never eaten candy before, but she thinks it looks sweet and tasty, and she wants all of it. The people tell Kitty that candy is not good for cats and say no. Kitty gets angry and decides to take the candy anyway. She eats it. The candy is sweet and tasty, but it is also very sticky. Kitty’s mouth gets stuck and she cannot open it. Then the people brush her teeth and remind her that candy is not good for cats. After that, Kitty is still hungry. They ask if she wants fish, and this time Kitty says yes. Kitty likes fish a lot and does not like candy.

summary_text: A child remembers a time in the fall when the family had a box of rags. The child did not have a coat, so Mama sewed the small pieces of cloth together. She worked carefully and made a coat of many colors. While she sewed, she told a Bible story about Joseph and his coat of many colors. She also said she hoped the coat would bring good luck and happiness. When the coat was finished, Mama kissed it, and the child felt proud and happy to wear it. Even though the family had no money, the child felt rich in the special coat made with Mama’s love. Then the child hurried off to school with patched britches and holes in the shoes. The other children laughed and made fun of the coat, but the child told them about Mama’s love in every stitch and tried to explain that the coat was worth more than their clothes.

At school, the class waited all day for the Valentine party. When Mr. Owl said it was time, Franklin looked in his bag and found only his hat, mittens, homework, and a ball. His Valentines were gone. Franklin’s mother looked for them and found them outside in slushy snow, ruined. Franklin felt very sad and ran to the cloak room. Mr. Al told him his friends were waiting and asked if he would stop giving a card to Bear just because Bear had lost his cards. Franklin said no. Then he saw his friends give him many Valentines, and Bear told him he did not need a card to know Franklin was his friend. That night Franklin said he had good friends and wanted to make extra special Valentines next year.

video_title: HOW TO CATCH A TURKEY 🦃 | Fun Thanksgiving Storytime with Grandma!
summary_text: On Thanksgiving day, a turkey tells his story. One year ago, he was at a school where a play was being prepared. Some children said there would even be a turkey on stage for Thanksgiving Day. The turkey got scared and ran away from his pin. He rushed into the science room, knocked over flasks and beakers, and the children chased him with loud calls, catapults, and mashed potatoes. He escaped through a maze of books and ran past chairs, bags, and desks. Then he went outside, but the playground was still full of tricks, so he ran back inside. The principal chased him, and he hid in the coach’s room, then ran into a curtain. The curtain led to the show. There, he took a deep breath and stepped out. A child pointed at him, people smiled, and the crowd cheered. The turkey danced, and that was the start of his mascot career.

video_title: Easter Stories for Kids ~ OLLIE'S EASTER EGGS Read Aloud ~ Bedtime Story Read Along Books
summary_text: Goth and Gertie gather eggs. Boo Boo and Pey gather eggs too. Olly hops nearby and watches. Then Gossy dyes her egg bright red, Gertie dyes her egg bright blue, Boo Boo dyes her egg bright purple, and Pey dyes his egg bright yellow. Ali stares at the bright eggs and shouts, “I want eggs!” Gossy hides her egg in the green grass, Gertie hides her egg in the yellow straw, Boo Boo hides her egg in the red tulips, and Pey hides his egg under the green turtle. Olly rolls each egg out of sight and then hides all the eggs under his blanket. After that, Gossy and Gertie hunt for the Easter eggs in the tulips and under the turtle. Boo Boo and Pey hunt for the eggs in the grass and in the straw. They all scurry and search past Olly and Ali. At the end, Ali says, “For small goslings, stop and stare!” and Olly shouts, “Easter eggs!”

video_title: SNEEZE BIG BEAR SNEEZE Read Aloud ~ Story Time ~  Bedtime Stories  ~ Kids Read Aloud Books
summary_text: Big Bear walked through the autumn woods while the wind blew all around him. First, leaves flew off the trees when Bear sneezed. Bear said the wind did not do it, and he tried to nail the leaves back with a hammer and tacks. Then he came to an apple tree. When he sneezed again, the branches shook and the apples fell to the ground. Bear put the apples back on the branch. After that, Bear went to the lake and saw twenty geese. When he sneezed, the geese flew away with loud honks and flapping wings. The wind kept saying it did these things because it was fall. At last, the wind told Bear that it whips leaves off trees, drops apples, scares geese south, and makes Bear sneeze. Bear listened and went to his den. The door slammed shut, and Bear hid in bed and turned out the light.

video_title: HANUKKAH COOKIES WITH SPRINKLES Read Aloud ~ Hanukkah Stories for Kids ~ Jewish Holiday Books
summary_text: Every morning Sarah watches from the window as her mom goes to work and waves from the bus stop. She also sees Saul open his store and put bad fruits and vegetables in a box by the side of the store. One day Sarah sees an old man take an apple from the box and eat around the bad spots. Grandma says he may be poor and hungry. Sarah thinks about him at school and saves her snack cookie for him. She asks Mom to leave it near Saul’s store. Later the man finds the cookie and eats it. Sarah tells her friends, and they wrap more cookies. Her teacher says this is called sadaka, giving to someone who has less. Sarah and Mom also leave juice and a sandwich for the man. Soon Sarah sees his face and thinks she knows him. At a Shabbat and Hanukkah party, she learns his name is Morris Berger. After that, food is left for him every day.

video_title: Storytime! ~ ON THE NIGHT YOU WERE BORN  Read Aloud ~ Story Time ~  Bedtime Story Read Along Books
summary_text: On the night you were born, the Moon smiled and the Stars came to look. The night wind and the rain whispered that life would never be the same because there had never been anyone like you. They whispered your wonderful name, and the sound of your name traveled across the Farmland, over the ocean, and through the trees. Everyone heard about the one and only ever you. The story says no one had ever seen such eyes, such a nose, or such wiggly toes. When the polar bears heard this, they danced until dawn. The geese flew home, the moon stayed up until morning, and the ladybugs stayed too. Later, when you wonder how much you are loved, you can listen for the geese honking, the bears dancing, the wind whispering your name, or a bird sitting at your window. They are all hoping to see you smile. The story ends by saying the world has never known anyone like you, and never will again.

video_title: TOO MUCH GLUE! Read Aloud ~ Read A Long Books ~ Storytime
summary_text: Maddie loves glue at home, but her art teacher says, “Too much glue never dries.” In art class, Maddie uses the fullest bottles of glue and makes a big glue mess with sequins and googly eyes. Then she jumps onto the table and rolls around until she is stuck. She tries to get off, but she cannot move. Her teacher, Noah, Izzy, Owen, Luke, Grace, the school nurse, and the principal all try to help in different ways. They use lassos, a tow truck, blotting, and a big paper fan, but the glue only gets messier and thicker. At last, Maddie’s teacher’s drying idea works, and the glue dries. Maddie is still stuck until her dad comes to school. He peels her off the table and calls her a masterpiece. At home, he opens the dry glue shape, fixes it, and hangs it on the fridge. The principal sends a note asking Maddie to use tape instead of glue.

video_title: HARRY THE DIRTY DOG ~ Read Along Story Time ~  Bedtime Story Read Aloud Books
summary_text: Harry was a white dog with black spots, and he liked almost everything except baths. One day he heard water running in the tub, so he buried the scrubbing brush in the backyard and ran away from home. He played in the street where they were fixing it, then at the railroad, and then with other dogs. Each time he got dirtier and dirtier. He even slid down a coal shoot and became so dirty that he looked like a black dog with white spots. Soon Harry felt tired and hungry, and he wondered if his family thought he had really run away. So he hurried back home. At the house, his family did not know him at first. Harry tried his old tricks, but they still said he was not Harry. Then he dug up the scrubbing brush and showed it to them. The family gave him a bath, and when they scrubbed him, they finally knew it was Harry. Afterward, he was white again with black spots, and he went to sleep happily.

He played where the street was being fixed, at the railroad, and with other dogs, and each time he got dirtier. Then he slid down a coal shoot and became so dirty that he looked like a black dog with white spots. After a while, Harry felt tired and hungry and wondered if his family thought he had really gone away, so he ran back home. He crawled through the fence and waited by the back door. The family saw a strange dirty dog and did not know it was Harry, even when he did his old tricks. Finally, Harry dug up the scrubbing brush and showed it in the bathtub. The children bathed him, everyone recognized him, and he became white with black spots again.

summary_text: One winter morning at 6:53, Mr. McGee and his little dog Dee woke up to fresh snow and a beautiful sky. They decided to try skiing before driving to Mount Snow. Mr. McGee said they would practice on a small hill near the house with a view of the bay. Soon they reached a place where nothing was in their way. Mr. McGee put on his skis, and Dee rode in the pack on his back. He slid slowly downhill, but a curious moose was nearby. The moose saw them and froze. Mr. McGee could not steer, so he asked the moose to step aside and then yelled, “Duck!” Their skis snagged on a spruce log, and Mr. McGee and Dee flew into a ravine and got stuck across it. The moose returned, stepped on the skis, and made them spring up. Mr. McGee and Dee landed safely. Mr. McGee said they still needed a lesson and should let someone else use the skis for a while.

Later she found her cards on the bus, gave her special cards to Jeremy, and came home to hugs and gifts from her family.

video_title: Stone Soup - Cooking Experiment!  #kidslearningvideos
summary_text: A young man walked all day and all night until he was tired and hungry. He came to a big house and knocked on the door. A little old lady opened it, but she said she had no food to give him. The young man asked for something to do and said he could make soup from a stone. The old lady was surprised, but she let him use a pot. She filled it with water and put it on the fire. The young man dropped a round gray stone into the pot and asked for more things to make the soup better. One by one, the old lady added onions, carrots, beef bones, pepper, salt, butter, and barley. The soup bubbled and grew thicker and better. At last they ate it together. Before he left, the young man took the stone from the pot, put it in his pocket, and said he would cook it more tomorrow.

video_title: When a Wreckless Bear Pushes a Witch Too Far:  #kidsbooksreadaloud
summary_text: Forever Green Forest was peaceful until Bruce, a big shaggy bear, came out of a canyon and stayed there. When he felt playful, he liked to tumble rocks down the hills. The rocks smashed logs and bushes and scared the rabbits and quail away. One day Bruce pushed a huge boulder off a bluff. It rolled fast and crashed near Roxy, a witch, and her cat, Clinker. Roxy was angry and ran to her cabin. There she baked a blueberry and honey pie and added a magic shrinking spell. She set the pie on a stump and waited. Bruce followed the smell, ate the pie, and laughed. Soon he became sleepy and fell asleep against a tree. While he slept, he shrank smaller and smaller until he was tiny. When he woke, rabbits and quail chased him, and he ran into the creek. Later, Roxy and Clinker found him, took him home, and kept him as a small pet bear.

summary_text: Forever Green Forest was peaceful until Bruce, a huge shaggy bear, came from a canyon and began frightening the smaller animals. When he was in a playful mood, he liked to tumble rocks down hills, crushing logs and bushes and sending rabbits and quail racing away. One day he pushed a giant boulder off a bluff, and it rolled into a berry patch where Roxy, a crafty little witch, was picking blueberries with her cat Clinker. Angry that the boulder almost hit her, Roxy followed Bruce and decided to teach him a lesson. She baked a blueberry-and-honey pie with magic ingredients and left it on a stump. Bruce ate it, and soon he became sleepy and shrank while he slept, all the way down to the size of a chipmunk. The forest animals chased him, and he fled into the creek. After he realized Roxy had tricked him, she found him again, had Clinker bring him to her cabin, and kept him as a tiny pet bear. Bruce forgot his old ways, and the forest became quiet again.

Later a storm came, the mast was hit by lightning, and Jeremy helped find a place to bury the treasure. After the storm, the pirates gave him a flag and sailed away, and Jeremy went to soccer practice.

After that, the Wolf went to the third little pig’s brick house and asked for sugar. The pig was rude, and the Wolf got angry. Police came, and the Wolf was taken to jail.

video_title: A Spoonful of Sugar: How a Vaccine Inspired a Disney Classic | Story of the Week
summary_text: The story is about a father who loved words and listened carefully before he spoke. He brought word builders on his honeymoon because he enjoyed how words sounded. He and his brother, Uncle Dick, made songs for Mary Poppins, including one called The Eyes of Love. But Walt Disney asked them to write a song that fit Mary Poppins better, and they felt sad because nothing was working. One day, the child came home from school after getting the oral polio vaccine. The child explained that the medicine was put on a sugar cube and eaten, not given as a shot. The father heard this, shook his head, and called Dick right away. The next day, they wrote the song line, “A spoonful of sugar helps the medicine go down.” The story ends by showing that the father often found ideas in family life and turned ordinary things into something special.

video_title: The Shared Sisterhood Between Veterans
summary_text: Two older people talk about their families, their pasts, and how they met. One person says his son disowned him and used a hurtful word, and he worries he may never get to talk to his grandchild. The other person says her daughter also disowned her. They talk about growing up feeling different from other children. One liked playing a girl’s part in pretend games, but had to act like someone else to survive. He spent 15 years in the Army as a paratrooper in the 82nd Airborne Division and says soldiers had to seem very tough. After leaving the military, he finally began wearing women’s clothes because he had been afraid to before. Later, they met at a transgender support group at the VA. They joked with each other, and people started saying they were really sisters. They often sit together at Denny’s for coffee for many hours. At the end, they say that losing their children hurts, but they are always there for each other and are glad to be sisters.

They worked day and night until almost no forest was left. Greta saw that the animals were sad and scared, so she decided to help them. The next day she stood in the middle of the forest with a sign that said, “Stop.” For three days the giants walked past her. The giants felt ashamed, said sorry, and promised to do better. They stopped cutting trees and began gardening, cooking, repairing, tidying, and sharing. Soon the forest became beautiful again.

video_title: Balloons over Broadway: The True Story of the Puppeteer of Macy's Parade - Thanksgiving Read Along
summary_text: Tony Sar loved to make things move. When he was a little boy, his father asked him to feed the chickens every morning. Tony tied ropes and pulleys from the chicken coop to his bedroom window so he could open the coop door without leaving bed. In the morning, he pulled the rope, the chickens ate, and his father was so impressed that Tony never had to do the chore again. When Tony grew up, he moved to London and began making marionettes out of wood, cloth, and strings. His puppets moved so well that people thought they were real. Later, in New York City, Macy’s asked him to create holiday window puppets and then help with a parade. Tony made new puppets and floats, and the first Macy’s parade was a big success. When the animals scared children, Tony made larger balloons from rubberized silk and filled them with helium. On Thanksgiving Day, the giant puppets rose into the sky and marched through New York City, starting the famous Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.

summary_text: Henry Brown was a slave, and he did not know his birthday. He worked with his brothers and sisters in the big house. One day, his master was very sick and called Henry and his mother upstairs. Henry hoped he might be set free, but the master gave Henry to his son instead. Henry then worked in a factory and was lonely. There he met Nancy, and later they were married. They had children, but Nancy feared their master might sell them. Soon Henry learned that Nancy and the children had been sold at the slave market. He was very sad and could not work or sing. After many weeks, Henry decided to escape. With help from James and Dr. Smith, he put himself in a box and sent it to Philadelphia. The trip was rough, but the box finally arrived. The box was opened, and Henry stood up free in Philadelphia on March 30, 1849. From then on, people called him Henry Box Brown.

The pasta does yoga, the cookies do magic, the marshmallows stack tall, the English muffins act, the popcorn jumps high, and the cheese plays music. When the show begins, the egg plans to sit in the audience. Soon, though, some acts have problems. A muffin forgets his lines, so the egg helps. No one volunteers for a magic act, so he steps in. He also helps as a spotter, uses his lucky bottle cap drum when the drum set breaks, and brings a flashlight and sewing kit when the lights and costumes go wrong. By the end, everyone thanks him and says he made the show better. The egg learns that helping others is a talent too.

video_title: Goodbye Autumn, Hello Winter - A Calming Read Aloud with Moving Pictures
summary_text: In late autumn, the canard pack says hello as the wispy winds blow the leaves from the oak tree. The leaves float up in the sky. Robins and Cardinals get ready to fly far, far south. Horse, sheep, and deer say hello too. They know it will soon be cold, so they stay inside their stables. They eat the last leaves and berries, and their fur gets thicker for winter. Chrysanthemums and daisies keep standing while the sunlight still warms them. Then the setting sun comes, and the evening grows longer. Shadows stretch across the streets. Clouds cover the sky like a soft blanket. Northstar shines on the darkest nights. Evergreens shake in the wind, and Silent Night comes. Frost and icicles decorate the windows and eaves, and snowflakes fall like a white curtain. At the end, autumn is gone, and winter arrives.

video_title: Stories from the Black Lagoon Series - 30min Read Aloud | 9 Books: Teacher,  Librarian, and more!
summary_text: The class goes to the school library, and the children are very scared because they have heard many strange things about it. They say the library is behind the boiler room and is called the Media Center of the Earth. Miss Beamster is the librarian, and the children call her the laminator because they think she laminates anyone who talks. Her assistant is Eigor. On the way, the class passes signs that warn, “No talking beyond this point” and “No breathing beyond this point.” They also go through a decontamination room, put on hairetss and rubber gloves, and use a gum detector. Inside the library, the books cannot be checked out because Miss Beamster bolts them together to keep them in alphabetical order. The children also hear about story time, the Dewey decimal system, and many silly rules. At the end, the class enters, sits in small chairs, and Miss Beamster gives the narrator a book of knockknock jokes, which makes the library seem fun.

Bird and Squirrel catch snowflakes, and Bird explains that each snowflake is a different shape. Squirrel also notices his breath in the cold air, and Bird says it is not smoke. Then Squirrel skates on a frozen puddle, slips, and crashes. After that, he sees a snow squirrel and thinks it is rude for not answering. He also worries that eight hazelnuts are missing. Bird tells him the snow squirrel is only made of snow. The next day, Squirrel keeps thinking about it. Later, when the snow disappears, Bird shows him that the snow squirrel vanished in the night, but the hazelnuts are still there.

Oscar was a small, funny-shaped dog. The other dogs teased him and called him names, and even Oscar’s mother did this when the dogs went to obedience school. Oscar felt upset, but on Halloween he thought about costumes and trick-or-treating instead. When he got home, his mother had made him a big hot dog bun costume with mustard. Oscar did not want to hurt her feelings, so he wore it.

That night, the dogs met on the Block in scary costumes. When Oscar arrived, they laughed at his costume and ran off to trick-or-treat. Oscar’s costume slowed him down, and he got no treats. Later, the dogs saw a monster near a graveyard and jumped into a pond. Oscar looked carefully and saw that the “monster” was really two hory cats. The cats ran away, and Oscar swam to the dogs. His costume helped as a life raft, and he carried them back to shore. The dogs shared their treats with Oscar and called him hero sandwich.

A jet plane lands, and belt loader takes off the luggage. Tractor tows the bags. Bulldozer clears a path. Cement mixer pours concrete for new runways. Hydrant dispenser fills fuel tanks, and tug pulls a plane for a check. More airplanes and trucks keep working while the airport grows. Cargo plane flies, and rubber removal machine cleans the runway. Crane truck, lift truck, and skid steer also help. Then snow starts to fall, and the runway gets covered. Snow plows, sweepers, blowers, and tankers clear the snow and ice. Icing truck sprays the planes so they can fly. When the big job is done, the airport crew waves goodbye, and the trucks roll off to sleep.

When they reach the place, they use a map to explore and walk toward the river. Archie says he is hot and his feet hurt, so Dad gives him binoculars to help him look around. Archie sees a bright blue feather and a bluebird building a nest in a tree. They also see a bunny, but when they get too close, it gets scared away. Dad says they can count the tree rings to learn its age. Along the trail, they watch ants carrying food and leaves, and Archie sees a squirrel with a snack in its cheek. Mom points to a sign that says to turn right, and soon they reach the river. There they see lily pads, a green frog, and flat rocks that Archie skips across the water. At the end, they head home as the sun sets and get ready for bed.

summary_text: Peanut likes to do things in a special way. Peanut does cartwheels on the basketball court, eats banana pancakes on their birthday, and cuts their own hair while hula hooping. Sometimes people think Peanut is weird, but friends often join in the fun. Peanut also wants to be a rhythmic gymnast. Peanut asks Dad to help with the outfit, Mom to help with the choreography, and Sammy to pick up the music and make it funky. Peanut dances, spins, tumbles, dives, swings the hoop, tosses the ball, juggles the batons, and twirls the ribbon. Peanut forgets to tie their shoes, but turns the stumble into a triple axel tumble and sticks the landing. The judges agree that the routine is perfect, and Peanut keeps doing things their own way.

video_title: Caps For Sale
summary_text: There was once a peddler who sold caps. He wore many caps on his head: his own checked cap, then gray caps, brown caps, blue caps, and red caps on top. He walked through the streets calling, “Caps, caps for sale. 50 cents a cap.” One morning nobody bought any caps, so the peddler became hungry. He left town and walked into the country. He came to a big tree and sat down to rest. He leaned back carefully and then fell asleep. When he woke up, he felt his head and found only his checked cap. He looked everywhere, but the other caps were gone. Then he looked up and saw monkeys in the tree wearing his caps. The peddler asked for his caps back, but the monkeys copied him and said, “tus, tus, tous,” and other sounds. Finally, he threw down his own cap. Then the monkeys threw down all the caps. He put them back on his head and walked back to town, calling, “Caps, caps for sale. 50 cents a cap.”

The next morning, more leaves are gone, and Squirrel worries again. Bird tells him to go back to his nest and relax. The next day, Squirrel looks for the leaf thief. Bird shows him that the leaf thief is really the wind. The wind shakes the trees and blows the leaves away in autumn. Bird explains that the leaves will grow back in spring. Squirrel understands and goes home.

video_title: I Just Forgot
summary_text: Sometimes the child remembers things and sometimes the child forgets. In the morning, the child brushed teeth but forgot to make the bed. After breakfast, the child put dishes in the sink but forgot the milk. The child almost forgot to feed the puppy, but the puppy reminded them. The child watered the plants and fed the goldfish. Then the child got ready for school and reached the bus on time, but forgot the lunchbox. Mom brought it to school. After school, the child played in the rain and remembered the rain slicker but forgot the rubber boots. At snack time, the child had cookies and milk and forgot to count the cookies. Later, Dad came home, and the puppy got the paper first. At bedtime, the child washed up, picked up some things, and then noticed the toys were still not put away. One thing was never forgotten: Mom always read a bedtime story, and the child always kissed her good night.

video_title: Tops & Bottoms
summary_text: Once there was a lazy Bear who had lots of money and land, but he only wanted to sleep. Nearby lived Hair and Mrs. Hair, who had lost their land after a bad bet with a tortoise. Their children were hungry, so Hair made a plan. He went to Bear and said they could be partners and share a field. Bear would sleep while Hair and his family did all the work. Bear agreed and chose the top half of the first crops. Hair and his family planted, watered, and weeded. At harvest time, Hair gave Bear the tops and kept the bottoms. Then Bear wanted the bottoms next time, so they planted again. This time Hair gave Bear the bottoms and kept the tops. For the third crop, Bear asked for both tops and bottoms, but Hair gave him the tops and bottoms and kept the middle. After that, Bear woke up and said he would farm for himself. Hair later bought back his land and opened a vegetable stand.

It also saw a car’s headlights and then fireworks sparkling in the night. When it became quiet again, the firefly flew on, flashing and searching. At last, it saw a group of fireflies flashing their lights. Then the lonely firefly was not lonely anymore.

video_title: What Do You Do With a Chance? By Kobi Yamada and Mae Besom (Read-Aloud by Story J)
summary_text: One day, a chance came to the storyteller. It flittered around, brushed against them, and circled as if it wanted to be caught. The storyteller reached out, but then pulled back, and the chance flew away. After that, the storyteller thought about the missed chance and wished they had taken it. Later, another chance came. The storyteller tried to grab it, missed, and fell down. Feeling embarrassed, the storyteller decided to ignore every chance that came after that. Soon, chances seemed to disappear. The storyteller began to worry that no more chances would come. Then they thought that maybe they only needed to be brave at the right time. They promised to be ready if another chance appeared. One day, they saw something shiny in the distance, ran toward it, and let go of their fear. This time, they caught the huge chance and held on tight. It felt wonderful to soar and fly. Now the storyteller knows that holding back means missing out, so when a chance comes, it should be taken.

video_title: "Pocket Full of Colors: The Magical World of Mary Blair, Disney Artist Extraordinaire" Read Aloud
summary_text: Mary was a little girl who loved collecting colors instead of marbles or dolls. When her family moved out west, she said goodbye to her yellow house and kept her friend lemon with her. On the trip through the desert and into California, she noticed many new colors, like rust, Sienna, Azure, golden fruit, and steel gray buildings. She saved these shades in her sketchbook for later. Mary went to art school and met Lee, who showed her rosy pink and blushing red. Later, Mary worked at Walt Disney Studios, where the men in charge wanted only black and white. They changed or rejected many of her colorful ideas. Walt Disney liked her work and took her to South America, where Mary found even more colors. After she returned, she made new art for Disney films, but most of it was still turned down. Then Mary left and worked on other art jobs. Later, Walt asked her to help create a colorful ride about cultures from around the world. Mary agreed and became the leader of the project. The ride, It’s a Small World, was a great success.

video_title: "Corduroy" Read Aloud

Then one morning, a little girl named Lisa saw him and wanted him, but her mother said no because he was missing a button on one shoulder strap. That night, after the store closed, Corduroy climbed down from his shelf to look for the button. He rode an escalator, went to the furniture floor, and found a button on a mattress. She had saved money in her piggy bank and bought Corduroy. She carried him home, and in her room she sewed on a new button. Lisa said she wanted a friend, and Corduroy said he did too.

Roy and Silo watched other penguin families and saw that the mothers laid eggs and the parents took turns keeping them warm until they hatched. Since Roy and Silo had no egg, their nest felt empty. Roy first sat on a rock, but nothing happened. Then Mr. Gramzy found an egg that needed care and gave it to them. Roy and Silo kept it warm, turned it every day, and waited. At last the egg cracked and a baby penguin hatched. Mr. Gramzy named her Tango because it takes two to make a tango. Roy and Silo fed her, taught her, and later took her swimming. Tango was the first penguin in the zoo to have two daddies.

Another pair zipped to the stables and fell into the hay. The horse sent more undies up like a roller coaster ride. Some undies hit the roof, and the king of crowing flew up shouting as he went. More undies flew by the coop and loop-de-looped in the air. One pair landed in the meadow, and some covered the farmer’s jeep. A pair even went by a billy goat, who caught it in his jaw. At last the farmer came out and asked for his underwear back.

summary_text: One winter morning, Peter woke up and saw that snow had fallen all night. After breakfast, he put on his snow suit and ran outside. The snow was very deep, and his feet made crunch, crunch, crunch sounds as he walked. He tried walking in different ways and found a stick in the snow. Snow fell from a tree onto his head. Peter wanted to join the big boys in their snowball fight, but he knew he was not old enough yet. So he made a smiling snowman, made snow angels, and pretended to be a mountain climber. He climbed a big hill of snow and slid down. He packed a snowball and put it in his pocket for tomorrow. Then he went home, told his mother about his fun day, and went to bed. In the night, he found his pocket empty and felt sad. He dreamed the snow was gone, but when he woke up, the snow was still there. After breakfast, he went outside again with his friend from across the hall.

video_title: "Amazing Grace" by Mary Hoffman Read Aloud
summary_text:
Grace loved stories very much. She liked hearing them, reading them, and making them up in her head. She also liked acting them out, and she always gave herself the most exciting part. She played heroes, sailors, explorers, and fairy tale characters. Sometimes she got Ma and Nana to join her, and then she became Dr. Grace and led the action.

One day, Grace’s teacher said the class would do Peter Pan. Grace wanted to be Peter, but Raj said Peter was a boy’s name, and Natalie said Peter was not black. The teacher said there would be auditions. Grace felt sad at home, but Ma and Nana told her she could be anything she wanted. On Saturday, Nana took Grace to town to see Rosalie Wilkins in Romeo and Juliet. Grace watched the ballet and then played Juliet in her room. At auditions on Monday, Grace acted like Peter Pan very well. The class chose her for the part, and the play was a big success.

video_title: Seven Spools of Thread: A Kwanzaa Story | READ ALOUD | Storytime
summary_text: In a small village in Ghana, an old man lived with his seven sons after their mother died. The boys were strong and handsome, but they argued all day. They fought about the crops, the weather, and even dinner, so family meals often lasted until morning. One day the old man died, and the village chief told the brothers that their father had left them an inheritance. The brothers began fighting at once over who should get everything. The chief stopped them and gave them a task: by moonrise, they had to turn silk thread into gold or lose their home. At first they could not do it, but then they talked calmly and decided to work together. They made beautiful multicolored cloth from the thread and sold it to the king's treasurer for a bag of gold. The chief then gave them their inheritance, and the brothers taught the village how to make the cloth too.

Mama has braided her hair and places a sparkly tiara on MJ’s head, telling her she will be the queen of kindergarten.
Mama explains that queens brighten every room, are caring and kind, and are helpful to others.
Daddy drives MJ to school in his pickup truck, which he calls the royal chariot.
At school, Miss Loving Good tells the class to find their name cards.
MJ finds hers, decorates it, and learns that each student will have a weekly job.
She wants to be window monitor.
When she sees Raina looking sad, MJ remembers Mama’s words and holds Raina’s hands until Raina smiles.
MJ also helps Leo, shares lunch, joins recess games, makes art, sings in music, and plays soccer in gym.
At the end of the day, she gives Samson the picture she made, and Mama lets her keep the tiara because she followed the queen rules.

video_title: SQUARE by Mac Barnett | READ ALOUD
summary_text: Square lives by a hill with a secret cave. Every day he goes down into the cave, takes a block from below the ground, pushes it up, and brings it to the pile on top. One day Circle floats by and tells Square he is a genius and a sculptor. Square does not really understand, but Circle says his block looks like him and tells him to make one of her. Circle leaves, and Square worries about what to do. He tries to shape the block so it looks like Circle, but it does not work. He keeps working and working until he scrapes the whole block away, and only rubble is left. Square feels sad and falls asleep. The next morning Circle comes back early. Square says he is finished. Circle looks down and says the work is beautiful and perfect. She tells Square he is a genius, even though he still thinks he only pushes blocks.

video_title: Crown: An Ode to the Fresh Cut by Derrick Barnes | READ ALOUD
summary_text: A person goes to the barber shop for a fresh cut. When it is their turn, they sit in the chair and wear a cape like royalty. The barber gives them a tight fade, a high low, or a bald cut, and the fresh cut makes them feel strong and confident. The story says the barber works slowly and carefully with a razor, shaving cream, and other tools to make clean lines and neat sides. People in the shop notice the result, and the person in the chair feels amazing when they see the cut in the handheld mirror. The barber also uses alcohol or witch hazel, which stings a little. At the end, the person removes the cape, pays the barber, and leaves the shop feeling magnificent, flawless, and like royalty.

After school, Fizza and Aia walk home together, and Fizza wants to show Mama her picture.

video_title: Vlad the Fabulous Vampire
summary_text: In a dark woods castle, a stylish vampire named Vladisa Varnab Roland Dragal, the fourth of his name, loved black clothes. He wore black capes and outfits, but he had pink rosy cheeks that made him look different. Vlad hid his cheeks because he worried his friends would not like him if they knew. One night, he tried to tell his best friend Shelly, but he could not find the words. Instead, he made himself new black clothes to cover his face. Soon, Vlad learned that even the fanciest clothes could not hide who he really was. He felt alone and left his friends behind. Then he heard Shelly in trouble with a troll. Shelly also had a secret and asked Vlad not to tell anyone. Vlad and Shelly shared their secrets, and Shelly showed him something special. Together they went beyond the dark woods, and Vlad found courage. He learned he did not need to hide to feel good about himself.

Pete, Bob, and Dad take the long list to the supermarket called Meow Foods. Then the wind blows the list away, so Dad says he remembers the list, and Bob says he does too. In the store, they go from aisle to aisle and pick milk, cheese, bacon, chicken, eggs, spaghetti, macaroni, bow ties, apples, raspberries, treats, and ice cream. Pete and Bob also choose tulips for grandma. At the end, Dad says they got everything except the fish, but the car is full of yummy treats, and they go home after a fun trip.
