video_title: 50 Below Zero
summary_text: In the middle of the night, Jason kept waking up and hearing strange sounds. Each time, he found his father sleepwalking in a different place. First, his father was on top of the refrigerator in the kitchen. Then Jason found him sleeping in the bathtub. After that, he found him asleep on top of the car in the garage. Each time Jason called, “Papa, wake up,” and his father jumped up, ran around three times, and went back to bed. Jason said the house was going crazy, and he was very tired. Later, Jason saw his father’s footprints going out into the snow on a very cold night. Jason worried his father would freeze, so he put on many warm clothes, followed the footprints, and found him by a tree. Jason could not lift him, so he got a sled and pulled him home. He then tied his father’s big toe to the bed so the sleepwalking would stop.

video_title: 50 Below Zero
summary_text: In the middle of the night, Jason kept waking up and hearing strange sounds in his house. Each time he opened a door, he found his father sleepwalking in a different place. First, his father was on top of the refrigerator. Then he was in the bathtub. Later he was on top of the car in the garage. After another sound, Jason looked through the kitchen, bathroom, garage, and living room, but found no one. Then he saw the front door open and his father's footprints going into the snow on a night that was 50 below zero. Jason feared his father would freeze, so he dressed in warm clothes, followed the tracks, found his father by a tree, and could not wake him. He brought him home on a sled, pulled him inside, put him in the tub, and tied his big toe to his bed. After that, when Jason heard another sound, he found his father stuck in the middle of the floor and said the sleepwalking was over.

Behind the triangle was a cave, and Tim went inside. He looked up, crawled through a round opening, went down stairs, and walked straight ahead to a rectangle door. He opened it, saw another rectangle opening, and climbed up and through. There he found his birthday gift: a puppy with big blue eyes. At the end, a map showed the path Tim took, and the puppy was right outside his back door.

video_title: Franklin in the Dark
summary_text: Franklin the Turtle could do many things by himself, like slide down the riverbank and use buttons and zippers. But he was afraid of small dark places, so he would not crawl into his shell. Each night, Franklin’s mother shined a flashlight into his shell and told him there was nothing to be afraid of. Franklin still thought creepy slippery things and monsters lived inside. So Franklin went out to ask for help. He met a duck, a lion, a bird, and a polar bear, but each one was afraid of something different and had something they used to feel safe. Franklin did not need their things. At last, he met his mother again. They walked home beside the pond. His mother gave him supper and a warm hug, then sent him to bed. Franklin finally crawled into his shell and said good night. Then, when no one was looking, he turned on his nightlight.

video_title: Duck in the Fridge

Then he ordered a bigger kit with dogs, but that did not work either. The dogs played cards, and the ducks and sheep made a band. Daddy kept trying, but each new kit only brought more animals and more noise. At last, he found Mother Goose and started to read it. The ducks, sheep, dogs, and cows all liked the stories. Daddy said everyone should go to sleep, and they did. After that, he read Mother Goose every night, and everyone got sleep.

video_title: Groundhug Day
summary_text: Moose is planning a big Valentine’s Day party for two weeks away. Squirrel, Bunny, and Porcupine help with ideas like balloons, cards, and hugs. Then Bunny says there is a problem: tomorrow is Groundhog Day, and if Groundhog sees his shadow, he will go back into his hole for six more weeks and miss the party. Moose and his friends make a plan to stop that from happening. Squirrel wants to change the calendar, and Porcupine says he will blindfold Groundhog. But the animals argue all night and do not notice morning coming. Groundhog wakes up, sees his shadow, and goes back into his hole. Moose asks why, and the friends learn that Groundhog is afraid of shadows. They show him dancing leaf shadows, cloud shadows, silhouettes, and shadow puppets. Groundhog enjoys them all. At the end, he still goes back to his warm hole, but he gives the others a nose kiss and they call it Ground Hug Day.

video_title: 'The Three Billy Goats Gruff' read by Gary Oldman
summary_text: A troll lived under a bridge in mud and trash. He was very hungry and waited for animals to cross above him. One day he heard clip-clop sounds and climbed up to stop a little goat. The goat said his name was Billy Goat Gruff and told the troll he was too small to eat. He also said his big brother would come later and would be bigger and tastier. The troll let him pass. Then the second Billy Goat Gruff came. He said the same thing, and again the troll let him cross after hearing about the bigger brother. At last, the third Billy Goat Gruff arrived. The troll tried to threaten him, but the big goat lowered his horns and rammed the troll. The troll flew off the bridge and down the waterfalls. The three goats went to the grassy ridge and stayed there eating grass.

video_title: 'Calvin Can't Fly' read by Jonathan Pryce
summary_text: Calvin was a starling born in a very big family under an old barn. While his brothers, sisters, and cousins found worms, grass, dirt, and water, Calvin found a book. He learned to read and spent his days in the library, where he read about pirates, dinosaurs, planets, wind, and butterflies. The other starlings called him names, and Calvin felt sad. When fall came, it was time to fly south, but Calvin could not fly. His family left, then came back and tied him with string and scraps of cloth so they could carry him along. While they flew, Calvin saw places he had read about. Later, Calvin heard bad weather coming and warned everyone about a hurricane. His family listened and hid in a cave. The storm passed, and the starlings were safe. They celebrated Calvin, and then Calvin discovered he could fly too. Together, they flew south.

video_title: 'The Rooster Who Would Not Be Quiet!' read by Anna Sawai
summary_text: In the village of La Paz, everyone and everything sang all day long. The dogs barked, mothers sang, engines hummed, and fountains made music. The village was so noisy that people could not hear, sleep, or think. They fired the mayor and then voted for Don Pepe, who promised peace and quiet. After he won, new laws told people not to sing in public, then not to sing at home, and then not to sing at all. Soon La Paz became completely silent. Some people left, some learned to hum, and others were glad to rest. Seven quiet years passed. Then a merry gallito and his family came to a mango tree. The next morning the rooster sang, but the mayor said singing was not allowed. Don Pepe tried to stop him by cutting down the tree, taking away his hen and chicks, putting him in a cage, and covering him with a blanket. Still, the gallito kept singing. At last, the village gathered to listen, and the rooster said a song lives on as long as someone sings it.

video_title: 'The Three Questions' read by Meryl Streep
summary_text: Nikolai was a boy who wanted to be a good person, but he did not always know what to do. He asked his friends three questions: when is the best time to do things, who is the most important one, and what is the right thing to do? Sonya, Gogol, and Pushkin each gave answers, but Nikolai was not sure they were right. So he went to see Leo, an old turtle living high in the mountains. Leo was digging a garden, and Nikolai helped him finish the work. Then a storm came. Nikolai heard a panda calling for help, carried her to Leo’s house, and made a splint for her hurt leg. He then found the panda’s baby in the forest and brought the little one back safe and warm. The next morning, Leo explained that the answers were in Nikolai’s actions: the right time was the time he was helping, the important ones were the people with him, and the right thing was to do good for them.

video_title: 'Memoirs of a Hamster' read by Melanie Lynskey
summary_text: Seymour the hamster starts with a perfect life in his cage. He has seeds, soft wood shavings, and room to run. Then Little Girl brings him an exercise wheel, a water bottle, and yogurt drops. Seymour loves running on his shiny FuzzyBoy 360 wheel every night. One night, Pearl the Cat tells him he runs a lot but never leaves the cage. Pearl says there is a sunroom and a staircase made of sunflower seeds, and she warns him about Hoover. Seymour cannot stop thinking about these things. He makes a plan called Operation Tasty Treat and escapes by using the wheel and a sunflower seed to open the lid. But Pearl was lying. The staircase is only carpet, and the sunroom has no yogurt drops. Seymour gets chased by Pearl and Hoover and hides under the sofa. At last, Little Girl finds him, and Seymour is safe again in his cage, happy with his seeds and room to run.

video_title: 'Velma Gratch and the Way Cool Butterfly' read by Kyra Sedgwick
summary_text: Velma Gratch was the youngest of three sisters, and when she started first grade, everyone remembered Frieda and Fiona but not her. Frieda was known for her singing, and Fiona for running and spelling. Velma felt left out, so she tried to get noticed by singing too loud, running too slow, and doing badly in class. Then she learned about butterflies in science and loved the word metamorphosis. Her class visited the Butterfly Conservatory, where she saw many butterflies and learned about migration. One monarch butterfly landed on Velma’s finger and would not leave. It stayed with her all day, through school and even at home. Because of this, everyone finally knew Velma well. Later, Velma took the butterfly to the park with her class and sisters. When the monarch’s friends were released, it flew away with them to Mexico. At last, everyone remembered Velma.

video_title: 'The Sound of Silence' read by Simu Liu
summary_text: Little Yoshio ran out into Tokyo and listened to many sounds. He heard his boots splash in puddles, rain on his umbrella, and a koto player tuning her instrument. The koto player played beautiful music and told Yoshio that the most beautiful sound was ma, or silence. Yoshio went to school wondering where silence could be. He listened all day, but there was always noise. At recess he sat in the bamboo grove, but the wind and bamboo still made sound. On the way home he heard buses, trains, and traffic lights. At home he heard chopsticks, slurping, and bathwater dripping. That night he tried to stay awake to find silence, but he fell asleep. The next morning, he got up early and went to school before anyone else. In the empty classroom, while reading a book, he suddenly found silence. He learned that silence was there between sounds all along.

video_title: 'My Brother Charlie' read by Holly Robinson Peete
summary_text: Callie and her twin brother Charlie have always been together, even in Mommy’s tummy. They share curly hair, brown eyes, hot chocolate with marshmallows, their dog Harriett, music, football, and names that start with C. Callie is two minutes younger and loves to talk and watch the sky. Charlie is skinnier, goofier, and quieter. As babies, Callie showed love by talking, snuggling, and kissing Mommy, but Charlie did not. Mommy saw that Charlie was different and later learned that he has autism. This makes it harder for him to make friends, show feelings, and stay safe. Sometimes Charlie is hard to understand and can ruin playdates, but he also shows love in his own ways. He smiles, plays hand games, helps with Harriett, and runs to comfort Callie when she gets hurt. One day, after Callie hurt her toe, Charlie said, “Don’t cry, Callie, I love you.” Callie said it back, and she knows their love is shown in many ways.

video_title: 'Julius, the Baby of the World' read by Rosario Dawson
summary_text: Before Julius was born, Lilly was happy to be a big sister. She gave him things, shared secrets, and sang lullabies to him every night. After Julius was born, Lilly did not like sharing. She took her things back and said, “These are mine!” She pinched his tail and said mean things into his crib. Her parents loved Julius very much. They kissed his wet pink nose, looked at his small black eyes, and stroked his sweet white fur. Lilly thought this was disgusting. Julius stayed in her room, and Lilly had to be quiet while he slept. Her parents told Julius he was beautiful and special, and they also sang him letters and numbers. Lilly tried to scare Julius with disguises and magic, and then she pretended he was not there. Nothing changed. Lilly got upset, but her parents still loved Julius and praised him. One day, Lilly told Julius a story that called him a germ, and she was sent to the uncooperative chair. Later, at a family party, Cousin Garland said mean things about Julius. Lilly defended her brother, showed how to kiss, admire, and stroke him, and made everyone repeat that Julius was the baby of the world.

Skeleton dances until Zombie steps in his way and knocks him apart again. A skeleton girl sweeps up his bones, glues him back together, and asks him to dance. Everyone cheers and all the monsters do the Halloween Hustle together.

video_title: 'I'm Not Scared, YOU'RE Scared!' read by Seth Meyers
summary_text: Bear was an easily scared bear. At night, he tied a bell to his door because he was afraid someone might sneak in, and he was even afraid of his own reflection. She read scary stories, slept with her door open, and brushed her teeth while hanging from a tree branch by her ears. One day, Rabbit said they were going on an adventure. Bear wanted to read about adventures instead, but Rabbit kept asking if he was scared. Bear said no and went with her. They crossed a stream, went around a dark forest by bus, rode a train and helicopter over a mountain, and came to a rope bridge. Bear finally said he was scared of the bridge and went home. Then Rabbit fell through the bridge, and Bird woke Bear. Bear rushed out, crossed the stream, forest, and mountain quickly, and saved Rabbit. After that, Bear admitted he was scared, Rabbit said she was too, and Bear learned that sometimes it is okay to be scared.

video_title: 'Never Play Music Right Next to the Zoo' read by John Lithgow
summary_text: A boy went to a concert with his sister, mother, and father at a band shell next to the zoo. The summer air was warm, and the music went on so long that he fell asleep in his seat. Then the conductor became very upset because wild animals were storming the stage. The lions, elephants, bears, raccoons, monkeys, bison, camel, yak, bonobo, ferret, jackal, hippo, tigers, and goats took the instruments and played them. The audience stayed calm, but the boy was frightened. After the animals finished, they bowed, left the stage, took off their fancy clothes, and went back to their cages. Then the boy’s sister told him to wake up or they would leave him behind. The story says never play music next to the zoo and do not fall asleep when an orchestra plays.

video_title: 'How I Met My Monster' read by Nancy Cartwright
summary_text: One night, a child reached under the bed for a truck and found a note from Mr. Zee. It said monsters had a final test there. The child thought it was a trick from the parents and did not believe in monsters. But then strange voices came from under the bed, and five pairs of eyes blinked in the dark. A yellow monster named Mr. Zee came out with four little monsters. He taught them Monster Rules and asked each one to try to get the child into bed and keep the child there until sleep. Genghis made only a tiny burp. Morgan tried shadow puppets and made the child sneeze. Abigail scared the child for a moment, but the child got out of bed again. Then all the monsters vanished. The child went to the kitchen for crackers and later found Gabe had grown big after eating people food. Gabe stayed under the bed, sharpened claws, and asked for toes. The child gave him a stuffed monster, and Gabe snuffled it. The child laughed, yawned, and fell asleep.

video_title: 'Trombone Shorty' read by Angela Bassett
summary_text: The story is about a boy who grows up in Tremé, a neighborhood in New Orleans, where music is everywhere. His big brother, James, plays the trumpet, and the boy and his friends pretend to be in the band. During Mardi Gras, brass bands parade past his house, and people dance in the streets. The boy loves the music and says he wants his own music to sound like gumbo, with many different sounds mixed together. He and his friends make their own instruments and play like real musicians. One day he finds a broken trombone and takes it outside when a parade passes. James sees him and calls him Trombone Shorty, and that name stays with him. He practices hard, carries his trombone everywhere, and learns songs by listening to James. Later, his mother takes him to the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival, where he plays with Bo Diddley onstage. After that, he starts his own band, joins James’s band, and keeps playing music in New Orleans and around the world.

Mo felt sad, but he told them he was still Mo, still a Romero, and still a zombie who loved vegetables.

video_title: 'The Elves and the Shoemaker' read by Chrissy Metz
summary_text: There was once a good shoemaker who became very poor. He and his wife had only enough leather to make one last pair of shoes. The shoemaker planned to cut the leather at night and sew the shoes in the morning. But when they came to the workshop, they found two finished shoes on the table. A dandy gentleman came to the shop, tried the shoes on, and paid double. The shoemaker bought leather for more shoes. Again, each night, he cut the leather, and each morning the shoes were finished. Soon the shoes were famous, and the shoemaker and his wife were no longer poor. Near Christmas, they stayed up and watched. At midnight, two tiny elves came in and made the shoes. The next day the couple made warm clothes and shoes for the elves. That night the elves found the gifts, put them on, danced, sang, and ran away. After that, they were never seen again, and the shoemaker and his wife lived happily.

video_title: 'Sylvester and the Magic Pebble' read by Reid Scott
summary_text: Sylvester Duncan lived with his mother and father in Oatsdale. He liked to collect pebbles. One rainy day he found a bright red pebble that was round like a marble. Happy and excited, he started home to show his parents. On Strawberry Hill, he saw a hungry lion. He got scared and said, “I wish I were a rock,” and he turned into a rock. The magic pebble fell beside him, and he could not touch it. Back home, his parents searched for him for a long time, but they could not find him. Seasons changed, and Sylvester stayed a rock on the hill. One May day, his parents had a picnic there. His mother sat on him, and his father picked up the red pebble and put it on the rock. Sylvester wished to be himself again, and he changed back. His parents hugged him, and they took the pebble home and locked it in a safe.

video_title: 'The Tale of Peter Rabbit' read by Rose Byrne
summary_text: Peter Rabbit lived with his mother and his three sisters, Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail, under a big fir tree. One morning Mrs. Rabbit told them not to go into Mr. McGregor’s garden. She went to the baker’s, and the three good bunnies went to pick blackberries. Naughty Peter went into Mr. McGregor’s garden instead. He ate lettuces, beans, radishes, and parsley. Then Mr. McGregor saw him and chased him. Peter ran all around the garden, lost his shoes, and got caught in a gooseberry net. He escaped, but left his blue jacket behind. He hid in a shed, jumped into a can, sneezed, and ran out a window. At last he found the gate and got back to the wood. He rushed home tired and wet. His mother put him to bed and gave him camomile tea. Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail had bread, milk, and blackberries for supper.

video_title: 'Clark the Shark' read by Chris Pine
summary_text: Clark the Shark went to Theodore Roosterfish Elementary and loved school, lunch, and recess. He was the biggest and strongest fish, but he was also too loud and too wild. He shouted, munched too much lunch, and played too rough, so the other fish stopped sitting with him, eating with him, and playing with him. Clark asked Mrs. Inkydink what was wrong. She told him he needed to stay cool and remember that there is a time and a place for everything. Clark tried, but he kept forgetting. Then he made rhymes to help himself remember. He said, “When teacher’s talking, don’t go walking,” “Only munch your own lunch,” and “Easy does it, that’s the way.” These helped him behave better. Later, a scary new kid, Sid the Squid, came to school and made a mess. Clark helped him play safely and taught him to stay cool. Everyone cheered for Clark, and he told his mother what he learned.

video_title: 'Hey, That's My Monster!' read by Lily Tomlin
summary_text: One night, a child looked under the bed for his monster, Gabe, and found a note saying Gabe had left because someone else needed him more. The child learned that his little sister Emma was now sleeping in a toddler bed, but she kept getting out and making noise at night. The child went to Emma’s room and found Gabe there. Gabe said he would give the child three chances to get Emma to sleep. First came Agatha, a slime-covered monster, but Emma laughed and wiped her noses. Then came Cynthia, a monster with claws, but Emma thought she was pretty and decorated her tail. Next came Vladimir, with tentacles, but Emma played with him too. After three tries, Gabe stayed with Emma. Then Stella, Gabe’s little sister, arrived with a snack and hiccups. Emma was scared of Stella’s hiccups and toes, so Stella became the perfect monster for Emma. Emma stayed in bed, the child went back to his room, and Gabe returned to his own bed.

video_title: 'Strega Nona' read by Mary Steenburgen
summary_text:
A long time ago, in a town in Calabria, there lived Strega Nona, the “Grandma Witch.” People whispered about her, but they still came to her for help. She could heal headaches, help girls find husbands, and remove warts. As she got older, she needed help in her house and garden, so she hired Big Anthony. She told him to sweep, wash dishes, weed the garden, feed and milk the goat, and fetch water. She also told him never to touch the magic pasta pot.

One day, Big Anthony saw Strega Nona make pasta by singing to the pot and blowing three kisses to stop it. Later, after she left to visit Strega Amelia, he tried the spell himself. Pasta poured out and filled the house, then the town, and people ran for plates and bowls. Big Anthony forgot the three kisses, so the pasta would not stop. At last Strega Nona returned, sang the song, blew the kisses, and stopped it. She made Big Anthony eat the pasta for his punishment.

video_title: 'Carla's Sandwich' read by Allison Janney
summary_text: Carla brought strange sandwiches to school all week. On Monday, Buster saw her green sandwich and called it gross, so he moved away. On Tuesday, Leslie said Carla’s banana and cottage cheese sandwich was disgusting and sat elsewhere. On Wednesday, Natie did the same when Carla ate a crunchy peanut butter, cracker, and cheddar sandwich. On Thursday and Friday, Carla brought more unusual sandwiches, and by Monday she had to eat alone because no one wanted to sit with her. Then Miss Pimento announced a picnic. At the picnic, Carla had a Combo Deluxe sandwich with lettuce, tomato, raisin, bean sprout, pretzel, and mayonnaise. Buster forgot his sandwich and got very hungry. Carla offered him one, and after seeing everyone else eat, Buster finally tried it. He loved it and said it was the best sandwich he ever ate. Soon the whole class wanted to try creative sandwiches too. The next day, everyone brought unusual lunches, and Carla surprised them by eating peanut butter and jelly, saying she liked to be different.

video_title: 'The Kissing Hand' read by Barbara Bain
summary_text: Chester Raccoon stood at the edge of the forest and cried because he did not want to go to school. He wanted to stay home with his mother, his friends, his toys, his books, and his swing. Mrs. Raccoon held his hand and told him that sometimes people must do things that feel strange and scary at first. She said Chester would like school and make new friends. She also said she knew a special secret called the Kissing Hand. She showed him by kissing the middle of his left palm. Chester felt the kiss go from his hand to his heart. Mrs. Raccoon told him to press his hand to his cheek when he felt lonely and think, “Mommy loves you.” That night, Chester went to school. Before he went in, he kissed his mother’s hand and gave her a Kissing Hand too. Then he danced away to school, and Mrs. Raccoon smiled and felt his love in her heart.

video_title: 'Library Lion' read by Mindy Sterling
summary_text: One day, a lion came to the library. He walked past the desk and into the stacks. Mr. McBee told Miss Merriweather, but she said to leave the lion alone because he was not breaking any rules. The lion sniffed books, rested in the story corner, and stayed for story hour. When story hour ended, he roared because he wanted more stories. Miss Merriweather said he must be quiet if he wanted to stay. The little girl asked if he could come back tomorrow, and Miss Merriweather said yes. The next days, the lion came early and helped by dusting encyclopedias, licking envelopes, and helping children reach books. People liked him in the library. Later, Miss Merriweather hurt her arm while reaching for a book. The lion roared to get Mr. McBee to help, and Mr. McBee learned there can be a good reason to break a rule. After that, the lion came back, and Miss Merriweather and Mr. McBee were happy to see him again.

video_title: 'I Need My Monster' read by Rita Moreno
summary_text: One night, the child looked under the bed and found a note from Gabe the monster. It said he had gone fishing and would be back in a week. The child could not sleep without Gabe’s scary sounds, so the child tried to find a new monster. First came Herbert, but he did not seem scary enough. Then came Ralph, but his claws were neat and polished, not scary. Next came Cynthia, who had sharp claws and a tail, but she was a girl monster, and the child said a boy monster was needed. Then Mack came, with big claws and a long tongue, but he still was not quite right. At last, Gabe returned. He said fishing was boring and that the child was hard to scare. The child said no other monster could scare like Gabe. Gabe came back under the bed, and everything felt normal again.

The child could not sleep without Gabe’s scary noises, so the child knocked on the floorboards and waited for a replacement.
The first substitute, Herbert, arrived with no claws and did not seem scary enough.
Then Ralph came, but his claws were smooth and polished, so he was sent away too.
A third monster, Cynthia, had sharp claws and a tail, but the child did not want a girl monster.
Next came Mack, who had claws and a big, scruffy look, but his long tongue made the child laugh.
After that, Gabe returned from fishing and said the fish were too easy to scare.
He showed his green ooze, spiked tail, and claw-sharpening, and the child admitted that no other monster could scare like him.
Gabe stayed, the child hid under the blanket, and the child was ready to fall asleep again.

video_title: 'Chester's Way' read by Vanessa Marano & Katie Leclerc
summary_text: Chester liked doing things the same way every day. He cut sandwiches diagonally, got out of bed on the same side, tied his shoes in double knots, ate toast with jam and peanut butter, and carried a tiny first-aid kit. His best friend Wilson was just like him, and they did many things together. They played baseball, rode bikes with hand signals, dressed alike for Halloween, and shared picnics in every season. Then Lilly moved into the neighborhood. Lilly did things her own way, too. She wore band-aids, talked backwards, used disguises, waved at cars, and carried a squirt gun. At first, Chester and Wilson hid from her. One day, older boys bothered them, and a fierce cat scared the boys away. The cat was Lilly in disguise. After that, Chester, Wilson, and Lilly became friends. They shared lunch, sleepovers, and new ideas. They taught each other hand signals, wheelies, backwards talk, and double-knotting shoes.

video_title: 'Brave Irene' read by Al Gore
summary_text: Mrs. Bobbin, a dressmaker, finished a beautiful gown for the duchess, but she had a bad headache and felt too sick to carry it. Her daughter, Irene, wanted to help, so she tucked her mother into bed, gave her tea with lemon and honey, and packed the dress in a big box. Irene dressed warmly and walked out into a cold, snowy wind. As she crossed the fields and Apple Road, the wind pushed her, shook the box, and finally tore the gown free. Irene was very upset, but she kept going with the empty box until she got lost in the dark snow. She fell into a hole, then found the glowing palace. The wind helped her by turning the box into a sled, and the gown was caught in a tree nearby. Irene put the dress back in the box, took it to the palace, and gave the duchess the story. The duchess welcomed her, and later Irene was taken home in a sleigh while her mother was preparing for the morning.

video_title: 'Enemy Pie' read by Camryn Manheim
summary_text: One summer, a boy had a tree house, a sister at camp, and a baseball team, but his summer did not feel perfect. His new neighbor, Jeremy Ross, moved in next to his friend Stanley, and the boy did not like him. Jeremy laughed when he struck the boy out in baseball and invited Stanley to a trampoline party but not him. The boy made an enemy list and put Jeremy on it. His dad said he knew a way to get rid of enemies and showed him an old recipe called Enemy Pie. Dad would not say what was in it, but he said it was the fastest way to get rid of enemies. The boy helped by bringing strange things like weeds, worms, rocks, and gum, while Dad cooked. Then Dad said the pie worked only if the boy spent a day with his enemy and was nice to him. The boy visited Jeremy, played with him, shared lunch, and had fun. By the end, Jeremy was no longer an enemy, and the pie turned out to be delicious.

video_title: 'Guji Guji' read by Robert Guillaume
summary_text: An egg rolled through the trees, across the meadow, and down the hill. It rolled into Mother Duck’s nest. Mother Duck did not see it because she was reading. Soon the eggs cracked. One duckling had blue spots, so Mother Duck named him Crayon. The next had brown stripes, so she named him Zebra. The third was yellow, so she named him Moonlight. The fourth duckling looked very odd and said, “Guji Guji,” so that became his name. Mother Duck taught all four ducklings to swim, dive, and waddle. Guji Guji learned fast and was bigger and stronger, but Mother Duck loved all her ducklings the same. Then three crocodiles came from the lake. They looked like Guji Guji and told him he was a crocodile too. They said to bring the ducks to the bridge. Guji Guji thought hard, made a plan, and took the ducks to the bridge the next day. The crocodiles waited below, but Guji Guji dropped rocks on them. The crocodiles ran away. Guji Guji saved the ducks, and everyone danced and celebrated.

video_title: 'Harry the Dirty Dog' read by Betty White
summary_text: Harry was a white dog with black spots, and he liked almost everything except baths. One day, when he heard the water running in the tub, he took the scrubbing brush and buried it in the backyard. Then he ran away from home. Harry played in the street where people were fixing it, and he got dirty. He played at the railroad and got dirtier. He played tag with other dogs and became dirtier still. Then he slid down a coal chute and became the dirtiest of all. He changed from a white dog with black spots into a black dog with white spots. After a while, Harry felt tired and hungry and wondered if his family thought he had really run away, so he ran back home. At the house, no one knew he was Harry until he found the scrubbing brush, took it into the bathtub, and let the children scrub him. Then his family knew him, and Harry became clean again and very happy.

video_title: 'Somebody Loves You, Mr. Hatch' read by Hector Elizondo
summary_text: Mr. Hatch was a quiet man who lived alone and did the same things every day. He walked to the shoelace factory, ate lunch by himself, bought a turkey wing, read the paper, and went to bed early. One Valentine’s Day, he found a package on his porch. Inside was a heart-shaped box of candy and a card that said, “Somebody loves you.” Mr. Hatch was surprised and happy. He laughed, danced, and put on a tie and aftershave. After that, he began smiling and talking to people. He shared candy at work, helped Mr. Smith at the newsstand, and found little Melanie Todd when she was lost. He baked brownies, and the neighborhood children came to his house for a picnic. Later, Mr. Goober the postman said the valentine had been delivered to the wrong house. Mr. Hatch gave back the box and card and felt sad again. But the next Saturday, everyone in the neighborhood came to his house with hearts, candy, streamers, and a sign that said, “Everybody loves Mr. Hatch.”

video_title: 'The Night I Followed the Dog' read by Amanda Bynes
summary_text: The storyteller has a dog that seems plain and boring. The dog can fetch, roll over, and shake hands, but he mostly sleeps and eats. Then one morning, the storyteller saw his dog jump out of a limousine wearing a tuxedo. That night, he decided to follow him. He watched the dog go into a special doghouse with a living room, a bathroom, and fancy clothes. The dog changed into his tuxedo and left in a limousine. The storyteller followed to a place called The Dog House, where two bulldogs tried to stop him. His dog let him in and explained that it was a place where dogs could relax, eat treats, and be themselves. The storyteller stayed a while, then went home with a photo of them together.

video_title: 'When Pigasso Met Mootisse' read by Eric Close
summary_text: Pigasso was a young pig who loved to paint, and Mootisse was a young bull who loved to paint big, bright pictures. Soon, many pigs and cows wanted to see their art, and both artists became famous. But too many visitors came, and Pigasso got tired of the noisy pig pen. Mootisse also got tired of the crowded cow town. They each found a quiet farm and moved there. Then they met as neighbors across the road. At first they were friendly, but soon they began to tease each other about their paintings. Pigasso called Mootisse a Mad Cow, and Mootisse called Pigasso an Art Hog. They got angry and painted their houses in a big art battle. After that, they built a tall fence between them. Later, they missed each other and painted on the fence. They laughed, took the fence down, and became great friends.

video_title: 'Stellaluna' read by Pamela Reed
summary_text: In a warm forest, Mother Bat had a tiny baby bat named Stellaluna. One night, an owl attacked Mother Bat while she was flying for fruit. Stellaluna fell into the forest and then into a bird nest where three baby birds lived: Pip, Flitter, and Flap. Stellaluna was hungry, but she did not want the bugs Mama Bird brought. At last she ate a grasshopper. She tried to live like the birds. She stayed awake in the day, slept at night, and ate bugs. She still liked to hang by her feet. Mama Bird made her follow the nest rules. When the babies grew, they learned to fly. Stellaluna flew too, but she was clumsy and got lost after flying far away. In the dark, she met other bats and found her real mother. Mother Bat took her to eat fruit and fly at night. Later, Stellaluna visited the birds, and the birds and bats learned they were different, but still friends.

video_title: 'A Bad Case of Stripes' read by Sean Astin
summary_text: Camilla Cream loved lima beans, but she never ate them because her friends did not like them and she wanted to fit in. On the first day of school, she worried about what to wear and tried on forty-two outfits. When she looked in the mirror, she found that she was covered with stripes from head to toe. Her mother kept her home, and Dr. Bumble came to check her. The next day Camilla went to school, but the other children laughed at her and called out colors and shapes. Each time they shouted, her skin changed again. The principal sent her home because she was too distracting. Soon more doctors, specialists, and experts came, but none could help. Then many people brought her strange cures, and Camilla changed into even more unusual things. At last a kind old woman offered her plain lima beans. Camilla admitted she loved them, ate them, and all the strange changes disappeared. After that, she ate lima beans whenever she wanted and never had stripes again.

summary_text: Sophie is a young woman who has just turned 18. She lives in a world where witches and magic are common. While walking through the market, she sees a handsome young man and becomes interested in him. He is really a wizard named Howl, and he is looking for an apprentice. Before Sophie can speak to him, a witch named Madame Sulleman appears and casts a spell that turns Sophie into an old woman. The curse can only be broken if Howl confesses his undying love, but he will only do that if Sophie breaks the curse first. With help from a talking fire demon named Calcifer, Sophie enters Howl’s moving castle and becomes his apprentice. As she lives there, she grows more confident. Howl begins to care for her, but he is afraid to confess his love. Sophie finally uses all her power to break the curse and becomes young again. Howl kisses her, and together they defeat Madame Suliman and free Calcifer.

video_title: The Magic Story
summary_text: Matthew met a girl named Goldilocks on the way, and she welcomed him in for lunch. They shared a large bowl of oatmeal and ate until they were full. After Matthew said goodbye, he returned to the castle path. Soon, a vicious wolf chased him, so Matthew ran to the hut of the three small pigs. The wolf tried to blow the house down, but he failed because he was too tired. Matthew then hurried to a bridge, where a grumpy old troll jumped out and said he would eat him. A large billy goat knocked the troll into the lake, and Matthew thanked his new friends. Next, he ran past a race’s starting line and finished first ahead of the dozing hare and the tortoise. After that, a big beanstalk appeared, and Matthew climbed it to the castle. He could not open the door, so he went in through a window. Inside, he saw a harp, a goose that laid golden eggs, and a magician with The Magic Story. The wizard gave Matthew the book, told him to go home, and shot the book. Matthew disappeared, then was reunited with his family. He later read the book, which began to shine again, and he vanished once more.

She made him take her to the lights, and they began a big adventure.

video_title: The Gingerbread Man
summary_text: An old man, an old woman, and a little boy lived together. One morning, the old woman made a gingerbread man with icing hair and clothes and little dough eyes and nose. She put him in the oven and told the little boy to watch him while she and the old man went to dig potatoes in the garden. But the little boy did not watch all the time. The oven door opened, and the gingerbread man jumped out and rolled away. The little boy ran after him, and the old man and old woman ran too, but the gingerbread man was too fast. He went on and met two men digging a well, then two men digging a ditch, and he said he could outrun them. They all chased him, but they could not catch him. Next he met a bear and then a wolf, and he outran them too. At last he met a fox, who asked him to come closer. The gingerbread man did, and the fox snapped him up.

video_title: Snow White storytelling
summary_text: Snow White lived in a far away land as a princess, but she did not want to act like a perfect royal girl. She wished she could run in the forest, climb trees, and eat snacks. One day, while walking in the castle gardens, she met a little bird. The bird told her that the woodland creatures were having a picnic and asked her to come live in the forest. Snow White packed bread and cheese and ran away from the castle. In the forest, she found a little cottage made of twigs and leaves. A family of deer invited her inside and showed her a room with flower walls and a soft moss bed. Snow White told them about the castle, and they told her about the forest. She felt happy and like she belonged. The next day, she explored the forest with her new friends. At sunset, she returned to the castle, smiling. After that, she often went back to the forest to stay with the deer.

video_title: South Huntington Public Library's Story Time - The Watermelon Seed
summary_text: A crocodile loves watermelon very much. He eats it for breakfast, lunch, dinner, and dessert. He says he has loved it since he was a tiny baby crocodile. While eating, he swallows a seed by mistake. Then he gets worried and says the seed is growing inside his guts. He thinks vines will come out of his ears, his stomach will stretch, and his skin will turn pink. He does not want to be in a fruit salad and asks for help. Soon his stomach feels funny, and he burps. After that, the seed comes back out. The crocodile says no more melon for him, never again. Then he thinks about it and takes just a tiny tiny bite anyway, chomp chomp chomp. At the end, he hopes he does not swallow the seed again.

video_title: South Huntington Public Library's Story Time - Swashby and the Sea
summary_text: Captain Swashby loved the sea and moved to a small house near the beach when he retired. He liked being alone and did not want neighbors. Then a girl and her granny moved into the house next door. They brought umbrellas, beach chairs, and fun noises. Swashby wrote messages in the sand to make them go away, but the sea changed the words a little. The girl read the words and played or sang instead. She and Granny invited Swashby for tea, but he said no. Later, the girl played with shells, buckets, and shovels, and Swashby showed her how to use the wet sand and clam shells. Then the sea moved in, tickled the girl’s toes, and washed away her sculpture. Swashby helped when the girl drifted away in a bucket, and everyone laughed and hugged. After that, Swashby shared tea, food, and sea glass with them. He learned that neighbors could be friends, and he wrote, “Thank ye friend,” to the sea.

video_title: South Huntington Public Library's Story Time - What the Ladybug Heard
summary_text: On a farm lived a fat red hen, a duck in a pond, a goose in a pen, a sheep, a hog, a horse, a dog, a prize cow, two cats, and a ladybug. The animals made their sounds, but the ladybug never said a word. Then the ladybug saw two men in a big black van. She heard them whisper a plan to steal the fine prize cow. They wanted to open the gate at night, go past the horse, turn by the duck pond, pass the hog, not wake the dog, go past the sheep, and get to the cow shed. The ladybug spoke for the first time and told all the animals. She said the thieves were coming and explained their route. The animals listened, and the ladybug told them not to fear. She whispered a plan to each one. In the dead of night, the two men came onto the farm. The animals made noise and confused them. The men fell into the duck pond. The farmer woke up, called the police, and the men were caught. After that, the farm animals were safe, and the ladybug still never said a word again.

summary_text: A regular girl and her best friend do many things together. She makes things, and he unmakes things. One day the girl decides to make the most magnificent thing. At last, they look at it, ride it, and see that it is the most magnificent thing.

On the ride home, the road turns and curves, but the moon seems to follow Max. It peeks through trees, goes over a bridge, past cows, through a town, and even at a tunnel. Then dark clouds cover the sky, and Max cannot see the moon. When he gets home, he thinks the moon will not shine for him all the way home. In bed, he feels lonely and misses Grandpa. Then the clouds move away, the moon comes back, and soft yellow light fills his room. Max remembers Grandpa's words and falls asleep peacefully.

He asked if swimming was like flying, and dad said it was almost the same.

video_title: South Huntington Public Library’s Story Time - Anansi the Spider
summary_text: Anansi was a spider in Ashanti land. He had six sons: See Trouble, Road Builder, River Drinker, Game Skinner, Stone Thrower, and Cushion. One day Anansi went far from home and got lost. Back home, See Trouble saw that his father was in danger and told his brothers. Road Builder made a road, and the six brothers hurried to help. They found that a fish had swallowed Anansi. River Drinker drank all the river water, and Game Skinner split open the fish so Anansi could come out. Then a falcon carried Anansi high in the sky. Stone Thrower hit the falcon with a stone, and Anansi fell down safely. Cushion came next and helped him land softly. The spider family was happy to be together again. Later, Anansi found a beautiful globe of light in the forest. He wanted to give it to the son who saved him, but he could not choose. He asked Nyame to hold it, and because the sons argued all night, Nyame took the light into the sky, where it still shines.

summary_text: This is Milo, and he wants to be a baker. He likes making cupcakes, cookies, and pies, but he keeps making mistakes. He goes home and bakes again, but he still uses salt instead of sugar, vinegar instead of water, and too much baking powder. The cookies turn bitter and the batter turns green. Milo feels upset and wants to quit, but he remembers Chef Gustaf saying to keep trying. He calms down, makes a list, focuses, and keeps baking. After many tries, he makes his 11th batch of cookies and later enters a cooking contest. Chef Gustaf tastes Milo’s cookies and says they are the best. Milo wins and learns that not giving up is the secret ingredient.

While the students are at lunch, the pencils band together and write a letter. In the letter, they explain all the ways they are treated badly and say they are going on strike. When the children come back, a young girl reads the letter first and cries. She says the pencils are right and should be treated better. Then the students begin handling the pencils gently. The story ends by saying school supplies should be used with care.

video_title: Nobody Hugs a Cactus Read Aloud 🌵 | Funny & Heartwarming Storytime for Kids [English] 2025
summary_text: Hank was a cactus living in a pot by a window that looked out at the hot desert. He liked quiet and wanted to be left alone. Rosie the Tumbleweed came by and said hello, but Hank ignored her. A tortoise, a jack rabbit, a coyote, a cowboy, a lizard, and an owl all passed by too. Hank yelled at each one and told them to go away. The owl would not give him a hug, and Hank began to feel lonely. The next morning, he felt sad inside. Then the wind blew an old cup onto Hank’s face, and he could not get it off by himself. Rosie came back and knocked the cup off for him. Hank felt sorry for being rude, so he grew a flower for Rosie. When Rosie returned, Hank gave her the flower. Rosie was so happy that she hugged him. Hank and Rosie got stuck together, but they did not mind, because it was better than being alone.

The alien ship takes everyone back to the Bamboo Grove, where they eat a bamboo and jelly bean feast.

video_title: Children's Books Read Aloud | 🐊😂Funny Gator Read Aloud | Kindness
summary_text: Allan was a very scary alligator. Every day he polished his scales, sharpened his nails, and brushed his big teeth. Then he went into the jungle and scared the frogs, monkeys, and parrots. Allan loved being scary. At night he went back to the swamp, did his crossword, and took out his false teeth. He kept his false teeth in a secret place, and no one knew about them. One morning Barry the beaver saw Allan and got very frightened. Barry hid behind a bush, and Allan’s false teeth fell out. When Allan woke up, his teeth were gone. He went into the jungle anyway, but without his teeth he was not very scary. Allan went home feeling sad and cried until the next morning. Then the jungle animals came to his swamp and brought back his teeth. They told Allan to stop scaring them. Allan agreed, and after that he became Allan the Gardener, Allan the Hairdresser, Snappy Cuts, and Allan the Dentist. Sometimes he even let Barry borrow his teeth.

video_title: It Will Be Okay | Read Aloud Stories (With Sound Effects)
summary_text: Every afternoon, giraffe and zebra walked together to the watering hole. But one day giraffe could not go. He called for zebra and, after looking around, zebra found him high in a tree, holding on tightly. Giraffe whispered that he had seen a spider and was scared it might crawl on him or chase him. Zebra told giraffe that he was bigger, stronger, and faster than the spider, and asked him to come down. Giraffe still felt worried and embarrassed. Zebra did not leave. He waited beside the tree as the sun went down. At last giraffe slowly climbed down and thanked zebra for staying with him. Zebra said that if something bothers a friend, it is not silly. Then they started toward the watering hole. Soon giraffe saw a spider walking alone. Giraffe felt brave and asked if it wanted to join them, but the spider quickly ran up a tree. Zebra said the spider was scared now, and giraffe stayed with his friend.

Sally found the squirrel skis, the rabbits, and the nuts they had paid with. Then she helped bring the squirrels warm food, and later the town gave them a ski chalet where they could ski safely.

In America, he saw that England ruled the colonies and taxed many things. He became a patriot and gave speeches against British rule. When British soldiers marched into Lexington in 1775, the American Revolution began. Alexander joined the army, drilled his troops, and later fought at Yorktown in 1781. He led a charge against a weak British barrier and helped win the battle. After the war, he worked to build the new nation, helped write the Federalist Papers, and became Secretary of the Treasury. He later died in a duel with Aaron Burr.

video_title: 👶 You Are New 👶 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

The child fits in tiny spots, gets carried a lot, and wears little baby shoes. The child can open wide and yell, and sometimes makes funny smells. The child can feel mad, scared, and blue because everything is new. The child takes baths, gets washed clean, and then gets cuddled in cozy time. The child plays peekaboo and has fun. Every day the child stretches and grows and learns new things. Soon the child is not new anymore, but then new times come again with new games, new friends, new books, new places, and new adventures. It is okay not to know what to do. The world of being new is waiting.

video_title: 🌈 A Color of His Own 🌈 Nickelodeon Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]
summary_text: Parrots are green, goldfish are red, elephants are gray, and pigs are pink. Most animals have their own color, but chameleons change color where they go. One chameleon sat on a tiger’s tail and thought he could stay on a green leaf and be green forever. He climbed onto the greenest leaf. In autumn, the leaf turned yellow, and the chameleon turned yellow too. Then the leaf turned red, and he turned red. When winter winds blew the leaf from the branch, the chameleon went with it and was black in the long winter night. When spring came, he walked into the green grass and met another chameleon. He told his sad story. The older chameleon said they could stay together. They would still change color, but they would always be alike. So they stayed side by side and were green, purple, yellow, and red with white polka dots together.

Penguin and the pine cone played together, and they stayed in each other’s hearts.

Grandma was happy to see him, but dogs are not allowed in the hospital. A nurse came to check Grandma and did not see Clifford because he was very small. Clifford licked the thermometer and thought it was candy. Then the nurse gave Grandma a shot, and Clifford ran away because he hates needles. He ran through the hall, where children saw him and played with him. Some girls dressed him up, and then he rushed off again. A child helped him find a safe place in the nursery. Later, Mom and Emily Elizabeth came back, said goodbye to Grandma, and took Clifford home. Grandma got a new dog from the gift shop. Now Clifford visits the hospital sometimes to cheer up his friends.

In the morning, Nudles was awake and smiling, and he made a new list for us.

Gigi feels tired and thirsty, but she and her mother place empty pots on their heads and begin their long walk, singing as they go. Halfway there, they stop at a giant kite tree and eat sweet Shea nuts. When they reach the well, they hear water running, see their friends, and wait while the pots are filled. On the way home, the walk feels harder because the pots are heavy and their bodies are tired. At home, the family boils water, washes clothes, and cooks food. Gigi drinks, sings, dances, and hears her mother say they will journey again tomorrow.

video_title: 🍂 The Very Last Leaf 🍂 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]
summary_text:
Lance Cottonwood was the best and brightest student in his class from his first day of school in the spring. He loved learning about being a leaf and did well in wind resistance, photosynthesis 101, and changing colors in autumn. But when the final exam came, Lance felt afraid because the test would make him fall from the top of his tree to the grass below. He was jealous of his neighbor Doug, an evergreen, because Doug stayed on his branch all winter.

When autumn arrived, the other leaves let go and fell, but Lance stayed on the tree and made excuses. His classmates noticed he was scared. The days grew colder, and Lance tried to stay up all winter like Doug. His teacher told him it was okay to be scared and helped him talk about his worries. Lance saw that the leaves below were safe and having fun in leaf piles and crafts. He took a deep breath, let go, and floated gently down. He passed the test and rejoined the others below.

At the end, Daddy brings out Mila’s bike without training wheels. Mila falls, tries again, and then asks for help. Mommy and Daddy help her learn, and she rides on her own while everyone cheers.

Later, Louis played trumpet, Naveen asked Tiana to dance, and they twirled under the light of Evangeline, the evening star.

Big bear went to his cozy den, put on his pjs, blew out the light, and said, “Good night.”

video_title: ✏️ Stories for Kids Read Aloud ✏️ Pencils on Strike by Jennifer Jones [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]
summary_text: A group of pencils talked about their hard life at school. They said students often tossed them, rolled them, snapped them, chewed on them, bent them, and left them in bins. The pencils said they were important because they help students write, fix mistakes, and work on paper, but they still did not get kind treatment. While the students were at lunch, the pencils got together and wrote a letter with their complaints. They said they would go on strike and not take the rough treatment anymore. When the students came back, a young girl read the letter first. Her eyes filled with tears, and she said the pencils were right. She told the others to treat the pencils better and practice using them carefully. One by one, the students began to handle the pencils with more care. The story ends by reminding readers to use school supplies gently so they will last and be ready when needed.

After that, they laughed, hugged, and had tea, ice cream, lobster, and s’mores together.

summary_text: Meg was a box attack who loved to make things from boxes. She built tiny houses, tall towers, and twisty tunnels. Her mother was proud of her and sent her to maker school. There Meg met many makers, like blanketeers, spaghetti texts, tin foilers, and egg cartoneers. Meg was the first box attack in class, and she learned how to make box structures useful, strong, and beautiful. Then Simone arrived. Simone was also a box attack, and she made things Meg had never seen before. The two girls started to argue about how to build. On maker match day, they had to work as a team, but they did not want to. Meg wanted a tree house, and Simone wanted a ship. They built on the same big box and kept making their sides bigger and bigger until the whole thing was used up. Their work almost crashed. Then they stopped arguing, joined the last pieces together, and made one new creation. They did not win first place, but they became friends.

summary_text: Splat the Cat and his class rode the bus to the ice cream factory. The cats were very excited and shouted, “I scream! You scream! We all scream for ice cream!” Mr. Jellybean, the factory manager, welcomed them and started a tour. He led them to a back room with chairs and desks instead of ice cream. He talked a long time about freezers, and the cats grew tired and sleepy. Splat began to daydream about making ice cream. He leaned on a big red button, and alarms rang. Ice cream came rushing out in a huge wave and flooded the factory. After the class cleaned up, Mrs. Wimpy Dimple counted the heads and found that Seymour was missing. Splat and the team searched through the sticky mess, cleaning as they went. At last, they found Seymour high on a beam with his mouth full of ice cream. Seymour jumped into Splat’s paws, and Mr. Jellybean thanked the class for cleaning the factory.

Luna Girl loses her helpers, and her moths come back when she is gentle. The PJ Masks cheer, “Hooray! Cause in the night we saved the day.”

video_title: 🐶 Kids Book Read Aloud 🐶 Clifford the Big Red Dog by Norman Bridwell [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]
summary_text: The child has a dog named Clifford. Clifford is a very big red dog, bigger and redder than the other dogs on the street. They have fun together and play games. The child throws a stick, and Clifford brings it back. They also play hide and seek, and the child can find Clifford. Clifford can sit up and beg, and he can help when they camp out because he does not need a tent. Clifford is not always good. He runs after cars and cats, digs up flowers, and chews shoes. He eats and drinks a lot, and his house is hard to keep. But Clifford is a good watchdog, and bad boys do not come around anymore. One day, the child gives Clifford a bath, combs his hair, and takes him to the dog show. Clifford does not win first prize, but the child still keeps Clifford and likes him best.

video_title: 🚜 Mighty, Mighty Construction Site | READ ALONG VIDEO | Stories for Kids Read Aloud
summary_text: At the big construction site, five trucks wake up in the morning and get ready for work. They see a brand new job: a giant building plan. The job is too big for only five trucks, so Cement mixer blows his horn. More mighty trucks come fast, and soon ten big trucks are in the yard. Skid steer breaks rocks, and Bulldozer clears the land. Excavator digs trenches, and buckhoe sets down drainage pipe. Crane truck lifts a beam, but he runs out of supplies. Then a mighty flatbed arrives with more supplies, and the work starts again. Front end loader and dump truck move dirt and gravel. Cement mixer pours concrete, and pumper sends it up high into the building. The team works hard together, finishes the job, and drives away at night to rest.

video_title: Sonic the Hedgehog Ch. 2 by Michael Teitelbaum VIDEO READ ALONG | Kids Book Read Aloud | Ages 7 - 9
summary_text: Uncle Chuck was driving a tractor when it crashed into Robotnik and his newest robot. The robot broke apart, and Uncle Chuck and Robotnik got trapped between the tractor and a tree. Robotnik was angry and asked how they would get free. Not far away, Sonic was playing baseball against nine kids by himself. He ran so fast that he could pitch, catch, and throw the ball before the other players could react. Then Sonic heard someone crying for help from Uncle Chuck’s workshop. He stopped the game and rushed there in a blue blur. Sonic saw Uncle Chuck and Robotnik trapped by the tractor. He tried to push the tractor, but it was too heavy. Then he remembered Uncle Chuck’s magic power ring. Sonic ran into the workshop, got the ring, and came back glowing bright yellow. With the ring’s power, he lifted the tractor with one hand and freed them. Sonic carried Uncle Chuck and Robotnik to the hospital.

video_title: Walt Disney’s Alice in Wonderland Meets the White Rabbit [ READ ALONG VIDEO ] | Kids Book Read Aloud
summary_text: Alice was in Wonderland when she saw the White Rabbit hurrying across the meadow and saying, “I’m late, I’m late for an important date!” Alice followed him into a hollow tree. Inside, she slipped on white pebbles and fell down, floating past cupboards, lamps, clocks, mirrors, and a rocking chair. At the bottom, she saw the White Rabbit go through a tiny door she could not fit through. Alice wandered alone and met strange talking animals, but they could not help her find the Rabbit. Later, she came to a little house and saw the White Rabbit again. He called her Marianne and told her to get his gloves. Alice looked for them, but he left again. She followed him farther into Wonderland, where she met Tweedledee, Tweedledum, the Mad Hatter, the March Hare, the Cheshire Cat, and Jabberwock. The Cheshire Cat told her about a shortcut, and it led her to a garden where gardeners painted roses red. The Queen of Hearts came with a procession, and the White Rabbit was her trumpeter. Alice said she was not frightened, called them a pack of cards, and ran back to the riverbank, glad to be home.

He checks the pillow, the blanket, under the stove, the front door, the wood box, and the china shelf. Mother bear and father bear keep guessing where little bear is hiding. They find teddy, bunny, a mitten, rabbits, and a mouse, but not little bear. Father bear even eats chocolate cake near the mirror. At last little bear comes down from father bear’s shoulders and lands on the sofa. Father bear carries him to bed, and little bear giggles as he goes.

video_title: Old Black Fly Storytime | Memphis Public Library
summary_text: Old black flies buzzed around all day and made many troubles. He ate the crust of an apple pie and bothered the baby until she cried. He coughed on the cookies with chocolate bits and drove the dog nearly out of his wits. He frolicked on the eggs for a birthday cake and licked up the frosting. He danced on the garbage sack and got sweet honey on his dirty back. He hid in the ivy by the kitchen sink and stole some jelly. He played on the keys by the kitchen door and landed on the grocery list. He locked up the milk in kitty’s bowl and nibbled noodles in the casserole. He crawled in the olive oil spills and pestered the parrot. He snoozed on grandma’s bed, rode the red ribbon, sniffed the salami, and ran around sister’s teacup. He slept on clean underwear, played on the vase, dozed on the window, and buzzed around mama’s yarn. At the end, he landed on the table, and the old black flies were done buzzing around.

summary_text: Dr. De Soto was a mouse dentist who did very good work. He treated small animals in a chair, larger animals on the floor, and extra large animals in a special room. He and his wife would not treat cats or other dangerous animals, and a sign on the door said so. One day a well-dressed fox came with a bandage on his jaw and begged for help because his tooth hurt. Mrs. De Soto let him in, and Dr. De Soto checked his mouth. He found a rotten tooth and bad breath, so he said the tooth must come out. The fox dreamed about eating mice while the tooth was pulled. Dr. De Soto made a gold tooth for him overnight. The next day the fox came back, and Dr. De Soto put in the new tooth. Then he used a secret formula that made the fox’s teeth stick together. The fox had to leave with his mouth shut, and the De Sotos had outfoxed him.

summary_text: It was hot and dry in the land. The red soil was cracked, and the porcupine knew rain was coming because she could smell it. She whispered, “The rain is coming,” and told the zebras. The zebras saw the lightning and told the baboons. The baboons heard the thunder and told the rhino. Then the first raindrop splashed down, and the rhino felt the rain and told the lion. The lion said he could smell, see, hear, feel, and taste the rain. Soon it rained and rained until the rivers flowed fast and the water holes were full. After the rain stopped, tall grasses grew, and the trees made fresh green leaves. The lion rested in the shade, dino lay in the cool mud, the baboons ate fruit, the zebras drank water, and the porcupine said the rain would come back again when it was time.

summary_text: The sky turns gray, and dark clouds gather over the hill hollow. One by one, animals hurry there to stay safe. First bird comes in, then mouse, squirrel, rabbit, chipmunk, woodchuck, raccoon, possum, red fox, and skunk. Each new animal makes the count grow until ten critters are huddled together in the hill hollow. All night long, the storm keeps going. The wind blows, the leaves swirl, lightning cracks, rain falls, and thunder rumbles and grumbles. In the morning, the sky is clear again. But Alton and the others hear a new rumble and grumble. They turn around and find two sleeping bears making the sound. Before the bears get their scent, the animals fly away, counting backward from ten to one. Then they see that the big storm has changed into a very big beautiful day.

video_title: Thunder Cake Storytime
summary_text: On hot summer days at Grandma’s farm in Michigan, the sky grew dark and thunder scared the child, who hid under the bed. Grandma, called babushka, told the child it was “thunder cake-baking weather” and said they must make a Thunder cake before the storm came. She explained that the child should count the seconds between lightning and thunder to know how far away the storm was. They found the recipe, wrote down the ingredients, and hurried outside. As the storm moved closer, they gathered eggs from Nellie Peck hen, milk from the kick cow, chocolate, sugar, flour, three overripe tomatoes, and strawberries. Grandma stayed calm and helped the child keep going. They mixed the batter, put the cake in the oven, and finished just as the storm reached the house. They ate the cake together, and after that, the child was no longer afraid of thunder.

video_title: The Cat that Ate the Palace
summary_text: In a palace, a king and a queen were bored because they had to listen to nobles, advisers, and courtiers all day. One day the queen left the throne room and walked through the palace to the kitchen. There she found a little cat and gave it cream on a silver dish. The cat did not like being called little, so it ate the queen. Then it ate the cook, the pastry chef, the birds and bees in the garden, the cleaning servants, the guards at the throne room door, the king, the nobles, the advisers, and a young stable boy. Inside the cat’s belly, everyone was crowded together. The stable boy used a piece of straw to tickle the cat’s throat. The cat sneezed and threw everyone back out, in reverse order. After that, the cat was empty again, and it went on its way, licking its paws.

video_title: Super Great Kids' Stories - World Wide Stories for Kids - The Luck Child
summary_text: A man and a woman lived in a cottage in the forest and had a baby boy. They took him to a fortuneteller, who said that when he was 16, he would marry a princess and become a king. Later, a king in disguise visited their cottage. He did not want the fortune to happen, so he took the baby away, put him in a wooden box, and threw him into the river. But the baby was found by the Miller's young assistant at a mill. The Miller and his wife raised the child as their own. When the boy grew up, the king gave him a letter to take to the castle. Robbers changed the letter, so the queen married him to the princess instead of harming him. The king then sent him to fetch three golden hairs from the devil. The young man found answers to three other problems on the way, got the golden hairs from the devil's granny, and returned home. In the end, the king went to the river fairman, became the new fairman, and the young man became king after marrying the princess.

The fish took her to a watery world with green grass, fat cows, fruit trees, cream, and honey. Kia ate there, then returned home full. She went every day, and the fish sang, “KIA KIA, please be brave.”

One day at the lake, a shining purple fish spoke to her and took her to a watery world with fruit trees, fat cows, cream, and honey. video_title: Super Great Kids' Stories - World Wide Stories for Kids - The Fox and The Crow
summary_text: A mother fox lived with her cubs in a cozy den. In the daytime they played, roamed, hunted, and explored. At night they curled up together, and the mother told them stories. One night she told a story about a fox who walked on a sunny day and smelled cheese in a tree. He saw a crow with cheese in its beak. The fox said kind words and asked the crow to sing. The crow opened his beak to sing, and the cheese fell into the fox’s mouth. The cubs laughed and giggled at the story. The youngest cub liked it best. She thought about it all night and the next day went out alone. She found a crow with cheese and used the same kind words. Then she asked the crow to tell her how he became so wise. The crow began to talk, and the cheese fell down. The little fox caught it and went home. That night, she told the story to the others.

video_title: Super Great Kids' Stories - World Wide Stories for Kids - Anansi and The Magic Pot
summary_text: Anansi, his wife Asu, and their children had very little food because the rains did not come and the harvest failed. Anansi went to the farm with his hoe and dug in the dry ground for root vegetables. Instead of vegetables, he found a buried pot. The pot spoke to him and sang, “Do not wash me” and “Wrap me, tap me, and I will cook.” Anansi asked for chicken stew, and the pot filled with stew. He ate it all, then hid the magic pot in the bushes and went home. He told Asu he had found nothing, and she gave him only hot water with salt and pepper. Later, Anansi returned to the farm many times and used the pot to make porridge and more stew. He kept the pot secret and did not share. One day Asu followed him, saw the pot, washed it at the river, and the magic went away. When Anansi came home and asked the pot to sing, it would not cook anymore.

video_title: Read Aloud- Beatrice's Goat By: Paige McBrier
summary_text: Beatrice lives in the village of Kiss Inga in western Uganda with her mother and five younger brothers and sisters. Before the goat came, she worked in the fields, helped with the younger children, and wished she could go to school like the children she saw sitting on benches under the jackfruit trees. Her mother then told her that their family was one of 12 village families to receive a goat. Beatrice helped build a shed and plant elephant grass and other plants for the goat to eat. When the goat arrived, Beatrice named her Disa Luck. Two weeks later, the goat gave birth to twins, which Beatrice named Melinda WA and Surprise. Beatrice fed the goat well, sold the extra milk, and saved the money. After enough money was saved, her mother said Beatrice could pay for school. The next week, Beatrice started school in her new uniform, and she went off with the goat beside her, ready for a new life.

video_title: Read Aloud- We Are All Wonders By: R.J. Palacio
summary_text: The child says he is not an ordinary kid. He does ordinary things like riding a bike, eating ice cream, and playing ball, but he does not look like other kids. His mom says he is unique and a wonder, and his dog Daisy agrees. Some people do not see that. They stare, point, laugh, and say mean things behind his back. video_title: Read Aloud: Let The Children March By: Monica Clark-Robinson
summary_text: The story begins with a child explaining many things Black people could not do, like play in white playgrounds, go to white schools, or drink from white water fountains. One spring night, the family goes to church to hear Dr. King. He tells everyone it is time to march for freedom, and he asks for peaceful protestors. The parents worry about jobs and safety, but the children say they can march. On May 2nd, many boys and girls meet at church and walk together, singing freedom songs. Police warn them to stop, spray them with water, and threaten dogs, but the children do not leave. Many are arrested and taken to jail. Inside the crowded jail, they sing “We shall overcome.” The marches continue for seven days. The jails fill up, President Kennedy notices, and leaders make a deal. Desegregation begins, and the child finally plays on a playground and eats in a diner that had once been closed to them.

video_title: Read Aloud- The Tree Lady By: H. Joseph Hawkins
summary_text: Catherine Olivia Sessions, called Kate, grew up in the woods of Northern California. She liked gathering leaves, pine needles, and flowers to make necklaces and bracelets. At school, she learned to read, write, and count, but she loved science most of all, especially trees. Kate felt the trees were her friends. She studied them in college and learned about soil, insects, plants, and how trees grow. In 1881, she became the first woman to graduate from the University of California with a science degree. After college, Kate moved to San Diego and saw that it was a dry desert town with very few trees. She worked as a teacher and vice principal for two years, then left to become a gardener. Kate searched for trees that could live in hot, dry places. She found many kinds and planted them all over San Diego.

summary_text: Catherine Olivia Sessions, called Kate, grew up in the woods of Northern California. As a girl, she gathered leaves, pine needles, and flowers to make necklaces and bracelets. In the 1860s, when many girls were expected to keep clean and not study science, Kate liked school and especially loved learning about trees, plants, wind, and rain. She felt trees were her friends and liked how they sheltered people and animals. Later, she left home to study science at the University of California. She learned with microscopes and studied how plants live, and in 1881 she became the first woman to graduate there with a science degree. After that, she moved to San Diego and worked as a teacher and vice principal. She saw that the city park was dry and full of garbage, so she left teaching to become a gardener. Kate hunted for trees that could grow in desert soil, planted them across San Diego, helped organize tree-planting parties for Balboa Park, and after the 1915 fair she earned awards and was called the mother of Balboa Park.

summary_text: After church, CJ and his Nana wait in the rain for the bus. CJ does not like the wet weather and asks why they do not have a car. Nana points out the trees, the bus, and the people around them. Mr. Dennis, the bus driver, pulls a coin from behind CJ’s ear and makes him smile. On the bus, CJ sees many people: a man with a guitar, an old woman with butterflies in a jar, and a blind man with a spotted dog. Nana greets everyone kindly and tells CJ to do the same. When the guitar player sings, everyone closes their eyes and listens. CJ feels the music and imagines bright, beautiful things. At the last stop on Market Street, CJ sees broken buildings and dirty streets. He asks why it is so dirty, and Nana shows him the rainbow and the good things around them. CJ says he is glad they came. Nana then takes him to the soup kitchen to help serve food to people who need it.

video_title: Read Aloud: Make Way For Ducklings By: Robert McCloskey
summary_text: Mr. and Mrs. Mallard flew from place to place looking for a home. Mrs. Mallard said no to many places because she was worried about foxes and turtles. When they reached Boston, they were tired and found a pond in the public garden. They stayed there and ate peanuts the people threw to them. Mrs. Mallard liked the pond and said it was a good place for a nest. But when she saw cars, bikes, and other rushing things, she said it was not safe for babies. So the Mallards flew to other places and found a quiet island near the Charles River. There they built a nest, and Mrs. Mallard laid eight eggs. The ducklings hatched, and their names were Jack, Kack, Lack, Mack, Nack, Quack, Back, and Quiet. Mr. Mallard went away for a trip, and Mrs. Mallard taught the ducklings to swim, dive, and walk in a line.

On the long drive to Cedar Tree Campground, they read comic books, play cat’s cradle, look out the window, and sing.
When they get there, Ernestine helps try to set up the tent, but it is harder than she thought.
Then Samantha and Jackie go swimming in the lake, and Ernestine stays nearby because she feels nervous about the fish.
After lunch, they go hiking, and Ernestine’s pack feels heavy, so she stops for water and eats some food to make it lighter.
Back at camp, they eat tofu hot dogs, broccoli salad, and s’mores.
At night Ernestine cannot sleep at first, but Jackie takes her to look at the stars and a shooting star.
In the morning they eat pancakes, swim again, pack up, and go home.
Ernestine says she wants to come back next year and asks her dad about s’mores.

video_title: Happy Birthday Cupcake!
summary_text: It is Cupcake’s birthday, and she wants to share it with friends. She asks Muffin to help plan a party, and they take a long walk while Cupcake thinks of ideas. First, Cupcake wants a beach party with sprinkle castles and sun play, but Muffin says the beach is very hot and some friends might get drippy. Next, Cupcake thinks of a floating boat party, but Muffin says the ship might rock and soup could lose lunch. Cupcake then suggests makeovers with frosting and sprinkles, but Muffin says some friends might think that is icky. Cupcake tries musical chills, but Muffin says someone sitting down fast could get squished. Cupcake runs out of ideas and suggests the lambo with prizes. At last, she decides to rest in her garden. When she opens the gate, all her friends are there. They dance, some get a little drippy, and Cupcake gets a little squished during limbo. Still, it becomes the best birthday party anyone can remember.
