video_title: Rosie and Meow's Amazing Secret Garden Adventure - Read Aloud Bedtime Story
summary_text: Rosie was a small girl who loved to dream about having superpowers. Every night she went to sleep with her soft toy, Foy meow. One night, a mysterious Force carried Rosie and meow away to a secret garden. Rosie woke up and saw beautiful plants and flowers all around her. Mia told Rosie that they had been chosen by The Secret Garden to help save it from pretend monsters that came at night and hurt the garden with their big footprints and swinging tails. Rosie felt unsure at first, but Mia told her she did not need special powers, only courage and faith in herself. Rosie agreed and went with Mia to find the monsters. They faced many obstacles, but Rosie stayed brave. At last, they reached the monster’s lair. Rosie held meow tightly, a bright light shone around her, and her superpowers awakened. Rosie and meow defeated the monster. When the sun rose, the garden was safe again, and Rosie learned that her true superpower was courage and faith in herself.

video_title: 🐘🦆 Kids Book Read Aloud: Pocoyo : A Little Something In Between
summary_text: Po and Pcoo played with building blocks and worked well together. They built a big castle tower, but they needed one more block to finish it. Pcoo took a block from the bottom and put it on top. Then the tower fell down. Po got angry with Pcoo, and Pcoo blamed Po. Soon both friends were angry and did not want to talk or play. They stacked blocks and built a tall wall between them. Ellie came, but when she saw how stubborn they were, she left. Po and Pcoo played alone on their own sides of the wall, but it was not fun. Pcoo found a photo and felt sad because he missed Po. Po saw the picture too, and he felt sad as well. They both cried. Then Ellie came back and pushed the wall far away. Po and Pcoo saw each other again, ran to hug, and learned that making up is better than being angry. Hooray for friends!

video_title: Pumpkin Moonshine - Read Aloud Book for Kids!
summary_text: Sylvian was visiting her grandmummy in Connecticut on Halloween. She put on her bonnet and went with Wiggy to the cornfield on the hill to find the biggest pumpkin for a pumpkin moonshine. The hill was steep, so they puffed like steam engines. In the field, Sylvie found a very large pumpkin, but she could not lift it, so she rolled it along like a snowball. When the pumpkin reached the sloping edge, it began to run away down the hill. It bumped over stones and bushes and rushed into the barnyard. The goats, hens, and geese were frightened, and the pumpkin hit Mr. Hemelscamp, who was carrying a pail of white wash. Sylvie helped him up and said sorry to the animals. Then she told Grandpop, who cut the top off the pumpkin, took out the seeds and pulp, and made a face in it. They put a candle inside and placed the pumpkin moonshine on the front gate post. Sylvie saved the seeds, planted them next spring, and many pumpkins grew.

video_title: The Tale of Two Bad Mice by Beatrix Potter
summary_text: There was a beautiful doll’s house with red bricks, white windows, curtains, a front door, and a chimney. It belonged to two dolls, Lucinda and Jane. One day, Lucinda and Jane went out in their doll’s parameulator, and the nursery became quiet. Then Tom Thumb and Hunker Monker, two mice, came out from a hole near the fireplace. They walked into the doll’s house and found a lovely dinner on the table. Tom Thumb tried to cut the ham, but it was hard. Hunker Monker tried too, but the food would not work as real food. Tom Thumb smashed the ham, and it broke into pieces because it was only plaster. The mice broke the pudding, lobsters, pears, and oranges too. They found the fish would not burn, and the tiny jars held only beads. After that, they made more mischief and carried off things from the house.

video_title: The Tale of Two Bad Mice by Beatrix Potter
summary_text: There was a beautiful doll’s house with red brick walls, white windows, muslin curtains, a front door, and a chimney. It belonged to two dolls, Lucinda and Jane. One morning they went out in their parameulator, and the nursery was empty and quiet. Then Tom Thumb and his wife, Hunker Monker, who were mice, came out from a hole near the fireplace and went into the doll’s house. They found a table set with a dinner of ham, fish, pudding, pears, and oranges. Tom Thumb tried to carve the ham, but it was hard, and Hunker Monker could not take the fish off its plate. Soon they discovered the food was only painted plaster. Angry and disappointed, they smashed the dinner and made a mess. They also found that the rice, coffee, and sego jars held only beads. After that, they took Jane’s clothes and some of Lucinda’s things, including a bolster, a cradle, a chair, a bookcase, and a bird cage. When Lucinda and Jane returned, they saw the damage. Later, Tom Thumb left a crooked sixpence in their stockings, and Hunker Monker came every morning to sweep the doll’s house.

video_title: The Tale of Benjamin Bunny by Beatrix Potter
summary_text: One morning little Benjamin Bunny heard a pony and saw Mr. McGregor and Mrs. McGregor ride past in a gig. When they were gone, Benjamin hopped to the wood behind Mr. McGregor’s garden to visit his family. There he found his cousin Peter Rabbit, who looked poorly and wore only a red cotton pocket handkerchief. Peter said Mr. McGregor had chased him in the garden and taken his clothes. Benjamin told Peter that Mr. and Mrs. McGregor were away for the day. The two rabbits went to the wall and looked into the garden. Peter climbed down a pear tree, and Benjamin followed. They found Peter’s coat and shoes on the scarecrow. Benjamin tried on the tamashanter, and they filled the pocket handkerchief with onions. They walked on, but Peter heard noises and wanted to go home. Soon they hid under a basket when a cat came and sat on top of it for five hours. At last old Mr. Benjamin Bunny came, chased the cat away, took the rabbits out, and went home with them. Peter got his clothes back, and his mother forgave him.

They are all wild and free.

video_title: 🦎 The Mixed-Up Chameleon - Animated and Read Aloud for Kids
summary_text: A small green chameleon sat on a shiny green leaf. When it moved to a brown tree, it turned brownish. On a red flower, it turned reddish. On yellow sand, it turned yellowish and was hard to see. When it was warm and had food, it turned sparkling green. When it was cold and hungry, it turned gray and dull. When the chameleon was hungry, it sat still and waited. Its eyes moved up, down, and sideways until it saw a fly. Then its long, sticky tongue shot out and caught the fly. That was its life. Then one day the chameleon saw a zoo it had never seen before. It saw many beautiful animals and wished it could be big, white, and like them. Its wish came true, but it was not happy. It wished to be like many animals. Then a fly flew by. The chameleon was hungry, but it was mixed up and could not catch it. It wished to be itself. That wish came true, and it caught the fly.

video_title: 🦍 From Head to Toe - Animated and Read Aloud for Kids
summary_text: The story says, “I can do it,” over and over. First, the speaker says, “I am a penguin,” and moves an item in the head. Then the speaker says, “I am a giraffe” and bends the neck. After that, a buffalo raises its shoulders, a monkey waves its arms, and the speaker says, “I miss you” and claps hands. Next, a gorilla thumps its chest, a cat arches its back, and a crocodile wiggles its hips. Then a camel bends its knees and a donkey kicks its legs. At the end, the speaker says, “I am I,” wiggles the toes, and says again, “I can do it.”

Then he eats eight foods cooked on a hot skillet. Next, he eats nine fruits. At the end, The Very Hungry Caterpillar and his friends eat ten favorite foods together and get ready to start the day.

The captain shouts, “10 rubber ducks overboard!” After the storm stops, the ducks bob in the sea and drift apart in different ways. One meets a dolphin, one a seal, one a polar bear, one a flamingo, one a pelican, one a turtle, one an octopus, one a seagull, and one a whale. The 10th duck floats on. The next morning, it meets a mother duck and her ducklings. At night, they swim to their nest, and the little rubber duck goes with them. The moon says, “Good Night!” and the duck says, “Squeak!”

The anteater asked, “Why are you so boring?” The sloth did not answer. It said it was not lazy. Then the sloth yawned and said it liked to do things slowly, slowly, slowly.

video_title: 🌰🌱🌻The Tiny Seed by Eric Carle | Animated Read Aloud for Kids | A Beautiful Nature Story!
summary_text: In autumn, a strong wind blows flower seeds high into the air and carries them far away. One tiny seed goes with the others. Some seeds fly too high and burn in the sun. One lands on a cold mountain and cannot grow. One falls into the ocean and drowns. One lands in a hot desert and cannot grow there either. A bird eats one seed, and a mouse eats another in winter. The tiny seed is too small to be seen, so it is safe. When spring comes, snow melts, birds fly, the sun shines, and rain falls. The seeds begin to grow roots, stems, and leaves. Some plants are hurt by weeds and children, and one flower is picked. The tiny plant keeps growing all summer until it becomes a giant flower. Birds, bees, and butterflies visit it. In autumn again, the wind shakes the flower, and many tiny seeds fly out to begin the story again.

summary_text: Mr and Mrs Seahorse drifted gently through the sea. Mrs Seahorse wiggled and twisted and said it was time to lay her eggs. Mr Seahorse helped, and Mrs Seahorse laid the eggs into a pouch on Mr Seahorse’s belly. Mr Seahorse said he would take good care of them. As he drifted on, he saw other fish hiding in the sea, like trumpet fish, lionfish, leaf fish, and stonefish. Then he met Mr Stickleback, Mr Tilapia, Mr Kurtus, and Mr Bullhead. Each fish had eggs or babies to care for. Mr Stickleback had built a nest. Mr Tilapia had eggs in his mouth. Mr Kurtus had eggs on his head. Mr Bullhead was babysitting after the eggs hatched. Mr Seahorse kept swimming and heard how they cared for their eggs. At last, it was time for the seahorse babies to be born. Mr Seahorse wiggled and twisted again, and the babies tumbled out of his pouch and swam away. One baby tried to go back, but Mr Seahorse said the babies were ready to be on their own.

It fit him well, but it looked plain. In March, he met a small sea anemone and asked it to live on his shell, and it agreed. In April, he found a little sea star and put it on his house. In May, a crusty coral came to live on the shell too. In June, a snail helped clean the house. In July, a sea urchin came to protect it. In August, they all went into dark seaweed and could not see well. In September, a lanternfish came to light the way. In October, Hermit Crab added smooth pebbles around his shell. In November, his shell felt small again, and he missed his friends. In December, a smaller hermit crab moved into the shell. The next January, Hermit Crab left and found another big shell to fill with new friends.

video_title: 🌙 Papa, Please Get the Moon for Me | Animated Story Read Aloud for Kids | MovingStories
summary_text: One night, Monica looked out her window and saw the moon. It looked very close, and Monica wanted to play with it. She stretched her arms, but she could not reach it. Monica asked Papa to get the moon for her. Papa took a very long ladder and carried it to a very high mountain. He put the ladder on the mountain and climbed up and up until he reached the moon. Papa told the moon that Monica wanted to play with it. The moon said it got a little smaller every night. When it was just the right size, Papa could take it. The moon became smaller and smaller, and Papa brought it down to Monica. Monica jumped and danced with the moon. She hugged it and threw it in the air. Then the moon got smaller and smaller until it disappeared. Later, Monica saw a thin moon again, and each night it grew bigger.

video_title: George and the snowman
summary_text: One winter morning, George rode through the forest in his yellow truck to look for fire sticks for the cabin stove. He saw Mr. Snowman and asked if everything was all right. Mr. Snowman said he was worried about the birds because the snow covered everything and they could not dig for worms. George said he had an idea and hurried home. In the kitchen, he baked seed cookies for the birds from mashed bananas and sesame seeds. His mom asked what he was doing, and George said the birds would love them. Then he loaded the warm cookies into his trailer and drove back to the snowman. Mr. Snowman thanked him and said George had a heart full of kindness. George laughed and said the birds had tummies full of seeds. The next morning, George saw that the snow was gone and the birds could find food again. After that, whenever it snowed, George brought seed cookies so the birds never went hungry.

video_title: All The Ways To Be Smart by Davina Bell, a read aloud read along story for kids by Tippy Toes Nook
summary_text: The story says that smart means many different things. A child can be smart at drawing witch's hats, gluing wings on bats, telling rhyme, and knowing time. Children can be smart when they build cubbies, make slime, paint patterns, wheel wagons, and build boats from boxes. They can also be smart when they pretend to be mermaids or ride dragons. The story says smart is not only about tests or knowing all the answers. Smart can be kindness when someone is crying, sharing, caring, and being sorry when you are naughty. It can be saying hi and bye when people feel shy, picking what to wear, and asking questions. Smart is also counting, matching shapes, reading, writing, spelling, and telling stories. In the end, the story says everyone is smart in their own special way, and no one does the very same smart things as you.

video_title: Wombat Stew by Marcia K Vaughn - a read aloud read along story by Tippy Toes Nook
summary_text: A very clever dingo sat by a billabong and decided to make wombat stew. He put a billy on the fire and said he needed the fat wombat for his stew. Platypus came by first and said mud would be good in a stew, so dingo let him tip in big blobs of mud. Then emu came and said feathers would help, so dingo dropped in feathers. Blue-tongue lizard came next and said flies were good, so he caught many flies and added them too. Echidna arrived and said a stew needed slugs, bugs, and creepy crawlies, so he put those in as well. Koala came down from the gum tree and said nuts would be nice, so he added nuts. At last dingo said only the wombat was missing. When he bent down to taste the stew, he found it was bad and rushed away into the bush. The others had tricked him, and the wombat was safe.

video_title: Be Brave, Little Penguin by Giles Andreae  (a read aloud - read along kids video by Tippy Toes Nook)
summary_text: In the cold Antarctic sunshine, a family of penguins lived with their friends. Little penguin Pip Pip was the smallest one. While the other penguins swam in the ocean, Pip Pip stayed away because he was afraid of the sea. He felt sad and lonely. His daddy asked what was wrong, and his mummy held his hand. She told him to try the water slowly and to trust her. Pip Pip worried the water would be freezing, dark, and deep, and he feared monsters. His mummy kissed him and said he might find friends, light, warm water, and fish. Pip Pip went to the edge, closed his eyes, held his breath, and jumped. At first his mummy could not see him and was scared. Then she heard him call, “Mommy, mommy! Look! I’m swimming!” Pip Pip swam happily, jumped up from the water, and then landed with a bump. His friends came around him, and he said that sometimes all you have to do is be brave and jump.

video_title: The Detective Dog by Julia Donaldson - a read aloud and read along kids video by Tippy Toes Nook
summary_text: Detective Dog had a very good nose. She lived with Peter, a six-year-old boy who often lost his clothes and toys. Detective Dog sniffed out Peter’s missing things, like the bus in the bowl, the book in the bed, the sock in the sofa, the shoe in the shed, the Teddy, and the ball. Every Monday, she went with Peter to school. There she smelled children reading books about dinosaurs, knights, planets, frogs, dragons, and dogs. One Monday, Detective Dog smelled a wrong smell in the classroom. Mr Jones looked worried, Peter cried, and the books were gone. Detective Dog found a cap on the shelf, then followed the smell of the thief through the town, past the traffic lights, the farm, the zoo, and the takeaway shop, and on into the woods. She found a man with a sack full of books. He said his name was Ted and that he had only meant to borrow them. Peter took Ted to the library, where Ted got a library card and could borrow books for free. After that, Ted read books in his backyard, and Detective Dog kept visiting the school on Mondays.

video_title: 📚 Kids Book- Read-Aloud  📚 The Night Before Kindergarten 🧸 By Natasha Wing. Art by Julie Durrell.
summary_text: The night before kindergarten, the children were excited and a little scared. They packed erasers, crayons, pencils, and backpacks, and they set out their clothes for the morning. When school day came, they washed their faces, brushed their teeth, and posed for pictures. Their parents packed snacks and drove them to school, and some children brought blankets or stuffed bears. The parents worried the children might cry, so they offered to stay a little longer. At school, the teacher, Miss Sunrise, welcomed everyone with a smile. The room had toys, books, and maps, but no beds for naps. The children colored, painted, played Simon Says, tumbled, skipped, stood on their heads, and sang silly songs. Soon, each child had a friend. Then the parents came to say goodbye, and many were sad and crying. Miss Sunrise gave them one last hug and sent them away. At the door, the children waved and said, “Don’t cry Mom and Dad kindergarten is cool.”

The animals pushed Hippo toward the river, and his tooth popped out. The animals helped him stand up. Hippo said thank you, but now his head hurt.

video_title: 📚 Kids Read-Aloud Book 📚 Monty The Manatee By Natalie Pritchard. Pictures by Natalie Merheb.
summary_text: Monty the manate was shy on his first day at Sea school near the ocean’s Gates. He waved goodbye to his mommy and slowly paddled to school. Monty tried to make friends with the jellyfish in the sea grass, but they told him to leave them alone. He met Sydney the shrimp, who shouted at him, and Monty said sorry. At lunch, Monty offered food to Sammy Seal, but Sammy said he liked fast and cool creatures and did not want to play. Then other fish laughed at Monty and said mean things about manatees. Suddenly, a big shark came racing toward them with open jaws. Monty stayed very still like a rock, just as his mommy taught him, and tucked the others under his tummy. The shark swam away, and the other sea creatures cheered for Monty. They said sorry for being mean, and Monty said they should all be friends and stop the bullying. From then on, they played nicely, and Monty shared a message about being kind and seeing what is on the inside.

summary_text: The child goes many places and keeps doing small things that are not allowed. Each time, an adult stops the child and asks, “What if everybody did that?”

In his den in the Dell, he thought he heard, “Drive a Jeep!” So Big Bear drove a Jeep south of town. After that, Old Man Winter whispered again, but Big Bear thought he heard, “Sweep Big Bear sweep.” Big Bear swept a house room by room. Then he heard, “Leap Big Bear leap,” and he played leapfrog with a frog. Next, he heard, “Dive deep Big Bear dive deep,” so he dove into Clear Blue Lake and swam to shore, very tired. Finally, he heard, “Climb a mountain steep Big Bear steep,” and he trudged to the mountaintop. At last Old Man Winter told him it was winter time and he should go to bed. Big Bear went back to his cozy den, put on his PJs, blew out the light, and said, “good night.”

video_title: 📚Kids Read-Aloud Book📚 Goodnight, Goodnight, Construction Site By Sherri D Rinker & Tom Lichtenheld
summary_text: At the big construction site, the tough trucks work all day to build a building and make a road. When the sun goes down, it is time to stop. Crane truck lifts one last beam, swings it into place, folds in his boom, and gets ready for bed. Cement mixer spins all day, pours his last load, pulls up his chute, turns off his light, and stops his engine. Dump truck carries dirt, dumps one final load, lowers his bed, locks his gate, and rests his wheels. Bulldozer pushes the ground flat, turns off his engine, stops his tracks, and curls into his dirt bed. Excavator scoops dirt and sand, digs a few more holes, pulls up his boom, sets down his scoop, and snuggles in. Then all the trucks are tucked in tight, and the day is done.

When it is time for washing, he does not want soap, water, brushes, or combs. Mom blocks the bathroom door, but the tiger ducks and runs past her very fast. Next, he eats a big breakfast of Tiger Flakes and blood orange juice, which makes him ready for more adventures. In the forest, he hides in a place that turns out to be a trap, and it snaps shut around him. He calls for help and struggles, but tiger mom rescues him by pulling him free. Later, he goes into the snow, plays happily, and then returns inside to find a tiger cake. After frightening Dad, he is sent to his room, where he builds a safe hideaway and later joins his tiger family for crafts and cuddles before falling asleep.

video_title: 📚 Kids Read-Aloud Book 📚 Sticks By Diane Alber.
summary_text: On a very hot summer day, a popsicle melted fast and became a sad, sticky stick in a puddle. The stick cried and wondered where he belonged. Then Twig, a stick made of wood from a tall tree, talked to him and said he had once been part of a tree too. Twig and another friend, Brush, showed the stick that they had also started as plain sticks before they found new things to do. Twig drew a line, and Brush painted with red, yellow, and blue. Still, the stick felt upset and said he could only melt. Twig took him back to the puddle where he first changed, and there she saw a tiny stick house in the tree. A blue bird flew down, lifted the stick, and placed him in the last open space. The stick found his new place, made tree art, and learned he could have a fresh start.

video_title: 📚 Kids Read-Aloud Book 📚 Highlighters On Strike. By Jennifer Jones.
summary_text: The highlighters say they are bright and colorful and help make school pages easy to see. They add yellow ink to black and white words so important things stand out. But the students do not treat them gently. The students press them hard, push them into desks, bend and snap them, chew the ends, and often lose the caps. The highlighters also get tossed around in bins and scratched by pencils. Because of this rough treatment, their ink dries out and they stop working well. One day during recess, the highlighters choose the brightest one and write a note in big yellow letters. The note says they are tired of being treated like junk and that the highlighters are going on strike. When the students return from outdoor play, they find the note and read it quietly. They gather together and write back to say they are sorry and will treat the highlighters carefully. The highlighters agree to give them another chance, but say they will strike again if the mistreatment happens again.

video_title: 📚 Kids Read-Aloud Book 📚 Hey, That's My Monster! Kids Favourite Monster Story
summary_text: One night, a child looked under the bed for his monster, Gabe, and found a note saying Gabe had gone to help someone else. The child learned that his little sister Emma needed a monster because she kept climbing out of her toddler bed at night. He went to Emma's room to get Gabe back, but Gabe gave him three chances to make Emma fall asleep. Emma came in, and the child tried three different monsters. First came Agatha, a slime-covered monster, but Emma laughed and wiped her nose. Next came Cynthia, who had claws, but Emma decorated her tail with bracelets. Last came Vladimir with tentacles, but Emma played with him too. Then Gabe came back. He growled and told Emma to get into bed, and she finally stayed there. Gabe said he would stay with Emma, so the child went back to his own room, where he found out that Gabe's little sister Stella had brought Gabe a snack. Stella's hiccups and toe-tickling scared Emma, so Stella became Emma's monster. The child happily returned to bed with Gabe back under his bed, and everyone was ready to sleep.

video_title: 📚 The Power Of Kindness - Kid's Read-Aloud Book 📚 Kindness Is My Superpower by Alicia Ortega.
summary_text: A boy has a favorite toy named Teddy. One day he is in a bad mood and teases his friend Lisa for wearing glasses. Lisa cries at school. When he gets home, his mom tells him that hurting people’s feelings is wrong and that he should be kind. The boy asks what kindness means, and his mom explains that kindness can be using gentle words, helping others, respecting older and younger people, and doing good deeds. The boy thinks about her words all night and decides to be kind in the morning. At breakfast, he thanks his mom, makes his bed, puts away his toys, and behaves well on the bus. At school, he welcomes a new boy, helps him find his classroom, greets his friends, and shares his crayons and pens. He then says sorry to Lisa, and she smiles and forgives him. After school, he waits his turn, helps find a lost ball, picks up rubbish, opens doors, helps an old lady cross the street, covers his sleeping dad with a blanket, helps his sister tie her shoelace, and waters his neighbor’s flowers.

summary_text: One night, a child reached under the bed for a truck and found a note from Mr. Z saying monsters were meeting there for a final test. At first, the child thought it was a trick from the parents, but then voices and five pairs of eyes appeared under the bed. A yellow teacher monster named Mr. Z led four smaller monsters. He tested them on rules for scaring a child and keeping the child in bed. Jenus tried to roar but made a tiny noise, so he was sent away. Morgan tried shadow puppets, but they made the child sneeze, so she was sent away too. Gabe then made a huge scary shadow, which got the child back into bed, but the child got up again to look for food. Abigail tried to catch the child in the kitchen, but she failed. Later, Gabe grew huge after eating people food, scared the child, and stayed with the child until sleep came.

But the mom smiled and said it was not a mess. The scribbles had moved onto the easel and made a glowing masterpiece.

video_title: 📚 Kid's Read-Aloud Book 📚 Angry Ninja  By Mary Nhin.
summary_text: One day, the little sister used the jump rope without asking, and the child got very angry. The child felt a tight throat, a fast heart, and heavy breathing, and then exploded with anger. Later, Positive Ninja came over, and they played pig. When the child started losing, the child got upset again. Positive Ninja said anger is normal, but the way you handle it matters. Positive Ninja showed the 1 + 3 + 10 strategy. First, say one word like “relax” or “breathe.” Then take three slow, deep breaths. Last, count to 10. Positive Ninja also said to use an “I am” statement, like “I’m mad at you for breaking my toy.” After that, the child went inside for chocolate cake and found that the sister had eaten the last slice. The child felt angry again, but remembered the strategy. The child said “Breathe,” took three deep breaths, counted to 10, and said, “I’m upset that there’s no more chocolate cake.” It worked.

summary_text: The dinos love donuts. They dip them in jelly, add sprinkles, and eat the glazed and cake-crumb ones. Their dancing makes the palm trees shake, their footprints make pools, and dust floats like wigs around their heads. The dinos wait in line for donuts because they need a lot of food. A child makes a giant donut for the dino dance. The dinos love it, but they do not like the center hole, because they fear rocks. video_title: Virtual Storytime Parker Looks Up
summary_text: Parker Curry loved to dance in her tutu and dreamed of being a Dancing Queen. On a rainy Tuesday, she did not go to dance class. Instead, her mother took Parker, her sister Ava, and her best friend Gia to the museum. They put on boots and jackets and went inside, splashing and smiling. In the museum hall, the girls saw many paintings, including prancing horses, blooming flowers, a necklace, peacocks, fish, and many feathers. Then Gia ran to a playroom, and Parker followed her. The girls played with purple hair, a pirate hat, and sunglasses. When it was time to go home, Parker saw a row of frilly white tutus and began dancing after Gia. Then she stopped at a portrait of Michelle Obama. She looked at the painting and listened to her mother describe Michelle Obama as a mother, lawyer, writer, and hero. Parker felt strong and hopeful, and she shared the moment with Ava.

He goes faster down the slope, with his scarf flying behind him. Bunny jumps over one hole, but then he falls into another hole. Inside the hole is Bunny’s house. His mom is there with hot chocolate. After a long day on the slopes, Bunny warms up with hot cocoa.

Then he brushed his teeth, and the hiccups were so strong that his jaw came off. After that, he polished his bones and carved a pumpkin, but he kept hiccuping while he worked. He also tried cutting his cooking and raking leaves. Later, Foreign played with a ghost. They were playing catch, and it was also like baseball. Because the hiccups would not stop, Foreign missed the ball. The story ends with the ghost speaking to the skeleton.

video_title: Virtual Storytime: 'Antiracist Baby'
summary_text: Anti-racist baby is taught to help make society fair. The story says babies can be taught to be racist or anti-racist, and there is no middle way. It gives nine steps. First, children open their eyes and notice all skin colors. Second, they use their words to talk about race, because silence does not stop racism. Third, they point to unfair policies instead of blaming people. Fourth, they say there is nothing wrong with people, even when people are treated differently. Fifth, they celebrate all differences. Sixth, they knock down the stack of cultural blocks and welcome each group’s own ways of speaking, dancing, and creating. Seventh, they confess when they say racist things and learn from mistakes. The story also says anti-racist babies keep learning and growing. In the end, they believe racism can be overcome and they do not judge a book by its cover.

When they get off the train, Julian asks if abuela saw the mermaids.
Abuela says she did.
Julian then says, “I am also a mermaid.” At home, he gets ready to make a mermaid look.
He uses a plant for a headdress and curtains for a mermaid tail.
When abuela gets out of the shower, Julian feels scared because she looks unhappy.
But abuela calls him over and gives him a necklace to go with his outfit.
Then she takes him outside and says, “You’ll see.” Julian whispers, “Mermaids,” and abuela answers, “Like you, mijo.” Then they join the mermaids together.

summary_text: The child tells us about eyes that look different from other eyes. When Mama comes home from work, her eyes crinkle into crescent moons, and she scoops the child up, tickles them, and makes them laugh. At bedtime, Mama tucks the child in and looks at them like they are a miracle. The child also says Amma’s eyes are like this too, even though Amma is older and her eyes do not work the same way they used to. Amma can still see into the child’s heart and read their mind. The child sees stories in Amma’s eyes. The story also mentions little sister waiting for big sister to come home from school. In the end, the child says these family eyes are beautiful and belong to Mama, Amma, and the child.

video_title: Virtual Storytime: Baby Danced the Polka
summary_text: It was nap time on the farm. The cows, goats, pigs, and sheep were sleepy. Baby closed his eyes in bed. Mama told baby to stay in bed while she and papa did chores. But baby got up and danced the polka with a polka dotted pig. He laughed and said, “Whoa, papa's whiskers! Whoa, mama's wig! Go!” Mama and papa told baby again that it was nap time. But baby did not stay in bed. He boogie woogied with a frisky little goat, then chance the cha-cha with a chocolate colored cow. Each time, mama and papa asked baby to listen and rest. Then baby danced with a shaggy little sheep. Mama said she gave up, and papa said baby was not sleepy. At last, mama said to get the fiddles, and they had a big pokefest in Arkansas. They danced until night came. Papa got tired. Then mama and papa kissed baby and put him to bed, with dance dreams in his head.

Smoke fills the air, and they hurry to Luigi’s. There, the team gets out hoses, ladders, and water. One firefighter hooks the hoses to the fire hydrant, and others carry the hoses and ladder. Inside, they find a baby and bring the baby back to the family. After the fire is out, Luigi’s food truck makes dinner for the firefighters. The story ends with a reminder to get low and go if there is a fire.

video_title: Virtual Storytime - Dave the Potter: Artist, Poet, Slave by Laban Carrick Hill
summary_text: Dave lived about 200 years ago and was a slave. He worked with clay, which came from dirt mixed with water from the river. He carried heavy clay to his spinning potter’s wheel and threw as much as 60 pounds at a time. He kicked the wheel fast and shaped the wet clay with his hands and thumbs. Leonardo tried many scary faces, but they did not work. One day, he had an idea. He wanted to find the most scaredy cat kid in the whole world and scare him. Leonardo looked around and found Sam. He snuck up on Sam and made a loud monster roar. Sam cried, and Leonardo thought he had finally scared someone. But Sam said Leonardo did not scare him. Sam was crying because his big brother took his action figure, broke it, and hurt his toe and tummy. Leonardo listened and then made a big change. He became a wonderful friend and gave Sam a hug. He told Sam it was okay. After that, Leonardo and Sam had fun together.

video_title: All Ages Virtual Storytime: Alma and How She Got Her Name
summary_text: Alma has a very long name: Alma, Sofia, Esperanza, Jose, Pura, Canela. She tries to write it on paper, but it does not fit. Alma tells her daddy that her name is too long. Daddy asks her to come close so he can tell her the story of her name. He starts with Sofia, Alma’s grandmother, who loved books, poetry, jasmine flowers, and Daddy, and who taught him how to read. Then he tells about Esperanza, Alma’s great-grandmother, who hoped to travel and followed her sailor son in her heart. Next he speaks about Jose, Alma’s grandfather, an artist who painted everyday life and taught Daddy to see and love their people. He also tells about a family tradition with a red string for protection. Then he tells about Candela, another grandmother, who stood up for what was right. At the end, Daddy says he chose the name Alma just for her. Alma says it fits her just right and that she is Alma with a story to tell.

video_title: Virtual Bilingual Storytime w/ Ms. Claudeth: ¿Debo compartir mi helado/Should I Share My Ice Cream?
summary_text: The child shows little hands and makes them dance. One hand comes out, dances, closes, and goes away. Then the other hand does the same. Then both little hands come out together and dance. After that, they close and go away again. Next, the child has a cold ice cream on a hot day and is very happy. The child sees Piggy, the best friend, and thinks about sharing the ice cream. The child worries that Piggy may not like the flavor and thinks about eating it alone. Then the child looks for Piggy and decides to share, so Piggy can be happy too. But before the child can share, the ice cream melts. The child cannot give Piggy any ice cream now. Piggy then asks for some ice cream, and the child says thank you, that would make me happy. The story ends with sharing happening in a different way than planned.

video_title: Virtual Bilingual Storytime: Please, Mr. Panda / Por favor, Sr. Panda
summary_text: Mr. Panda has many donuts. He walks around and asks, “Would you like a donut?” He offers donuts to many animals and people, like the blue one, the yellow one, the pink one, and the blue and yellow ones. At first, most of them say no, or they want a different donut, or they change their minds. Mr. Panda keeps asking, “Do you want a donut?” and many times he says he will not give one, then says, “I regretted it.” Later, one friend says, “Please, Mr. Panda,” and asks kindly for a donut. Mr. Panda gives out the donuts, and the friend says thank you. In the end, the donuts are shared, and Mr. Panda says goodbye.

video_title: Baby & Me Storytime: Giving Thanks!
summary_text: Ten fat turkeys sit on a fence. One by one, they do silly things and fall off. One turkey swings from a vine, one tries to roller skate, one flaps away, and one balances bricks. Then another turkey does a swan dive, another rides on a board, and another swallows a bee. After that, one turkey whistles in a shoe, one blows bubble gum, and the last plump turkey jumps up and down. Each time, the count gets smaller: nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one, and then none. The fence breaks with a crash. At the end, the turkeys are in a tree instead, and they say they found a new place to be.

video_title: Virtual Family Storytime with Ms Cindi: 'Twas The Night Before Thanksgiving
summary_text: On the day before Thanksgiving, eight children rode a school bus on a field trip through the fall leaves. They saw a tiny farm and met Farmer Mac Nugget, who wore denim and called to his turkeys by name. The turkeys ran, flapped, and greeted the children. Then one child saw an axe by the door and asked about it. Farmer Nugget said the turkeys might be chopped up and roasted for Thanksgiving. The children became upset and cried. Farmer Nugget and the teacher went to the well and brought back water for everyone. After the children drank, they felt calmer and were mysteriously fatter. They thanked Farmer Nugget and left on the bus, huffing because they felt stuffed. When the bus drove away, no turkeys were left on the farm. The next evening, eight families had eight fluffy turkeys as guests, and everyone ate vegetables, jelly, and toast. They gave thanks for love and living and had a happy Thanksgiving.

After the warm-up song, the story starts a silly dance contest for a story time dance party. The leader tells everyone to dance in silly ways and then freeze when the music stops. In the middle, the dancers move fast, move slow, jump up and down, and make silly faces. They also dance with a partner and stop when the leader says different words like food, free, breathe, eyes, and freeze. At the end, everyone stretches their arms up high and then goes all the way down when the music gets lower. The story ends with praise for the dancers and their sweet moves.

summary_text: Goldilocks was a little girl who went into the forest to play and pick flowers. She saw a pretty little house and walked inside because she was thirsty and wanted water. In the kitchen, she found three bowls of soup. The first soup was too hot, the second soup was too cold, and the third soup was just right. Then she felt tired and sat in three chairs. The first two chairs were too big, and the last chair was just right, but it broke. Goldilocks went upstairs and tried three beds. The first bed was too hard, the second bed was too soft, and the third bed was just right. She fell asleep in that bed. Then the three bears came home. They saw that someone had eaten their soup, sat in their chair, and slept in their bed. Goldilocks woke up, saw the bears, ran down the stairs, and hurried back into the forest.

video_title: Preschool & Toddler Storytime with Ms. Kris: Bear Snores On
summary_text: In a cave in the woods, a great brown bear sleeps through the long cold winter. He snores in his deep dark lair while the snow falls outside. A mouse creeps into the cave and makes a small fire. The mouse and the bear do not wake up. Then a badger comes in, and they share honey nuts. More friends come too, like a wren, a raven, and a mole. They all go into the bear’s den, make food, and talk and chatter. The bear keeps sleeping through all the noise. At last, the fire stirs the bear awake. He grumbles because everyone had fun while he slept. The friends share more corn and tea with him. Bear eats and drinks, and then he tells tall tales through the night. When the sun comes up, the bear cannot sleep, but his friends snore.

She tells him to stop the drama and be patient, and she says she loves him. She gives him two kisses, and Llama Llama snuggles into his soft pillows.

video_title: Preschool & Toddler Storytime with Ms. Kris: Froggy Gets Dressed
summary_text: It was cold, and Froggy woke up to see snow outside. He wanted to play in the snow, but his mother told him frogs should sleep all winter and wake up when the snow melted. Froggy said he was awake and wanted to go out. His mother told him to look down because he had forgotten something to wear. Froggy took off his hat and boots, then put them back on and went outside. Soon his mother told him to look down again. Froggy saw he had forgotten his shirt, so he went back inside. Then he took off his mittens, untied his scarf, and took off his hat, but he kept on his pants, boots, and socks. He put on his shirt and went out again. His mother asked if he forgot anything else. Froggy had on a scarf, coat, shirt, pants, boots, and socks, but he was missing his underwear. Froggy went back inside, took off some clothes, got too tired, and went back to sleep.

video_title: Babystorytime & Lapsit with Ms. Lolly: Clifford's Family
summary_text: Emily Elizabeth and Clifford lived in a small town, but they were born in the big city. One day they went back to visit the city and see Clifford’s family. They found Clifford’s mother first. She had not seen him since he was a tiny puppy, so she checked his teeth and looked at his ears. Then they learned where Clifford’s brothers and sisters lived. Clifford’s sister Claudia lived nearby. She walked with her blind owner, and Clifford saw that Claudia helped her. At the park, a taxi blocked the crosswalk, and Clifford moved it out of the way. Next they found Clifford’s brother Nero at the fire station. The alarm rang, and Nero ran into the building while Clifford helped. Then they visited Bonnie on a farm. Bonnie herded sheep, and Clifford helped with the cows. A bull was there, but Clifford jumped away safely. Finally, they visited Clifford’s father, who lived with many children and seemed very happy. Clifford wished they could all live together, but they had people who needed them.

summary_text: In India, on a big river island, a boy loved trees. He saw that the floods were taking away the land and leaving sandbars. Animals lost their homes, and the boy worried that people and animals would be in danger. He told the village, and the elders gave him 20 bamboo saplings. The boy went by canoe to a sandbar and planted them one by one. Every day he brought water, carried buckets, and cared for the young plants. He worked hard until the bamboo grew into a thick patch. Then he brought cow dung, earthworms, termites, ants, and seeds from other villages to make the soil better. He kept planting as he grew up. Soon the small patch became a big forest. Buffalo, rhinos, snakes, gibbons, birds, and elephants came back. The man kept planting more grass and fruit trees, and he protected the forest so it could stay alive.

summary_text: In India, on a big river island, a boy loved trees because they gave shade, food, and shelter. Every rainy season, floodwaters washed away more land, and the island became smaller. The boy saw animals left on sandbars with no homes, and he worried that animals and people would suffer without trees. He told the village, and the elders gave him 20 bamboo saplings. He took them by canoe to a sandy sandbar and planted them one by one. Each day he carried water from the river, built a watering system, and kept caring for the plants even when he was tired and sore. The bamboo grew into a thick patch. The boy then brought cow dung, earthworms, termites, ants, and seeds from other villages to make richer soil. Over many years, the bamboo patch grew into a large forest, and wildlife returned. Later, the man kept planting, protecting, and pruning the forest, which became known as Malai.

summary_text: Late late at night, Mouse heard strange sounds in her house: a sigh, a scratch, a scrape, and an odd little cry. She searched the closet, behind the door, the cupboard, the drawer, and under the chair. Mouse thought it must be a ghost and asked, “Who’s there?” The next day she told her friends. Ren said to set a trap, Spider offered to spin a web, Bunny brought peas to spread on the floor, and Mole said to turn out the lights. Goat said it would not work. That night Mouse tried the plan, but she slipped on a pea and fell into the web herself. The next day Goat said the best way to catch a ghost was cheese. Mouse put cheese on the table, behind the door, and under the chair, then hid in the closet. She heard nibbling and switched on the light. A skinny young mouse was there. He asked to stay, and Mouse let him stay after a bath. His name was Malachi Gim crack, but she called him Mac. The story ends with Mouse and Mac sharing a party and cheese.

summary_text: Little Craig loved birthday parties, but he did not get invited to many. One day, Joey, the new kid at school, gave Craig a bright blue invitation to his party. Craig was very happy and told Joey he would be there. At home, Mom put Joey’s party on the family calendar. The next day, Craig got another invitation from his friend Dan. He thought he could go to both parties, but Mom showed him that both parties were at the same time on the same day. Craig first wanted to choose Dan’s party, then he wrote a letter to Joey saying he could not come. Mom asked him to think about how Joey would feel. Craig also thought about going to both parties for a short time, but Mom helped him see that would not be fair either. In the end, Craig kept his word and went to Joey’s party. He ate cake, played games, won a prize, and made a new friend. Mom was proud of him.

The parent loved every part of the baby, from the hands and feet to the cheeks, nose, and toes. The baby smiled, and the parent stayed near through laughter and cries. The parent comforted the child and helped when the child was afraid. Then the child learned to walk, said Mama and Dad, and began to talk. The child laughed at the park, clapped at a barking dog, and loved to bang pots. The parent rocked the child to sleep, saved a first curl, and watched the child play, grow, and sleep, loving the child forever.

summary_text: Having a dinosaur is hard work. Dino poo is messy in the backyard, and diapers are stinky. So the grown-up asks, “How do you potty train a dinosaur?” First, they find a potty just the right size. Then they teach the dinosaur when it is time to go, and sometimes they set the dinosaur on the potty again and again. Next, they teach the dinosaur to wipe, even though the dinosaur has tiny arms. The dinosaur also learns to flush and wash its clothes. Sometimes the dinosaur does not want to stop playing, so the grown-up reminds it that the toys will still be there later. When the dinosaur goes potty well, it gets a reward and hears, “Good job.” There may still be accidents, but the grown-up is patient. In the end, the dinosaur gets the hang of it.

Polly follows the bus, and the children get off to begin kindergarten adventures.

summary_text: A child and Nana work in the garden through spring, summer, and fall. Up in the garden, they wait for the snow to melt, because it is not quite time to plant. Down in the dirt, worms, insects, and other small creatures are already busy. The child helps snap stalks, pull weeds, and spread compost. Then it is time to plant seeds, and Nana tells the child to give them water and pat them down. As the days grow warm, carrots and peas grow, bees visit flowers, and the child weeds in the hot sun. Rain falls, and Nana sprays the child with the hose. Later, they pick tomatoes, beans, cucumbers, and zucchini. Bats, skunks, spiders, snakes, and other animals work in the garden and dirt. summary_text: Louise was a cat who lived near a fire station and liked to visit around town. One night, after too much catnip and sardines, he saw Tabitha through a thick glass door. Louise and Tabitha looked at each other, but Tabitha’s owner kept saying, “Shoo, Louise! Shed!” The next day Louise brought Tabitha a bouquet of sardine tins, pine, and feathers. Then he brought mice, pigeons, and even balloons. He kept trying, but the owner always chased him away. Louise asked his friends for advice. They said he was an outside cat and Tabitha was an inside cat. Louise made a plan and went to Tabitha’s door again. This time the owner opened the door, and Louise went inside with Tabitha. Soon a doorbell rang, and Louise had to leave again because they looked alike. Later, when Louise was riding in the fire truck, he saw Tabitha in danger. He rescued her, and both cats were rewarded and stayed together inside.

summary_text: The Wi-Fi goes down, and Mommy howls, Daddy bellows, and Nana smirks. The child has many ideas and wants to do things, but the Wi-Fi is no use, so the family whines. Popo cooks lucky foods like a whole chicken, fish with the head and tail on, and long noodles.
The family hangs red decorations, an upside-down sign for luck, and wears new red clothes.
Po also avoids unlucky things like the number four, bad words, and sleeping on New Year’s Day.
On New Year’s Day, she greets family, helps with offerings, gives oranges, and receives lucky red envelopes called lcy.
The story ends with Po happy but tired after a busy day of following the lucky customs.

summary_text: Kora loved the smells and tastes of Mama’s Filipino dishes, and she wanted to be a real cook. Kora felt proud and thanked Mama.

summary_text: Anil loved hearing stories about a far away village with green wheat fields and coconut palms. One day he asked who was telling the story, and his grandfather, D, began to speak. Anil and D went outside to find more adventures.

summary_text: William Wilberforce saw people from Africa being taken as slaves. He knew this was wrong. He told many people about the bad slave ships in 1807. After hearing him, the leaders of Great Britain agreed that the slave trade should end. Harriet Tubman did not like being told what to do, and she had to follow rules because of her dark skin. In 1849 she ran North to Freedom. She helped other people escape too. Her secret path was called the Underground Railroad. Abraham Lincoln saw many people working as slaves in America. In 1863 he became president and signed a paper saying all the slaves would be free. Susan B. Anthony wanted girls to vote too. She tried to vote and got arrested. She kept speaking for fairness, and in 1920 women in America got the right to vote.

Later, Mom told Craig that some people treat others badly because of skin color, and that is called racism. She also told him to feel good about himself. Craig felt better, ate ice cream, and took one more ride on his bike.

Then he brought balloons, which was hard for a cat to do. Every day, Louise and Tabitha kept staring at each other until Sho chased Louise away. After that, Louise asked his friends for advice over a bowl of cream.

summary_text: Leo was a busy boy with too many things to do. He thought making a list might help, but the list kept getting longer. Leo wished there were two of him. Then a knock came at the door, and another Leo appeared. This second Leo took the list and said they could finish it together. Soon a third Leo came, and then more Leos kept joining. They made a team of four, then five, then six. After talking for a long time, they decided they needed a seventh Leo. With seven Leos, there was even more work. Leo said they would need eight just to rest a little. Eight Leos worked very fast, but then they thought maybe nine or even ten Leos would help. All the Leos kept working. One Leo shouted that there was no time to stop or rest. Finally, Leo became tired and went to sleep. When he woke up, the other Leos asked what he had done. Leo said he had been dreaming. Dreaming was not on the list, so the other Leos disappeared. Leo then thought about doing less but doing his best, and he decided one Leo was enough.

summary_text: There was a boy who had no toys. Every day he went to the park and sat under a big tree while other children played. Sometimes they let him join, and sometimes they did not, so he felt sad. One day he found an unusual stick leaning against the tree. Use it well, and you can be anything you want to be." The boy carried the stick everywhere and imagined many things, like a fisherman, a canoe paddler, and a hiker. He grew up, built a house on a hill, and gave his time, wealth, and heart to others. When he became old, he still went to the park. He saw a little girl sitting alone under the tree, so he placed the stick there. She picked it up, became a princess, a fencer, and a surfer, and sang the words too. Then the old man smiled and went home.

The child tried tying crayons to the unicorn’s horn. Then glitter scribbles shot everywhere, on the floor, ceiling, and lamp. The child worried because their mom was coming. In the end, the child learned that great art can begin with a scribble, and a unicorn can make art too.

summary_text: Mikey was getting ready for a party, but he could not choose what food to serve. He thought about pizza, tacos, burgers, hot dogs, pork, fried rice, pasta, Chinese food, and Italian food. He remembered food from family birthdays and felt confused because he liked both his mom’s Italian food and his dad’s Chinese food. He went to the park because his head felt full of choices. There, his friend Sophia saw that he was sad and asked what was wrong. Mikey said he could not pick a dish for his party tomorrow. Sophia told him he did not have to choose only one kind of food. She said he could have both. Mikey liked this idea and ran home to tell his family. He decided to make fried rice with marinara sauce. The next day, his mom cooked the rice and vegetables, and everyone helped. When the friends tasted the food, they liked it very much. The party ended with everyone saying, “Different is good.”

summary_text: Po comes from China to celebrate Chinese New Year in America. She says it is a time for new beginnings. Papa helps the family get ready. They sweep dirt out the back door, clean the windows, and do not clean on New Year’s Day because that would take away good luck. Po also helps with bath time and says hair should be washed before the new year, not on New Year’s Day. Mama and Po make special foods like chicken, fish, and long noodles. The family hangs red and gold decorations, paper cuts, and a sign for luck that is turned upside down so luck can arrive. They stay awake past midnight, drink tea, and wait for the New Year. Po, Mama, and friends play ma Jang. At last, Chinese New Year’s Day comes, and everyone says, “Happy Chinese New Year.”

summary_text: Kora loved Mama’s kitchen and wanted to be a real cook. Her older sisters and brother usually did the grown-up jobs, while Kora only got small jobs. One day, when her sisters went to the mall and her brother went outside, Kora asked Mama what they would make. Mama let Kora choose, and Kora asked to learn pansit. Mama gave Kora her red apron and told her about L, who wore it long ago when he cooked for Filipino farm workers in California. Mama and Kora got the ingredients and soaked the rice noodles in water. Kora shredded cooked chicken, chopped vegetables, and helped stir the noodles in the big pan. She made a small mess with the noodles, and Mama showed her how to check if they were soft. At dinner, the family tasted the pansit and said Kora had done the grown-up jobs. Daddy said it tasted like L’s soup, and Kora felt proud.

summary_text: This is unicorn. This is horse. Unicorn has a sapphire horn, a silver coat, a rainbow mane, and perfect white teeth. Unicorn eats pink cupcakes, makes rainbows, and dances. Horse is not like unicorn. Horse sits grumpy and does other things. Many animals love unicorn. Squirrel uses unicorn’s horn for ring toss, bird lines nests with unicorn’s long hair, and the animals share cupcakes. Horse says he does not like unicorn, but he really wishes he were unicorn. One night, two men come quietly to the paddock and tie up unicorn. They put him in their truck and drive away. The other animals wake up and try to help, but squirrel cannot run fast enough, bird cannot fly fast enough, fox cannot run on the road, and turtle cannot run at all. Horse thinks, then runs after the truck and uses his big teeth to free unicorn. Unicorn thanks horse, and horse says, “You’re welcome.” After that, horse and unicorn both share things, and they become friends.

summary_text: One day, a new family moved to Alphabet City. The family was made of punctuation marks, and Exclamation Point led the way on their first day at a new school. Exclamation Point was excited, Question Mark wondered about everything, Period helped bring the line to a stop, and Comma kept pausing and asking others to wait. When they arrived, the letters stared and asked who they were. The punctuation family explained that they were not letters, but they liked being around words. The class let them join in. Exclamation Point made the words sound exciting, Question Mark asked questions, and Period ended sentences neatly. Comma tried to fit in, but as the day went on, he felt smaller and smaller. He thought he only got in the way, so he quietly left the classroom. Soon the letters and punctuation made too much noise, the words became tangled, and everyone fell into a messy pile. Outside, the others found Comma and told him that he had an important job. Comma returned to the class, and the family worked together again.

summary_text: Little Sock lives in a drawer with other socks. At night, after the other socks go to sleep, he sneaks out of the drawer and through a hidden tunnel in the back of the dryer. This tunnel leads to Sock City, a place where only socks can go. In Sock City, there are many fun things to do, and some can be done alone. But some things are better with a friend. Little Sock looks around and sees another sock who is alone. He wonders if she could be his friend. He feels nervous and thinks about how to ask. Then he takes a deep breath and says, “Will you be my friend?” She says yes, and they are happy. The story ends by saying that making new friends is fun and that some things are better with a friend.

summary_text: Zoe woke up in the morning when the sun was shining and the birds were singing. She and her mom had a whole day together, and they went many places. Never?” and Mom said, “Not here.” Then they went to the park, where Mr Jones said no walking on the grass. Mom said, “But here—run wild, my child!” Next they visited Grandma, who said no wet shoes, but Mom said they could splash in the rain. Zoe went to school for painting day, and her friend said paint goes on paper, not on you. Later, at a store, they were told no children could play there, but Mom said, “But here—play!” Then Zoe had a playdate with Ada and made a couch fort. At bedtime, Mom tucked Zoe in and said there were no more adventures today.

summary_text: Mikey M danced to the front door and told his mom he was almost four. He said his friends would come over, presents would fill the driveway, and there would be a big cake. His mom smiled and said a party is not complete until food is chosen. Mikey started thinking about pizza, tacos, burgers, hot dogs, pork, and fried rice, but he could not decide. He asked his grannies for help. One granny said that in Hong Kong they ate Chinese food. The other said her roots were Italian, so pasta was important. Mikey also thought about birthday meals at his cousin’s parties, but he still felt stuck. He ran to the park and met his friend Sophia. Sophia reminded him that his mom is Italian and his dad is Chinese, so he could choose both. Mikey hurried home and picked fried rice with marinara sauce. The next day, his friends helped make the food, and everyone loved it. The party shouted, “Different is good!”

summary_text: A story speaks to a boy and tells him to dream big, work hard, be kind, and help others. It says to say hello, please, thank you, and I love you. Sarah dreamed of a husband, a family, and a job she loved. When a new law freed people from slavery, Sarah moved to Chicago. She married Archibald Good, rented rooms to people who needed help, and saved money for her own furniture store. Sarah listened to her customers and learned that many families needed more space. She made a fold-up cabinet bed, fixed it when it broke, and kept trying until it worked. Sarah then asked for a patent. After waiting and sending papers again, she finally received the patent for her cabinet bed, and her name was printed in history.

summary_text: Craig Robinson lived in Craig's Town, where children looked different but all wanted the same shiny yellow 10-speed bike. Craig wanted that bike after seeing it in the store window. He asked and asked, did chores, and finished homework until Mom finally said they could buy it. Craig was very happy and rode his new bike to Rainbow Beach. He went to buy ice cream, but a tall police officer stopped him and said the bike was stolen. Craig said Mom had bought it, but the officer put the bike in his car and took Craig home. Mom was angry and talked to the officer. Then the officer gave the bike back and left. Craig and Mom went for ice cream in the park, and Mom told him that some people may treat him unfairly because of his skin color. She said no one can make him feel bad if he feels good about himself. Craig understood, and then he rode home with his bike.

Uncles, aunts, and cousins are there, and everyone talks and plays games.
The child says the laughing helps keep eyes open.
The family has a big feast with fish and many other foods, and then everyone makes dumplings.
The child waits to eat them at midnight.
Some families also honor gods and ancestors by praying or leaving food offerings.
Some people leave fish leftovers so they can have extra food in the New Year.
At midnight, fireworks and firecrackers go off, and Chinese New Year begins.
The child is still awake.
The story also tells one old story about a monster named Nen, who came at New Year’s time.
People learned to scare Nen away because Nen was afraid of loud noises and the color red.

summary_text: Po and Papa get ready for Chinese New Year by following many lucky rules. Po says the family must sweep out bad luck before the new year, so the child sweeps dirt out the back door and cleans the windows very well. Po also says not to clean on New Year’s Day, because that could sweep away good luck. Next, Po gets a bath ready and tells the child to wash hair before New Year’s Day, because washing on the holiday is bad luck. The child washes three times and helps with the baby brother too. Mama makes a whole chicken and a fish with the head and tail still on, so the family will stay together and have a good beginning and ending. She also cooks long noodles, and the child eats them without breaking them. Red and gold banners, paper cuts, and a lucky sign are put on the door, and everyone stays awake to welcome Chinese New Year’s Day.

summary_text: On Christmas Eve, Marie and Fritz waited outside a bright ballroom and peeped through the keyhole. They smelled spruce tree, puff pastry, and music. At last the doors opened, and Fritz ran to the gifts while Marie looked at the room and the tall Christmas tree with candles, ribbons, and apples. Their godfather, Judge Drosselmeyer, showed Marie a wooden doll called the Nutcracker. He cracked a walnut in the doll’s mouth, and Marie loved the toy and hugged it. Fritz wanted to try it too, but he used a very hard nut and broke the Nutcracker’s jaw. Marie took the doll away, bandaged his jaw with a ribbon, and sang to him until she fell asleep under the tree.

summary_text: Ronnie Lott was a boy who always kept going when things were hard. He bought bright red shoes because a commercial said they would help him fly high. Ronnie jumped, but he fell down. He got hurt and sat by his shoes. Then he felt a little rumble inside. That rumble was Grit, and it told him, “Don’t ever quit.” As Ronnie grew, Grit stayed with him. Ronnie played sports and kept trying new things. He learned to be careful and respectful too, when his coach and dad helped him understand his mistakes. In high school, Ronnie joined the football team and knew he wanted to play. He missed tackles and dropped balls, but he kept trying. Later, he played football as a professional. He got hurt and lost part of a finger, but he still kept going. After football, Ronnie still shared his Grit by helping children and cheering for his family.

With her new coach, Peter, and her parents’ love, she got past her fear. At Nationals, she made some mistakes and became an alternate. Then she hurt her ankle before the competition, so she cheered for her teammates and supported them. She still competed on the uneven bars and won a silver medal. Now Samantha coaches children and tells them to dream, practice, and support each other.

Then the story tells about a toothless dinosaur with a long pointy beak and long pointy wings. This dinosaur can fly and fish. Then there is a stegosaurus with a spiky tail, plates on its back, and a small hat. It eats mostly plants. At the end, the story names a tyrannosaurus rex with big teeth, a short tail, long back legs, and short arms. It eats meat and is the fiercest dinosaur.

summary_text: Two children talk about being scared. One says, “I am not scared,” but then they both name scary things like snakes, hairy spiders, fried ants, an alien with pink eyes and furry teeth, and a roller coaster with a snake. At first they are not friends, but they try to play together. They make music, then play dinosaur hunters. A friend comes back, and all three children play together. In the end, they say they are best friends and play spies and build a castle, adding flags, towers, arches, windows, stairs, a gatehouse, and a drawbridge until it is perfect.

summary_text: Julia wakes up to a beautiful sunrise and decides to hike to Pancake Peak by herself. They ask Julia to help them get back down the mountain. Julia does not like this change, but she helps them return safely to the base of Pancake Peak. The friends rest for a sunny picnic at Hash Brown Hill, and Fitz shares snacks from his pack so he can carry it again. They keep going, but Bacon Bridge is broken. Violet warns them about a trap and protects the group from danger. At the end, Julia reaches home in time for dinner and eats with her new friends.

summary_text: The story begins by saying that poop is yucky, but it also says that every creature poops, from aardvarks to the humped zebu. It explains that different animals have different names for poop, like guano for bat or sea bird poop and dung for other animals. Then the story shows many kinds of poop, such as monkey dung, dog poop, rabbit pellets, raccoon tubes, owl whitewash, wombat cubes, and bird poop. Monkeys may fling poop, and a dog may drop poop too. The story then tells how poop can be useful. Termites use it to make mounds, dung beetles roll it into balls, and some animals spread seeds in their poop so new plants can grow. It also says poop can mark scent and help soil. In the end, poop is used for farming, cooking, heat, houses, souvenirs, and even cow pie flinging at fairs.

summary_text: The story teaches that monsters can be noisy, messy, hungry, selfish, mean, wild, tired, or grumpy, and children can help them behave. If a monster is noisy, whisper, “Be quiet.” If it is hungry, give it a fork and a spoon and say, “Chew your food.” If it is selfish, say, “Take turns.” If it is mean, walk away and say, “Good bye.” If it scares you, scare it back and say, “Boo.” If it makes a mess, say, “Clean up.” If it is wild, give it a timeout and say, “Sit still.” If it is tired and grumpy, send it to bed and say, “Go to sleep.” If it asks nicely, kiss it and say, “Good night.” The story says that next time you catch a monster running wild, you will know what to do.

video_title: Arts and Crafts for Kids: Painting With Leaves!
summary_text: The story explains a leaf painting craft. The speaker talks about learning about leaves and says chipmunks and green leaves are favorites. To make the craft, children need paper, paint in the primary colors blue, red, and yellow, a sponge, and paper plates. First, they go outside to gather leaves from yards or a park, choosing many shapes and sizes. Next, they put one primary color on each plate. The story says blue and yellow can make green, and red and yellow can make orange. Then they place the leaves on the paper with space between them. After that, they dip the sponge in paint and sponge it around the leaves, holding the leaves still so they do not move. Finally, they peel off the leaves to see a pretty leaf painting.

video_title: What If You Had Animal Hair!?
summary_text: The story asks what it would be like to wake up with animal hair instead of human hair. It first talks about polar bear hair, which has two layers and keeps the bear warm in cold, wet weather. Then it describes reindeer hair, which is thick, hollow, and helps the animal stay warm and float in water. Musk ox hair is very long and shaggy, and it protects the animal in winter and summer. Oryx hair is short and pale, so it helps the animal stay cool in the desert. Lion hair is a big mane that makes a male lion stand out. Zebra hair has black and white stripes that help confuse hunters. The story also explains sloth hair, arctic fox hair, giant pangolin scales, porcupine quills, and mole hair. At the end, it says wild animal hair might be fun, but people do not need hair like animals do, so they do not have to choose.

video_title: TOO MANY CARROTS by Katy Hudson | SPRING BOOKS FOR KIDS | EASTER BOOKS FOR CHILDREN | BUNNY BOOKS
summary_text: Rabbit loved carrots. He picked up carrots wherever he went and hid them in his cozy hole. But Rabbit could not sleep because his home was too crowded. He asked Tortoise for a place to stay, and Tortoise offered to share his house. Rabbit said it was cozy, but then he brought his carrots inside too, and the house became too tight. Rabbit and Tortoise tried Bird’s nest next, but Rabbit carried the carrots up the tree. The branch wobbled, snapped, and Bird lost his nest. Then Squirrel let Rabbit stay in his house, but Rabbit brought more carrots, and the house could not fit them all. Last, Beaver offered his house. Rabbit wanted to bring even more carrots, but then rain came, Beaver’s house collapsed, and all the friends were left cold and tired on the riverbank. Rabbit saw that he had caused the trouble. He shared everything with his friends, and things got better.

In the morning she got dressed, ate breakfast, cleaned her room, and went outside to stand with her family under the tree. She wanted to look perfect for the photo. But while she waited, she realized she had forgotten to go pee. At first it was only a small feeling, but it got stronger and stronger. She crossed her legs and tried to stay still. She watched her brothers, Grandma, Uncle Phil, and Grandpa as she waited. The story stops as Felicity stands there trying to hold on.

Bunny, Giraffe, and Bear painted the fence. Mole, Grasshopper, and Cheetah cleaned the sandbox. Soon the work felt hard and messy, and everyone got tired. Mouse stopped the group at lunch and said they should work smarter, not harder. He explained that this meant using clever ideas. The friends tried new ways to work. Cheetah used bags and a wheelbarrow. Kitten suggested each friend do one step at a time. Bunny, Giraffe, and Bear changed how they painted. By the end of the day, the playground looked beautiful, and the friends were happy with what they had done.

People called these places world wonders, but Kora always thought they were not wonderful enough. When she grew old, she returned home and found the hill house empty and for sale. She bought it and planned many big ideas, but she could not choose one. While she thought, she fixed the house, painted the walls, repaired the fence, planted a garden, and got chickens. Then she met children in the woods who were building a secret hideout, and she asked to help.

video_title: The Vanishing Lake – 🚣‍♀️ Fun, creative children's story about Lake Loughareema in Ireland!
summary_text: Mera rode in Granddad’s car to his home beside Larima, a lake with a little island and his pet otter, Cara. The lake was usually normal, but sometimes it disappeared completely, and then rain filled it up again. Mera asked Granddad where the water went, and he gave funny answers about sheep, mermaids, narwhals, and Giants from Over the Mountain. Mera looked for clues on the dry lake bed and stayed awake to catch the lake vanishing, but she never did. At last, she said it was a mystery and did not care anymore. Granddad took her up the mountain and gave her binoculars. They waited until Mera saw a huge herd of mammoths drinking at the lake. The mammoths made the whole lake dry up and then left. Granddad told Mera to keep it a secret, and as they walked home, it began to rain.

Canoli said Thanksgiving was not just about food. It was also a time to show love and thanks. The dogs decided to be on their best behavior to show their owners they were thankful.

When winter comes, he dreams of spring, buds, and singing things. Then a small baby crow falls from the sky with a broken nest and a hurt wing. Later, five eggs are hidden nearby, and Scarecrow guards them as he waits for more baby crows.

video_title: The Three Little Pigs – 🐷🐷🐷 Read aloud of the classic tale about the value of hard work!
summary_text: A mommy pig, a Daddy Pig, and three little pigs lived at the edge of a beautiful forest. When it was time for the three little pigs to leave home, Daddy Pig warned them to watch out for the big bad wolf. The first little pig got tired and built a straw house. The second little pig built a house from sticks and branches. The third little pig kept walking until he found a nice place by a stream. He worked hard and built a strong brick house. Then the hungry big bad wolf found the first little pig and said, “Little pig, little pig, let me come in.” The pig said no, so the wolf huffed and puffed and blew the straw house down. The first pig ran to the stick house. The wolf blew that house down too, and the two pigs ran to the brick house. The wolf could not blow it down. He climbed down the chimney, landed in hot soup, burned his tail, and ran away. The three little pigs stayed safe in the brick house and lived happily ever after.

They can say sorry and ask for forgiveness. In the end, the speaker says they are connected to friends, family, and the world, and they will keep trying to be their best self. They are full of hope.

video_title: @DrSeuss - The Tooth Book (Dr. Seuss Beginner Book Video)
summary_text: The story says many kinds of living things have teeth, like uncles, policemen, zebras, unicycle riders, and little girls named Ruthie. Teeth are found in many places, even underground, and in all directions. Mr. Donald Driscoll Drew says teeth help people chew. Smiling Sam the Crocodile says teeth help him smile. Hi Trapezer Mike Macabre says teeth help him with his job. Quincy Quick says teeth help him speak, and without them he would sound like ducks. Simon Snead the snail has no teeth, and Pam the Clam says she cannot eat many foods without teeth. Jimbo Jones says teeth are needed to play trombones. Hilda Hen says both women and men have teeth, and children grow two sets. They lose the first set and then grow 32 new teeth. The story ends by warning not to ruin teeth by chewing trees, breaking them on knots, or biting bottle tops. It says to keep teeth safe and be kind to the dentist.

summary_text: A child says they are not going to get up today. The alarm rings and the birds peep, but the child stays in bed because the bed is warm and the pillow is deep. The child says other kids are getting up in many places, like Switzerland, Memphis, Spain, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Maine, London, Paris, and Berlin, but not them. They say breakfast can be taken away and the egg can go back to the hen. They also say tickling feet, shaking the bed, and pouring cold water will not work. Neighbors try to wake the child, but it does not help. The child keeps snoozing and says they do not want to walk or talk, only lie there woozy snoozing. Even treats, animals, police, papers, peas, beans, Marines, TV, and a brass band do not make the child get up. At the end, someone says the child really means it, so the egg can be kept.

After that, Yertle was no longer king, and the turtles were free.

video_title: Dr Seuss -  “Horton Hears a Who” read by Jeff Goldblum
summary_text:
One hot day in the jungle of Nool, Horton the Elephant was splashing in a pool when he heard a tiny yelp from a speck of dust. Horton looked closely and guessed that a very small person must be on the speck. He gently lifted the dust speck onto a clover and said, “A person’s a person, no matter how small.” The sour Kangaroo and her young one laughed at him and said no one could live there. Horton kept the clover safe and walked with it, even when the news spread and the jungle animals made fun of him.

Later, the Wickersham brothers grabbed the clover and gave it to a black-bottomed eagle named Vlad Vladikoff. Horton chased after it all night. By morning, the clover had fallen into a huge field of clovers, and Horton searched and searched until he found it. The mayor of Whoville told Horton that all the Whos were safe but needed help after the fall. When the Kangaroos and Wickershams tried to take Horton away, the Whos made a loud noise, and Horton’s friends heard them. Their voices proved they were real, and Horton saved them.

Their mama fed them bugs, and Stellaluna was very hungry, so she ate bugs too. She learned to stay awake in the day and sleep at night, but she still liked to hang by her feet. The bird mama was upset and told Stellaluna to obey the rules. Later, Stellaluna learned to fly with the birds, but she got lost in the dark. Then she met other bats and found her own mother. The bats showed her fruit, and Stellaluna was happy. At last, Stellaluna brought the birds to meet the bats, and they all stayed friends even though they were different.
