summary_text: In a warm forest, a mother fruit bat cared for her baby, Stella Luna, and carried her while searching for food. One night an owl attacked the bats. Mother bat was hit, and Stella Luna fell into the forest. She landed in a bird nest with three baby birds named Flap, Flitter, and Pip. The birds’ mother fed them bugs, and Stella Luna was hungry enough to eat them too. Soon she learned to live like the birds: she stayed awake in the day, slept at night, and ate bugs, though she still liked hanging by her feet. She met other bats, found her real mother, and learned that bats can fly at night and see in the dark. At the end, Stella Luna showed her bird friends her bat family, and they all stayed friends even though they were different.

video_title: 🎃From Seed to Pumpkin 🎃| Read Aloud for Kids! | Fall Books for Kids!
summary_text: When spring winds warm the earth, a farmer plants hundreds of pumpkin seeds in dark, moist soil. The seeds crack open underground, and roots grow down while stems send green shoots up through the earth. In less than two weeks, tiny seedlings appear. Two seed leaves open and reach toward the sun. The leaves use sunlight, water from the soil, and air to make sugar, which feeds the plant. Soon the seed leaves dry up, and broad prickly leaves unfold. The farmer keeps weeds out because weeds take water from the soil that pumpkin plants need. The stems do not stand tall; they spread across the ground and form tangled vines. Flower buds appear, and bright orange flowers open. Bees carry pollen from male flowers to female flowers, and then tiny hard fruits begin to grow. All summer, warm sun and rain help the fruits grow bigger. By autumn, the green pumpkins turn yellow and then orange. After about four months, the patch is full of ripe pumpkins.

video_title: 💕 The Valentine Bears 💕| Read Aloud for Kids! | Valentine's Day Books!
summary_text: On October 14th, Mrs. Bear and Mr. Bear settled into their den for winter. Mrs. Bear set her alarm for February 14th, because she had a special plan for Valentine's Day. Four months later, she woke up while Mr. Bear kept sleeping. She made a sign that said, “It’s nice to share Valentine’s Day with someone you love,” and hung it on the wall. She brushed out leaves, dug up a pot of summer honey, and put out crispy critters for Mr. Bear. She also got two valentine poems she had written in summer. Then she went outside, broke ice on the pond, and filled a berry can with cold water. Mrs. Bear tried again and again to wake Mr. Bear, but he kept sleeping. At last she shouted, “One, two, three. Surprise!” Mr. Bear woke up, hugged her, and showed her chocolate covered ants. They shared their treats, read the poems, and ate together until the den was empty. Then they went back to sleep until spring.

video_title: 💕 The Day It Rained Hearts 💕| Read Aloud for Kids! | Kid's Books Online!
summary_text: One day it rained hearts, and Cornelia Augusta caught one heart, then another, and many more. She thought it must be close to Valentine's Day, so she began making valentines. She looked at each heart and chose the best ones for her friends. She found seven hearts that looked alike and strung them together with a needle and thread. She took one special heart, pasted it on paper, and glued a white, soft cotton ball on it. She knew right away who that card was for. Then she used the biggest heart to make more cards by drawing circles and cutting them out. The smaller hearts were arranged on paper, painted with many colors, and folded in half. Cornelia Augusta put stamps on all the valentines and mailed them. After that, it never rained hearts again where she lived, but each next year she found other ways to make valentines.

Llama helps Grandpa get into the water, and they swim, float, toss a beach ball, and go bodyboarding. Llama and Grandpa feel proud and do not want to go home.

video_title: 💦 Froggy Learns to Swim 💦| Summer Books | Read Aloud for Kids!
summary_text: It was a hot day, and Froggy’s mother said it was a great day for a swim. Froggy and his parents flopped to the pond. Froggy’s father and mother went into the water with a splash, but Froggy stayed out and said he did not know how to swim. He wanted to swing instead. Froggy swung higher and higher until he flew right into the pond. He cried that he was drowning, and his mother came to help him. She told him frogs are born in the water and are great swimmers. Then she showed him how to float, put his face in the water, kick like a frog, and say, “bubble bubble” and “chicken airplane soldier.” Froggy tried, but he still had trouble. He went home for his flippers, then for his mask and snorkel, and kept trying again. At last, he began to swim. When it got cold and his mother said it was time to get out, Froggy did not want to leave. He put on his bathing suit and flippers again and went back into the pond, swimming and saying the words all night long.

Her father also told her that space was far away, but she might get there sooner than she thought.
That night Mae dreamed of dancing in space and seeing Earth like a crystal ball.
The next day, she told her class she wanted to be an astronaut, but the other children laughed.
Miss Bell suggested she become a nurse instead, and Mae felt disappointed.
At home, her mother comforted her and told her not to give up.
Mae kept dreaming, believing, and working hard, and in the end she went to space and waved to her parents from her spaceship.

The snow sits in little mounds, and if you wait, it gets smaller and smaller until it is gone. Then spring comes. Spring brings leaves and blossoms to the trees. It turns the grass green and adds little flowers. Seeds start growing, and an egg can become a bird. Spring also brings sun, rain, and more rain. There can be mud and puddles, so umbrellas may be needed. In the garden, green shoots push through the dirt. Spring calls out the willows and new kittens too. Spring may come quickly or slowly, and it changes a lot. When spring is finally here to stay, there are buds, bees, boots, bubbles, worms, wings, wind, and wheels. You can see, smell, and hear that spring is here. Then it is time to wait for summer.

video_title: Love Monster and the Scary Something by Rachel Bright read-aloud
summary_text: It was very late in Cutesville, and everyone was asleep except Love Monster. He had his hot milk with chocolate sprinkles, walked up the stairs, read bedtime stories, and snuggled with teddy. But that night, he could not fall asleep. He listened to the dark night and heard tick tock sounds, wind in the leaves, and owls. Then he heard something in the yard, and then downstairs. He hid under the covers because he thought something had come inside. The sound went bump, shuffle, crunch, crunch up the stairs, and Love Monster thought it had big teeth and was hungry. At last, he could not stay hiding. He got up, turned on his flashlight, and went to see. He found a tiny fluffy bunny, and the bunny was not alone either. They laughed together, and Love Monster saw that the dark was not so spooky after all.

But that night he could not fall asleep. The night felt darker and spookier, and he heard many sounds outside, like tick tock from the clock, wind in the leaves, and owls in Cutesville. Then he heard a strange noise in the yard, then downstairs, and then on the stairs. He thought something with terrible twisterly toenails and big teeth was coming up to get him. At last, Love Monster could not stay hidden anymore. He turned on his flashlight, got out of bed, and went to see what was there. He found that he was not the only one awake. After that, the dark did not seem so spooky, and Love Monster learned that when you face what you fear, it may not be scary after all.

video_title: A Crankenstein Valentine by Samantha Berger Read Aloud
summary_text: On Valentine’s Day, Frankenstein is easy to spot. He has brand new heart undies, and someone says, “Happy Valentine’s Day, my love.” He may get a big red smooch on the school bus, eat a heart-shaped peanut butter and jelly sandwich, heart-shaped apple slices, and use a napkin covered in hearts. He also makes his own kind of Frankenstein valentine. But Frankenstein does not like the mushy Valentine’s Day chocolate with hairy coconut inside. He does not like helping make Valentine’s Day garlic or the Valentine’s Day garden. He also does not want to be in the Valentine’s Day school pageant. In the end, the story says Frankenstein only wants one thing for Valentine’s Day: a best friend who understands exactly how he feels. It ends by saying there are 364 days until next Valentine’s Day.

summary_text: Jim pansy was napping in the sun when Oxpecker woke him up and showed him a flower from her boyfriend. She said he was making her a romantic dinner for Valentine’s Day. Jim asked what Valentine’s Day was, and Oxpecker said it was a day for love, with hearts, sweets, flowers, and romance. Jim thought it sounded gross and went to find his neighbor Norman. But Norman was busy making love cards. Jim then saw many couples everywhere. They exchanged cards, looked at each other, giggled, danced, cuddled, snuggled, and kissed. Jim said Valentine’s Day was the grossest holiday. Norman agreed that the kissing was gross, but he said Valentine’s Day is also about many kinds of love. Jim’s mom said people can love their parents and children, and Norman said friends love each other too. Jim’s dad said Valentine’s Day is for showing people that you love them. Jim felt loved by the things in his arms and decided to make Valentines for his friends and family. He thought Valentine’s Day might not be so gross after all.

summary_text: Mary Lou loved Herby, a slug with a shiny slime trail and a talent for finding the best tomatoes. She thought about him all the time, but she was too shy to speak to him. summary_text: Mr. Hatch was a tall, thin man who did not smile. Every day he went to the shoelace Factory, ate lunch alone, bought a newspaper and a turkey wing, then read and went to bed early. One Saturday, he found a brown package on his porch from Mr. Goober the postman. Inside was a heart-shaped red box of candy and a card that said, “Somebody loves you. You only.” Mr. Hatch was amazed because he thought he had no friends. He laughed, dressed up, and started acting in new ways. He helped Mr. Smith at the newsstand, found little Melanie Todd for Mr. Todd, and baked brownies for the neighborhood. Soon children and parents came to his house for brownies, lemonade, and music. Later, Mr. Goober returned and said the Valentine had been delivered to the wrong house. Mr. Hatch felt sad and stopped smiling. But his neighbors remembered how kind he had been. They filled his porch with hearts, candy, streamers, and a sign that said, “Everybody loves Mr. Hatch.” Then Mr. Hatch smiled and laughed and joined his friends.

video_title: A Rainbow of My Own
summary_text: The child sees a beautiful rainbow and wants to catch it. The child puts on a raincoat and hat and runs outside very fast. But when the child gets to the place where the rainbow should be, it is gone. The child thinks that maybe on another rainy day, a rainbow will come and stay for a while. The child imagines a rainbow following along, circling and whirling like a bird’s wings. They play with it by hopping over it, climbing up one side, and sliding down the other. The rainbow also makes a peacock fan and a hammock for playing. Then they play hide and go seek, and the rainbow hides in a flower garden where the flowers look like a rainbow too. After that, the sun comes out and the pretend rainbow disappears. Later, the child goes home and sees a glow in the room window. Inside, the sun shines through the water in the goldfish bowl and makes a rainbow on the wall, a rainbow of the child’s very own.

video_title: The Story of Ferdinand the Bull by Munro Leaf Read Aloud
summary_text: In Spain, there was a little bull named Ferdinand. While the other young bulls ran, jumped, and butted heads, Ferdinand preferred to sit quietly and smell the flowers. His favorite place was under a cork tree in the pasture. His mother worried that he might be lonely, but Ferdinand kept saying he liked to sit there and smell the flowers. She saw that he was happy and let him stay. As Ferdinand grew up, the other bulls became strong and fought each other, hoping to be chosen for the bull fights in Madrid. Ferdinand still liked his quiet place best. One day, five men came to choose the biggest and fiercest bull. Ferdinand was not trying to impress them, but when a bee stung him, he jumped up, snorted, and acted wild. The men thought he was fierce and took him to Madrid. In the bull ring, Ferdinand would not fight. He sat down, smelled the flowers, and was sent home.

video_title: The Little Auto & Mr. Small - 1934 by Lois Lenski w/ Music
summary_text: Mr. Small has a little Auto. It is red and shiny, and he keeps it in the garage at the end of the driveway. One day he oils it, pumps up the rubber tires, and fills the radiator with water. Then he gets ready for a drive. He steps on the starter, the engine begins to hum, and the little Auto backs out of the garage and goes chug chug down the driveway and road. Mr. Small toots the horn and scares the ducks and chickens. A small dog follows, but soon falls behind. The little Auto goes fast, passes a horse and buggy, and goes uphill and downhill until it comes to town. Mr. Small drives on the right side of the street, waits at a stop sign, stops at a filling station for 5 gallons of gas, and later waits by a trolley car. He parks to buy a newspaper, then starts home. A red light makes him stop, rain makes him put up the top, and a flat tire makes him jack up the car and put on the spare. When the sun comes out, he washes and polishes the little Auto and puts it back in the garage, shining like new.

video_title: The Biggest Bear  - Caldecott Honor Published 1952
summary_text: Johnny Orchard lived on a farm at the top of a valley near the woods. His grandfather had planted a few apple trees, and they were the only apple trees in the valley. Johnny felt embarrassed because the other barns had bear skins hanging up, but his barn did not. After hearing about the bears other men had shot, Johnny said that if he ever saw one, he would shoot it quickly and get the biggest bear skin in the valley. Instead, when he went into the woods, he found a bear near a stump and gave it maple sugar. The bear followed him home and ate the sugar. Johnny’s parents were surprised, but the bear stayed and ate milk, chicken mash, apples, pancakes, and more maple sugar. He also got into neighbors’ cornfields, smokehouses, maple buckets, and sheds, and he grew very large. Soon the neighbors complained, and Johnny’s father said the bear had to go back to the woods. Johnny tried taking him west, then east, then south on Galls Island, but the bear always returned. Finally, Johnny and his father took him north into the woods, where men from the city zoo caught the bear in a trap and said he would have a fine place to live.

video_title: Frederick - Caldecott & 100 Best Children's Books
summary_text: In a meadow near an old stone wall, a family of field mice lived in a home by the barn and granary. The farmers had moved away, so the barn was empty and winter was coming. The mice worked day and night to gather corn, nuts, wheat, and straw. Frederick did not carry food like the others. When they asked why, he said he was gathering sun rays for the cold winter days. When they asked again, he said he was gathering colors because winter is gray. When they thought he was dreaming, he said he was gathering words because winter days are long. When snow came, the mice stayed in their stone hideout. At first they had food and told stories, but soon the food was gone and it was cold and quiet. Then Frederick shared his sun rays, colors, and words. His story made the mice feel warm and happy. They clapped and said, “You are Frederick!”

video_title: Inch By Inch -  w/ EFX & Music Read Aloud
summary_text: A hungry robin saw an inchworm on a twig and was about to eat him. The inchworm said, “Don’t eat me! I am useful. I measure things.” The robin asked the inchworm to measure his tail. The inchworm counted, “One, two, three, four, five inches.” The robin was pleased and said his tail was five inches long. Then the robin flew with the inchworm to measure other birds. They measured the canary’s beak, the heron’s legs, the pheasant’s tail, and even the whole hummingbird. One morning, the nightingale met the inchworm and told him to measure her song. The inchworm said he could measure things, not songs. The nightingale said she would eat him for breakfast if he did not try. So the inchworm began to measure while the nightingale sang. He counted and counted until the song was very, very long and hard to measure. At the end, the inchworm forgot what he was doing and thanked the nightingale.

Swimmy asked them to swim and play, but they said they could not because they were afraid of being eaten. Swimmy told them they must think of something. After thinking, he said they should swim together like one big fish. He taught them to stay close, and he said he would be the eye. Then they swam together in the water and chased the big fish away.

It came up just as the little boy had known it would. The seed had grown into a carrot because he kept watering it and removing the weeds.

video_title: A Tree Is Nice w/ Words & Music

Trees can hold swings and baskets of flowers, and they are good for resting a hoe. Trees make shade for cows, picnics, and baby naps. A tree near a house helps keep it cool and blocks the wind.

video_title: One Morning in Maine w/ Words, Music & EFX
summary_text: One morning in Maine, Sal woke up thinking about her trip with her father to Bucks Harbor. While getting ready with her little sister Jane, Sal found that one of her teeth was loose. She ran to her mother, who told her that this was a sign she was growing into a big girl and that a new tooth would grow in later. Her mother also said that when the tooth came out, Sal could put it under her pillow and make a secret wish. Sal went outside to help her father dig clams and asked several sea animals if they had teeth. She watched fishhawks, loons, seals, and seagulls, then the tooth fell out while she was working in the mud. Sal was sad because she could not save it for her wish, and she and her father looked for it but could not find it. On the way home, Sal picked up a gold feather and wished on that instead. The family then went to Bucks Harbor by boat, where the motor had to be fixed, and Sal’s father bought milk and groceries. Sal later shared ice cream with Jane and said their wishes were used up, and the family headed home for clam chowder.

video_title: Fish is Fish w/ Words, Music & EFX Read Along
summary_text: At the edge of the woods, a minnow and a tadpole lived in a pond and were inseparable friends. One morning, the tadpole found that he had grown two little legs. He proudly said he was a frog, but the minnow argued that he could not be a frog because he had been a little fish the night before. They argued until the tadpole said, “Frogs are frogs and fish is fish and that's that.” Over the next weeks, the tadpole grew front legs and his tail became smaller. He became a real frog and climbed onto the grassy bank. The minnow grew into a full-fledged fish and kept wondering what had happened to his friend. Later, the frog returned and told the fish about birds, cows, and people he had seen while hopping around the world. The fish imagined these things and longed to see them too.

video_title: Hedgie's Surprise w/ Words, EFX & Music
summary_text: A speckled hen named Penny laid one egg every day, but little Tompton came every morning and took it for his breakfast. He was tired of porridge, so he climbed into the hen house, took Penny’s warm egg, cooked it in his little kettle, ate it with salt, and then slept in the hay loft until evening. Penny did not like this, but she kept quiet until she saw Goosey Goosey with a line of goslings. Then Penny wanted chicks of her own. She tried to stop Tompton, but he still took her egg. The little hedgehog, Hedgie, saw what was happening and offered to help. The next mornings, Penny and Hedgie gave Tompton an acorn, a strawberry, a mushroom, and a potato instead of an egg. Each time he cooked the food and ate it, but he woke up hungry again. At last Hedgie hid in a straw nest. Tompton grabbed him, got stuck on his prickles, and ran home. After that, Penny’s eggs hatched into five baby chicks, and Tompton went back to eating porridge.

video_title: Coco Storybook - Disney Pixar film - Audio Read Aloud for Kids bedtime
summary_text: In Santa Cecilia, Miguel Rivera lived with his big family, including Mama Coco. Every Día de los Muertos, the Rivera family remembered relatives who had died, and Abuelita always said no music because of Mama Imelda’s sad past. Miguel loved music anyway. He learned guitar from videos of Ernesto de la Cruz and sneaked out with his dog Dante to enter a talent show. When he fell onto the family ofrenda, he found a photo that showed Ernesto with Mama Coco’s family. Abuelita broke Miguel’s guitar, so Miguel went to Ernesto’s tomb and took a guitar from the wall. When he played it, he was sent to the land of the dead. There he needed a blessing to go home. Mama Imelda would not bless him, so Miguel searched for Ernesto with Héctor, a skeleton who helped him. Miguel learned the truth: Ernesto had stolen Héctor’s songs and tried to keep the secret. In the end, Miguel returned home, helped Mama Coco remember her papa with the song “Remember Me,” and the Rivera family allowed music again.

summary_text: Lucy, Tom, Bob, and M were spending a weekend with their granddad on a gray, drizzly day when everyone felt bored and grumpy. Grand Dude tried to cheer them up by showing postcards and using a shiny magic compass. When Lucy picked a postcard of a sandy beach, he waved the compass over it and the children were suddenly on the beach. They rode flying fish, built sandcastles, and ate ice cream, but then crabs pinched Bob and more crabs came from the sea, so Grand Dude used the compass again. The next postcard took them to a desert valley, where they met a cowboy and rode horses. A herd of wild buffalo rushed toward them, Tom fell, and Grand Dude lassoed him back onto his horse just in time. After Tom asked for somewhere less stampy, they were taken to a hill with flowers and cows, but an avalanche came down the mountain. The cows flew them away safely. At last, Grand Dude used a photo of his house, and the compass sent them home for bed, where they brushed their teeth, washed, and fell asleep.

summary_text:
On a snowy mountain, Gertie was the littlest yak in the herd. She had curly wool and grippy hooves, but she wished she were bigger, with tallness, huge hooves, and humongous horns. Her mother told her that yaks come in different sizes and that it was good to be small for now. Gertie still wanted to grow right away, so she ate many vegetables, climbed mountains, ran, hopped, skipped, and read books, hoping to become large. But no growing happened, and she felt upset.

Then the herd heard that another yak was stuck on a steep cliff ledge. Mommy yak said the herd could not reach him because their hooves were too heavy and their horns were too wide, but Gertie was small and grippy, so she was the only one who could help. Gertie climbed quickly to the ledge, where a small yak was shivering. She told him to hold on, let him climb onto her back, and carried him safely home. The herd cheered, and her mother hugged her and said Gertie had bigness inside. Gertie then felt happy being the right size for herself.

video_title: 🦊🌨️ANIMALS IN WINTER🌨️🦊Nonfiction Winter Science Read Aloud Book for Kids
summary_text: As the days grow short and cold, winter comes and many animals get ready in different ways. Birds like Bluebirds and Orioles fly south to warm places with food, and later they will return north in spring. Monarch butterflies also migrate south after gathering in trees by the hundreds. Some bats fly south, but others stay in caves and hibernate all winter. Woodchucks, also called groundhogs, eat a lot in fall, then crawl into their tunnels and sleep for up to four months. Pikas do not hibernate or migrate. They live in high mountains and gather grass in summer, dry it on rocks, and hide it under stones for winter food. Squirrels bury nuts and acorns and eat them later, though some forgotten nuts may grow into trees. Other animals, like mice, deer, rabbits, and foxes, must keep hunting for food all winter. People can help by putting out food, birdhouses, and other winter shelters. In the end, the days grow longer and warmer, and spring comes.

As soon as the story begins, the Gingerbread Man pops out of the page and runs away, saying, “Run, run as fast as you can!” The children try to catch him, but he keeps escaping. He says their traps will not work because he has help from other fairy tale characters. Peter Pan, called the boy who never grew, helps him first. Then Harry Potter uses a magic spell. Next, the Wizard of Oz friends remind him that courage, brains, and heart are not enough to stop him. Sherlock Holmes, Robin Hood, Little Red Riding Hood, Jack and the Beanstalk, Alice in Wonderland, and Peter Rabbit also help him get past different traps. At the end, the Gingerbread Man wins again, but he notices the children look sad. He decides to go back so the story can have a happy ending, and he invites them to try again: “Can you catch me?”

video_title: Llama Llama Holiday Drama | READ ALOUD
summary_text: Llama Llama gets very upset while waiting for Christmas. He sees holiday lights, candles, bread, and red and green clothes, and he learns there are only 15 more shopping days. Then there are ads, store displays, snow, and elves, and there are only 12 more shopping days. Mama takes him shopping, but he still does not know what gifts he will get. At home, Mama and Llama Llama bake cookies for school, measure sugar, roll dough, and frost a big batch. Llama also does holiday activities at school like making a snowman, a star, and a candle jar. While he waits, he makes a present for Mama with sparkles, sticks, and glue. Later, he helps decorate with stockings, snowflakes, and lights, but he keeps waiting and gets tired of all the noise and work. Then Mama tells him to cuddle and rest. She says the true gift is having each other. Llama Llama hugs Mama, feels warm and snug, and wishes happy holidays.

video_title: Llama Llama Holiday Drama | READ ALOUD
summary_text: Llama Llama and a friend play a game to find the right shadow for each stocking. First, they look at a stocking with a candy cane sticking out of the top. They compare it with the shadows and choose the one with the bigger candy cane, not the smaller one. Next, they find the stocking with Jingle Bells on it and match it to the shadow with bells, not the one with round balls. Then they see a stocking with two puff balls and find its shadow. Last, they match the stocking with holly leaves on the side. When all the stockings are matched, the game is finished, and everyone says thank you for playing.

video_title: READ ALOUD: Bluey Christmas Eve with Veranda Santa (Bluey)
summary_text: On Christmas Eve, Bluey’s family is at the Heeler house after dinner, and everyone is waiting for Santa. Bluey is very excited because presents are already under the tree. Muffin wonders how Santa gets in without a chimney, and Bluey says he might use the veranda. Then Bingo jumps out and says, “Let’s play Veranda Santa!” The kids decide Dad will be Veranda Santa, and they all go to bed and pretend to sleep. Dad tiptoes across the veranda and leaves presents under the pillows. In the morning, the children are happy with their gifts, but Bluey does not want to accept Bingo’s sorry when she takes the pencil case. Later Bluey becomes Veranda Santa and tells the others they get no presents because they peeked. After the family says sorry, Bluey accepts it. Then Socks helps Bingo, but Bluey gets upset when Socks bites and does not say sorry. Mom and Dad explain that Bluey should say sorry too, and Bluey finally apologizes to Socks. At the end, the family plays Veranda Santa one more time.

video_title: READ ALOUD: Pete the Cat Saves Christmas!
summary_text: The day before Christmas, Santa gets sick in the cold winter wind and catches a bad chill. Pete loads the presents and sends the reindeer off. Then the mini bus flies like in a movie, and Pete says it is totally groovy. As children sleep in their beds, Pete and the reindeer deliver gifts through chimneys and cross names off Santa’s list. The list is very big, but Pete keeps going until the last house. At the break of Christmas Day, Pete and the reindeer return to the North Pole, where Santa, the elves, and the townsfolk celebrate and thank him.

video_title: Ruby Bridges Goes to School - My True Story - Words
summary_text: A long time ago, many people believed black people and white people should be kept apart. This was called segregation. Black children and white children could not always go to the same schools. The United States government said this was wrong and said children should be able to go to any school they wanted. Ruby Bridges was a little girl who first went to kindergarten at a school for black children. She liked her teacher and friends, but the William Franz Elementary School was closer to her home. The government said Ruby should be allowed to go there. In 1961, Ruby’s mother took her to the Franz school, and marshalls came to keep them safe. Some people stood outside and yelled at her, and many parents took their children home. Ruby stayed with her teacher, Mrs. Henry, and learned math and reading. After many months, other children came back, and Ruby finally had friends to play with. Later, many people read about Ruby, and artists and writers made her story famous. When Ruby grew up, she visited schools and told children to be kind to each other.

video_title: Wilma  Unlimited - How Wilma Rudolph Became the World's Fastest Woman Read Aloud
summary_text: Wilma Rudolph lived in Clarksville, Tennessee, with her large family. She loved to run, laugh, and play, but before she was five, she became very sick. Doctors found that she had scarlet fever and polio, and people said she might never walk again. Wilma could only move by hopping on one foot. Her mother took her by bus to a hospital in Nashville, where doctors and nurses helped her do exercises. At home, Wilma kept practicing, even when it hurt. She was sad when her school would not let her attend because she could not walk. Later, she got a steel brace and returned to school, where other children made fun of her. Wilma kept working hard. One Sunday at church, she took off her brace and walked down the aisle by herself. After that, she practiced more, and when she was 12, she no longer needed the brace. She then played basketball, won many games, and later went to the Olympics in Rome. There she won three gold medals and became known as the fastest woman in the world.

video_title: I Am Rosa Parks - Read Along w/ Words on Screen
summary_text: Rosa Parks grew up in America at a time when black people were treated unfairly. As a child, she was small and often sick, but she learned to stand up for herself. When she was 11, a boy on rollerskates shoved her, and she pushed him back. His mother yelled because Rosa was black, but Rosa stayed calm and told the truth. At school, Rosa saw that black children had a small old wooden school with one room, few books, and only five months of school. White children had a new brick school with many books, a playground, and nine months of school. Black children had to walk, while white children rode buses. Later, Rosa worked with the NAACP and fought for fair laws. She would not use separate water fountains or elevators. Then, at age 42, she was told to give up her bus seat. She stayed seated, was arrested, and her action helped start the Montgomery bus boycott. After 381 days, the bus rules changed, and people could no longer be separated by skin color.

Michael backs out of the garage, and his father tells him to brush off the dust. Michael has found something very unusual in the garage.

summary_text: One day at school, Duncan opened his crayons and found a stack of letters with his name on them. Each crayon had a complaint. Beige Crayon said he was called light brown or dark tan, and he wanted to be known as beige. Gray Crayon was worn out from coloring elephants, rhinos, hippos, whales, and other large animals. White Crayon felt invisible because he was used on white paper and only worked for snow or empty spaces. Black Crayon said he was only used for outlines and wanted to color a black beach ball sometimes. Green Crayon liked his job, but he asked Duncan to settle an argument between Yellow and Orange, who both claimed to be the color of the sun. Blue Crayon said he was Duncan’s favorite but was now too short to see over the box. Pink Crayon complained that Duncan never used him. Peach Crayon said Duncan had peeled off his paper wrapping, leaving him embarrassed and naked. Duncan wanted to make the crayons happy, so he made a new picture. His teacher gave him an A for coloring and an A+ for creativity.

video_title: The Sour Grape | kids storytime, classroom read aloud, jory john, pete oswald, SEL lesson for kids
summary_text: The story is about a grape girl who calls herself sour because she keeps grudges when people upset her. She says she remembers every wrong, like when a banana bumped into her, an orange did not call her back, and a lime never returned her scarf. But she was not always like that. She grew up in a close-knit bunch of about 3,000 grapes living on a vine. Her family was kind and funny, and her grandparents visited on weekends to teach them to be kind, forgiving, considerate, and grateful, or “grapeful.” For a while, she stayed sweet and polite. Then her birthday party changed everything. She planned a big celebration with a ferris wheel, a magician, hay rides, snacks, and fireworks, but nobody came. She waited until sunset and felt upset. After that, she became bitter and started holding grudges. Later, when she was late meeting Lenny, he acted just like she did. Seeing the sky and park made her think differently, and she later found out she had written the wrong birthday date on the invitation. She realized the party had been her mistake. After that, she began talking things out, letting go of grudges, and being kinder again.

video_title: The Bad Seed | kids storytime, classroom read aloud, jory john, pete oswald, SEL lesson for kids
summary_text: The story is about a seed who calls himself a Bad Seed. He hears other seeds say he is bad, and he tells many ways he acts badly. He never puts things back, is late, tells jokes with no ending, does not wash, lies, cuts in line, stares, glares, and does not listen. He says he has always been this way, but he was not always bad. Long ago, he was a small seed on a sunflower in a field with a big family. One day the sunflower changed, and later he was in a bag of sunflower seeds. A giant took him, and he thought he would be lost forever. He was spit out, flew through the air, and landed under the bleachers. A piece of gum softened his fall. When he woke up, he felt different and became a bad seed. He lived alone in a soda can until he decided he did not want to be bad anymore. He tries to be good by saying please and thank you, smiling, and holding doors open, even though he still makes mistakes. In the end, others notice he is not all that bad anymore.

video_title: The Smart Cookie | kids classroom read aloud, story time, bravery, perseverance, growing confidence
summary_text: A cookie lives in a bakery near a river and tells about feeling unsure when he was young. He went to school in a gingerbread house with kind Miss Biscotti, but he did not raise his hand much, finished tests last, and sometimes made mistakes like spelling do wrong or adding when he should subtract. At night he worried in a cookie jar with many roommates and felt lost at sea. One day Miss Biscotti gave the class a new homework task: make something completely original. The cookie tried cooking, building, and making a sculpture, but nothing worked. Then he watched the rain and the river and had an idea to write a poem called My Crummy Days. He worked hard and felt excited when he finished. The next day he read the poem aloud in class. The other children listened, laughed, and clapped. Miss Biscotti said it was completely original and told him to keep writing. After that, he felt braver in school and learned that people can be smart in different ways.

Jabari and his dad said they did it, and Jabari said the next project would be a rocket to Jupiter.

summary_text: When summer began, Wallace went west because his parents wanted him to rest and calm his wild imagination. He rode a westbound train to visit Aunt Fern, but a group of Cowboys captured him and took him to their Cow Camp instead. The cattle boss said they needed a new Cowboy because the old one had quit, and Wallace agreed to help. He wrote Aunt Fern a note to tell her where he was. That night he got new clothes and looked like a Wrangler, but he learned that being a cowboy meant more than wearing boots and a hat. Over the next days, he learned roping, riding, and making fire with sticks. Soon everyone said Wallace was a first-rate cowhand. When the roundup was over, Aunt Fern invited him and the Cowboys to a barbecue. While they were eating, the cattle began to stamp and a stampede started. Wallace found a tablecloth on the ground and spun it like a lasso. The cattle ran away, and the Cowboys cheered and called him a true Buckaroo.

When she started school, she was excited at first, but the other children giggled when Mrs. Chud read her name. Joe said it was too long, Rita said it barely fit on her name tag, and Victoria said it was a flower name and that she would change it if it were hers. Chrysanthemum went home upset, and her parents told her her name was beautiful and perfect. The next day, the teasing continued, and Victoria said Chrysanthemum looked like a flower. Chrysanthemum had a bad dream about being picked apart like a flower. Later, Mrs. Twinkle, the music teacher, explained that her own name was Delphinium Twinkle and that she had been thinking of Chrysanthemum as a name for her baby. Hearing this made Chrysanthemum feel proud again. In the end, the class musical was a success, and Mrs. Twinkle later named her baby girl Chrysanthemum.

video_title: MONKEYS for Kids | Fun Monkey Facts for Children!
summary_text: Monkeys live in many places, like mountains, jungles, grasslands, rain forests, and cities. Some monkeys live in trees, and others live mostly on the ground. Snow monkeys, also called macaques, live in the mountains of Japan. In winter, they stay warm by bathing in hot mountain water that comes from inside the Earth. New World monkeys live in Central and South America. They are small, have flat noses, and live in trees. Capuchin monkeys are one kind of New World monkey. Old World monkeys live in Africa and Asia. They are bigger and have noses that are not flat. Vervet monkeys are one kind of Old World monkey. Monkey mothers stay close to their babies, and the babies learn from them. Young monkeys play, wrestle, and tumble. Boys often leave to join another troop, while girls usually stay with their moms. Monkeys also groom each other to show care.

video_title: The Mitten by Jan Brett - Winter Read Aloud for Children
summary_text: Nikki wanted new mittens made of wool as white as snow. His grandmother Baba did not want to make white mittens at first because she said they could be lost in the snow. Nikki wanted them, so Baba made them. She told him she would look to see if he was safe and sound when he came home, and then she would look to see if he still had his Snow White mittens. Nikki went outside, and soon one mitten dropped in the snow. A mole found it and crawled inside. Then a snowshoe rabbit came by and squeezed in too. A hedgehog, an owl, a badger, a fox, and a great bear all came to live in the mitten as well. The mitten stretched, but Baba's knitting held. Then a tiny mouse climbed in. The mouse tickled the bear, and the bear sneezed. The sneeze sent the mitten and the animals flying apart. Nikki saw the mitten in the sky and ran to get it. When he got home, Baba saw that he was safe and still had his mittens.

video_title: A House For Hermit Crab
summary_text: Hermit crab lives on the ocean floor in a shell house. His hard skin protects him, but his soft tummy needs the shell. One day in January, he grows too big for his little shell and steps out. He feels scared without a house. In February, he finds a bigger shell and moves in. It fits just right, but it looks plain. So in March he asks a sea enemy to decorate it. In April he adds a starfish. In May he adds coral. In June he adds a snail to clean the house. In July he adds a sea urchin to guard it. video_title: Peter's Chair
summary_text: Peter was building a tall block tower, and when it was finished, it crashed down. His mother told him to play more quietly because there was a baby in the house. Peter looked into Susie’s room and saw the cradle, the high chair, and his crib. They were painted pink for the baby. Peter felt upset and saw that his old chair had not been painted yet. He picked it up and ran to his room. He said, “Let’s run away, Willie!” Peter packed a shopping bag with cookies, dog biscuits, his blue chair, his toy crocodile, and a picture of him as a baby. Willie took his bone. They went outside and sat in front of the house, but Peter was too big to fit in his little chair. Then his mother called from the window and said they had something very special for lunch. Peter and Willie pretended not to hear. Soon Peter came up with an idea, and his mother knew he was home when she saw signs. Peter then sat in a grown-up chair with his father. He said, “Daddy, let’s paint the little chair pink for Suzie.” They did.

video_title: The Tail Of Three Trees
summary_text:
Once on a mountaintop, three little trees dreamed about what they would become. The first tree wanted to be a treasure chest full of gold and jewels. The second tree wanted to be a strong sailing ship for kings. The third tree wanted to stay on the mountain and grow so tall that people would think of God when they looked at her. Years passed, and the trees grew tall.

Then three woodcutters came. They cut down the first tree, the second tree, and the third tree. The first tree was made into a manger in a carpenter’s shop, not a treasure chest. The second tree was made into a small fishing boat and carried smelly fish, not kings. The third tree was cut into beams and left in a woodpile.

Later, the first tree held baby Jesus in a manger. The second tree carried Jesus on a lake, and he stopped the storm with one word. The third tree became the cross for Jesus, and on Sunday morning people remembered God’s love. The trees learned that God used them in ways better than they had dreamed.

video_title: Horton Hears A Who!
summary_text: In the jungle of Newell, Horton the elephant heard a tiny cry while he was splashing in a pool. He looked around and found only a little speck of dust floating in the air. Horton believed someone small was on it, so he gently lifted the clover and carried it to safety. A sour kangaroo and her young kangaroo laughed at him and said there was no one there. Horton still protected the speck because he said, “A person’s a person, no matter how small.” The news spread, and the Wickersham brothers took the clover away and gave it to the eagle Vlad Vladikov. Horton chased the eagle all night until the clover was dropped in a huge field of clovers. Horton searched and searched until he found the Whos in Whoville. The mayor asked everyone to make noise, and after Jojo added one last “Yop,” the Whos were heard. Horton was saved, and the kangaroos finally agreed to protect the Whos too.

video_title: Mufaro's Beautiful Daughters - An African Tale
summary_text: In a village in Africa, Mufaro lived with his two beautiful daughters, Manyara and Nyasha. Manyara was often rude and boasted that she would be queen while Nyasha would be her servant. Nyasha was kind, worked in her garden, and sang while she grew millet, sunflowers, yams, and vegetables. One day, a small garden snake named Nyoka stayed with Nyasha and helped make her garden even better. Later, a messenger announced that the king wanted a wife and invited the most worthy and beautiful daughters to come to the city. Mufaro told both daughters to go, but Manyara secretly left early. On the way, she ignored a hungry boy, insulted an old woman, laughed at laughing trees, and ran past a strange man with his head under his arm. When Nyasha traveled the same road, she shared food, gave seeds, and showed respect. At the palace, Manyara ran out in fear, saying a monster snake was inside. Nyasha entered and found Nyoka, who revealed he was the king and chose her as his wife. A great wedding followed, and Mufaro said he was happiest because Nyasha became queen and Manyara served in the queen’s household.

video_title: Somebody Loves You, Mr. Hatch
summary_text: Mr. Hatch was a lonely man who lived by himself, worked at the shoelace factory, and followed the same quiet routine every day. On Valentine’s Day, Mr. Goober the postman delivered a package to his porch. Inside Mr. Hatch found a heart-shaped box of candy and a card that said, “Somebody loves you.” Mr. Hatch was amazed because he had no friends, but the message made him laugh, dance, and smile for the first time. He dressed up, walked around the neighborhood, and began greeting people. At work and in town, he spoke kindly, shared candy, watched Mr. Smith’s newsstand, and helped Mr. Todd find his missing daughter, Melanie. He baked brownies and made lemonade, which led to a backyard picnic with children and parents. Later, Mr. Goober admitted the Valentine had been delivered to the wrong house. After Mr. Hatch gave back the box, he felt sad and returned to his old quiet life. Then the neighbors learned how much he had helped them. They surprised him with decorations, candy, streamers, and a sign that said, “Everybody loves Mr. Hatch!”

video_title: Snowflake Bentley
summary_text: Wilson Bentley, also called Willie, was born in 1865 on a farm in Jericho, Vermont, where heavy snow was common. He loved snow more than anything and spent his happiest days watching snowflakes land on mittens, barns, and fields. His mother taught him at home, gave him books, and later gave him an old microscope. Willie used it to study flowers, raindrops, grass, and especially snow. While other children played in the snow, he caught single snowflakes and learned that each crystal had six branches and that no two were exactly alike. He tried drawing snow crystals for three winters, but they melted too soon. Then, at age 16, he read about a camera with a microscope and wanted to photograph snowflakes. His parents bought the expensive camera, but the first pictures failed. Willie kept trying, learned new methods, and finally made clear photographs. He shared them with others, gave talks, and became known as the snowflake man. He later published Snow Crystals, worked until the end of his life, and died after walking home in a blizzard.

video_title: The Littlest Watchman
summary_text: Benjamin was a young watchman who sat at night beside an old tree stump on a hillside near Bethlehem. His father had taught him that watchmen waited for the sign of the promised king. Long ago, God’s people had broken the world through sin, but God promised to send someone from the family of Jesse to rescue them and restore everything. The watchmen kept repeating the promise and kept looking for a shoot from the stump. Benjamin tried hard, but the job was boring and full of distractions. Bugs, owls, teasing children, and the laughing shepherds made it difficult. One day many travelers passed by, and Benjamin began to wonder if the promise would ever happen. He looked away from the stump and watched the shepherds. Then a bright light filled the sky above them, and he heard singing. When he looked back, a small green shoot had appeared on the stump. Benjamin remembered the promise and ran into Bethlehem shouting that the king had come. A shepherd opened a door and invited him in to meet the king and join the watch.

video_title: Mortimer's Christmas Manger
summary_text: Mortimer was a wee mouse who lived in a big house in a dark hole under the stairs. He liked being unnoticed, but he did not like his hole because it was cold, cramped, and creepy. Each day he sneaked out to look for crumbs and tidbits. One day he saw a Christmas tree with twinkling lights and a bright star. Next to it was a little house and a bed that looked just right for him. Mortimer climbed the tree, reached the table, and found small statues. He moved the statues away and crawled into the baby’s wooden bed. Every day he found food like cookie crumbs, fruitcake morsels, and peppermint candy, but the statues were always put back. Then, on Christmas Eve, Mortimer heard a man tell the Christmas story about Joseph, Mary, Bethlehem, shepherds, wise men, and a baby born in a stable with no room in the inn. Mortimer saw that the baby statue was Jesus. He put all the statues back, laid the baby in the manger, prayed, and later found a new house just his size. He thanked Jesus for making room for him.

video_title: Thank You, Sarah
summary_text: Thanksgiving was fading away in the United States. People in New England still celebrated it, but many other regions did not, and the holiday was in danger of being forgotten. Sarah Hale became the person who fought to save it. She was a magazine editor, writer, and mother of five, and she used her pen as her main tool. Sarah wrote thousands of letters and articles to push for Thanksgiving to become a national holiday. Women across America also wrote letters after reading her work, and many states began to recognize Thanksgiving. Sarah then wrote to several presidents, including Zachary Taylor, Millard Fillmore, Franklin Pierce, and James Buchanan, but they all refused or did not act. During the Civil War, Sarah wrote to Abraham Lincoln and explained that a holiday could help bring the country together. Lincoln finally agreed. In 1863, he made Thanksgiving a national holiday for all Americans.

video_title: Fletcher And The Falling Leaves
summary_text: Each morning, Fletcher saw that the forest was changing. The green trees turned dusty gold, and his favorite tree became brown. Fletcher worried and told his mother, “I think my tree is sick.” His mother said it was only autumn. Fletcher went back and told the tree not to worry, but more leaves kept turning brown. One day, the wind blew a leaf off the tree. Fletcher caught it, called it Twee, and tried to put it back on the branch with grass and a twig. The leaf still fell. The next day, strong wind blew many leaves away. Fletcher tried to save them, but a squirrel and a porcupine each took leaves for their own nests and warm places. Then friendly birds came and put the leaves back on the tree. Later, the wind blew again and the last leaf flew away. Fletcher kept it safe in the den overnight. In the morning, the wind stopped, and the tree was covered in shining icicles. Fletcher hugged the tree and went to breakfast.

video_title: Library Lion
summary_text: One day a lion came to the library. He walked past the circulation desk, through the stacks, and into the story corner. Mr. McBee told Miss Merriweather, the head librarian, that there was a lion in the library. Miss Merriweather asked if he was breaking any rules. When Mr. McBee said no, she told him to leave the lion alone. The lion stayed for story hour and listened to the stories. When story hour ended, he roared because he wanted more. Miss Merriweather said he must be quiet or leave. The little girl asked if he could come back if he promised to be quiet, and Miss Merriweather said yes. The next day the lion came early and helped in the library. He dusted encyclopedias, licked envelopes, and let children stand on his back. Soon everyone liked having him there. Later the lion tried to help Miss Merriweather reach a book, but she fell and hurt her arm. Mr. McBee called a doctor. After that, the lion stayed away until Mr. McBee found him and told him a new rule allowed roaring to help a hurt friend. Then the lion came back, and Miss Merriweather ran to greet him.

video_title: A Library Book For Bear

Bear grumbled, but he had promised, so he put on his red roller skates and went with Mouse in a basket. The library looked very big, and Bear said there were too many books. Mouse tried to help by finding a book about pickles, but Bear did not like the books Mouse brought. He shouted about rockets and wooden canoes and kept being told to use a quiet voice. The story ended with a treasure chest full of pickle slices made of diamonds and gold. Bear liked pickles even more, and Mouse rode home with seven new books.

At school later, Miss Kirby still stomped and roared, but Bobby had seen her outside school too.

summary_text: The story explains the rule, “Do unto otters as you would have otters do unto you.” Mr. Rabbit thinks about how he wants otters to treat him. At the end, Mr. Rabbit says that this is how he would like otters to treat him, and that the rule is simple.

summary_text: One bright fall day, Sophie picked a squash at the farmer’s market and decided it was her friend. She named it Bernice, drew a face on it with markers, wrapped it in a blanket, and rocked it to sleep. When her parents wanted to cook it, Sophie said Bernice was not for supper. Bernice went everywhere with Sophie, including the library and the garden, and Sophie treated her like a pet. Her parents tried to explain that Bernice was a squash and would get mushy if they did not eat her, but Sophie would not agree. As winter came, Bernice became softer. Sophie learned from a farmer that squash need fresh air, good dirt, and a little love, so she planted Bernice in the garden and covered her with soft soil. After winter, a green sprout appeared. In summer, Bernice grew into two tiny squash named Bonnie and Baxter, and Sophie loved them too.

video_title: Wonders Grade 5- One Hen
summary_text: Cojo lives in a village in the Ashanti region of Ghana with his mother. After his father dies, Cojo stops going to school and helps his mother gather firewood to sell. Their village has a special money plan. Each family saves a little, and one family borrows the savings to start something important. Cojo’s mother uses her loan to buy a cart for firewood. Cojo asks for the leftover coins and buys a brown hen with a bright red comb. He takes care of the hen, checks for eggs, and soon she lays many. Cojo and his mother eat some eggs and sell the rest at the market. With the egg money, Cojo buys more hens, then goes back to school. He studies hard, earns a scholarship, and later goes to agricultural college. After college, he borrows money from a bank and starts a big poultry farm. His farm grows, helps many people, and Cojo’s family becomes stronger too.

video_title: Wonders Grade 5 Weslandia
summary_text:
Wesley lived in a town where he felt different from everyone else. He did not like pizza or soda, and he thought professional football was stupid. He would not shave half his head like the other boys, even when his father offered him five dollars. He had no friends and was often chased by tormentors. Every day his mother asked what he learned at school. One day Wesley realized he could use what he learned to make a summer project. He decided to grow his own food crop and found his own civilization.

He turned over a patch of ground in his yard, and after a windy night, plants began to grow. The plant made fruit, roots, leaves, bark, and fibers that Wesley used for food, drink, clothes, oil, and tools. He made a hat, a robe, a sundial, new games, and even a new language. He named his land Westlandia. By the end of summer, Wesley had a whole civilization, and when he went back to school in September, he had no shortage of friends.

video_title: Mountain Chef (@LiterallyCultured Read Aloud)
summary_text: Tai Singh was born in the mountains near Virginia City, Nevada. He grew up loving the Sierra and learned to write in English and Chinese. As a Chinese American, life was hard, but Tai Singh made big plans. He became a trail cook and worked for map makers in the mountains. In 1915, Stephen Mather hired him to cook for a camping trip with important guests. Tai Singh planned meals for many days and worked with an assistant named Eugene. Each morning they woke early, made the fire, cooked breakfast, packed lunch, and moved camp. They washed dishes, packed the stoves, and cooked fine dinners at the next campsite. One day a mule wandered away with fancy food, so Tai Singh changed his plans and cooked a simpler meal. Later another mule fell off a cliff, and he had to make more new food. At the end, he gave the campers fortune cookies, and they remembered the trip and helped support the national parks.

Tai Singh planned meals for 30 people for 10 days and cooked breakfast, lunch, and dinner while traveling from campsite to campsite. After other accidents, he still fed everyone well. At the end, he gave each camper a fortune cookie with a message about the mountains. Later, Congress created the national park service, and Sing Peak was named for him.

video_title: Kamala Harris: Rooted in Justice (Literally Cultured Read Aloud)
summary_text: Eve comes home from first grade upset after Calvin says girls cannot be president. Her mother explains that he is wrong and begins telling Eve the true story of Kamala Harris. Kamala is born in Oakland to parents Shyamala and Donald, and her family has roots in India, Jamaica, Berkeley, and Oakland. Her parents take her to civil rights marches and teach her about peace, justice, and freedom. Kamala and her sister Maya visit their grandparents in Zambia and learn that justice runs in their family. When Kamala is seven, her parents divorce, and she moves with her mother and Maya to Berkeley. She rides a bus to school in a richer white neighborhood, where she learns with children from many backgrounds. At the Shelton House, Mrs. Regina Shelton encourages her and helps her feel confident. Kamala later studies at Howard, works hard, wins student elections, and prepares for a career in law and public service. She becomes district attorney, attorney general, and a U.S. senator, then runs for president before ending her campaign. The story ends with Eve ready to speak up for herself.

video_title: Kamala and Maya’s Big Idea (Literally Cultured Read Aloud)
summary_text: Kamala and Maya looked at the empty courtyard and wished for a playground. They told Mommy, and she said they should ask the landlord, the person who owns the building. Kamala wrote a letter, Maya drew a picture, and they went to ask him. The landlord said no. That night, the sisters asked the other children in the building, and the children also wanted a playground. Kamala wrote a longer letter, but the landlord said the project would cost too much. He said they could do it themselves if they wanted. The children asked their parents and neighbors for help. Most people said no, but Mr. Green said maybe he could find scrap lumber and sand. Soon the children built parts of the playground. Miss Lopez said maybe they could get an old tire for a teeter-totter. More maybes turned into yeses. They had a potluck, and later Miss Flores helped them find a slide. After a bake sale and a sidewalk sale, the slide arrived. Kamala and Maya rode it first, and the landlord said they did a good job.

video_title: The Floating Field: How a Group of Thai Boys Built Their Own Soccer Field (Read Aloud)
summary_text: Pret Hemman lives in a village on stilts with his family. Before school, he helps his father load the Longboat with nets while his mother makes coffee and cuts jack fruit. Pret’s father fishes for groupers and prawns, but Pret dreams of other things. After school, Pret and the boys go to the sandbar near the pier to play soccer. They use poles, boats, and the tide to make their game work, and they play until the water comes back and covers the field. One day they watch the World Cup at Uncle’s coffee shop and decide to make their own team. Pret suggests building a field, so the boys collect wood, barrels, styrofoam, old boat parts, and dock pieces. They build a floating field at the pier, even when villagers say it cannot be done. After weeks of work, the field is finished. The boys play there every day, and more villagers come to watch and cheer.

video_title: Love in the Library (@LiterallyCultured Read Aloud)
summary_text: Tama works in the library at Minoka, a prison camp for Japanese Americans. She does not like the desert, the dust, the fences, or the guard towers, and she tries not to look at the guards. Every day, George comes to the library with books he returned the day before. Tama has been in Minoka for a year, and life there is hard. The weather is very hot in summer, very cold in winter, and muddy in spring and fall. Families live in single rooms and have no privacy. Tama keeps working because she loves books, even though she does not know when she will leave. The library gives her a small place of comfort, and George’s smile helps too. One day, Tama feels sad and cannot find the right word for all her feelings. George tells her there is a word: “human.” Later, Tama sees that George loves her. They marry, have a son in Minoka, and keep hoping for change and beauty.

summary_text: Mom is cooking in the kitchen, and Grandma is standing near her. The family is getting ready for New Year’s, which is the child’s favorite day. Mom says, “A dragon would bring health and Fortune.” The child and friends help decorate the street with F Chun and Red Lanterns. They look for a red Dragon’s Tail and think they see a real dragon. This dragon can control water, and the child learns he is hard to catch. They try to trap him with tacos, but then they change to noodles and sticky rice. The dragon likes them and comes back for more. They try to make him sleepy, then they try gold, but nothing works. At last, they use the Dragon Dance, but the dragon is still not caught. The street is messy, so they clean up. The child tells Mom sorry and says they tried their best. Mom hugs the child, and the family watches fireworks together. The child feels lucky and says, “Better luck next year.”

video_title: 🪨 The Crow and the Pitcher—Aesop's Fables Short Read Aloud for Kids
summary_text: A very thirsty crow looked everywhere for water. At last, she found a pitcher with some cool water inside. But the pitcher had a narrow neck, and the crow could not reach the water at the bottom. She tried, but she still could not drink. Then the crow stopped and thought. Soon she had an idea. She picked up small pebbles from the ground and dropped them into the pitcher, one by one. Each pebble made the water rise a little higher. The crow kept adding pebbles until the water came up close enough for her to drink. At last, she could reach the cool water and take a drink. After she was refreshed, the crow said, “Necessity is the mother of invention.”

At school, he drew his teacher on the whiteboard as a funny witch, and his teacher caught him and said, “We are not amused, David.” David also made silly noises in class and was sent out. When he hopped on a cart and kicked it around like a racer, he went too fast, and his mom was upset. Another time, he got his head stuck in the stair railing. He also tried to sneak cake, but his mom stopped him. Then curiosity caused him to stick a peanut with its shell up his nose, so he had to see a doctor. He drew a beard and mustache on his face, scared his mom with a loud day, ran around almost naked after his shower, and would not settle down at bedtime.

video_title: MAD, MAD, MAD 🤪🔥💥(Adapted from the book by Leslie Patricelli)
summary_text: Matt says he is sometimes happy and sometimes sad. He sees a beautiful cat, and then he gets mad, mad, mad. He screams and roars, falls on the floor, and cries and shouts. He says he cannot get it out. Then Daddy wants to take the dog outside, but Matt says no. He changes his mind again and does not want to stay or go. Matt sits and flops on the floor. Ouch. Mom helps by bringing his blankie. Matt hugs the blankie, but he is still cranky. Then Dad tells him to breathe in and breathe out. Matt does it, and he feels better. He says he did it himself. After that, he thinks about the naughty cat and says, “I’ll get you.” He hugs and smiles, and his happy feeling comes back for a while. The story ends by showing things that can help mad feelings go away, like pets, friends, coloring, bubble baths, naps, music, yoga, reading books, pillow punches, and laughing.

video_title: 📖 Binky - A Fun Baby Adventure! 👶✨
summary_text: A child loses Binky and feels upset. A grown-up says not to cry and offers to help find it. First, they look under the couch, under the bed, and in the toy box. The grown-up asks fishy, doggy, Mommy, and Daddy if they have Binky, but no one does. The search moves to the living room, where they look on the rug and behind the chair. The child gets worried and asks where Binky is. At last, Daddy sees it and says it is in the crib. The child is happy and thanks Daddy. In the end, the child has Binky again and goes to sleep with teddy bear.

video_title: 📚🎬 No No Yes Yes by Leslie Patricelli - An Animated Storybook ✨
summary_text: A little child sees many things and learns what is okay and what is not okay. At lunchtime, the child does not dump food on a head because that is messy and wasteful. The child does not draw on walls or on animals, and instead draws on paper. The child does not eat dog food and eats a banana instead. The child does not put a coin in the toilet or play with toys in the toilet. Instead, toys belong in the bathtub. The child also learns not to hit a friend with a toy mallet and to be kind and gentle. The child does not pull a cat’s tail and pats the cat gently. The child does not use scissors to cut hair, but can use scissors for crafts. The child stays safe by walking hand in hand with parents, turns book pages gently, and washes hands before reading. The child plays with bath toys in the tub, uses toilet paper and toothpaste the right way, stays away from outlets, treats plants gently, and can try on Daddy’s hat, play with blocks, and cuddle a blankie.

summary_text: A child says it must go party, but it is wearing a diaper. An adult says the child needs to learn to use the potty. Peach said Duncan peeled off his paper and left him naked. Duncan read all the letters and learned each crayon had something to say.

summary_text: Frog was in his garden when Toad came by and admired it. Toad said he wished he had a garden, so Frog gave him flower seeds and told him to plant them. He explained that Toad should leave them alone for a few days and let the sun and rain help them. Toad worried at night, used candles, read a story to the seeds, sang songs, read poems, and played music for them. At last he fell asleep, and Frog woke him to show him that little green plants were growing. Toad was happy, and Frog reminded him that it had been hard work. summary_text: George Washington was born in 1732 in a simple Virginia farmhouse. As a boy, he liked fishing, boating, watching ships, and riding horses. He learned to read and write in school and practiced his handwriting by copying rules. When he was 11, his father died, and George helped his mother run the farm and care for his younger sister and brothers. He found his father’s surveying tools and used them to measure land, and he liked surveying. When he was 16, he got a job surveying land in the Virginia wilderness. summary_text: In a twinkling forest, a cheerful skeleton named Skellyy loved moonlit walks, soft music, and his three best friends: Willow, Hazel, and Tany, who were friendly witches. The witches warned him that the whispering woods could be tricky after dark, but Skellyy still went to pick bone berries. In the woods, strange things moved, a bush puffed pink smoke, and Skellyy sneezed and spun around. When the smoke cleared, he found that he was lost. Back at the cottage, the witches saw he was gone too long. Tany got her moon map, and the three witches called their friend Greta to help. They flew through the woods and found Skellyy on a mossy rock. They took him home, and that night they made Moon Perry muffins instead and ate them under the stars.

Soon the house was full of noisy fairies, and the old woman shouted for them to stop.
The fairies quit the work for a moment, but then they tore everything apart again and kept making a mess.
The old woman went to the village wise woman, who explained that the fairies were helping because she had complained.
The wise woman told her to trick the fairies by turning everything upside down and never complaining again.
The old woman did this, and the fairies left.
After that, she did her own housework and ended by saying, “How I love it, love it, love it!”

video_title: 🍎 Johnny Appleseed by Reeve Lindbergh, Read Aloud Book for Kids 🍏
summary_text: In the early days of the American frontier, John Chapman, later known as Johnny Appleseed, traveled through the wilderness planting apple trees. One day he came to the Goodwin family’s home, where young Hannah Goodwin first saw him. He was thin, barefoot, and wore old clothes. The family invited him in, and he talked about the wide, wild land and the pioneers moving west. He said he could not stay because he had to keep planting apple trees across the Great Frontier. He carried a Bible and a sack of seeds, but no gun or knife, and he said he would harm no creature. Years passed, and Hannah heard stories of him walking through snow, rain, and dangerous land, sharing apple seeds and helping orchards grow. At the end of his life, old Hannah saw him again in her orchard. He thanked God for the trees, and later children were told to remember Johnny Appleseed and the apples he left behind.
